definitions.versionInForce: A version applies to a report made on a date from its effectiveFrom date up to, but not including, its supersededOn date. An empty supersededOn means the version is still open.

definitions.emergencyBand: Emergency categories are noHeating, noHotWater and waterLeakEscape. Clock-hour emergency limits apply only to occupied dwellings. A report in an emergency category on a dwelling that is not occupied on its report date falls under the routine working-day limit.

policy.approvalRule: Works whose latest written estimate, excluding VAT, is above the approval threshold in force on the report date need board panel approval before instruction. SECTION 2. DEFINITIONS (CLAUSE 1, ALL VERSIONS)
2.1 Landing time means the time at which the catch is weighed on the scale at a designated port, as recorded on the weighing ticket. It is not the time the vessel berths, the time unloading starts, or the time the declaration is lodged.
2.2 Designated port means a port on the Office register of weighing points. Fusthorpe Quay and Waxmouth Quay are on the register for 2026.
2.3 Declaration means the electronic landing declaration lodged with the Office by the holder or the master, showing the weight, the basis of the weight, the landing time and the vessel registration.

2.5 Total holding means, for one vessel and one stock unit, the annual allocation for the quota year, plus any tonnage transferred in and recorded under clause 4, plus any carry-in approved for that year. Tonnage left unused from an earlier year and recorded as lapsed is not part of the total holding.
2.6 Live weight equivalent means the weight of fish in live form. A landing declared in gutted weight is converted by multiplying its gutted weight by the conversion factor for the stock unit, then rounding to the nearest whole kilogram, with a result of exactly 0.5 rounded up.
2.7 Counted landing means a declaration whose status is ACCEPTED. A declaration whose status is VOID is not counted and takes no part in any holding calculation.
2.8 Tolerance means 2 per cent of the total holding for the stock unit at year end. An overage equal to the tolerance or less is within tolerance. An overage larger than the tolerance is above tolerance.

instrument.title: Laiport and Raxcombe Reach Lock Navigation Bylaws, consolidated working text

rules.text: Laiport Lock opens for passages from 06:00 to 20:00 on Monday to Saturday and from 08:00 to 16:00 on Sunday, subject to the amendments listed in the amendment register.
A vessel whose overall length is at or above the booking threshold in metres must hold a confirmed booked slot before entering Laiport Lock. A vessel below the threshold may enter on arrival.

A vessel holding a pilot-exemption certificate that is current on the date of passage may enter Laiport Lock on arrival whatever its overall length. A certificate is current from its issue date up to and including its expiry date.
A licensed pilot must be aboard any vessel of 25.0 m overall length or more when passing through Laiport Lock.
A booking request must be lodged at least 48 hours before the start of the requested slot. A request lodged less than 48 hours before the slot start is treated as not lodged for that slot.

In the Raxcombe reach, speed is set by overall length. Class 1 is under the class 1 bound in metres and is limited to 6 km/h. Class 2 runs from the class 1 bound up to but not including 20.0 m and is limited to 5 km/h. Class 3 is 20.0 m and over and is limited to 4 km/h. Registered tow vessels are excluded from the classes.
For reporting, a closure of one chamber only is not counted as a closure of Laiport Lock. A closure counts only when both chambers are closed to all traffic.

amendments.summary: Revised wording of clause 4.2 on fender placement. No change to thresholds, speed classes or hours.
Clause 3.1 booking threshold changed from 15.0 m to 14.0 m overall length.
Clause 5.4 class 1 bound changed from 10.0 m to 9.5 m. Other class limits unchanged.
Sunday opening hours at Laiport Lock changed to 08:00 to 14:00.
Proposed change to the pilot-aboard length, under consultation and not yet adopted.

SECTION 1. STANDING RULE STD-STG2-04
Issued 12 January 2026. In force from 12 January 2026 unless a later memo in Section 2 covers the same point.

1.1 A cadet advances from Stage 2 to Stage 3 only when all four of the following conditions are met at a Stage 2 progression assessment:
(a) dual instruction logged in Stage 2 totals at least the dual-hours threshold in force on the assessment date (the current figures are in Section 2);
(b) at least 8 solo circuits are logged in Stage 2. A solo circuit is one flown with the cadet as the only person aboard. A circuit flown with an instructor aboard is logged as dual and does not count as solo;
(c) the Stage 2 written examination score is at least the pass mark in force on the assessment date;
(d) the cadet holds a Class 2 medical certificate that is valid on the assessment date.

1.2 Illness allowance. Where a cadet's training was interrupted by illness for a continuous period longer than 14 days, the dual-hours threshold in 1.1(a) may be reduced by 2.5 hours. The allowance applies only if the Chief Flying Instructor signs an exception note on the cadet's file on or before the day the assessment is recorded. An interruption is measured as the number of calendar days from the first day missed to the last day missed, counting both of those days. An interruption of exactly 14 days does not qualify.

1.3 Dates and units. An assessment counts for the date on which it is held. Sessions may be logged in hours, in hours and minutes, or in minutes; 60 minutes equals 1 hour.

1.4 Simulator sessions are logged on a separate simulator sheet. They do not count as dual instruction under 1.1(a) and are not solo circuits under 1.1(b).

1.5 A written examination that is failed may be re-sat once, no sooner than 7 days after the first sitting. The re-sit result replaces the earlier result for progression purposes.

1.6 An assessment is recorded only when the assessing instructor has signed it and the Training Records Officer has countersigned it.

1.7 A circuit is logged once, at the time it is flown, from the aircraft flight log. A circuit that is later corrected is logged against the date of the original flight.

1.8 Where a later memo in Section 2 covers the same point as this section, the later memo governs for the assessments it covers.

1.9 The file is the source of record for progression. A verbal report does not change a figure on the file unless it is written into the file under 1.6.

Notice periods are counted as calendar days from the day the notice is received up to, but not including, the first festival day: the day of receipt counts and the first festival day does not.

2. CLAUSE 6 - POWER
v2 clause 6.1, replaced by Amendment 2A clause 2: Class H pitches take power from the organiser outlet and must not declare a draw above 16 A. Trader-supplied generators are not permitted on the site.
Amendment 2A clause 2 (replacement for 6.1): Class H pitches may draw up to 16 A from the organiser outlet. A Class H pitch whose most recent revised trader form declares a draw above 16 A must be supplied entirely by a generator hired and run by the trader in the trader's own name, and the organiser outlet may not be used for that pitch.
v2 clause 6.4 (not changed by Amendment 2A): Pitches in Zone A, the dedicated-feed zone, are outside clause 6.1 as amended and may draw up to 32 A from the organiser outlet. Pitches in every other zone remain subject to clause 6.1 as amended.

3. CLAUSE 9 - WITHDRAWAL AND PITCH DEPOSIT
v2 clause 9.2: Written notice received at least 35 days before the first festival day returns the full pitch deposit. Notice received 14 to 34 days before returns half of it. Notice received fewer than 14 days before returns none.
Amendment 2A clause 3 (replacement for 9.2): Written notice received 40 or more days before the first festival day returns the full pitch deposit. Notice received 14 to 39 days before returns half of the pitch deposit. Notice received fewer than 14 days before returns none.
Clause 9.1 (how to give notice) is unchanged. Pitch deposits are held by the site office until the festival closes and are returned only under clause 9.

4. CLAUSES 10 AND 11 - INSURANCE AND REQUIRED TRADER DOCUMENTS
Clause 10: each trader must hold public liability insurance of at least GBP 5,000,000, and the certificate must cover each festival day.
Clause 11: every Class H trader must have the following on file before the festival: (a) gas safety certificate covering every gas appliance; (b) PAT test certificate for every mains-powered appliance; (c) public liability certificate under clause 10; (d) fryer fire-suppression service certificate, where the trader declares a fryer. A document counts as on file on the audit date only if it is logged on or before that date. Logging after the audit date does not count for it.

5. CLAUSE 12 AND 13 - ALLERGENS AND FIRE SAFETY
Clause 12: traders must display a written allergen list at the point of sale for every item, using the fourteen allergen categories in the site food safety schedule.
Clause 13: each Class H pitch must have at least two fire blankets and one 6 kg dry powder extinguisher within reach of the fryer or griddle. Fire exits must be kept clear, and gas cylinders must be stored outside the trader unit in a rack secured to the site frame.

standards.title: Steam boiler certification and working-pressure control

clauses.text: Each locomotive boiler must hold a current thorough-examination certificate stating a working-pressure figure. A certificate runs for twelve months from its issue date and is current up to and including the day before the anniversary of that issue date.
A working-pressure figure set by an amendment applies from the effective date written in that amendment and remains in force until a later amendment changes it.

An amendment that replaces a figure set by an earlier amendment supersedes that earlier figure only from the effective date of the replacing amendment. Before that date the earlier figure continues to apply.
After a steam test is recorded as completed, the locomotive may carry passengers only once 48 hours have passed since the recorded completion time.
Where an examining inspector corrects a completion time by a later message, the corrected time is the recorded completion time and the earlier time is void.

A steam-driving qualification is granted at a passed road assessment and runs for twelve months from the assessment date. It is current up to and including the day before the anniversary of that date.
A person without a current steam-driving qualification may not be rostered as driver on a steam running day.

doc.title: PLK-3 and HKR-2 season tonnage rules
doc.apply_rule: A version governs any action dated on or after its from date and before the from date of the next version. Quota figures are taken as at the asof date and under the version in force on that date.

defs.D1: Base allocation: the tonnage in the vessel's season allocation letter for the stock.
defs.D2: Counted landing (version 3.1 onward): a landing for which a weighing certificate has been filed with the Board on or before the asof date. A landing with no certificate filed by that date is recorded but not counted for that asof date.
defs.D3: Swap-in cap: approved swap-in tonnage for a season may not exceed the swap-in cap percentage of base allocation. Swap-out tonnage does not count toward this cap.
defs.D4: Adjusted allocation: base allocation plus carry-over booked, plus approved swap-in tonnage, minus approved swap-out tonnage.
defs.D5: Carry-over cap: carry-over booked may not exceed the carry cap percentage of base allocation under the version that governs the booking date.

q4.instructions: Consider only PLK-3 landings for this vessel's 2026 season. Take all figures as at 10 March 2026, inclusive, under the rule version in force on that date. (a) Pending weight is the total weight of PLK-3 landings dated on or before 10 March 2026 for which no weighing certificate had been filed with the Board on or before 10 March 2026. A certificate filed after that date does not make a landing counted as at that date. (b) Remaining headroom is the adjusted allocation as at that date minus the counted landings as at that date. Adjusted allocation is the base allocation from the season allocation letter, plus carry-over actually booked (not merely claimed), plus approved swap-in tonnage in force, minus approved swap-out tonnage in force. A swap that has been superseded or amended counts only at its current tonnage, not in addition to the earlier entry. 2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 Qualifying dual hours means flight time that meets all three of these tests: (a) it is logged in the aircraft log with activityType DUAL; (b) a qualified flight instructor was on board for the whole flight; (c) the flight was not aborted before takeoff. Flight time logged as SOLO, simulator time logged as SIM, and any flight aborted before takeoff do not count, whatever their duration.
2.2 Solo hours means flight time logged in the aircraft log with activityType SOLO, taken at the activityType that stands at the date of this memo. A reclassification under Section 7 changes that activityType and so moves the entry out of this category.
2.3 Medical certificate validity: a certificate is valid on every date up to and including its stated expiry date. It is not valid on any date after its expiry date.
2.4 Booked date means the date shown on the most recent written booking confirmation for a check. Provisional holds, verbal agreements and earlier confirmations do not set the booked date.
2.5 Shortfall means the stage2MinimumDualHours in 4.1 less the qualifying dual hours at the date of this memo. A result of zero or less means there is no shortfall.
2.6 Durations written as a decimal number are hours. Durations written with h and m are hours and minutes, and are converted to decimal hours by dividing the minutes by 60.

3. STAGE 2 REQUIREMENTS
3.1 A student may sit the Stage 2 check only when qualifying dual hours are at least the stage2MinimumDualHours, and a medical certificate that is valid on the booked date of the check is held on file.
3.2 Solo hours do not count toward the stage2MinimumDualHours. Simulator hours do not count toward it either.
3.3 Where the hours condition in 3.1 is not met, the check may proceed only under an exception approved as set out in Section 5.
3.4 Booking of the check must be confirmed in writing to the student, showing the date, the panel location and the confirmation reference.
3.5 The panel will not accept a file in which the aircraft log and the flight-hour summary disagree. The flight-hour summary is generated from the aircraft log at the date of this memo. Any change to an activityType is recorded as an amendment under Section 7 and is not edited directly in the summary.
3.6 Hours carried over from another training school are entered in the aircraft log under the activityType they held at the sending school. No carried-over hours are recorded for ST-0417.

state.Notes: Scheme Secretary ruling of 2025-09-12: the isolation standard version that applies to a crop is set by its sowing date. A crop sown on or after a version's effective date is assessed under that version, whatever the date of the inspection, and a crop sown before that date is assessed under the earlier version. Distances and barrier widths are measured from the edge of the declared crop to the edge of the neighbouring crop, or across a barrier from edge to edge, to the nearest 0.1 metre. A measured figure equal to a stated minimum meets that minimum. Where a later Inspection Log entry records a new distance for a pair of fields, the later distance replaces the earlier one and the earlier entry stays on file. Where a later entry corrects a barrier width for the same pair of fields, the corrected width replaces the earlier one and leaves any distance on record unchanged. Shortfalls are worked out from the figures as recorded and reported to one decimal place. Clause 2.0-E is applied only where the barrier is a permanent feature of the holding as surveyed. Roguing on CLW-22-03 was completed on 2025-11-04 and those results are not part of this review. criteria.false: At least one hull's decision in the reply conflicts with a release condition or the cure rule.

q3.instructions: Which fault best explains the candidate reply's decision on HULL-0412?

criteria.no_fault: The decision for this hull is consistent with every rule condition that applies to it.
criteria.misread_pressure_test: The reply misreads the recorded pressure test result for this hull.
criteria.wrong_hull_reference: The reply attaches its reasoning to a different hull than the one it decides on.
criteria.wrong_launch_time: The reply uses a launch date or time other than the one on the request.
criteria.omitted_cure_check: The reply releases the hull without checking the minimum wait between final coat completion and planned launch.
criteria.unsupported_extra_hold: The reply holds the hull for a reason the rules do not require.

criteria.hold_pending_pressure_test: Hold the hull until a pressure test result is recorded.
criteria.reverse_to_hold_for_cure: Change the decision to hold because the minimum cure time is not met at the planned launch time.

Three: exactly three listed hulls have a decision with a stated reason
All: every listed hull has a decision with a stated reason

check.q4: Final coat 2026-04-06 07:30 to launch 2026-04-09 07:30 = 3 days = 72 h; minimum is 72 h and an equal gap meets the rule -> at least the minimum -> true.
check.q5: Hull integrity sign-off (2026-04-06) and pressure test pass (2026-04-06) are recorded; cure 2026-04-07 18:00 to 2026-04-09 07:30 = 37.5 h, below 72 h, so the release condition is unmet -> hold is required, reversing the reply's release -> reverse_to_hold_for_cure.
check.q6: Reply gives a decision with a reason for HULL-0412 (release), HULL-0415 (release), HULL-0419 (release) and HULL-0421 (hold): 4 of 4 listed hulls -> all listed hulls -> level 4.

FILE MEMO - CLERTCOMBE VINEYARD LEASE (PLOTS 1 TO 4)
Date of memo: 12 January 2026
From: Kyrie Grairford, Assistant Estates Manager, Beadaxis Land Trust (kyrie.grairford@beadaxistrust.example)
To: Tyllo Brealler, Operations Lead, Malldresex Vineyards Ltd (t.brealler@malldresexvines.example)
Copy: Skeaxine Cockmere, Land Surveyor (s.cockmere@beadaxistrust.example); Trisan Graidale, Solicitor (trisan.graidale@frandsonlaw.example)

PURPOSE
This memo brings together the terms that now govern the Clertcombe Vineyard lease after the Deed of Variation and the surrender of part of Plot 4. Where a later message corrects an earlier one, the later message applies, as set out below. Please file this with the lease and do not work from the 2019 copy alone.

1. LEASE BASICS
1.1 The lease is dated 14 May 2019. It was granted by Beadaxis Land Trust (the landlord) to Malldresex Vineyards Ltd (the tenant) over Clertcombe Vineyard, Plots 1 to 4.
1.2 The contractual term is fifteen years from 1 September 2019.
1.3 The rent year is the calendar year, running from 1 January to 31 December. Rent for each rent year is payable in advance on the first working day of that year.
1.4 Original clause 4.2 set the rent at £380 per planted hectare per rent year. A planted hectare means a hectare of planted vines, measured on the first day of the rent year. Headlands, tracks, unplanted ground and farm buildings are excluded from the measurement.
1.5 Schedule 1 recorded a planted area of 18.4 hectares at 1 September 2019: Plot 1 4.6 ha, Plot 2 4.9 ha, Plot 3 5.2 ha and Plot 4 3.7 ha. The 0.6 ha of headland shown on the plan is not part of that figure.
1.6 Original clause 4.4 provided for an annual index review of the rent. That clause is deleted by the variation in section 2.
1.7 The 2025 rent was paid in full on 2 January 2025 on the planted area then recorded, at the original rate in clause 4.2.

2. DEED OF VARIATION
2.1 A Deed of Variation was signed by both parties on 11 November 2025. Its effective date is 1 January 2026 (the Variation Date). Until the Variation Date the original lease terms continue to apply.
2.2 Clause 4.2 is replaced: the rent is £415 per planted hectare per rent year for every rent year beginning on or after the Variation Date. The definition of planted hectare in paragraph 1.4 continues to apply.
2.3 Clause 4.4 (index review) is deleted in full.
2.4 Clause 7.3 (harvest entry) is replaced. The tenant must give the landlord at least 14 days' written notice before entering any plot for harvest. Where a landlord works notice is in force for that plot on the date of entry, the notice must be at least the longer of 14 days and the period stated in that works notice.
2.5 The deed states that the replacement clause 7.3 governs every harvest entry on or after the Variation Date. Entries made before that date remain under the original clause 7.3, which required 21 days' written notice.
2.6 All other clauses are unchanged. The deed does not alter the surrender provisions in clause 9.

3. SURRENDER OF PART OF PLOT 4
3.1 On 3 June 2025 the tenant served a surrender notice for part of Plot 4. The notice gave the surrendered area as 1.4 ha and the surrender date as 31 August 2025.
3.2 On 18 August 2025 Skeaxine Cockmere sent the survey result. The surveyed area of planted vines given up was 2.4 ha, and the 1.4 ha figure in the notice was a transcription error. By email on 19 August 2025 both parties agreed that the surrender is for 2.4 ha with effect from 31 August 2025.
3.3 No other surrender, new planting, grubbing out or replanting has been recorded on the lease since 1 September 2019.
3.4 Obligations for the surrendered ground end on the surrender date. The tenant has no further duty to prune, spray or harvest that ground after 31 August 2025. The surrendered ground was planted and is removed from the planted area from the surrender date.

4. PLOT 3 DRAINAGE WORKS
4.1 On 2 October 2025 the landlord served a works notice for drainage works on Plot 3. The notice required 25 days' notice from the tenant before any harvest entry to Plot 3, until the works are certified complete.
4.2 On 9 October 2025 Kyrie Grairford wrote that the figure of 25 days in the works notice was a typing error and that the correct period is 30 days. The 30-day period replaces the figure in the works notice from the date of that email.
4.3 The drainage contractor has not yet issued a completion certificate. As at the date of this memo the works notice remains in force for Plot 3, and it stays in force until a completion certificate is issued and copied to the tenant.
4.4 The works notice covers Plot 3 only. Plots 1, 2 and 4 are not subject to any works notice.

5. EMAIL LOG (EXTRACTS)
5.1 21 November 2025, Tyllo Brealler: Is the 2026 rent measured on the planted area at 1 January or at harvest?
5.2 24 November 2025, Kyrie Grairford: The area is measured on the first day of the rent year, as paragraph 1.4 says, and the variation keeps that wording. Measurement is therefore on 1 January.
5.3 15 December 2025, Trisan Graidale: The counterpart copy of the deed was received on 12 December. This does not change the effective date, which is fixed by the deed at 1 January 2026.
5.4 6 January 2026, Tyllo Brealler: Thanks. The pump service is booked for 14 February 2026 and Malldresex will arrange access.
5.5 8 January 2026, Kyrie Grairford: Noted. Please send the harvest plan for each plot as soon as it is set.
5.6 9 January 2026, Skeaxine Cockmere: The reservoir meter on Plot 2 read 3,870 cubic metres at the last visit. The figure is for the abstraction licence file only and has no bearing on rent.
5.7 10 January 2026, Trisan Graidale: The frost claim letter is with the insurer and will be copied to the file once it is received.

6. OTHER MATTERS (FOR INFORMATION)
6.1 The frost damage on Plot 2 was assessed by the insurer at £2,350. The claim has not yet been confirmed for payment, and the frost damage does not affect the rent. No vines have yet been removed from Plot 2.
6.2 The landlord's insurance schedule renews on 1 March each year. The renewal premium is not a term of the lease.
6.3 Malldresex has asked whether a rent-free period could be agreed for 2027. The landlord has not yet responded.
6.4 Harvest picking windows for Plots 1, 2 and 4 are being set by the tenant's agronomist and will be circulated separately. In 2025 the first picking on Plot 1 started on 3 September. Picking windows do not change the notice periods in section 2.
6.5 The reservoir on Plot 2 holds 1,200 cubic metres. It is not part of any planted area and is not measured for rent.
6.6 For the file: the 2025 harvest entry on Plot 3 was made on 14 September 2025 on 21 days' notice under the original clause 7.3. That entry was made before the Variation Date and is not affected by the replacement clause.

7. STANDING OBLIGATIONS (RECAP)
7.1 The tenant must keep the headlands mown twice each summer and maintain the field drains on Plots 1, 2 and 4.
7.2 Spray records must be kept for seven years and produced to the landlord within 10 working days of a written request.
7.3 The tenant holds the water abstraction licence for the reservoir on Plot 2. The licence allows 4,500 cubic metres in any 12 months, and the landlord does not guarantee supply in dry summers.
7.4 Insurance of the vines against frost and hail is the tenant's responsibility. The landlord insures the buildings and the reservoir structure.
7.5 The boundary fence along the Neanness Road is shared equally. The tenant maintains the wire and the landlord maintains the posts.
7.6 Any change of use, including conversion of the vines to another crop, needs the landlord's written consent before work starts.

s1-definitions.restricted-reach: A reach listed in Schedule R1 of these bylaws. No other stretch of river is a restricted reach, even if it carries a restricted-reach sign.
s1-definitions.overall-length: Hull length plus the length of all fixed external fittings, such as bowsprits, fixed masts and davits. Portable items removed before the vessel is underway are excluded.
s1-definitions.consecutive-stay: Continuous time at one public berth. A departure from that berth lasting more than two hours ends the stay; a departure of two hours or less does not end it.
s1-definitions.gauge-height: Water level reading at the named gauge, measured from chart datum.
s1-definitions.available-depth: Chart depth over the shoal plus the gauge height at the time of transit.
s1-definitions.permit-day: A permit period counts its issue date as day 1, and ends at the end of its last counted day.

s2-restricted-reaches.2.1: Schedule R1 lists the restricted reaches. The Naillness shoal reach is listed as R1-04.
s2-restricted-reaches.2.2: A vessel of 12.0 m overall length or less may enter a restricted reach without notice.
s2-restricted-reaches.2.3: A vessel over 12.0 m and up to 24.0 m overall length may enter a restricted reach on a radio call to the reach controller given at entry.
s2-restricted-reaches.2.4: A vessel over 24.0 m overall length needs a harbour master permit under section 3 before entering a restricted reach.
s2-restricted-reaches.2.5: Naillness shoal reach (R1-04): chart depth over the shoal is 2.10 m. The squat allowance for under-keel checks is 0.30 m for all vessels in this reach.

s3-permits.3.1: A harbour master permit is issued for one vessel, one reach and one stated transit window.
s3-permits.3.2: A transit outside the stated window is not covered by the permit.
s3-permits.3.3: A permit remains in force for its validity period under the permit-day definition, unless revoked in writing by the harbour master.

s4-public-berths.4.1: A public berth may be used for a consecutive stay up to the limit that applies to that berth.
s4-public-berths.4.2: The default limit for a public berth is 72 consecutive hours.
s4-public-berths.4.3: Where an amendment sets a separate limit for a named berth, that limit replaces the default in 4.2 for that berth only.
s4-public-berths.4.4: A stay beyond the applicable limit needs a berth extension permit from the harbour master.

pol.title: Loan periods, renewals, holds and fines

amd.summary: From 2026-02-16 the audiobook and DVD renewal limit is 1 for renewal requests made on or after that date, whatever the checkout date. Holds marked ready on or after 2026-02-16 have a 5-day pickup window; holds marked ready earlier keep the 7-day window. Other rules unchanged.

rules.text: Loan period is counted in calendar days from the checkout date; the checkout day is not counted, so the due date is checkout plus the loan period. Due dates are not moved for closures. Books 21 days; music CDs 14 days; audiobooks 14 days; DVDs 7 days. Reference items do not lend.
A fine of 25p accrues per item for each calendar day after the due date, up to and including the report date. Fines are capped at £5.00 per item.

An item may be renewed only if on the request date it is not overdue, no other patron holds it, the borrower's account is not blocked, and renewals already made are below the renewal limit. Base renewal limit is 2 for all lending types, subject to the amendment.
Outstanding fines are accrued fines not yet paid. An account whose outstanding fines total £10.00 or more is blocked from borrowing new items and from renewing. Lower totals do not block the account.
A ready hold may be collected up to and including the last day of its pickup window, counted in days after the ready date. Base pickup window is 7 days.
Where the amendment and the base rules conflict, the amendment governs the matters it covers from its effective date.

state:
STELLPOXIX QUOTA BOARD
Quota Administration Unit

MEMORANDUM

ref: SQB-QA-2026-0418
issued: 4 December 2026
from: Rymys Dracroft, Quota Administration Officer (rymys.dracroft@stellpoxix-quota.org)
to: Skason Trysridge, Licensing Review Panel
copy: Stoxus Vemcaxer, Tronwold Harbour Office; Thurtard Rondgill, Bresbury Monitoring Unit
subject: DH-4 quota position for vessel VX-3307 at the close of Period 4

1. Purpose
This memo sets out the DH-4 quota position for vessel VX-3307, owned by Stallmere Ltd, at the close of Period 4 in 2026. It answers the items the panel raised at its October sitting: how a transfer-in registered in September is tested, which landings count toward the Period 4 position, when a declaration counts as late, and which banking allowance applies at year end. The register extract is in section 5 and the correspondence is in section 6. Read section 2 first, because several terms are narrower than their everyday meaning and the figures in section 5 depend on them. Unless stated otherwise, weights are live weights in kilograms and all dates are in 2026.

2. Definitions
These definitions apply to this memo, to the register and to the reporting calendar. Where a definition here differs from ordinary usage, this section governs.

2.1 Landing. A landing is the discharge of catch at port as recorded on a signed landing declaration. A landing counts toward quota on the date its declaration is signed, unless section 3.2 applies.

2.2 Live weight. Live weight is the landed weight multiplied by the conversion factor for the product form in Table 2. The result is rounded to the nearest whole kilogram, with halves rounded up. Only live weight is counted against quota. Landed weight is never counted directly.

2.3 Stock group DH-4. DH-4 means only the product forms listed under DH-4 in Table 2. Other species, even when landed on the same trip or on the same declaration, are not part of DH-4.

2.4 Available quota. For a stock, available quota is the annual allocation held on 1 January, plus transfers in accepted under section 4, minus transfers out registered in the same quota year.

2.5 Relating period. A declaration relates to the reporting period in which the catch was landed, as shown on the declaration. Its relating period does not change when it is signed.

2.6 Days late. A declaration is late if it is signed after the end of the period it relates to. Days late are counted from the first calendar day after that period ends, up to and including the signing date. A declaration signed on the last day of its period is not late.

2.7 Registration date. A transfer is registered on the date the Board enters it on the register, not the date the parties agree it. Earlier agreements do not change the version that applies.

Table 2. Conversion factors
Product form | Stock group | Factor
HK-G (hake, gutted) | DH-4 | 1.20
HK-H (hake, headed) | DH-4 | 1.30
MK-T (monkfish, tail) | MK-2 | 2.10

3. Reporting calendar and exceptions

3.1 Reporting calendar. Period 4 of 2026 runs from 1 August to 31 October 2026 and ends at 23:59 on 31 October 2026. Period 5 runs from 1 November to 31 December 2026. A bulletin issued on 2 October 2026 gave the Period 4 end as 30 October. That bulletin is superseded by this section, and the end date is 31 October.

3.2 Weather closure. Where a landing declaration cites a weather closure notice and the vessel was at sea when that notice was declared, the landing counts on the port arrival date stated on the declaration, not on the signing date. The exception needs the notice reference to appear on the declaration. Without the reference, section 2.1 applies.

3.3 Small boats. Vessels under 10 m may land on Board-approved small-boat days without the late-declaration rule in section 2.6. VX-3307 is 14 m and is not covered by this provision.

4. Transfers and rule versions

4.1 Version 2.1 of the quota transfer rules was in force from 1 January 2026. Under version 2.1, each transfer-in registration is limited to 20 per cent of the vessel's annual allocation held on 1 January. The banking allowance for unused quota is 10 per cent of that allocation.

4.2 Amendment A took effect on 1 September 2026. It reduces the transfer-in limit to 15 per cent and the banking allowance to 5 per cent of the annual allocation held on 1 January. It does not change Table 2 or section 2. Amendment A stays in force until it is replaced.

4.3 A transfer-in is tested under the version in force on its registration date. The banking allowance is set by the version in force on 31 December of the quota year.

4.4 The transfer-in limit applies to each registration separately. Registrations are not added together when the limit is tested.

4.5 Transfers out are not limited by percentage. They are deducted when registered.

4.6 A proposal in memo SQB-QA-2026-0377 for a banking allowance of 12 per cent was withdrawn before adoption and has no effect on any register entry.

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 Observing night means the period from 18:00 on the booked date to 06:00 on the calendar day after it. A booking is identified by its booked date.
1.2 Session means one spell of instrument use inside an observing night. Session time means the sum of the lengths of all sessions in one observing night, with closed pauses left out of that sum.
1.3 A closed pause is any period in which the dome is closed to observing during a booked night, whatever the cause.
1.4 Quarter means a calendar quarter: January to March, April to June, July to September or October to December.
1.5 Days before, for a cancellation, means the number of calendar days from the date the cancellation is received to the booked date.
1.6 A night counts as used if at least one session is recorded in it.

2. ALLOCATION
2.1 Each partner receives up to 12 allocated nights per quarter. Unused allocated nights lapse at the end of the quarter.
2.2 A night closed early by cloud or rain, meaning the dome is closed by cloud or rain before the booked end time, is restored to the partner's quota and is not counted as used if the session time in that night is under 2 hours.
2.3 A restored night is added back to the quarter in which its booked date falls.

3. BOOKINGS, CANCELLATION AND FEES
3.1 Partners book through the host scheduling office. Bookings are confirmed in writing.
3.2 A cancellation received fewer than 14 days before the booked date forfeits the night.
3.3 Session fee is GBP 70 per used night, payable in arrears. Restored nights are not charged.

4. MAINTENANCE CLOSURES
4.1 The dome is closed for drive servicing from 2026-04-13 to 2026-04-17 inclusive. No bookings are accepted for nights in that closure.
4.2 Replacement of the secondary guider from 2026-05-04 to 2026-05-05 does not stop bookings.

5. AMENDMENTS (each replaces the clause named; all other clauses stand)

PART A - BYLAW TEXT

Bylaw 4: Mooring at the Cleport and Taixgate landings
4.1 Vessels may moor at the public landings for up to 48 hours without charge.
4.2 Mooring beyond 48 hours requires a berth licence from the Harbourmaster.
4.3 Licence fees are set by the Board each January and are published on the notice board at each landing.
4.4 A vessel must not obstruct the Cleport slip while a Trust service vessel is launching.

Bylaw 5: Wash and wake
5.1 Vessels must reduce wash in any reach where a sign states a wash limit.
5.2 Wash limits are enforced by the Harbourmaster and do not replace the speed limits in Bylaw 7 or Bylaw 8.

Bylaw 6: Anchoring. Vessels may anchor in the Cleport basin only outside the marked fairway. Anchoring in the Narrows reach is not permitted except in an emergency.

Bylaw 7: Speed in the Tylbury Narrows reach. The reach is the water between Marker N1 (Cleport side) and Marker N2 (Taixgate side).

Version 1 (made 2025-03-18; in force from 2025-04-01 until superseded)
7.1 No vessel shall exceed 6 km/h in the Narrows reach.
7.2 Speed is the average over the reach, taken from the vessel's GPS record.
7.3 Trust service and emergency vessels answering a call are exempt from 7.1.

Version 2 (made by the Board on 2026-05-15; commencement date set by amendment notice A2, see Part B)
7.1 No vessel shall exceed 5 km/h in the Narrows reach.
7.2 Speed is the average over the reach, taken from the vessel's GPS record.
7.3 Trust service and emergency vessels answering a call are exempt from 7.1.
7.4 Exception: a vessel holding a current Narrows Passage Permit may travel at the speed stated on that permit. The stated speed must not be more than 8 km/h. A permit stating more than 8 km/h gives no speed relief, and 7.1 applies.
7.5 A permit is current on each day from its first valid day to its last valid day, both days included.
7.6 Vessel clocks: logged times must be station time. Where a vessel's clock is found to run fast, subtract the difference found at the latest inspection from every logged time until the clock is reset and the reset is recorded. Where it runs slow, add the difference.

Bylaw 8: Upper Tylbury reach. A separate limit of 9 km/h applies in the Upper Tylbury reach only. It does not apply to the Narrows reach.

Bylaw 9: Navigation lights. Vessels under way between sunset and sunrise must show the lights in the Trust's lights schedule. Lights are not a speed matter and do not alter Bylaw 7 or Bylaw 8.

Bylaw 10: Transit records. A master's transit record must give times as read from the vessel's clock, state the date of the most recent clock check, and give the GPS average speed over the reach.

1. SCOPE AND COUNTING
1.1 Applies to every instructor who delivers full-motion simulator sessions at the Saixholm site.
1.2 Hours for each session are end time minus start time, shown in decimal hours to one place.
1.3 Session types are IF (instruction flight) and CK (check ride). Status DONE means the session ran; status CXL means it was cancelled.
1.4 Cancelled sessions are excluded from every total in this memo.
1.5 Hours are totalled per instructor per calendar day, as defined in section 9.

2. DAILY LIMIT
2.1 Rev A wording, in force from 2026-02-01: an instructor shall not be rostered for more than 6.0 hours of simulator sessions in one calendar day.
2.2 Amendment A1 (rev B): clause 2.1 is replaced by the following. An instructor shall not be rostered for more than 5.5 hours of simulator sessions in one calendar day, subject only to clause 3. A1 takes effect on 2026-06-01 and applies to sessions dated on or after that date.
2.3 Sessions dated before 2026-06-01 remain under the Rev A wording of clause 2.1 and are not affected by A1.

3. CHECK-RIDE EXCEPTION
3.1 A CK session may take an instructor to up to 7.0 hours in one calendar day, provided the Chief Instructor has issued written authorisation for that instructor and that date before the session starts.
3.2 The authorisation carries a reference in the form CA-nnnn, the instructor name, the date covered, and the issue date.
3.3 The exception in 3.1 applies only to CK sessions. It does not change the weekly limit in clause 4.

4. WEEKLY LIMIT
4.1 No instructor may hold more than 24.0 hours of sessions in any week.
4.2 A week runs Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59, local time.

5. NOTES
5.1 Simulator bay 3 was re-cabled on 2026-06-04; bay 2 remained in use throughout. No effect on hours.
5.2 A visiting examiner panel from Stearfell is due on 2026-06-16. No change to this memo arises from it.

draft_reply.text: The latest Route 9 bus that gets you to Jarminster Bus Station in time leaves Bomfell Market Square at 10:50 on Saturday 16 May. The journey takes 32 minutes, so you arrive at 11:18. Please check the stop board on the day for any changes.

state.notes: Fare shown is the adult single. No fare change is planned this year.

q1.instructions: The arrival time the draft gives for its recommended bus is the correct arrival time for that departure, according to the timetable's running time.

criteria.false: The draft's arrival time does not equal the recommended departure time plus the timetable running time.

criteria.latest_in_time: The departure is the latest one from the boarding stop that reaches the destination by the required time.
criteria.too_late: The departure reaches the destination after the required time.
criteria.no_bus_named: The draft does not name any departure from the boarding stop.

q3.instructions: Rate how fully and accurately the draft reply answers the passenger's enquiry about the latest suitable bus and the journey time.
criteria: No suitable bus: the reply does not name a departure that reaches the destination by the required time, or names no departure at all.
Suitable bus, timing missing: the reply names a suitable departure but gives neither the journey time nor the arrival time.
Suitable bus, timing wrong: the reply names a suitable departure and gives both a journey time and an arrival time, and at least one of those two does not match the timetable.

Suitable bus, timing right, detail partly given: the reply names a suitable departure, and its journey time and arrival time both match the timetable, but it leaves out the travel date or the boarding stop.
Suitable bus, timing right, full detail: the reply names a suitable departure, its journey time and arrival time both match the timetable, and it states both the travel date and the boarding stop.

q4.instructions: Route 14's listed Saturday stops do not include Jarminster Bus Station.

criteria.true: Jarminster Bus Station is absent from Route 14's listed Saturday stops.
criteria.false: Jarminster Bus Station appears in Route 14's listed Saturday stops.

q5.instructions: Which correction, if any, must be made to the draft before it is sent to the passenger?

criteria.change_travel_day: The travel day the reply gives is wrong and must be replaced.
criteria.change_boarding_stop: The boarding stop the reply gives is wrong and must be replaced.
criteria.change_departure_time: The departure time the reply recommends is wrong and must be replaced.
criteria.no_change: The reply is accurate as written and can be sent without edits.
criteria.change_arrival_time: The arrival time the reply gives is wrong and must be replaced.

q6.instructions: Rate how many of the passenger's three stated requirements (travel date, boarding stop, and arrival deadline) the departure recommended in the draft meets, according to the timetable.
criteria: Meets at most one of the three stated requirements.
Meets exactly two of the three stated requirements.
Meets all three stated requirements.

criteria.no_fault: The reply states the total payable for the payment date the member specified, including any surcharge that applies on that date, and every other statement in the reply is correct.
criteria.tier_mismatch: The reply prices the membership using the fee for a membership tier other than the one the member holds.
criteria.rounding_slip: The reply's total is the correct amount for the specified payment date but is expressed to the wrong number of pence or whole pounds.
criteria.answers_other_date: The reply's total is the correct amount for a payment made on some other date. It wrongly concludes that the specified payment date falls outside the surcharge window, so the surcharge is left out and the total answers a different payment date from the one asked about.
criteria.lapse_rule_misread: The reply states the date or condition on which the membership lapses incorrectly.
criteria.arithmetic_slip: The reply adds a fee and a surcharge together but the sum it gives is wrong.

policy.settlementBasis: One final settlement, made after the adjuster's figures are agreed. No interim payments are made under this policy.

wording.lossMeasure: Loss percentage is the shortfall of measured yield below expected yield, divided by expected yield and shown as a percentage. Expected yield is the figure in force on the date of the loss event.
wording.standardExcess: The insured bears the first 10 percentage points of loss on each field. The payable loss percentage is the calculated loss percentage less 10 points.
wording.exceptionClause: Exception to the standard excess: where the calculated loss percentage on a field is 35 per cent or more, no excess is deducted and the full calculated loss percentage is payable. Below 35 per cent the standard excess applies.
wording.payment: Amount payable equals the payable loss percentage multiplied by the field's sum insured. Sum insured is insured area in hectares multiplied by sum insured per hectare.
wording.noticeRule: Notice of loss must reach the insurer within 14 calendar days after the day the loss is discovered. The day of discovery is not counted, and notice received on the fourteenth day is in time.

Subject: DEM-4 pool rules, carry-forward notices and March log extract

0. PURPOSE
This memo restates the DEM-4 pool rules for landing desks, lists the carry-forward notices on the register, records correspondence on notices and landings, and gives the DEM-4 log extract for 1 to 20 March 2026. Where this memo and a schedule differ, the amendment in section 5 governs for the matters it covers. Revision B replaces revision A, which should no longer be used.

1. SCHEDULES IN FORCE
1.1 Schedule DQ-1 (Version 1), issued 2025-09-30. Governs landings dated before 2026-03-01, and any landing that section 5.1 keeps under it.
1.2 Schedule DQ-2 (Version 2), issued 2026-01-22. Governs landings dated on or after 2026-03-01, subject to amendment A-3 in section 5.
1.3 A clause marked 'both schedules' applies to landings under either version.
1.4 Landing date means the date the catch is weighed at the port of landing, not the date the vessel sailed.
1.5 A landed weight is taken as keyed unless a correction under section 12 replaces it.

2. ANNEX: MONTHLY BASE ALLOCATION, DEM-4 [both schedules]
2.1 class_S (registered length under 10.0 m): 1,800 kg per calendar month.
2.2 class_O (registered length 10.0 m or more): 3,600 kg per calendar month.
2.3 Annex values are identical under DQ-1 and DQ-2.
2.4 HAD-7 and CRA-2 are not covered by this memo.
2.5 Weights may be keyed in kg or t. One tonne is 1,000 kg. Keyed weights are used as keyed, without further rounding.

3. CARRY-IN AND TOLERANCE [both schedules]
3.1 Landed weight counts toward the vessel's monthly total whichever pool debits it.
3.2 Allowance for a month = base allocation (section 2) less any carry-in deduction. Headroom = allowance less landings already recorded in that month.
3.3 If a vessel's landed total in a calendar month is above its base allocation, the overrun is deducted from the base allocation of the next calendar month. The deduction equals the overrun less a tolerance of 150 kg, and is never below zero.
3.4 Carry-in applies only to the immediately following calendar month. An overrun is not carried in twice.
3.5 A month with no overrun carries nothing forward.

4. POOL RULES
4.1 DQ-1: DEM-4 landings are debited to the general pool. Carry-forward notices are not provided for under DQ-1.
4.2 DQ-2: a landing by a class_S vessel is debited to the small-vessel reserve, which is 8% of the DEM-4 total.
4.3 DQ-2 exception: where a carry-forward notice (section 6) is in force for the vessel, the stock and the landing date, and the landed weight is within the notice tonnage, the landing is debited to the carry-forward pool instead of the reserve or the general pool.
4.4 A notice is in force on a date when that date falls within its validity window and the notice is not suspended on that date. A suspension applies on the date it is sent and continues until the date a reinstatement is sent; on the date a reinstatement is sent, the notice is not suspended.
4.5 DQ-2: a landing by a class_O vessel is debited to the general pool, unless the exception in 4.3 applies.
4.6 Desk check order when debiting a landing: (a) landing date and schedule version (sections 1 and 5); (b) vessel class (section 2); (c) whether a notice is in force on the landing date (sections 4.4 and 6); (d) whether the landed weight is within the notice tonnage.
4.7 A landing is debited once. A later change to a notice does not move an earlier landing (section 12.3).

5. AMENDMENT A-3 (issued 2026-02-18; amends DQ-2 only)
5.1 For class_O vessels, the Version 2 start date is deferred to 2026-03-16. Class_O landings dated 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-15 inclusive remain under DQ-1.
5.2 Class_S vessels are not affected by A-3.
5.3 A-3 does not change the annex in section 2 or the tolerance in section 3.

PART 1. BYLAW NB-07 AS MADE (IN FORCE FROM 2024-01-01)
1.1 Scope. This bylaw applies to every powered vessel navigating the Necombe Reach between marker 14 and marker 22, both markers included. Marker positions are listed in the Trust chart pack, sheet 4, and are not repeated here.
1.2 Measurement. Speed is measured over ground from the vessel's own GPS log. A breach is recorded when a logged speed is over the limit in force on the date of the log. A logged speed equal to the limit is not a breach.
1.3 General limit. Ten (10) knots, for any vessel not covered by clause 1.4.
1.4 Large vessels. Eight (8) knots for any vessel with a registered length over 12.0 m.
1.5 Permits. No powered vessel may navigate the reach without a current navigation permit (NP) issued by the Trust. The NP must be displayed on the vessel while under way.

PART 2. SURVEY CERTIFICATES
2.1 A survey certificate (SC) is valid until the expiry date printed on it.
2.2 Lapse rule. Where an SC expires and its replacement takes effect later, the vessel holds no valid SC on each day from the day after expiry up to and including the day before the replacement's effective date. Those days together are the lapse. The replacement's effective date is not part of the lapse.
2.3 No powered vessel may navigate the reach during a lapse.
2.4 A replacement SC is normally issued before its effective date. The issue date alone does not end a lapse; only the effective date does.
2.5 Surveyors must be on the Trust list at the date of survey. A survey by a surveyor not on the list does not create a certificate.

PART 3. ENFORCEMENT
3.1 The first breach recorded against a vessel is answered with a written warning under clause 3.2.
3.2 Written warning. The harbourmaster issues a written warning. A warning alone is not a suspension.
3.3 Second breach. Where a breach is recorded against a vessel and an earlier breach by the same vessel was recorded no more than twelve (12) months before it, the harbourmaster may suspend the vessel's NP. Before any suspension, the harbourmaster must give written notice of fourteen (14) days, counted from the date of the notice.
3.4 Written representations may be made within the notice period. Representations do not extend the notice period.
3.5 Breach records are kept for 36 months from the date of the log.
3.6 Fees. The renewal fee for an NP is set by the Trust each year. It is separate from any penalty under this Part.
3.7 A decision under this Part is notified to the owner in writing, copied to the permit holder's registered address on file.

PART 4. AMENDMENT A1 (REPLACES CLAUSE 1.4)
Made by the Trust board on 2025-09-18.
Clause 1.4 is deleted and replaced with the following text:
1.4 Large vessels. Six (6) knots for any vessel with a registered length over 12.0 m, unless the vessel's NP carries a wash-reduction endorsement (WRE). A vessel whose NP carries a WRE may use eight (8) knots.
Clauses 1.1 to 1.3, 1.5 and Parts 2 and 3 are not changed by A1.
The effective date of A1 is settled in the correspondence at Part 5.

2. DEFINITIONS
The terms below carry only the meanings given here wherever they appear in this file.
2.1 Season: the period from 1 April in one calendar year to 31 March of the following year, both days included. A date belongs to the season that began on the most recent 1 April on or before that date.
2.2 Counted volume (for a season): the total of gate weighbridge volumes, in cubic metres, of all loads dated within that season, excluding any entry marked VOID, less the salvage exclusion under Clause 4.1.
2.3 Salvage volume: timber from trees felled or uprooted by a storm, where a Salvage Notice covering that timber has been issued by the Authority. Timber without an issued Salvage Notice is not salvage volume, whatever its cause.
2.4 Clear days (between two dates): the days strictly after the earlier date and strictly before the later date. Neither of the two dates is counted.
2.5 Load date: a load counts on the date recorded at the gate weighbridge, not on the date of felling or haulage.

3. CAP
3.1 As originally granted, counted volume for each season must not exceed 18,000 m3.
3.2 Amendment A1, dated 2025-11-03, replaces Clause 3.1 with the following text: "For any season beginning on or after 1 April 2026, counted volume must not exceed 16,800 m3. The cap for the season beginning 1 April 2025 remains 18,000 m3."
3.3 The cap in force for a season is the figure that Clause 3.1 or Amendment A1 gives for that season's start date. Amendment A1 does not alter any other clause of the permit.

4. SALVAGE EXCEPTION
4.1 For any season, salvage volume is excluded from counted volume up to a maximum of 1,200 m3. Any salvage volume above that maximum is counted.
4.2 A Salvage Notice revoked before any load is booked against it contributes no salvage volume.
4.3 Salvage volume is taken from the gate weighbridge entries booked against each notice, not from the notice alone.
4.4 Salvage excluded in one season does not carry forward to the next season.
4.5 Salvage volume must be logged against a notice number on the gate sheet.

5. TOLERANCE
5.1 A breach of the cap occurs only when counted volume for a season exceeds the cap in force for that season by more than the tolerance in Clause 5.2.
5.2 An excess over the cap in force that is up to and including 2.5 per cent of that cap is tolerated and is not a breach. An excess above 2.5 per cent is a breach.
5.3 Tolerance is not carried forward from one season to the next.
5.4 A tolerated excess is recorded on the season file but is not a breach.

6. PERMIT RENEWAL
6.1 A renewal application lodged at least 60 clear days before the permit expiry date follows the standard route.
6.2 An application lodged less than 60 clear days before the permit expiry date, but on or before that date, follows the late route, provided no breach is open on the concession on the date of lodgement.
6.3 An application lodged after the permit expiry date is not accepted, and the area then goes to open tender.
6.4 A breach is open from the date the Authority records it in the breach register until the date the Authority records it as closed.
6.5 Permit expiry dates are not extended by correspondence.
6.6 An application sent by email is lodged on the date it is sent.
6.7 A renewal application must state the permit number and the concession reference.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 'Trading day' means a calendar day on which the stall is open to the public for the sale of goods for at least four hours. A day on which the stall is not open to the public for that period is not a trading day, even if the vendor is on site that day.
1.2 'Access day' means a day on which the vendor is on site to set up, stock or dismantle a stall and which is not a trading day.
1.3 'Working day' means a day from Monday to Friday that is not a holiday listed in Annex C. When counting working days after a given day, the given day is not counted and counting starts on the next day.
1.4 'Hot-oil cooking' means heating fat or oil in an open vessel to a set temperature above 100 °C, whether the heat source is gas or electric.
1.5 'Returning vendor' means a vendor that traded at an event run by the organiser on any date within the 24 months before the first day of the festival.
1.6 'Pitch supply allowance' means the maximum continuous electrical load, in watts, that the organiser supplies to one pitch.

SECTION 2. FEES
2.1 The fee is £180 for each trading day.
2.2 An access day is charged at half the trading-day fee.
2.3 No flat weekly rate is offered at this festival.

SECTION 3. PUBLIC LIABILITY
3.1 Each vendor must hold public liability cover of at least £2 million for the festival period. Item A1 of Section 8 replaces this minimum for hot-oil vendors.

SECTION 4. FOOD HYGIENE CERTIFICATE
4.1 A vendor must send its food hygiene certificate to the organiser at least 21 days before the first trading day. Item A2 of Section 8 replaces this period for returning vendors.

SECTION 5. ELECTRICAL LOAD AND GAS
5.1 The pitch supply allowance is 3,500 W for each pitch. Every appliance connected to the pitch supply must appear on the vendor's equipment schedule with its rated load. Connecting an appliance that is not on the current schedule is a breach of these terms.
5.2 Gas cylinders are not part of the electrical schedule. They must be kept in the caged gas store at the rear of the site, not under or beside the stall.
5.3 Where the organiser approves a change to the equipment schedule in writing, the latest approved revision applies from the date of that approval.

SECTION 6. INDUCTION, ACCESS AND EXCEPTION
6.1 Every vendor must complete the food-safety induction with the organiser before taking access to the site.
6.2 The induction cut-off date is 31 May 2026.
6.3 Exception: one access day is waived, with no fee payable, for any vendor that completed the food-safety induction on or before the induction cut-off date. The waiver applies only to an access day that falls before the first trading day.

SECTION 7. WASTE COOKING OIL
7.1 Waste cooking oil must be collected from the stall by the organiser's approved contractor within the period set out in this section, counted from the last trading day.
7.2 The period is three working days after the last trading day. Item A3 of Section 8 replaces this period for hot-oil vendors.

SECTION 8. AMENDMENT A (effective on issue, 20 May 2026)
A1. Public liability: a vendor using hot-oil cooking must hold public liability cover of at least £5 million. Every other vendor keeps the £2 million minimum in clause 3.1.
A2. Hygiene certificate: a returning vendor must send its food hygiene certificate at least 14 days before the first trading day. Every other vendor keeps the 21-day period in clause 4.1.
A3. Waste oil: a hot-oil vendor must have its waste cooking oil collected within four working days after the last trading day. Every other vendor keeps the period in clause 7.2.
A4. Nothing in this amendment changes Section 2, Section 5 or Section 6.

SECTION 9. SITE CONDUCT
9.1 Vendors must keep gangways clear during opening hours and must not leave cartons or cylinders on the public side of the stall.
9.2 The organiser may move a vendor to another pitch on written notice if a safety condition is not met. A move does not change the vendor's fees or access days.
9.3 Vendors must display the stall reference on the front fascia in characters at least 10 cm high.

ANNEX B. EQUIPMENT AND GAS RULES

B2. Extension leads must be rated for the total load connected through them and must not be daisy-chained.
B3. Any appliance that heats fat or oil in an open vessel must be shown on the schedule. Rated loads given in kilowatts are read as thousands of watts.

clause-7-1.text: Each fuel card may buy no more than 90 litres of fuel in any calendar day, counted midnight to midnight in base local time. A total of exactly 90 litres is permitted; a total above 90 litres is not.

clause-7-3.text: Fuel may be bought only at stations on the approved station list in this document. Purchases at any other station are not permitted.

clause-7-4.title: Precedence
clause-7-4.text: Where Annex B applies to the vehicle a card is issued against on the transaction date, the Annex B daily limit replaces the clause 7-1 limit for that card on that date. Clauses 7-2 and 7-3 apply in all cases.

annex-b.title: Long-haul allowance
annex-b.eligibility: Vehicle is listed on the long-haul register with a registration period that covers the transaction date.

subj: Monkfish allocation, April to June 2026, Group C trawl fleet

1. SCOPE
1.1 This memo sets how monkfish allocation is held, counted and transferred for Group C trawlers for the period 1 April 2026 to 30 June 2026, both dates included (the period).
1.2 Other species are governed by separate notices. Rows for other species in section 7 are shown for context only.
1.3 Declared weights are in kilograms unless the row is marked t. One tonne is 1,000 kg.
1.4 A vessel not listed in section 3 has no monkfish allocation under this memo.

2. ALLOCATION AND COUNTING
2.1 A vessel's effective allocation for the period is the section 3 figure, as replaced by section 6 where that applies, plus any approved transfer in to it under section 5, minus any approved transfer out of it.
2.2 Monkfish landed in the period is counted against the effective allocation at its declared weight, except where section 4 applies. Corrections under section 10 apply to the count.
2.3 Declarations dated before 1 April 2026 or after 30 June 2026 are not counted.
2.4 Counting runs to the close of the last date covered by the log extract in section 7. The extract in this memo runs to the close of 8 June 2026.
2.5 Declarations dated after that close are not in the extract and are not counted in this memo, whatever date they were received.
2.6 No rounding is applied to individual rows or to totals. Tonne rows are converted at 1 t = 1,000 kg before counting, and totals are carried at full precision.
2.7 Remaining allocation at a given close means the effective allocation less the monkfish counted for dates up to and including that close.

3. SCHEDULE A (as issued 2026-04-06)

KF-61 | Tholport | 18.0
KF-72 | Foumport | 22.5
KF-83 | Skalwych | 9.0

3.2 Reconciliation sheet RS-03, prepared 2026-04-30, still shows KF-61 at 18.0 t. It predates amendment 2 and does not apply.

4. BYCATCH EXCEPTION
4.1 Monkfish landed as incidental catch is declared with code INC. Code INC monkfish is counted against allocation only where the trip total for that code is above the threshold in 4.2.
4.2 The threshold is 250 kg per trip. A trip total of exactly 250 kg is not counted. A trip total above 250 kg is counted in full, which means every INC row for that trip is counted, not only the part above 250 kg.
4.3 Trip totals are taken across all INC rows with the same vessel and trip code and dated within the period.
4.4 Monkfish declared with code LAN is always counted in full, whatever its weight.
4.5 The exception in this section does not apply to any species other than monkfish.

5. TRANSFERS AND REGISTER
5.1 A vessel may transfer part of its monkfish allocation to another listed Group C vessel. A transfer needs written approval from Quota Control, recorded in the register below.
5.2 An approved transfer adds its tonnage to the receiving vessel's effective allocation and removes it from the giving vessel's effective allocation. This applies whatever the approval date and whatever the section 3 or section 6 figure in force on that date.

5.5 A transfer shows as approved only when the register records an approval date. Agreement given by telephone or by any other informal message does not count.
5.6 Each transfer is one row. Rows are not combined.

BICKSTOW REGIONAL FERRIES LTD - OPERATIONS PLANNING MEMO
memoRef: BRF-OPS-2026-0117

issuedOn: 2026-01-19
circulatedTo: Fexys Hullbrook, Fleet Operations; Parin Clexbrook, Terminal Services
routeName: Treasgate-Tallcombe crossing
reviewPeriod: 1 November 2025 to 30 December 2025, both dates inclusive

scheduleBasis: The route is timetabled for 6 scheduled sailings on each day of the review period, except 24 and 25 December 2025, which ran a reduced timetable of 4 scheduled sailings each day.

logSummary:
  weatherCancellations: 27 sailings did not sail at all and the logged cause was weather.
  mechanicalCancellations: 4 sailings did not sail; the logged cause was a mechanical fault.
  lateRunningSailings: 11 sailings sailed more than 30 minutes late and completed the crossing.
  otherRouteWeatherCancellations: 19 sailings on the Bickstow-Tallcombe route; reported separately and outside this review.

countingConvention: A sailing counts toward the weather-cancellation rate only if it did not sail at all and the logged cause is weather. Late-running sailings that completed the crossing and mechanical cancellations are not counted. The weather-cancellation rate is the counted sailings divided by the scheduled sailings in the review period.

mitigationOptions (expected weather cancellations avoided over the next 60 days):
  measureA retain_current_timetable: no change to vessel or timetable; cost GBP 0; avoids 0.
  measureB buffer_timetable_change: add 20 minutes of slack to each crossing; cost GBP 2,000; avoids 2.
  measureC ramp_maintenance_upgrade: upgrade linkspan hydraulics and ramp seals to a higher wind-tolerance standard; cost GBP 9,000; avoids 6.
  measureD standby_vessel_full_period: standby vessel held at Treasgate for all 60 days; cost GBP 48,000; avoids 14.
  measureE standby_vessel_weekends_only: standby vessel held for weekend days only; cost GBP 16,000; avoids 5.

decisionRule: Adopt the measure with the lowest cost per expected avoided cancellation (cost divided by avoided cancellations), considering only measures that avoid at least 6 cancellations over the next 60 days. If no measure qualifies, retain the current timetable.

otherNotes: Vessel FV-14 dry-dock inspection is booked for March 2026 and falls outside the 60-day window. Budget code TF-2231 covers this review. Stakeholder briefing is planned for 2 February 2026.

q1.instructions: Which category best describes what the weather-cancellation rate counts?

criteria.all_disruptions_on_route: Every disruption logged on the route, whatever its cause and whatever its effect on the crossing.
criteria.late_or_cancelled_sailings: Any sailing that either ran late or did not sail, regardless of cause.
criteria.any_cancellation_regardless_of_cause: Any sailing that did not sail at all, whatever cause was logged.
criteria.weather_full_cancellations: Only sailings that did not sail at all and were logged with weather as the cause.

criteria.retain_current_timetable: Make no change to the vessel or the timetable for the next 60 days.
criteria.buffer_timetable_change: Add a short fixed slack allowance to each crossing time.
criteria.ramp_maintenance_upgrade: Upgrade the linkspan hydraulics and ramp seals to a higher wind-tolerance standard.
criteria.standby_vessel_full_period: Hold a standby vessel on site for the whole 60-day window.
criteria.standby_vessel_weekends_only: Hold a standby vessel on site for weekend days only.

RONDPORT HARBOUR FESTIVAL 2026 - TRADER PITCH TERMS
memoRef: RHF-TP-26-04

issuedTo: Accredited traders and the Trader Liaison Desk

supersedes: RHF-TP-25-02 (withdrawn in full, see section 12)

Covering note: This memo sets out the terms for pitches, cancellations, refund payments and set-up access at the festival. Read sections 1 and 2 together, because the definitions narrow several terms used later. Section 5 amends the bands in section 2. Section 7 is a site notice issued after the memo was first circulated, and it changes one arrival window. Where a later section and an earlier section appear to conflict on the same matter, the later section governs.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Opening day means the first calendar day on which the festival is open to the public, as listed in section 4.
1.2 Notice interval means the number of whole calendar days from the day a written cancellation notice is received up to, but not including, the opening day. A notice received on the day before the opening day has a notice interval of 1 day. Every limit in sections 2 and 5 is inclusive.
1.3 Pitch fee means the sum allocated for the pitch in the trader's allocation letter. It excludes the booking deposit, which is never refunded under any band.
1.4 Received means the notice has reached the Pitch Office mailbox or the Pitch Office postal address. The receipt date is the calendar date on which it first reached either of them. A notice sent to any other address is not received until it is forwarded to one of them.
1.5 Set-up day means a day on which a trader may bring equipment and vehicles onto the site, as allocated in section 9.
1.6 Gross weight means the plated gross vehicle weight shown on the vehicle registration document. It does not include the weight of goods carried.

SECTION 2 - REFUND BANDS AS ISSUED
2.1 Band A: notice interval of 90 days or more. The full pitch fee is refunded.
2.2 Band B: notice interval of 60 to 89 days. Half of the pitch fee is refunded.
2.3 Band C: notice interval of 30 to 59 days. One quarter of the pitch fee is refunded.
2.4 Band D: notice interval of fewer than 30 days. No refund is due.
2.5 Where a band percentage gives a fraction of a penny, the refund is rounded down to the whole penny.
2.6 The bands in this section apply to the notice interval as defined in section 1.2 and to nothing else.

SECTION 3 - VEHICLE ACCESS AND ARRIVAL WINDOWS
3.1 Vehicles up to and including 3.5 tonnes gross weight may use any site gate on a set-up day, at any time the gate is open.
3.2 Vehicles over 3.5 tonnes gross weight must use the Harbour Yard Gate only, and must arrive within the arrival window for their set-up day.
3.3 The Quay Gate is for vehicles up to and including 3.5 tonnes gross weight only.
3.4 The standard arrival window for vehicles over 3.5 tonnes is 06:00 to 08:00 on each set-up day, unless a site notice changes it for a stated day.

SECTION 4 - FESTIVAL SCHEDULE 2026
4.1 Set-up days: Wednesday 2026-07-15 and Thursday 2026-07-16.
4.2 Opening day: Friday 2026-07-17.
4.3 Last trading day: Sunday 2026-07-19.
4.4 Public opening hours on each trading day are 10:00 to 22:00.
4.5 The Pondmouth Winter Market is a separate event with its own terms. Nothing in this memo applies to it. Its trading days are 2026-12-04 to 2026-12-06.

SECTION 5 - AMENDMENT 1 (issued 2026-05-04, effective 2026-05-11)
5.1 Band B now covers notice intervals of 65 to 89 days inclusive.
5.2 Band C now covers notice intervals of 30 to 64 days inclusive.
5.3 Bands A and D are unchanged.
5.4 This amendment applies to notices received on or after 2026-05-11. Notices received before that date are assessed under section 2 as originally issued.
5.5 This amendment does not change the definitions in section 1.

SECTION 6 - REFUND PAYMENTS AND BANK DETAILS
6.1 Refunds are paid by bank transfer only. The Pitch Office does not issue cheques.
6.2 A refund is paid only to an account with verified status. An account becomes verified when the trader returns the signed bank verification form to the Pitch Office.
6.3 Bank details sent by e-mail or by telephone do not verify an account and do not change the account on file.
6.4 Where the account on file is unverified, the refund is held for the trader. A held refund is not forfeited and is released once the account is verified.
6.5 Refund payments are released in the order the decisions were recorded.

SECTION 7 - SITE NOTICE SN-07 (issued 2026-06-08, in force from issue)
7.1 The Harbour Yard Gate is closed to all traffic on 2026-07-15.
7.2 On 2026-07-16 only, the arrival window for vehicles over 3.5 tonnes gross weight is 05:30 to 07:30. Section 3.4 applies on all other set-up days.
7.3 Nothing else in section 3 is changed by this notice.
7.4 Traders must confirm receipt of this notice to the mailbox in the header. Confirmation does not change any window.

SECTION 8 - CANCELLATION NOTICE LOG
The log lists every notice reference issued for the 2026 festival, in notice reference order.

SECTION 11 - DISPUTES
11.1 A trader who disagrees with a refund band must set out the notice reference, the receipt date and the reason in writing within 14 days of the decision.
11.2 The Pitch Operations Office decides disputes, and its decision is final for the 2026 festival.

SECTION 12 - WITHDRAWN EDITIONS
12.1 Memo RHF-TP-25-02 is withdrawn in full. It has no effect on any notice received in 2026.

SECTION 13 - SITE CONDUCT
13.1 Traders must keep the pitch clear of the access route at all times. Vehicles may not be parked on the access route after the set-up period has closed.
13.2 Fire extinguishers must be visible from each pitch and checked before opening day.
13.3 Pitch boundaries are marked with white tape on set-up day and may not be moved without written approval from the Pitch Office.
13.4 Traders must wear the site lanyard issued at accreditation whenever they are in the service yard.
13.5 Any change of trading name must be notified in writing to the mailbox in the header. A change of name does not change the pitch fee or the notice log.

SECTION 14 - CONTACT AND ESCALATION
14.1 Routine questions about allocations go to the Trader Liaison Desk.
14.2 Questions about refunds, bank details or cancellation notices go to the Pitch Office mailbox in the header, quoting the notice reference.
14.3 Telephone calls are not a valid way to give notice, change bank details or dispute a decision.
14.4 Escalations are passed to the Pitch Operations Office, which replies within five working days.
14.5 Out of hours emergencies on site are handled by the duty site manager, whose number is posted at the Drurtstow Quay gatehouse.

PART 1 - POLICY DMV-2, RESPONSE WINDOWS (BASE TEXT)
1.1 Purpose. This policy sets the time within which a damp, mould or ventilation repair reported by a member of Thecklow Court must be completed.
1.2 Definitions. In this policy:
(a) Report date means the calendar date on which the case is logged on the repairs line or portal, as shown in the register. The report date is never counted as a day in any window.
(b) Working day means a Monday to Friday, other than a day listed in Schedule 2.
(c) Priority means only: (i) damp or mould on a wall, ceiling or floor of a room in which a person under 16 sleeps; or (ii) water in contact with an electrical fitting. Damp or mould that meets neither (i) nor (ii) is not Priority, however severe it is.
(d) Standard means any case that is not Priority.
(e) Monitoring means a condition under inspection for which no repair has yet been ordered.
1.3 Response windows.
(a) Priority: complete within 2 working days of the report date.
(b) Standard: complete within 10 working days of the report date.
(c) Monitoring: no fixed window; the inspection is recorded at each review.
1.4 Category. The window runs from the report date and is set by the category shown in the register at the time of the extract.
1.5 Access. Where a member does not give access on a visit, the case stays open and its window is not paused.
1.6 Records. The register is the record of dates, categories and status. A date, decision or completion stated in an e-mail has no effect on the register until it is entered there.

PART 2 - AMENDMENTS
A1 (in force 2026-01-05): Schedule 2 updated for the year. No effect on any window.
A2 (approved by the Repairs Sub-committee on 2026-02-10): clause 1.3(b) is replaced by the following text: '(b) Standard: complete within 15 working days of the report date, for cases logged on or after 16 February 2026. Cases logged before 16 February 2026 keep the window of 10 working days.'
A3 (draft only, not adopted): proposal to set the Priority window at 1 working day. The Board has not voted on it and it has no effect.

PART 3 - DEADLINES, OVERDUE CASES, ESCALATION AND VARIATIONS
3.1 The deadline day of a case is the last day of its window, counted from the day after the report date and skipping any day that is not a working day.
3.2 A case is overdue on any date after its deadline day on which it is still open. A case closed on the register on or before its deadline day is not overdue.
3.3 An overdue case must be escalated in writing to the Maintenance Manager by the next working day after its deadline day, and the escalation recorded under esc in the register.
3.4 A deadline may be varied only by a written variation signed by the Maintenance Manager, stating the new deadline day and recorded under var in the register. A variation not recorded has no effect.
