clause_register.title: Permitted use
clause_register.current_text: Commercial grape growing only. No change of use without landlord written consent.

clause_register.title: Base rent
clause_register.original_text: Base rent GBP 8,400 per hectare per year, payable quarterly in advance.

clause_register.title: Yield rebate on base rent
clause_register.current_text: Yield is the weighed tonnage of the season's delivery notes for the block, divided by the block's leased area in hectares. If Block C yield is 6.0 t/ha or more, no rebate. If it is 4.4 t/ha or more but below 6.0 t/ha, rebate of 5% of the season's base rent. If it is 3.0 t/ha or more but below 4.4 t/ha, rebate of 10%. If it is below 3.0 t/ha, rebate of 20%.

clause_register.title: Spring cane pruning deadline
clause_register.original_text: Spring cane pruning completed by 31 March each year.

clause_register.title: Seasonal irrigation allowance
clause_register.current_text: Allowance per block per season: Block A 2,000 m3; Block B 1,500 m3; Block C 1,600 m3; Block D 900 m3. Season runs 1 April to 31 October. Meter readings are cumulative from 1 April.

clause_register.title: Herbicide use under the vine rows
clause_register.current_text: Tenant may use only products on the landlord's approved list, and must keep a spray diary for each block.

clause_register.title: Notice before vine support wire removal
clause_register.original_text: Fourteen days' written notice to the landlord before any planned removal of vine support wires.

clause_register.title: Drainage and ditch clearance
clause_register.current_text: Tenant clears field drains each autumn before 30 November. Landlord carries out any major drain works.

clause_register.title: Boundary fencing and gates
clause_register.current_text: Tenant maintains boundary fences around Blocks A to D. Landlord maintains the gates on the access lanes.

clause_register.title: Crop insurance for vines
clause_register.original_text: Landlord holds crop hail cover on the vines.

clause_register.title: Break option
clause_register.current_text: Either party may serve a break notice effective at the end of any season on 12 months' written notice.

clause_register.title: Access for landlord inspection
clause_register.current_text: Landlord may inspect the blocks on 48 hours' notice, not more than twice in any season.

clause_register.title: Written notices
clause_register.current_text: Notices under this lease must be in writing and sent to the contact named in the parties schedule. Notice sent by e-mail is treated as received on the day it is sent.

clause_register.title: Sub-letting
clause_register.current_text: No block may be sub-let or shared with another grower without the landlord's prior written consent.

night-cover-rule.night-window: Boardings that start from 22:00 up to, but not including, 06:00 local time
night-cover-rule.share-meaning: Minimum share of night-window boardings that must be covered by night-endorsed pilots

rest-rule.measured: elapsed time from disembarked-utc of the pilot's previous assignment to booked-boarding-utc of the next booking
rest-rule.shortfall-action: A relief pilot is assigned to the booking; the booked boarding time is not moved

working-day-rule.deadline: Report due by the fifth working day after the inspection date. The inspection date is not counted. Saturdays, Sundays and dates in holiday-list are not working days. A report issued on the deadline date is on time.

agreement.title: Shared-use access agreement for guest society observing nights on Jaisstow Hill instruments

host_party.name: Sertjaova Observatory Trust
host_party.site: Jaisstow Hill Observing Station, Pynthorpe Road

annual_schedule.levy_note: The site levy is shown separately on the annual schedule and is not part of any slot fee or refund under this agreement.

clauses.title: Counting of notice periods
clauses.text: Days in any notice period are counted from the day after the notice is received, up to and including the session start date. The day of receipt is not counted. The session start date is the calendar date on which the first night of the booked session begins, as shown in the current booking record.

clauses.title: Purpose
clauses.text: The host makes listed instruments available to the guest for member observing and education nights, on the terms of this agreement only. Instruments are not available to the guest for commercial hire.

clauses.title: Session allocation
clauses.text: Sessions are booked in whole nights. Each booked session gives the guest use of its instrument from the stated start time to the stated end time on the booked night, or for the booked number of minutes where only a length has been recorded.

clauses.title: Slot fee
clauses.text: Each session carries the slot fee for its instrument listed above, payable 30 days before the session start date. Fees exclude the site levy, which is shown separately on the annual schedule.

clauses.title: Maintenance windows
clauses.text: The host may close an instrument for maintenance on up to four nights a year, notified at least 21 days ahead. Sessions moved because of a maintenance window keep their slot fee.

clauses.title: Guest cancellation refund (original)
clauses.text: Written notice of cancellation received at least 14 days before the session start date earns a full refund of the slot fee. Notice received 7 to 13 days before the session start date earns a refund of half the slot fee. Notice received fewer than 7 days before the session start date earns no refund.

clauses.title: Form of refunds
clauses.text: Refunds are paid by bank transfer within 30 days of the notice being acknowledged. No credit against later sessions is issued in place of a refund.

clauses.title: Host cancellation for weather
clauses.text: Sessions cancelled by the host because of weather are rebooked at no charge to the guest. This clause does not change the guest's cancellation rights under clause 6.

clauses.title: Changes to bookings by the host
clauses.text: The host may move a confirmed session to a new start date by written notice to the guest's contact. A moved session keeps its instrument and its slot fee, and the new start date is the start date for all purposes under this agreement.

clauses.title: Governing terms
clauses.text: Where an amendment replaces a clause, the replacement governs from its stated effective date. The replaced text no longer applies to any notice received on or after that date, and applies to earlier notices only as it stood when they were received.

amendments.summary: Guest contact e-mail address updated to the society's current correspondence address.

amendments.replacement_text: Written notice of cancellation received at least 21 days before the session start date earns a full refund of the slot fee. Notice received 10 to 20 days before the session start date, both figures included, earns a refund of half the slot fee. Notice received fewer than 10 days before the session start date earns no refund.

conditionRules.emergencyExemption: Audible works may take place outside core hours only for emergency works where all three of the following apply: the works are needed to make a structure safe or to restore an essential service; the council is notified in writing within 24 hours counted from the time the works began; and the works stop once the emergency is contained. If any one of the three is not met, the exemption does not apply.
conditionRules.writtenExtensions: A written extension approved for a named weekday date allows audible works until the finish time stated for that date. Extensions apply to weekday core hours only and do not change Saturday hours. For the named date only, the extension governs in place of the core weekday finish time.

SECTION A - BYLAW TEXT (2019 EDITION, CONSOLIDATED FOR THE OFFICE FILE)
Clause 1.1 These Bylaws apply to all vessels using the lock at Folgate and to the approach channel within 500 m of the lower gates.
Clause 2.1 'LOA' means length overall, measured from the foremost point of the hull to the aftermost point of the hull, including fixed fittings.
Clause 2.2 'Passage' means the movement of a vessel through Folgate Lock from its first day of passage onward.
Clause 2.3 Where these Bylaws count days between two dates, the count runs from the first date up to but not including the second date. Every day counted is a calendar day.
Clause 3.1 Every powered vessel using Folgate Lock is assigned one passage category under clause 3.2 before its first passage in a calendar year.
Clause 3.2 (2019 wording) Category 1: LOA not more than 12.0 m. Category 2: LOA more than 12.0 m and not more than 15.0 m. Category 3: LOA more than 15.0 m.
Clause 3.3 A Category 3 passage requires a Category 3 permit issued by the Trust for the calendar year of the passage. Category 1 and Category 2 passages do not require a Category 3 permit.
Clause 3.4 Unpowered craft under 6.0 m LOA are exempt from clause 3.1.
Clause 4.1 (2019 wording) A request for a lock slot must be received by the Office at least 5 days before the first day of passage.
Clause 4.2 The declared maximum draught of a vessel passing Folgate Lock must not exceed 1.9 m on the first day of passage.
Clause 4.3 Requests may be sent by e-mail to the Office address listed in Section F or delivered by post. A request counts as received on the day the Office logs it.
Clause 4.4 The Office may close the lock for maintenance. Each closure is published on the notice board at the lock and on the Trust website. No slot is granted for any day inside a published closure.
Clause 4.5 A confirmed slot may be cancelled by the Office if the vessel has not reached the lower gates by the agreed time on the first day of passage.
Clause 4.6 A request covering two separate first days of passage is treated as two requests.
Clause 5.1 Speed within 200 m of the lock gates must not exceed 4 km/h.
Clause 5.2 A vessel may moor on the lock approach for no more than 2 hours without the Office's written agreement.
Clause 6.1 Lock staff may refuse passage to a vessel whose safety certificate has expired on the first day of passage.
Clause 7.1 The Office keeps a log of every request, decision and passage. Entries are made on the day of the decision.
Clause 8.1 'Trust' means the Jontrurara Navigation Trust, which makes and amends these Bylaws.
Clause 8.2 An amendment takes effect on the date stated in the Trust's notice of adoption. Where the notice gives different dates for different clauses, each clause takes effect on its own date.

1. DEFINITIONS (Licence Schedule D, version 2)
1.1 'Extraction day' means a calendar day on which at least one harvester or forwarder logs a felling or extraction cycle in the telemetry export. A day on which machines are only transported, serviced or used for road building is not an extraction day.
1.2 'Merchantable volume' means the solid volume, bark excluded, of stems with a diameter at breast height (DBH) of 35 cm or more, as recorded on scale tickets. Gross ticket volume less the volume of stems under 35 cm DBH gives merchantable volume. The block-month total is rounded to the nearest whole cubic metre once, at the total, with exact halves rounded up.
1.3 'Block-month' means one block's activity within one calendar month, from its first day to its last.

2.1 Schedule Q-2 (original) took effect on 1 October 2025. It sets a monthly merchantable-volume cap for each block: Block B-4 1,150 m3; Block B-7 880 m3; Block B-9 640 m3. Schedule Q-2 sets no extraction-day ceiling.

2.3 A volume above a cap does not by itself make a return an exception return. The excess is shown in the variance column of the standard monthly return.

domain: coastal path storm-damage repair prioritisation
state:
MEMO
To: Coastal Path Works Panel, Cilthorpe County Council
From: Faina Frumwelson, Principal Engineer (Coastal Paths)
Ref: CPW-25-0917
Date: 14 November 2025
Subject: Storm damage at Section C, Clenbury Head to Recombe Gap

1. Survey background
The 2025 condition survey covered 230 monitored sections of the coastal path. Between the spring and autumn surveys, 46 of those sections recorded new edge retreat. A bench-footing survey of 60 footings is reported separately.

2. Section C
The storm of 2 October 2025 removed about 40 metres of cliff-top path edge at Section C. The path width at the narrowest point is 1.4 m. Lighting unit 7 is out of service (ENG-4412). Section C is open to walkers behind a warning sign.

3. Options costed for five years
The loss if the edge fails is £80,000 per failure, the same for every option. Annual failure probabilities are the engineer's estimates for each option.

Option | Works cost (GBP) | Annual failure probability
reopen_as_is | 0 | 0.20
monitor_and_defer | 0 | 0.25
temporary_rock_armour | 40,000 | 0.05
close_and_fence | 75,000 | 0
repair_at_current_line | 150,000 | 0.02
realign_inland | 260,000 | 0.01

Decision rule: the panel adopts the option with the lowest five-year total cost. Five-year total cost = works cost + (annual failure probability x 5 x loss per failure). Lost-use income and diversion costs are not counted.

4. Contract for the chosen works
Three bids were received for the temporary rock armour works. A bid counts only if its completion time is within 10 weeks of contract start. Award rule: award to the lowest bid that meets the 10-week limit; if none does, the panel defers.
- Fickfindara Coastal Ltd: £91,400, completion 12 weeks
- Tolmilis Civils Ltd: £98,750, completion 9 weeks
- Kyrfalmere & Plexstead Civils Ltd: £94,200, completion 8 weeks

5. Other
Next meeting: 27 November 2025, Recombe Room.

q1.instructions: Under the decision rule in the memo, which option should the panel adopt for Section C?

criteria.reopen_as_is: Open the section to walkers now with no works and accept the failure risk.
criteria.monitor_and_defer: Carry out no works this year and keep the section under observation.
criteria.temporary_rock_armour: Install temporary rock armour at the cliff toe and keep the section under review.
criteria.close_and_fence: Close the section permanently and fence it off.
criteria.repair_at_current_line: Rebuild the cliff edge on its current line.
criteria.realign_inland: Move the path inland to a new line and build it there.

PURPOSE
This memo sets out the position of the two vessels named above as at 14 April 2026, after Amendment 2 and the register corrections in Section 6. It is issued to the Breandport landing desk so that declarations signed from 15 April can be checked against the correct figures. Do not rely on the position sheet of 2 March, which predates Amendment 2.

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 “Whitefish” in this memo means cod, haddock, whiting and saithe. Monkfish and megrim are excluded from that term and are reported under Schedule D.
1.2 “Landing” means the offloading of catch at a designated port, recorded on a landing declaration. A landing counts toward the quota period in which the declaration is signed, not the period in which the fish were caught. The signing date is the date written on the declaration, whatever day the declaration is received.
1.3 “Quota period” means 1 January to 31 December of the stated year.
1.4 “Live weight” is the weight of fish as caught. “Gutted weight” is the weight after heading and gutting. Gutted weight is converted to live weight by multiplying by 1.20 before it is set against quota. No other conversion factor applies.
1.5 “Trip” means the period from one departure from port to the landing declaration that closes it.

2. ALLOCATIONS FOR 2026
2.1 Vessel PBL-1184 (length 16.8 m) holds an annual cod allocation of 14.0 tonnes and an annual haddock allocation of 9.0 tonnes, as set in its 2026 allocation certificate.
2.2 Vessel PBL-2207 (length 8.4 m) holds an annual cod allocation of 4.5 tonnes. It holds no haddock allocation.
2.3 Both vessels are registered to Vartnouxix Fishing Ltd, Breandport.

3. AMENDMENT 2 AND CARRY-OVER
3.1 Amendment 2, issued 2 March 2026, reduces the 2026 cod allocation for PBL-1184 from 14.0 tonnes to 11.5 tonnes. The reduced figure takes effect from 1 March 2026 and applies to the whole of the 2026 quota period. Amendment 2 does not change any haddock figure.

3.3 No carry-over is recorded for PBL-2207.

4. EXCEPTION FOR SMALL VESSELS
4.1 A vessel under 10 metres may land up to 500 kg of cod per trip without deduction from its cod quota, provided the vessel is not on the watch list in Schedule B when the declaration is signed.
4.2 The exception is applied per trip, on the total cod of that trip. Where a trip's cod landings exceed 500 kg in total, the whole of that trip's cod is counted against quota. The exception does not cover part of a trip.
4.3 The exception does not apply to any vessel of 10 metres or more.
4.4 Schedule B lists PBL-2207 with effect from 27 March 2026. A listing applies to declarations signed on or after its effective date.

PART 1. CONSOLIDATED BYLAW TEXT, CLAUSE 14 (MOORING DURATION)

14.1 Definitions. Mooring period means the elapsed time from the moment the first mooring line is secured to a public landing until the moment the last mooring line is released from that landing. A stay is one mooring period.

14.2 Maximum mooring period. Consolidated text as amended by Amendment A3, effective 2026-03-01 (see Part 2). At Byxmouth Public Landing the maximum mooring period is 48 hours. At any other public landing the maximum mooring period is 72 hours.

14.3 Continuity. Time away from the landing during a mooring period counts toward that mooring period. Time away runs from the moment the vessel leaves the landing to the moment its first line is secured again at a public landing. A time away of less than two hours, ending with the vessel securing again at the same landing, does not end the mooring period. A time away of two hours or more ends the mooring period, and any later mooring is a new stay.

14.4 Winter lay-up exemption. A vessel holding a current winter lay-up permit is exempt from clause 14.2 for the permit period only. A permit that has expired, or has not been renewed, gives no exemption from the date it stopped being current.

14.5 Enforcement. Where a mooring period exceeds the applicable maximum by less than six hours, the harbour officer may issue a written notice requiring the vessel to leave within two hours of the notice. Where a mooring period exceeds the applicable maximum by six hours or more, the harbour officer may issue an immediate move-on direction and a civil penalty notice.

14.6 Transition. Clause 14.2 as amended applies to any mooring period that begins on or after the amendment's effective date. A mooring period that began earlier is governed by the text in force when it began.

14.7 Times. All times in the landing log are local time at the landing concerned. The landing log is the record of line-secured and line-released times for the purposes of this clause.

14.8 Appeals. A civil penalty notice may be appealed to the Navigation Review Panel within 14 days of the notice date.

Soucko,

This memo covers four consignments handled through the Remouth transfer point in the week of 6 April 2026, plus one older consignment shown for reference. It is for the holding-period review you asked for. The drivers followed dispatch instructions, so nothing below is a finding about individual drivers. Please read the rules block before the log, because the log entries only mean something against the rules as written.

Rules as they stand on the file:

Rule A (Code HW-6, section 4.1, general allowance): hazardous waste may be held at an approved transfer point for up to 72 hours, provided the load is sealed throughout and the vehicle is either attended or parked in a locked secure bay.

Rule B (Notice HW-N-2026/03, section 2, flammable waste): for a consignment of flammable waste (UN class 3) with a collection date on or after 1 April 2026, the holding period at a transfer point is limited to 24 hours. Where Rule B applies, it takes precedence over Rule A, so the 72-hour allowance in Rule A cannot be relied on for that consignment.

Rule C (Notice section 4, reporting): where a consignment has been held beyond the limit that applies to it, the operator must make a written report to the Remouth Regional Regulator within two working days of the consignment leaving the transfer point. A breach does not change the routing of the consignment; the duty is reporting only.

Measurement (Rules A and B): the holding period runs from the arrival time on the transfer-point log to the departure time on the same log, in local time, as elapsed clock time. Pauses, weekends and public holidays are not deducted.

Renewal_Rules.Grace_Period: The 14 calendar days after the expiry date. Day 1 is the day after expiry; a renewal received on day 14 or earlier is within grace.

Renewal_Rules.Rounding: All amounts are shown to the penny; no rounding is applied.

SECTION 1. STANDING POLICY RP-4 (issued 2024-09-01)
1.1 Scope. This policy covers every crew member signed on as driver or fireman for a steam footplate duty on the TWHB. The duty date of a footplate duty is the calendar date on which that duty starts.
4.1 Minimum rest between footplate duties is 10 hours, measured from the recorded sign-off time (SO) of the earlier duty to the recorded sign-on time (SI) of the later duty.
4.2 No crew member may be rostered for more than three firing turns in any rolling seven-day period. A rolling seven-day period is any run of seven consecutive calendar days, counting both the first and the last day of the run.
4.3 A gap exactly equal to the minimum rest in force is compliant. A gap shorter than the minimum, even by one minute, is not compliant.
4.4 The OL may authorise a reduction in rest only for a gala weekend, only in writing, and only where that written authority is recorded on this file before the roster for the affected duty is published. No dispensation may reduce rest below eight hours.
4.5 Rest is measured in elapsed clock time, across midnight where necessary. No rounding is applied to recorded SO or SI times.

A.1 Clause 4.1 of RP-4 is replaced by: "Minimum rest between footplate duties is 12 hours, measured as in clause 4.3."

2. RENT REVIEW CLAUSES (as signed in 2021)
4.1 The annual rent is reviewed on each 1 October during the term.
4.2 At each review the annual rent increases by the percentage change in the Regional Vineyard Price Index over the twelve months ending on 31 August before that review. The rent never falls at a review.
4.3 The percentage increase at any review is capped at 4.0 per cent.
4.4 Carry-forward: where the index change at a review exceeds the cap in clause 4.3, the part above the cap is carried forward and added to the increase at the following review.
4.5 Arrears deferral: if any rent due before a review date is still unpaid at the start of that review date, the review increase does not take effect on that date. It takes effect on the first quarter day after all such arrears have been paid.
4.6 Notices under this lease must be in writing and may be sent by e-mail to the contact named in section 1.
4.7 Review memorandum: the landlord's agent issues a memorandum stating the index change before each 1 October review. A memorandum is not a condition of the increase taking effect.

SECTION 1 - PURPOSE AND READING ORDER
This pack sets out the harvest ceiling rules that apply to concession CL-7, the felling entries logged against the concession, and the messages that changed the rules. Read sections 2 to 5 first, then section 6. Where a message in section 6 changes a figure stated earlier, the message governs. Section 7 lists items that concern other concessions or general administration and do not change any CL-7 figure. Section 8 is a glossary of terms used in this pack.

SECTION 2 - RULE VERSIONS

SECTION 3 - UNITS AND CONVERSION
Load tickets for CL-7 may record volume in cubic metres (m3) or in tonnes. Under version_3, a volume recorded in tonnes is converted to cubic metres at 0.85 m3 per tonne before it is counted. Volumes recorded in m3 are counted as recorded. No rounding is applied after conversion.

SECTION 4 - COUNTING RULES FOR A PERMIT YEAR
4.1 Each felling entry is assigned to a permit year by its felling date. A felling date belongs to a permit year when it falls on or after the permit year start date and on or before the permit year end date. Both the start date and the end date are included.
4.2 The permit-year ceiling for permit year 2026/27 under version_3 is 12,000 m3. This figure is subject to section 6.
4.3 Volume used in a permit year at a report date is the total of counted volumes for entries in that permit year whose felling dates fall on or before the report date. Entries with felling dates after the report date are excluded from that report.
4.4 Entries dated before 1 April 2026 are not counted toward permit year 2026/27.
4.5 The ceiling in force for a permit year is the figure stated in the most recent message in section 6 that applies to that permit year. If no message in section 6 applies, the figure in section 4.2 applies.
4.6 A ceiling is a limit on the volume counted, not a target. Volume at or below the ceiling in force is within the limit.

felling date: the date recorded on an entry as the date the stems were cut.
permit year: the twelve-month period from 1 April to 31 March, named by its two calendar years, for example 2026/27.
ceiling in force: the permit-year ceiling that applies after section 4.5 is applied.

SECTION 9 - PROCEDURE ON A CEILING QUERY
When a ceiling query is raised, the Concessions Office first identifies the permit year from the felling date, then applies section 4.5 to find the ceiling in force, then totals counted volumes up to the report date under section 4.3. The query is closed with a written note giving each of those three results and the source of each. Queries raised by holders are answered within ten working days. Where counted volume exceeds the ceiling in force, the district office issues a notice to the holder and suspends new felling on the affected cut blocks until the holder confirms a revised plan.

TRERDRONDEX HERITAGE RAILWAY TRUST
Locomotive Operating Memo

Memo Reference: LOS-MEMO-41-0403
Date Of Memo: 3 April 2026
From: Fraicko Hockdale, Operations Manager
To: Gortie Pemore, Appointed Boiler Examiner; Reartys Fuxley, Trust Secretary
Subject: Running span status and sign-off for Locomotive 41

Section 1: Definitions Used In This Standard
1.1 Firing Day means a calendar day on which the firebox of a locomotive is lit to raise or hold steam for any purpose. A calendar day counts as a Firing Day even if the firebox was lit for less than one hour and the locomotive did not move.
1.2 Running Span means a run of consecutive Firing Days. A Running Span begins on the first Firing Day after at least one calendar day that is not a Firing Day, and it ends on the last Firing Day before the next such calendar day.
1.3 Full Examination means a complete internal and external boiler examination carried out by the Appointed Boiler Examiner and recorded on a boiler certificate. An Interim Inspection is not a Full Examination, however thorough it is.
1.4 Wash-Out means a complete drain, internal wash and refill of the boiler, recorded in the locomotive log.

Section 2: Operating Standard LOS-4 (Two Versions)
2.1 Version 2 applies to any Running Span that begins before 1 April 2026. Under version 2, no locomotive shall be fired on an eighth consecutive Firing Day within a Running Span unless a Wash-Out has been recorded since that span began.
2.2 Version 3 takes effect on 1 April 2026 and governs every Running Span that begins on or after that date. Under version 3, no locomotive shall be fired on a sixth consecutive Firing Day within a Running Span unless a Wash-Out has been recorded since that span began.
2.3 A Running Span that began before 1 April 2026 stays under version 2 for all of its Firing Days, including any Firing Day on or after 1 April 2026.
2.4 Version 3, clause 3.1: From 1 April 2026, return to service after any Wash-Out completed on or after that date requires the signature of the Operations Manager and the countersignature of the Appointed Boiler Examiner.
2.5 Version 3, clause 3.2: Where the Wash-Out is carried out off site by an approved contractor, the contractor's Wash-Out certificate is accepted in place of the countersignature in clause 3.1.

Section 3: Locomotive 41 Record
Locomotive Number: 41
Locomotive Type: Tank 2-6-2T
Current Boiler Certificate: BC-41-24, Full Examination completed 8 November 2024 under version 2
Interim Inspection: 20 February 2026, no defects recorded

27 March 2026: not lit
28 March 2026: not lit

30 March 2026: lit, steam test, firebox lit 35 minutes, no movement

Next Actions

Cooperative.Registered Office: Unit 3, Skousport Road Offices, Thindness Park Estate

Governing Policy.Purpose: This rule sets how many guest nights a member household may host in a calendar quarter, so that shared stairwells, lifts and bin stores on the Thindness Park and Skousport Road estates keep to their designed use.
Governing Policy.Scope: Applies to every cooperative unit. Does not apply to contractors, tradespeople or emergency responders carrying out their duties.

Base Limit.Quarter Basis: Calendar quarter: 1 January to 31 March, 1 April to 30 June, 1 July to 30 September, 1 October to 31 December

Definitions.Guest: Any person who is not a registered occupant of the member household. An approved carer is treated as a guest only for nights that are not covered by a board carer approval.
Definitions.Approved Carer: A person named in a board carer approval. That person is treated as a non-guest only for the nights stated in that approval.
Definitions.Registered Occupant: A person recorded as a resident of the unit in the household membership file on the date of the stay.
Definitions.Counted Guest Night: A night on which a guest sleeps in the unit. The night of arrival counts. The night of departure does not count. An arrival and departure on the same day produces no counted night. A stay that runs across a month or quarter boundary is split, so that each night is assigned to the calendar month and calendar quarter in which that night falls.
Definitions.Limit Amendments: An amendment to the quarterly limit applies to each counted night that falls on or after its stated effective date, and to no earlier night. Where a later minute changes an earlier effective date, the later stated date governs.

Section 4 Approved Carers.Rule: A board carer approval covers only the nights stated in it. Nights covered by an approval are excluded from the count. Nights outside the stated dates are counted as guest nights.

Approval Register.Review: Renewal to be considered at a future board meeting

Section 6 Over-Limit Stays.Rule: A stay that would take a household above its quarterly limit may proceed only where a written board resolution approves the additional nights. A housing officer may log and forward a request but has no power to approve nights above the limit. Members and estates staff have no approval power for these nights.

domain: telescope observing-time access agreements for visiting research groups

definitions.observing_night: The period from 20:00 local time on one calendar date to 06:00 local time on the following calendar date. The night takes the calendar date on which it starts as its name.
definitions.notice_days: The number of calendar days from the date a request or cancellation is received up to the start date of the observing night concerned, found by subtracting the receipt date from the start date. The receipt date itself is not counted.
definitions.confirmation_grace: The period after a booking is confirmed during which a cancellation carries no fee whatever its notice. It is counted in calendar days after the confirmation date, which is not itself counted. A cancellation received on the last day of that count is still within the period; one received on the following day is outside it.
definitions.consumed_night: A night counted against a party's allocation for the calendar quarter in which it falls when its booking status shows it was used, or when it was cancelled after the confirmation grace period has ended. A night pending confirmation, a night restored under a host-certified weather closure, and a night cancelled within the grace period are not consumed.
definitions.continuous_outage: Telescope downtime within one observing night. Two downtime periods separated by a gap of less than 30 minutes form one continuous outage; a gap of 30 minutes or more keeps them as separate outages. The duration of a combined outage runs from the start of its first period to the end of its last period.
definitions.creditable_outage: A continuous outage of at least 2 hours, measured as its duration, whose cause lies with the host. An outage caused by guest equipment or guest staff is never creditable. A creditable outage entitles the party to one make-up session of equal length at no charge, which does not count against the allocation.
definitions.approved_observer: A named person listed for a party in the approved observer list, including any name added to that list by a later amendment.

base_terms.allocation: Each party's allocation for a calendar quarter is the number of observing nights in the allocation table for its tier, unless an amendment sets a different figure for that quarter.
base_terms.observer_swap: A change of observer on a booked night. A swap whose request is received with 7 or more days' notice needs written notice to the host only. A swap received with fewer than 7 days' notice needs written host approval and carries an administrative fee of 40 GBP, unless the replacement is on the party's approved observer list when the request is received; in that case neither the fee nor the approval step applies and written notice to the host is enough.
base_terms.weather_closures: A night lost to a weather closure is restored to the allocation only when the host certifies the whole night as closed.

domain: inland river navigation bylaws: public pontoon mooring stays and break rules

state.Issuing Authority: Leaxtesex Waterways Authority, Walminster Harbour Office
state.Bylaw Set: River Navigation Bylaws, Part 4: Mooring Stays on Public Pontoons

Registration Classes.G: General craft, subject to every clause in Part 4.
Registration Classes.T: Tender craft registered to a larger parent vessel.

Clauses As Originally Issued.Heading: Continuous stay limit
Clauses As Originally Issued.Text: A vessel may not remain continuously on a public pontoon for more than 5 nights.

Clauses As Originally Issued.Heading: Exception for tender craft
Clauses As Originally Issued.Text: A vessel registered in class T is exempt from clause 4.1 and from clause 4.3. Class T vessels still follow clause 4.4 for recording the nights of a stay.

Clauses As Originally Issued.Heading: Break in a stay
Clauses As Originally Issued.Text: A break occurs when a vessel is off the pontoon for a gap of at least 24 hours. A break ends the earlier stay, and any later nights count as a new stay. A shorter gap does not end the stay.

Clauses As Originally Issued.Heading: Counting nights
Clauses As Originally Issued.Text: A continuous stay runs from its first arrival date to its final departure date. Its nights equal the number of days between those two dates. Times of day are not used. A gap is measured in whole days between a departure date and the next arrival date, so a gap of one day equals 24 hours.

Clauses As Originally Issued.Heading: Logging
Clauses As Originally Issued.Text: The pontoon attendant must log each arrival and departure within 24 hours. Late entries carry a reason code.

Amendments.Change: Clause 4.3 is replaced. The break threshold becomes a gap of at least 48 hours instead of 24 hours. The rest of Part 4 is unchanged.

Clause 4.1 is replaced with: 'A vessel may not remain continuously on a public pontoon for more than 5 nights, except that on a pontoon in the Walminster Reach group the limit is 7 nights.' Transitional rule: the limit that applies to a stay is the limit in force on the date of that stay's first recorded arrival.
Clause 4.5 is replaced: late entries must be made within 48 hours, not 24 hours. Clauses 4.1 to 4.4 are unaffected.

Pontoon Register.Name: Canwych Slipway Pontoon
Pontoon Register.Note: Reserved for the slipway operator; not open to visiting craft.

Correspondence.Subject: Walminster stays pending A-2
Correspondence.Body: Until amendment A-2 is in force, apply the 5-night limit at every public pontoon, including the Walminster Reach group. I will confirm once the wording is final.

Correspondence.Subject: Re: Walminster stays pending A-2
Correspondence.Body: A-2 was issued on 18 March and takes effect on 1 April. My note of 12 March is withdrawn. Apply clause 4.1 as amended by A-2 to any stay whose first recorded arrival is on or after 1 April. Stays that began earlier keep the limit in force on their arrival date.

Correspondence.Subject: Queckmouth pontoon
Correspondence.Body: Queckmouth Lock Pontoon remains a public pontoon under Part 4. The pontoon attendant reports no change to berth allocation this spring.

scheme.administered_by: Dalskusex Seed Certification Authority, Hellfell office
scheme.applicability_rule: Each clause applies in the form in force on the date the lot is submitted for certification, unless an amendment states its own applicability test. Where an amendment states its own test, that test governs.

definitions.lot: A lot is the seed harvested from one field in one season. Seed from two or more fields is never combined into one lot.
definitions.sub_class_S1: Seed grown from a parent seed lot that is entered on the certification register. A lot with a registered parent is sub-class S1. A lot with no registered parent is sub-class S2.
definitions.isolation_distance: The straight-line distance in metres from the nearest sown edge of the candidate crop to the nearest sown edge of any other variety of the same species. Field boundaries, hedges and roads are disregarded.
definitions.oven_moisture: Moisture is determined by the oven method. Handheld meter readings are screening readings only and are never used to decide compliance.
definitions.official_sample_for_a_test: Where more than one official sample of a lot has been drawn for the same test, the official sample drawn most recently by its draw date governs that test. Earlier samples stay on file but do not decide the result.
definitions.retest: A retest is a second test made on a fresh official sample drawn after a germination result has been recorded as short of the applicable minimum. A sample drawn for any other reason is not a retest and does not use up the retest allowance.
definitions.governing_inspection: Where a field inspection visit is recorded as superseding an earlier visit, the superseding visit governs and the earlier visit is withdrawn from the file.

3.2_isolation.text: Certified seed of cereals must be grown at least 150 metres from any field of a different variety of the same species.

5.1_germination.text: Minimum germination for certified seed is 85 per cent.

7.1_retest.text: A lot whose germination falls short of the applicable minimum by not more than 3 percentage points may be retested once on a fresh official sample. A shortfall greater than 3 points is rejected without retest.

8.2_moisture.text: Seed moisture must not exceed 14.0 per cent by the oven method.

message_thread.body: The spring planting allocation for the D-04 perimeter is 1,950 seedlings, dispatched in two lots. This message does not touch any felling figure.

audit.scope: Return covering April to June 2026 and the felling log

q1.instructions: Rate the counted gross volume felled on TC-5084 during April to June 2026, using the bands in the criteria.
criteria: Low: under 2,000 m3 of counted gross volume
Moderate: 2,000 m3 or more but under 2,600 m3 of counted gross volume
High: 2,600 m3 or more of counted gross volume

q2.instructions: Counted gross volume felled on TC-5084 in May 2026 stayed within the monthly ceiling in force for May 2026.

criteria.true: The May counted total does not exceed the ceiling in force for May under the most recent instruction that names May.
criteria.false: The May counted total exceeds the ceiling in force for May under the most recent instruction that names May.

q3.instructions: Which description matches the felling status of compartment D-11 on TC-5084 on 2026-05-10?

criteria.open_unrestricted: Felling and haulage are open in the compartment with no compartment-specific limits.
criteria.marked_stems_only: Felling is limited to a defined list of marked stems; other limits on the compartment are set separately.
criteria.full_hold: No felling and no haulage are allowed in the compartment under a hold covering the whole compartment.
criteria.permit_lapsed: The authority to fell in the compartment has lapsed because the permit end date has passed.

q4.instructions: Rate the recovery ratio for TC-5084 over April to June 2026, calculated as the defined ratio in the record, using the bands in the criteria.
criteria: Under 0.40
0.40 or more but under 0.55
0.55 or more but under 0.70
0.70 or more

q5.instructions: Felling on TC-5084 was suspended by a closure order for at least five consecutive calendar days within April to June 2026.

criteria.true: A single closure order whose scope includes felling covers five or more consecutive calendar days, counted inclusively, with its whole span inside the period.
criteria.false: No single closure order whose scope includes felling covers five or more consecutive calendar days, counted inclusively, with its whole span inside the period.

check.q2: May counted total 150.0 + 221.7 + 190.2 + 133.6 + 210.9 = 906.4 m3 (void FL-0413 excluded); the 2026-04-17 message names only May and sets 850 m3, the latest message naming May; 906.4 > 850 -> exceeds -> false

check.q4: Accepted sawlog receipts dated 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30: MR-0302 402.5 + MR-0305 351.0 + MR-0306 277.9 + MR-0307 240.6 = 1272.0 m3 (MR-0303 pulpwood, MR-0304 rejected, MR-0301 and MR-0308 outside the period excluded); counted gross felled in the same period 2712.8 m3; 1272.0 / 2712.8 = 0.4689 -> 0.40 or more but under 0.55
check.q5: Closure order CO-26-06 has scope felling in all compartments and span 2026-06-10 to 2026-06-15: days 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 = 6 calendar days inclusive, all inside April to June 2026 -> 6 >= 5 -> true (CO-26-04 covers 4 days; CO-26-05 is haulage only)

domain: public library new-arrival loan periods and renewal holds

lending_rules.dated_rule_note: From the start date, a loan of an item flagged as new arrival on the checkout date uses the new arrival period; earlier loans used the standard period.
lending_rules.period_counting: The period counts from the day after checkout; the item is due on the last day of the period.
lending_rules.overdue_counting: An item is overdue for each day after its due date on which it has not been returned.
lending_rules.renewal_hold_rule: A renewal is refused while any hold on the item has status waiting or ready.

state.desk_note: Member's query about a fine on an unrelated title was closed on 2026-03-21 with no change to this loan.

q1.instructions: Which loan period applies to this checkout of the item under the lending rules?

criteria.fourteen_days: The new arrival period set by the lending rules for items flagged as new arrivals.
criteria.twenty_one_days: The standard adult loan period that applies to items not covered by the new arrival rule.
criteria.seven_days: A short loan period used for reference-restricted or local history material.
criteria.twenty_eight_days: A four-week loan period used for extended loan entitlements.
criteria.same_day_return: The item is due back on the same day it was checked out.
criteria.no_loan_permitted: The item may not leave the library under any loan period.

q2.instructions: The loan period that applies to this checkout is shorter than the standard adult loan period.

criteria.true: The applicable loan period is less than the standard adult loan period.
criteria.false: The applicable loan period is equal to or longer than the standard adult loan period.

q3.instructions: Under the lending rules, what is the outcome of the renewal request recorded on this loan?

criteria.renewal_granted: The renewal is allowed and the due date is extended.
criteria.renewal_refused_active_hold: The renewal is refused because a hold on the item has status waiting or ready at the time of the request.
criteria.renewal_refused_limit_reached: The renewal is refused because the loan has already used the maximum number of renewals.

q4.instructions: Rate how overdue the item is as of the review date, measured in days past its due date.
criteria: Not overdue: the item is returned or the review date falls on or before its due date.
Slightly overdue: 1 to 7 days past the due date.
Moderately overdue: 8 to 14 days past the due date.
Seriously overdue: 15 to 30 days past the due date.
Long overdue: more than 30 days past the due date.

q5.instructions: The renewal request was refused because the member had already used all of the renewals the rules allow on this loan.

criteria.true: The renewal refusal was caused by the renewal limit having been used up.
criteria.false: The renewal refusal was not caused by the renewal limit having been used up.

check.q1: Checked out 2026-03-02, on or after the new-arrival start date 2026-02-01; flag new_arrival set 2026-02-20 and expires 2026-04-30, so flag active on checkout -> new arrival period of 14 days applies, not the standard 21 -> fourteen_days
check.q2: Applicable period is the new arrival period of 14 days (checkout 2026-03-02 is after 2026-02-01 and inside the flag window 2026-02-20 to 2026-04-30); standard period 21 days; 14 < 21 -> true
check.q3: Hold H-9102 placed 2026-03-10; only status entry is waiting from 2026-03-10, so waiting on renewal request date 2026-03-14 -> hold rule refuses renewal; renewals so far 1, maximum 2, 1 < 2 so limit not reached -> renewal_refused_active_hold
check.q4: Checked out 2026-03-02; 14-day period counted from 2026-03-03 runs to 2026-03-16 (due); review 2026-03-27, item_returned false; 27 - 16 = 11 days overdue -> 8 to 14 band -> level 2
check.q5: Refusal was due to hold H-9102 waiting from 2026-03-10 through 2026-03-14; renewals used 1 of maximum 2, so limit not reached; statement is not the cause -> false

domain: membership renewals for a regional rowing club

membership-rules.grace-counting: Day 1 is the day after the due date; the due date itself is not counted. A payment received on or before day 21 is within grace.

state.request: Decide the renewal status for this member for the year beginning 1 April 2026. Say whether the renewal is accepted, whether a late fee applies, and which period the membership covers.
state.candidate-note: Renewal accepted. Payment was received on 17 April 2026 against a due date of 1 April 2026, which is inside the 21-day grace period, so membership continues without lapse and no late fee is charged. Membership runs from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 and the card can be issued.
state.newsletter-note: Spring camp at Martmouth moved to May; unrelated to renewals.

q1.instructions: Which renewal status should be recorded for this member's payment for the 2026-27 year?

criteria.renewed_on_due_date: Payment received on or before the due date, so no grace period is needed.
criteria.renewed_within_grace: Payment received after the due date but within the grace period, so membership continues without lapse and no late fee applies.
criteria.renewed_with_late_fee: Payment received after the due date and within the grace period, with the late fee added to the renewal.
criteria.lapsed_pending_rejoin: Payment received after the grace period, so membership has lapsed and a rejoin application is needed.
criteria.lapsed_fee_waived: Membership has lapsed, but the late fee has been waived by the club.
criteria.renewal_not_accepted: Payment refused because the membership year has not yet opened.

q2.instructions: The renewal payment falls within the grace period, so no late fee is due on it.

criteria.true: The payment date falls inside the grace window counted from the day after the due date, so no late fee applies.
criteria.false: The payment date falls outside the grace window, so a late fee applies.

q3.instructions: How many days after the due date was the renewal payment received, counting the day after the due date as day 1?

criteria.at_most_fourteen: Received 14 days or fewer after the due date.
criteria.twenty_two_or_more: Received 22 days or more after the due date.
criteria.fifteen_to_twenty_one: Received 15 to 21 days after the due date.

q4.instructions: How many of the three things the request asked for (the acceptance decision, the late-fee position, and the membership period) does the candidate note actually answer?
criteria: None of the three is answered.
Exactly one of the three is answered.
Exactly two of the three are answered.
All three are answered.

q5.instructions: The candidate note charges a late fee of £12.00 on this renewal.

criteria.true: The candidate note applies the £12.00 late fee to this renewal.
criteria.false: The candidate note does not apply the £12.00 late fee to this renewal.

check.q1: Due 2026-04-01; received 2026-04-17, after the due date; counting 2026-04-02 as day 1, 2026-04-17 is day 16; grace is 21 days, 16 <= 21 -> within grace, no late fee, membership continues -> renewed_within_grace
check.q2: Received 2026-04-17 = day 16 after due date (2026-04-02 is day 1; 17 - 1 = 16); grace 21 days, 16 <= 21 -> inside grace window -> no late fee -> statement true
check.q3: Due 2026-04-01; received 2026-04-17; 17 - 1 = 16 days after due date (April 2 counted as day 1 gives day 16) -> 16 is between 15 and 21 -> fifteen_to_twenty_one
check.q4: Note accepts the renewal (decision answered: yes); note says no late fee is charged (fee answered: yes); note states 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 (period answered: yes); 3 of 3 answered -> level 3
check.q5: Note says no late fee is charged; payment on day 16 is within the 21-day grace, so the £12.00 late fee (after-grace rate) does not apply; the note does not apply it -> statement false

domain: parcel delay tiers at a regional courier cross-dock hub

state.Tier_Rule_Note: A parcel is late when its delivered date falls after its promised date. Days late is the calendar-day difference between the delivered date and the promised date; an on-time parcel has zero days late.

q1.instructions: Rate the total number of days late across the express-service parcels in the log.
criteria: none: express parcels have a combined total of 0 days late
low: a combined total of 1 to 3 days late
moderate: a combined total of 4 to 6 days late
high: a combined total of 7 to 9 days late
severe: a combined total of 10 or more days late

q2.instructions: Group each parcel by the calendar week of its delivered date, where week 1 covers days 1 to 7, week 2 covers days 8 to 14, week 3 covers days 15 to 21 and week 4 covers days 22 to 28 of the month. Which week holds the parcel with the largest number of days late?

criteria.final_week: the week covering days 22 to 28 of the month holds the single largest days-late value
criteria.third_week: the week covering days 15 to 21 of the month holds the single largest days-late value
criteria.second_week: the week covering days 8 to 14 of the month holds the single largest days-late value
criteria.first_week: the week covering days 1 to 7 of the month holds the single largest days-late value
criteria.tied_weeks: two or more weeks each hold a parcel with the same largest days-late value
criteria.no_late_parcel: no parcel in the log was delivered after its promised date

q3.instructions: Rate the share of all parcels in the log that were delivered late.
criteria: 0: no parcel was delivered late (0 percent)
1: 1 to 49 percent of parcels were delivered late
2: 50 to 74 percent of parcels were delivered late
3: 75 percent or more of parcels were delivered late

q4.instructions: Every express-service parcel in the log was delivered after its promised date.

criteria.true: every express-service parcel has a delivered date later than its promised date
criteria.false: at least one express-service parcel has a delivered date on or before its promised date

q5.instructions: Rate the average days late per parcel across all parcels in the log, where the average is the total days late divided by the number of parcels in the log, counting on-time parcels as zero.
criteria: 0: under 2 days on average
1: 2 days to under 4 days on average
2: 4 days to under 6 days on average
3: 6 days to under 8 days on average
4: 8 days or more on average

q6.instructions: Which service level has the greater total number of days late across its parcels in the log?

criteria.standard_service: standard-service parcels have the greater combined days late
criteria.express_service: express-service parcels have the greater combined days late
criteria.equal_totals: both service levels have the same combined days late

check.q1: Express parcels PK-4401 (promised 2026-02-05, delivered 2026-02-09) = 4 days late; PK-4407 (promised 2026-02-14, delivered 2026-02-19) = 5 days late; total 4 + 5 = 9, which falls in 7 to 9 -> high
check.q2: PK-4411 promised 2026-02-20, delivered 2026-02-27 = 7 days late; PK-4401 = 4, PK-4407 = 5, PK-4402 = 0; largest is 7 (unique), delivered on day 27, within days 22 to 28 -> final_week
check.q3: Parcels delivered late: PK-4401 (02-09 after 02-05), PK-4407 (02-19 after 02-14), PK-4411 (02-27 after 02-20) = 3 late; PK-4402 on time (02-10 on 02-10); 3 / 4 x 100 = 75 percent, which is 75 or more -> 3
check.q4: PK-4401 delivered 2026-02-09 after promised 2026-02-05 (late); PK-4407 delivered 2026-02-19 after promised 2026-02-14 (late); both express parcels are late -> true
check.q5: Total days late = 4 + 0 + 5 + 7 = 16; parcels in log = 4; average = 16 / 4 = 4.0, which falls in 4 to under 6 -> 2
check.q6: Express total = 4 + 5 = 9; standard total = 0 + 7 = 7; 9 is greater than 7 -> express_service

domain: cycle hire dock bank occupancy logs

state.fault_rule: outage days = calendar date of clear_ts minus calendar date of open_ts

log.note: copied from n4

q1.instructions: How many bikes were docked at bank RS-14 at the 18:30 close check?

q2.instructions: Between the 17:50 full count and the 18:30 close check, the logged van moves increased the bike count overall.

criteria.true: The sum of the van_move changes logged in that window is positive.
criteria.false: The sum of the van_move changes logged in that window is zero or negative.

q3.instructions: Under the outage counting rule, how long was the outage of fault F-1187?

criteria.same_day: Opened and cleared on the same calendar day.
criteria.1_to_2_days: One or two calendar days apart.
criteria.5_days_or_more: Five or more calendar days apart.

q4.instructions: Rate how full bank RS-14 was at the 18:30 close check, using the occupancy rule.
criteria: Lower: under 50 percent occupancy
Middle: 50 percent or more but under 80 percent occupancy
Upper: 80 percent or more occupancy

q5.instructions: At the 18:30 close check, bank RS-14 held the same number of bikes as at the 17:50 full count.

q6.instructions: Which method gives the bike count to report at the close check under the hub's recording rule?

criteria.open_count_unchanged: Use the first full count of the day with no moves applied.
criteria.open_count_plus_all_moves: Start from the first full count of the day and apply every logged move.
criteria.last_full_count_unchanged: Use the most recent full count without applying any later moves.
criteria.close_check_as_keyed: Use whatever figure is typed into the close check entry.
criteria.docks_total_less_faults: Subtract faulted docks from the total dock count.
criteria.last_full_count_plus_later_moves: Start from the most recent full count and apply the moves logged after it.

check.q1: Last full_count is 15 at 17:50 (n4); van_move +5 at 18:10 (n5) is after it and before 18:30; moves at 11:05 and 13:20 are before n4 and excluded; 15 + 5 = 20; the close_check 15 is a copy of n4 -> 20 bikes, which is in 19 or 20 -> 19_to_20
check.q2: Moves between 17:50 (n4) and 18:30 (n6): only n5 at +5; sum = +5 > 0 -> increased overall -> true
check.q3: F-1187 opened 2026-04-29, cleared 2026-05-03; calendar dates 3 May minus 29 April = 1 (30 Apr) + 3 (1, 2, 3 May) = 4 days -> 4_days
check.q4: Bikes at close: 15 + 5 = 20; docks_total 24; occupancy = 20 / 24 = 83.3 percent; 80 percent or more -> upper level, index 2
check.q5: Count at 17:50 is 15; bikes at 18:30 = 15 + 5 = 20; 20 is not equal to 15 -> statement false
check.q6: Rule: close figure = most recent full_count plus van_move deltas keyed after it; this matches 'start from the most recent full count and apply the moves logged after it' -> last_full_count_plus_later_moves

domain: student housing tenancy break and rent apportionment

state.Document Title: Student Tenancy Break Register and Rent Schedule

Clause Register.Clause Text: The monthly rent for each room is GBP 640.00, payable in advance on the first day of each calendar month.
With effect from 1 January 2026 the monthly rent for each room is GBP 612.00. All other terms of clause 4.1 continue unchanged.
Clause Register.Applies To: All tenancies in the Mixfell and Cumthorpe schemes

Clause Register.Clause Text: The tenant may end the tenancy early by written notice to the landlord of at least 60 full days before the Break Date. Days are counted from the day after the notice is received up to and including the Break Date.

Clause Register.Clause Title: Early Break by Tenant, Amendment AM-3
Clause Register.Clause Text: The tenant may end the tenancy early by written notice to the landlord of at least 45 full days before the Break Date, counted in the same way as the original wording. This amendment applies to notices received on or after its effective date. A notice received before that date stays under the original wording.

Where the University has issued a written relocation instruction for the tenant, the tenant may give notice of at least 21 full days before the Break Date, counted in the same way as clause 9.2, provided a copy of that instruction is sent with the notice. This exception applies whichever wording of clause 9.2 governs the notice.

Rent is payable up to and including the Break Date. Where the Break Date is not the last day of a calendar month, rent for that month is apportioned by calendar days, using the number of days in that month, and the balance is credited to the tenant.
A lost fob is replaced at the tenant's cost of GBP 25.00 on collection from the lettings office during opening hours.

Break Requests Log.Log Note: Tenant withdrew the request after a change in placement. No deposit was affected.
Notice gives a change of course as the reason. No University document was attached. Acknowledged on 2026-02-11.
Relocation letter attached to the posted notice. Break date matches the move-out date given in the letter.

Rent due at revised rate under RV-02

Gas safety certificate for Cumthorpe House renewed to 2027-01-14.

Amendment AM-3 was approved by the board on 2026-01-08 and published to the schemes on 2026-01-12.
Clause 9.4 was not changed by AM-3 and was confirmed unchanged in the same review.

q1.instructions: For the break request logged as BR-0017, which outcome applies under the break clause that governs the notice?

criteria.refused_superseded_sixty_day_rule: Refused because the notice is shorter than the sixty-day minimum in the original wording of the break clause.
criteria.accepted_relocation_exception: Accepted because a relocation instruction is sent with the notice and the shorter exception period is met.
criteria.refused_notice_too_short_all_rules: Refused because the notice is shorter than every notice period available under the break clause.
criteria.accepted_without_notice_period: Accepted at the tenant's request although the required notice period is not met.
criteria.accepted_under_amended_forty_five_day_ru: Accepted because the notice meets the forty-five day minimum in the amended wording, which governs notices received on or after the amendment's effective date.

q2.instructions: For the tenancy of the break request logged as BR-0017, the rent payable for March 2026 is the full monthly rent in force, with no reduction for the early break.

criteria.true: The March 2026 rent is charged at the full monthly rate in force, with no apportionment for a break date within the month.
criteria.false: The March 2026 rent is reduced because the break date falls before the last day of March.

q3.instructions: For the break request logged as BR-0018, which outcome applies under the break clause and exception that govern the notice?

criteria.accepted_under_amended_forty_five_day_ru: Accepted because the notice meets the forty-five day minimum in the amended wording of the break clause.
criteria.refused_short_under_every_route: Refused because the notice is shorter than the amended minimum and also shorter than the period available when a relocation instruction is enclosed.
criteria.accepted_relocation_exception: Accepted because the shorter exception period applies when a relocation instruction is sent with the notice.
criteria.refused_relocation_instruction_missing: Refused because no relocation instruction was sent with the notice.
criteria.refused_superseded_sixty_day_rule: Refused because the notice is shorter than the sixty-day minimum in the original wording of the break clause.
criteria.accepted_on_tenant_reason_alone: Accepted because the tenant's stated reason for leaving is treated as sufficient whatever the notice period.

check.q1: BR-0017 notice received 2026-02-10, which is on or after the AM-3 effective date of 2026-01-15, so the 45-day wording governs; days counted from 2026-02-11 to Break Date 2026-03-27 inclusive = 18 (Feb 11-28) + 27 (Mar 1-27) = 45 days, which meets 'at least 45' -> accepted under the amended 45-day rule; relocation instruction not enclosed, so the exception is not needed.
check.q2: Rent under RV-02 from 2026-01-01 is GBP 612.00; Break Date 2026-03-27 is not the last day of March (31 days), so clause 9.5 applies: 27 of 31 days payable, 612.00 x 27 / 31 = 533.03, which is not the full GBP 612.00 -> statement false.
check.q3: BR-0018 notice received 2026-03-02, after 2026-01-15, so the AM-3 45-day wording governs; days counted from 2026-03-03 to Break Date 2026-03-20 inclusive = 18 < 45 -> standard route fails; relocation instruction enclosed (University letter dated 2026-02-26), so the 21-day exception applies, but 18 < 21 -> fails; neither route met -> refused short under every route.

domain: youth rowing club competition eligibility

copy: Kisus Druckcott (Trust chair); Vondbrunara Plant Hire (site file only); file

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.1 This procedure sets out how work that disturbs track, ballast, sleepers or rail is requested, classed, given notice and permitted on the Lairtfell branch, including the Lairtfell cutting, the Greamwold siding and the Greamwold yard.
1.2 It covers work on running lines, sidings and cutting drains. It does not cover rolling stock maintenance in the Greamwold shed, which is governed by WHRT-RSM-02.
1.3 Where a gang's own method statement differs from this procedure, this procedure prevails.
1.4 Volunteers working under a gang leader are covered by this procedure as if they were the gang leader's own staff for the purposes of section 10.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 Track disturbance length: the total length of track, measured along the running rail, over which rail, sleepers, ballast or formation are lifted, removed, packed or altered. Recorded in metres. A length given in yards is converted at 1 yard = 0.9144 metres.
2.2 Running-line clearance: the shortest distance, in metres, between any work area and the nearest running rail of an open line.
2.3 Working day: any day from Monday to Friday that is not listed in section 7.
2.4 Notice period: the number of working days that must fall strictly between the day a request is lodged and the planned start day. The lodging day is not counted. The planned start day is not counted. Each working day in between counts once. A job meets its notice period when that count is equal to or greater than the number required for its class and location.
2.5 A request is lodged on the date the Line Warden's register records it.
2.6 Non-working days inside the count are simply not counted. They do not restart or end the count.

3. JOB CLASSES
3.1 Class 1: hand-tool work only, with no track disturbance, carried out inside a fenced compound.
3.2 Class 2: track disturbance length of 30 metres or less, and running-line clearance of 2 metres or more.
3.3 Class 3: track disturbance length of more than 30 metres, or any work with running-line clearance under 2 metres.
3.4 A job takes the highest class that any one of its elements meets.
3.5 A job's class is fixed when its request is lodged. It is not changed by later edits to its method statement unless the Line Warden re-lodges the request.

4. NOTICE PERIODS
4.1 Class 1: no notice period. Gang leader sign-off is enough.
4.2 Class 2: 5 working days.
4.3 Class 3: 10 working days. (Clause 4.3 is replaced by Amendment 2, see section 9.)
4.4 Where a notice period is not met, the Line Warden shall not issue a permit unless section 6 applies.

5. PERMITS
5.1 The Line Warden issues the permit. A permit is not issued until the notice period has run, unless clause 6.1 applies.
5.2 A permit names the job, its class, its location, its start day and its end day.
5.3 A permit lapses if work has not started within 3 working days after its start day.
5.4 Permits are held in the site cabinet at Greamwold yard and must be shown to the gang leader on site.
5.5 A re-lodged request takes the lodging date of the re-lodged request for all purposes of section 4.

6. SAFETY-CRITICAL EXCEPTION
6.1 The Operations Committee may, by written certificate naming the job, certify that the work is safety-critical. For a Class 3 job so certified, the notice period may be reduced to not less than 3 working days. No other person may reduce a notice period.
6.2 The Line Warden may give verbal authority to make a site safe straight after a fault. Verbal authority under this clause covers making site safe only. It does not allow the works to start and does not shorten any notice period.
6.3 A certificate must be signed by the Operations Committee secretary and filed with the register entry for the job before the reduced start day.
6.4 A certificate that has been requested but not issued has no effect. Work may not start on the strength of a request.

9.4 A draft Amendment 3, on volunteer induction, has been written but not approved. It is not in force and changes no clause in this procedure.

10. ROLES
10.1 Line Warden: keeps the register, issues permits, and may give verbal authority under clause 6.2.
10.2 Operations Committee: meets quarterly; issues safety certificates under clause 6.1.
10.3 Gang leaders: sign off Class 1 work, keep method statements on site, and brief volunteers. Gang leaders do not sign off Class 2 or Class 3 work.
10.4 Hi-vis vests and hard hats are required for all track work. Radio channel 4 is used at the Lairtfell cutting.
10.5 Volunteers complete the induction card before their first shift on track. The card is held at Greamwold yard.

11. RECORDS
11.1 Register entries are kept for six years after the job closes. Before and after photographs are kept in the Greamwold yard cabinet with the permit.
11.2 Printed copies are uncontrolled. The register extract at section 8 is the controlled copy for 2026-03-11.

13. HIRE AND EQUIPMENT NOTES
13.1 The mini-digger from Vondbrunara Plant Hire is delivered to Greamwold yard. Days of use are booked through the Line Warden.
13.2 The operator must hold a current Trust induction card before the machine enters a running-line area.
13.3 Ballast wagon hire is outside this procedure. Enquiries go to the Greamwold yard foreman.

14. SITE CHECKS
14.1 Before any Class 2 or Class 3 work starts, the gang leader walks the site with the permit and records the running-line clearance on the permit form.
14.2 Where the clearance recorded on site differs from the clearance in the register, the Line Warden is told the same day and the register is corrected before work starts.
14.3 Lookouts are posted at both ends of any work area on a running line. Lookouts carry red flags by day and lamps after dusk.
14.4 Spoil from cutting jobs goes to the spoil stack at Greamwold yard, not onto the cess.
14.5 Volunteers under 18 do not work on track.

15. HOUSEKEEPING
15.1 Gang method statements are dated and signed by the gang leader. A copy goes to the Line Warden.
15.2 The site cabinet is locked when the gang is off site. The key is held by the Line Warden and by the Greamwold yard foreman.
15.3 Tea and welfare arrangements are set out in WHRT-WEL-01.

policy.deductible_rule: taken once per claim, from the gross payment

log.text: Hail hit Plalwych Mill Farm on the evening of 9 June. P-07 looks flattened across the whole field. P-05 and P-11 were not touched. Notice given now.
First visit. Sample cut of ten 1 m2 quadrats taken on the P-07 headland strip only. Assessed yield 4.10 t/ha. Provisional pending a full-field count.
Full-field recount on P-07 using twenty quadrats spread across the field. Assessed yield 3.55 t/ha. This recount replaces the 18 June figure, which came from the headland and should not be used.
The register expected yield for P-07 (6.40 t/ha) came from the 2024 variety trial and is withdrawn. Revised expected yield for P-07 is 6.20 t/ha, for this claim and any later restatement of it.
P-11 harvest booking moved to 22 July. No claim activity on this parcel.

state.notes: Claim CL-0391-B is open on parcel P-07 only. Winter cereals hail is settled under E-14 on yield shortfall alone; the receipts route is not available for cereals. Flat per-hectare payments belong to the grassland schedule and do not apply to this file. The holder asked whether the 18 June figure would stand; the desk replied that the later full-field recount governs the file. Payment has not been released. Weather station readings are supplied for the record only and have not been used to set the loss. Oats parcel P-05 and oilseed rape parcel P-11 are not part of this claim and their harvest bookings are held separately. Next review 2026-07-20. The holder's bank details are held on the payments file and are not repeated here.

2.2 Clause 4.2 of RA-2024 (response categories) was replaced in full by Board resolution BR-2026-01, passed on 2026-01-15 and effective from 2026-02-02. A job is governed by the wording of clause 4.2 that was in force on the day the job was reported.

3. Clause wording
3.1 Original clause 4.2, superseded from 2026-02-02: Emergency, attend within 24 hours. Urgent, attend within 5 working days. Routine, attend within 20 working days. Planned works have no response target.
3.2 Clause 4.2 as replaced by BR-2026-01: Emergency means a fault that presents immediate danger to people or property, to be attended within 12 clock hours of the report time. Routine means any other fault, to be attended within 15 working days. Planned works have no response target. Despite the above, a loss of heating in a dwelling between 1 November and 31 March inclusive is an emergency, whatever other details the report contains.

PART 2 - RULE VERSIONS AND CORE RULES
2.1 Quota Rules Version 2 (Sergate edition) was in force from 2026-01-01. It governs any trip that departed before 2026-05-01.
2.2 Quota Rules Version 3 takes effect on 2026-05-01. It governs any trip that departs on or after 2026-05-01, whatever the date of landing.
2.3 Each trip is governed by one version only: the version in force on the date the trip departed.
2.4 Trip break period: 48 consecutive hours in harbour under Version 2; 24 consecutive hours in harbour under Version 3.
2.5 Gutted-weight landings are converted to landed weight by multiplying the recorded gutted weight by the gutting factor. The gutting factor is 1.25 under Version 2 and 1.18 under Version 3. Landings recorded in landed weight are not converted.
2.6 Discards are never deducted from the allocation. Only landed weight, after any conversion under 2.5, is deducted.
2.7 Only approved quota transfers change the allocation. A transfer changes the allocation from the date of the signed approval letter filed on this file.
2.8 Reporting: the position is stated as at the report date and covers all landings in the allocation year up to and including that date.
2.9 Converted weights are taken to the nearest whole kilogram.
2.10 Quota not used by the end of the allocation year lapses. The 2026 position is not carried into 2027.
2.11 Landing dockets dated on a weekend or public holiday are processed on the next working day. The processing date does not change the landing date used on this file.
2.12 Times in the trip log are local time at Sergate. Dates are written year-month-day.
2.13 Crew numbers, vessel length and gear type are recorded for safety and licensing. They have no effect on the quota position.

PART 3 - DEFINITIONS (AS REPRODUCED FOR THIS FILE)
3.1 'Fishing day' means a calendar day, 00:00 to 23:59 local time, on which the vessel is at sea for at least 6 hours. Time in harbour, at moorings, or in transit within 2 nautical miles of the harbour mouth is not sea time.
3.2 'Trip' means the period from one departure from harbour to the next return to harbour, unless a harbour stay ends it under 3.3.
3.3 A harbour stay ends the current trip when the time from the return time in the trip log to the next departure time in the trip log is at least the trip break period. The trip break period is the one set by the version governing the trip being ended. A stay shorter than the break period does not end the trip.
3.4 'Gutted weight' means the weight of fish after gutting and before icing, as entered on the landing docket.
3.5 'Landed weight' means the weight of the catch as entered on the landing docket when it was weighed in landed form.
3.6 'Allocation year' means 1 January to 31 December of the stated year.

definitions.qualifying_minutes: Minutes of continuous supervised firing on a steam locomotive recorded in a single logged session. definitions.lodging_date: The date on which the complete application is received by the training office. Only sessions dated on or before the lodging date count toward that application.
definitions.session_dating: A session counts toward an application whatever version of this procedure was in force on the session date. Only the lodging date limits which sessions count.
definitions.governing_version: The version in force on the lodging date: the version whose effective_from is on or before that date and whose effective_to is either empty or on or after that date. A version whose effective_from falls after the lodging date does not govern that application.

lease.rent_review_basis: Open market value, no less than the prior year's rent per hectare

definitions.frost_event: A night on which the frost station first records a reading below 0.0 degrees Celsius between 1 April and 31 May inclusive. The event date is the calendar date on which that first reading is taken.
definitions.qualifying_loss: The shortfall of harvest weight recorded at the weighbridge below a block's Schedule 3 expected yield for the season. Loss of canopy, shoots, fruit not yet set, or vines is not qualifying loss and is not counted toward any threshold in clause 7.4.
definitions.season: The calendar year in which the harvest is picked and weighed.
definitions.fan_start: The time at which the fan set on a block is switched on, as entered in that block's start log.

7.4_rent_abatement.wording: Where a block suffers qualifying loss in a season that exceeds the threshold in clause 7.4.2, the landlord shall grant the tenant a rent abatement for that block for that season, calculated under clause 7.4.4.
7.4_rent_abatement.7.4.2_threshold: The threshold is a shortfall greater than 25 per cent of the block's Schedule 3 expected yield.
7.4_rent_abatement.7.4.4_calculation: Abatement is the base rent per hectare, multiplied by the block area in hectares, multiplied by the number of percentage points by which the qualifying loss exceeds the threshold, divided by 100.

clauses.7.5_exception: Clause 7.4 does not apply to any block where the qualifying loss results from the tenant failing to run frost protection on that block as required by clause 7.6 during the frost event.
clauses.7.6_frost_protection: On each frost event the tenant shall start the frost fans on every block within 30 minutes of the frost station's first reading below 0.0 degrees Celsius in that event, and shall keep a start log for each block showing the time each fan set was started.
clauses.7.8_rent_payment: Rent is payable quarterly in advance on the payment dates in the lease schedule. Late payment bears interest under clause 11.2.
clauses.7.9_insurance: The tenant shall insure the vines against wind and hail damage. Frost losses are not insured by the landlord and are dealt with under clause 7.4 only.
clauses.7.10_assignment: The tenant may not assign or sublet any part of the vineyard without the landlord's written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
clauses.7.11_landlord_station: The landlord shall maintain the frost station and its power supply, and shall make the station readings available to the tenant on request.
clauses.11.2_interest: Interest on late rent accrues at 4 per cent above the bank base rate from the due date until payment.
