contents: Section A (Standard Terms, Version 1); Section B (Amendment Notice, Version 2); Section C (Allocation Notice); Section D (Correspondence); Section E (Access Office Log extract); Section F (Instruments and site items); Section G (Other items held in this pack); Section H (Site maintenance notes)

SECTION A. STANDARD TERMS OF ACCESS, VERSION 1
Effective date: 1 October 2025.

A1. Scope. These terms govern observing time on the Pleholm Ridge 1.2 m Telescope that the Trust makes available to approved visiting groups. Time is allocated in blocks of consecutive nights. Each block is named in an allocation notice issued by the Access Office.

A2. Nightly allocation. Each block carries a nightly allocation stated in its allocation notice. The standard nightly allocation is 6.5 hours of telescope time per night, which is 390 minutes. The Trust may reduce a nightly allocation only by written notice that names the affected night.

A3. Observer conduct. Visiting groups keep to the observing plan in their allocation notice and follow the Pleholm Ridge site safety rules. A group that breaches the site safety rules may be asked to leave the dome for the rest of the night, and the night is then treated as used.

A4. Notice of cancellation. A group that wishes to cancel a block must send written notice to the Access Office. Notice is given when the Access Office receives it, and the receipt time recorded in the Access Office log is the time of receipt. The notice period is found by subtracting the date of receipt from the date of the first night of the block. The result, in calendar days, is the notice period.

A5. Late cancellation. The minimum notice period is 14 calendar days. A cancellation whose notice period is below the minimum is a late cancellation. A late cancellation forfeits the whole block. A forfeited block returns to the open pool, and the group has no claim to it.

A6. Trust-fault exception. A cancellation is not treated as late under clause A5 where the Trust has issued a written fault notice for the telescope, dome or instrument that prevents observing on the block and that names the block. Any other reason for cancelling is outside this exception, including travel, staffing, funding or equipment changes on the group's side.

A7. Scheduling changes. Where the Trust moves a block by written notice, the new dates replace the dates in the allocation notice from the date of that notice. The nightly allocation and the number of nights do not change on a move unless the notice says so.

A8. Records. The Access Office keeps the receipt time of every notice in its log. The log is the record of receipt for all purposes under clauses A4 and A5.

A9. Publication and data. Groups acknowledge the Trust in any published result made with telescope time. Data from a block are subject to a twelve-month embargo unless the group agrees otherwise in writing with the Access Office.

A10. Instruments. The telescope is equipped with a CCD imager, a low-resolution spectrograph and a guide camera. A group may ask in writing for a change of instrument. A change is made only if Scheduling confirms it in writing.

A11. Observing plan. The observing plan in the allocation notice lists target fields in priority order. Changes to the plan are agreed with Scheduling and do not change the block dates or the nightly allocation.

A12. On-site lead. Each group names one on-site lead in writing before its block. The lead is responsible for the dome and the instruments during the block.

A13. Accommodation. The Trust publishes a list of accommodation near Pleholm. Accommodation is not part of the allocation and each group arranges its own.

A14. Headings and amendments. Headings are for reference only. An amendment applies to the allocations that its own application clause names, and to no others.

SECTION B. AMENDMENT NOTICE, VERSION 2
Issued: Friday 27 February 2026.
Effective: 1 March 2026.

PART A - BYLAW TEXT (consolidated 2025 edition)

Cl 1.1 Scope. These bylaws apply to every vessel that enters, leaves or waits in the chamber of Frolbury Lock on the Vaillstow reach, including hire craft run by Skoukandell Hire Ltd and Treackholm Hire Ltd.

Cl 1.2 Measurements. Draught is the certified draught shown on the vessel's survey certificate. It may be recorded in metres or centimetres. The Office converts every value to metres before applying a passage band.

Cl 2.1 Chamber use. Only one vessel may occupy the chamber at a time, except that a tender may be lashed alongside its parent vessel. Vessels are admitted in the order their applications were accepted, subject to cl 2.3.

Cl 2.3 Priority. Vessels on a published closure-recovery run take priority over other applications for the first working day after a closure ends.

Cl 3.2 Passage categories (2025 table; replaced by Amendment No. 2, see Part B):
  Category A (standard): draught up to and including 1.20 m. No notice. No pilot.
  Category B (notice): draught over 1.20 m and up to and including 1.80 m. Notice under cl 3.4. No pilot.
  Category C (pilot): draught over 1.80 m. A licensed pilot must be aboard.

Cl 3.4 Notice. A Category B passage needs at least 48 hours' notice of the scheduled lock-entry time.

Cl 4.2 Lock keepers. The lock keeper on duty may hold a vessel at the upstream gate for up to 30 minutes for safety reasons and must log the hold in the chamber book.

Cl 5.1 Lodging. Notice is counted from the time the application is received by the Office to the scheduled lock-entry time. An application lodged with less notice than its category requires is refused and must be resubmitted with a new entry time.

Cl 5.3 Closures. The Office may close the lock to all passages for maintenance. A closure notice gives a first and last day; both days are closed.

Cl 6.1 Records. Every amendment, notice and message that changes a clause is filed in this file in date order.

1.1 Each pitch is a single trading unit of 3.0 m by 3.0 m unless the pitch schedule in section 10 states otherwise.

1.4 Public liability cover of at least 5,000,000 GBP must be on file before set-up access is granted.
1.5 Pitch markings are painted in white and must not be moved without written consent from the trading manager.

SECTION 2 - TRADING HOURS
2.1 The standard trading window is 10:00 to 22:00 on each trading day.
2.2 Clearing and cleaning must finish by 23:30 on each trading day.
2.3 Early opening: a trader holding a hot-food check certificate may open from 08:00 on the first trading day only, provided the certificate has been logged against the trader reference with the safety officer on or before 2026-05-31. A certificate logged after that date does not qualify. No early opening is available on any other day.
2.4 Amplified sound is not permitted before 11:00 on any day.

SECTION 3 - DEPOSITS AND CANCELLATION
3.1 The pitch deposit is 480 GBP per pitch and is held by the organiser until the end of the festival.
3.2 The refund band is set by the number of calendar days from the date the cancellation notice is received by the trading manager up to the first trading day. That number is found by subtracting the receipt date from the first trading day date.
(a) 60 days or more: the full deposit is returned.
(b) 30 to 59 days: half of the deposit is returned.
(c) Fewer than 30 days: none of the deposit is returned.
3.3 Medical exception: where a trader cancels because of a documented medical reason, the full deposit is returned whatever the notice period. The documented reason must be sent with the notice.
3.4 Where the organiser cancels a pitch, the full deposit is returned.

SECTION 4 - ELECTRICAL SUPPLY
4.1 The standard supply to each pitch is 6.0 kW.
4.2 Each trader must submit an appliance schedule listing every electrical item with its rated power in kW. Gas appliances are not listed in the electrical schedule.
4.3 Declared load above 6.0 kW is referred to the site electrician, who decides whether an upgrade can be supplied.
4.4 Where a trader amends the appliance schedule in writing, the most recent written schedule replaces the earlier one for that pitch.

SECTION 5 - GAS AND SAFETY
5.1 Each pitch may hold up to two LPG cylinders of 13 kg or less, connected through a regulator that carries a current test label.
5.2 Cylinders are not counted in the electrical schedule.
5.3 One fat-rated fire extinguisher per pitch must be on site from the start of set-up access.
5.4 Generators are not permitted on any pitch.

6.2 No other clause is changed by any amendment issued to date. Clause 2.3 is unchanged.

SECTION 7 - PRICING AND MENU RULES
7.1 Traders set their own prices but must display a price board at the front of the pitch.
7.2 Each item on the price board must show the single total price the customer pays.
7.3 Single-use plastic cups and straws are not permitted. Reusable or compostable items must be used.
7.4 Alcohol sales need a licence held by the organiser and are outside this file.
7.5 Menu boards are checked on the first trading day, before the 10:00 opening.

8.1 Cooking fat and oil must go into the grease bins at each row. Pouring fat or oil down any drain is prohibited.

PART A. POLICY SHRT-PM-7, boiler firing limits and passenger eligibility
Revision 3, in force from 2026-01-12. Times in the firing log are local, 24-hour clock. Dates are ISO (year-month-day).

A1. Purpose
This policy decides which steam locomotives may haul passenger trains on the Damwold Valley Line. It covers every locomotive listed in Part B. Terms defined in A2 carry the meaning given there wherever they appear in this policy, in Part C, in Part C2 and in Part D.

A2. Definitions
washoutDay: the calendar day on which a boiler was last examined, washed out and tested under a boiler certificate. The washoutDay is never counted. Counting starts on the calendar day after it.
firingDay: a calendar day, midnight to midnight, on which a boiler is raised to steam and held under steam for one continuous steaming of at least 4 hours, measured from steamUp to fireDown as recorded in the firing log. Steamings shorter than 4 hours are ignored, and shorter steamings on the same day do not add together with a qualifying steaming. A day containing one or more qualifying steamings counts once only.
firingCount: the number of firingDays that fall after the washoutDay and on or before the date being assessed.
applicableLimit: the standard limit in A3, unless a written amendment under A4 names the locomotive, in which case the limit stated in that amendment.
passengerEligible: a locomotive that holds a boiler test certificate in date on the day of running and whose firingCount to that day is no more than its applicableLimit.

A3. Standard limit
The standard applicableLimit is 40 firingDays. A boiler is passengerEligible while its firingCount is 40 or fewer.

A4. Amendments
A written amendment signed by the Boiler Inspector and sent to the Operations Office may set a different applicableLimit for the locomotive it names. It takes effect on the date of the message. It applies to the whole firingCount since the washoutDay and does not reset the count already logged. It does not apply to any locomotive it does not name. A message from any other officer alters an applicableLimit only if it is itself a written amendment under this section.

A5. Passenger running
Only a passengerEligible locomotive may haul passengers, at any load or speed. A locomotive that is not passengerEligible may still be steamed for non-passenger work such as shunting, but may not haul passengers until a new washout has been carried out.
Where the rostered locomotive for a passenger train is not passengerEligible on the day, the Operations Manager must either substitute another passengerEligible locomotive for the same train, or cancel the train if, and only if, no passengerEligible locomotive is available on that day. These are the only permitted courses. No person or body, including the Board, may waive an applicableLimit or the certificate requirement.

A6. Records
The Locomotive Foreman keeps the firing logs in Part C and Part C2 from the washoutDay onward. Entries are copied from the crew sheets. No totals are kept on the log sheets.

scheme_rules.title: No outright bar
scheme_rules.txt: Nothing in this scheme bars a structure type outright. A structure that no exemption covers needs a permit before it is erected or kept on a plot; a permit may be granted or refused on its merits.

scheme_rules.title: Measurement
scheme_rules.txt: Floor area is the external footprint of the structure, recorded in m2 to one decimal place. Plot area is the surveyed figure in m2 recorded on the site survey.

scheme_rules.title: Small non-habitable structure exemption, earlier version
scheme_rules.txt: A non-habitable structure is exempt if floor area is no more than 10.0 m2 AND surveyed plot area is at least 150 m2. A cold frame is also exempt if its floor area is no more than 2.0 m2, whatever the plot area.

scheme_rules.title: Small non-habitable structure exemption, current version
scheme_rules.txt: A non-habitable structure is exempt if floor area is no more than 8.0 m2 AND surveyed plot area is at least 150 m2. A cold frame is also exempt if its floor area is no more than 2.0 m2, whatever the plot area. This version governs structures erected on or after its in-force date; a structure erected earlier is judged under the version in force on its erection date.

scheme_rules.title: Holder reply window
scheme_rules.txt: A holder has 21 days to reply to a permit notice. The notice date is not counted. Day 1 is the day after the notice date and the window closes at the end of day 21. A reply received on or before the last day is in time. A reminder does not restart or extend the window.

state:
PUCKPOCKOVA RIVER AUTHORITY - INTERNAL MEMO
Memo ref: RNB-REV-0622     Status: final for the stated review window
From: Frema Wyxgill, Compliance Officer (f.wyxgill@puckpockova.example)
To: Ruckie Bendcott, Harbour Master, Soxbury Lock Office
Cc: Mesine Coucarwick, Records; Grinda Tertstead, liaison, Virdrisex Marine Services Ltd
Date: 2026-05-15
Subj: Speed review, vessel NB-6134, Ryhaven Reach
Review window: 2026-03-20 to 2026-05-10 inclusive

1. PURPOSE
This memo records the speed review for vessel NB-6134 over the review window above. It applies the River Navigation Bylaws as amended. Where a log entry conflicts with a later correction, the correction governs (see item C4 in section 4).

2. VESSEL AND REGISTER
2.1 Reg. no. NB-6134. Type: hire launch, length 9.1 m, twin screw, passenger certificate PC-3047.
2.2 Registered operator: Virdrisex Marine Services Ltd, Grouxwold Depot.
2.3 Not on the wash-exempt list (list dated 2025-12-01).
2.4 Enforcement register: no steps recorded for NB-6134 before 2026-03-20. Register last updated 2026-03-02.
2.5 Operator contact: Grinda Tertstead, grinda.tertstead@virdrisex.example.

3. BYLAW EXTRACTS (AS AMENDED)
Bylaw 4, Ryhaven Reach
4.1 (original, until amended) The speed limit in the Ryhaven Reach, between marker RR-0 and marker RR-9, is 6 knots.
4.1 (Amendment No. 2, replaces original 4.1 in full) The speed limit in the Ryhaven Reach, between marker RR-0 and marker RR-9, is 5 knots, taking effect at 00:00 on 2026-04-01. Before that time the original 4.1 applies.
4.2 A passage is measured as the average speed over the full run from RR-0 to RR-9, in knots over ground, as recorded by the lock logger.
4.3 A passage is an excess only when its average speed is strictly greater than the limit in force on the date of the passage. An average equal to the limit is not an excess.
4.4 Where the Compliance Officer records a corrected logger reading after recalibration, the corrected reading replaces the logged reading for all purposes in a review.

Bylaw 5, Grouxwold Harbour (separate; not applicable to the Ryhaven Reach)
5.1 Within 200 m of the Grouxwold quay wall the limit is 4 knots.

Bylaw 7, enforcement steps
7.1 An excess is classed by how far the average is above the limit: (a) excess up to and including 1.0 knot: advisory notice; (b) excess more than 1.0 knot and up to and including 2.5 knots: written warning; (c) excess more than 2.5 knots: fixed penalty notice.
7.2 The steps rise in this order: advisory notice, written warning, fixed penalty notice, referral to the harbour court.
7.3 Repeat excess: if a vessel has an earlier passage that was an excess under bylaw 4.3 within the 30 days before the passage being assessed, the step given by 7.1 for the passage being assessed is raised by one step in 7.2, but no higher than fixed penalty notice. This applies whatever step the earlier excess attracted.
7.4 Calendar days are counted. An earlier passage is within the 30 days if its date is no more than 30 days before the date of the passage being assessed.

Bylaw 8, appeals (for information)
8.1 A recipient may ask for a review within 14 days of the notice date. A review request does not suspend the step taken.

Bylaw 9, Soxbury Lock hours (for information)
9.1 Soxbury Lock operates 06:00 to 20:00 daily, closing at 18:00 on Mondays.

1. Purpose
This memo sets out the rules the selection panel applies when deciding whether a registered member may be named to the Skeackhaven Relay squad for the selection date of 2026-05-09. It also records the register and training data for the two members who have asked for a ruling before the panel meets. Other squads and fixtures are not covered by this memo.

2. Rules
2.1 A member is eligible on the selection date only if all three of the following are met:
(a) Registration: the member's current continuous registration period is at least the minimum for the member's age group (see 2.2).
(b) Training: the member has at least 3 attended Thursday training sessions in the 30-day window, or holds a coach's written waiver on file.
(c) Medical: no medical suspension is in force on the selection date.
2.2 Age group is set by age on the selection date. Members aged 16 or over need at least 60 days of continuous registration. Members aged under 16 need at least 30 days.
2.3 The continuous registration period starts on the first day of the member's current uninterrupted run of membership and counts that day. 2.4 The 30-day window is the 30 calendar days ending on the day before the selection date, with both end days included.
2.5 A session counts as attended only if the coach has marked it attended. Sessions cancelled by the club are not scheduled and are left out of any attendance count.
2.6 A medical suspension is in force on any date from its start date to its end date, both included. A suspension that ended before the selection date is not in force on it.

domain: railway heritage trust steam locomotive passenger-running eligibility
state:
LOSSKOCKON RAILWAY HERITAGE TRUST
Engineering memo LRHT-ENG-0527: passenger-running status of steam Locomotives 41 and 58 under PRS-4

Date: 2026-05-12
From: Mollin Brackmere, Mechanical Lead, Pesthorpe Engine Shed (m.brackmere@losskockon-trust.example)
To: Cyran Skoxer, Operations Manager (c.skoxer@losskockon-trust.example)
Cc: Quoys Frouxlock, Safety Trustee (q.frouxlock@losskockon-trust.example); Plous Wurmere, Volunteer Coordinator
Subject: June running on the Clouminster branch: which engines may take passengers

1. Purpose
Cyran asked for a written position before the June timetable is fixed. This memo sets out the running standard in force, the transitional provision that bridges the change, and the register status of both engines at the close of the last day of the old standard. It supersedes my note of 2026-04-02 and the draft circulated on 2026-03-28. Nothing in the June plan should be built from either of those two documents.

2. Which version applies
The Passenger Running Standard (PRS-4) governs every passenger movement on the Clouminster branch. Version 3 applied up to and including 2026-04-30. Version 4 took effect on 2026-05-01 and governs every running day from that date onward. Version 3 used a 56-day washout limit and had no transitional clause. Version 3 must not be used for any running day from 2026-05-01, except that clause 7.4 of version 4 refers back to the passenger status a locomotive held under version 3.

3. Effective date and the email trail
On 2026-04-02 I wrote that version 4 would take effect on 2026-04-15. That date came from the draft I was working from at the time. On 2026-04-09 the Gaixplurova Boiler Inspection Services office asked us to wait until the engine register had been reconciled, and on 2026-04-21 the Trustees resolved (minute 14/26) that version 4 take effect on 2026-05-01. The 2026-05-01 date is the one that applies. The 2026-04-15 date in my earlier note is withdrawn and should be deleted from the planning folder.

4. Standard Category A test (version 4, clause 5)
To carry passengers under Category A, a locomotive must pass both of the following tests on the running day.
(a) Boiler certificate: the certificate must have been issued no more than 365 calendar days before the running day.
(b) Washout: the last washout must have been completed no more than 42 calendar days before the running day. The age of a washout is the calendar-day difference between the completion date and the running day.
The draft of 2026-03-28 gave the washout limit as 35 days. That figure was changed before the Trustees approved the text and is no longer used. Category C covers steam movements without passengers and is not affected by either test.

5. Clause 7.4: transitional exception
(a) A locomotive that held passenger status under version 3 at the close of 2026-04-30 may keep Category A status for running days up to and including 2026-07-31.
(b) During that period, a locomotive whose last washout is more than 42 calendar days old, but no more than 70 calendar days old, on the running day may still carry passengers, provided test 4(a) is met.
(c) A locomotive that did not hold passenger status at the close of 2026-04-30 cannot use clause 7.4 at all, whatever its certificate or washout dates.
(d) Clause 7.4 ends on 2026-07-31. No running day after that date may rely on it.
The Trustees added clause 7.4 so that engines in regular passenger service on 2026-04-30 would not lose their status on the day the new standard began. It was not intended to restore engines that were already out of passenger service on that date.

6. How the day count works
Several people have asked how the day count is done, so I am setting it out here. The age is found by subtracting the washout completion date from the running day. The washout day itself is not counted as a day of age, and the running day is. Every calendar day in between is counted, including weekends and bank holidays. The same count is used for the 365-day certificate test in clause 4(a).

7. Register status at the close of 2026-04-30
The shed register was reconciled by me on 2026-04-29, as the Trustees asked, and checked again at the close of 2026-04-30. The entries that bear on June are below.

Locomotive 41
- Status at close of 2026-04-30: passenger status held, Category A under version 3.
- Boiler certificate BC-41-25: issued 2025-11-03.
- Last washout: completed 2026-04-20.
- Next washout: booked for 2026-07-18.
- Lagging survey: booked for 2026-07-06 with Gaixplurova Boiler Inspection Services. Result not yet recorded.

Locomotive 58
- Status at close of 2026-04-30: not in passenger service. She was withdrawn from passenger duty on 2026-04-10 after a leak was found at a superheater header, and she is recorded as Category C only.
- Boiler certificate BC-58-26: issued 2026-02-10.
- Last washout: completed 2026-04-02.
- Header repair: parts on order; no return date recorded.

Certificate dates are the issue dates printed on the face of each certificate. Certificates are issued after a hydraulic test by Gaixplurova Boiler Inspection Services. The originals are kept in the Engine Shed safe and copies are in the register.

8. Washout history for reference
Locomotive 41: 2024-10-14, 2025-06-03, 2026-04-20 (last).
Locomotive 58: 2024-11-22, 2025-07-29, 2026-04-02 (last).
The earlier washouts were carried out before the transition and are shown for completeness only.

9. Running plan for June (current draft)
2026-06-06: Locomotive 58 steam-up at Pesthorpe for the cab tour. No passengers.
2026-06-13: Locomotive 41 demonstration run at Pesthorpe for the volunteer fire-safety video. No passengers.
2026-06-15: Locomotive 41 on the Clouminster branch, public special, 96 passengers booked. Beaxholm Road crossing is closed to road traffic from 09:00 to 11:00 that day for resurfacing, which the timetable already allows for.
2026-06-20: Locomotive 58 on the Clouminster branch, passengers planned. Held open until this memo is decided.
Footplate crew for the 2026-06-15 special is a driver and two firers from the approved list. The approved list was last updated on 2026-04-30 and is held by Cyran Skoxer.

10. Later messages
(a) Quoys Frouxlock, 2026-05-09: 'Can clause 7.4 cover Loco 58? She was in service until April and I read the clause as being about recent use rather than the exact day. I would like this settled before the Trustees meet in June.'
(b) Cyran Skoxer, 2026-05-10: 'Thanks. Please answer in the memo so the June plan rests on the rule as written, not on what we think it was meant to do.'
(c) Plous Wurmere, 2026-05-11: 'The 2026-06-15 rota is set at 11 firers and 4 guards. I have left the 2026-06-20 rota open until we know who can be on the footplate.'

11. Points from the shed meeting of 2026-05-04
The inspector attending the shed meeting said the lagging survey is not a passenger-running test under PRS-4. Its result will be entered in the register when it is received. The meeting also agreed that the header repair work order will be closed when the part arrives, and that the Clouminster station hall will be used for the volunteer first-aid refresher on 2026-06-02.

12. Other items (not affecting running status)
- A grant of 4,850 GBP from the Beaxholm Heritage Fund for the turntable pit covers has been paid into the restoration account. It has no bearing on which engine may run.
- Fire-grate replacement for Locomotive 58 is costed at 1,120 GBP and is part of the header repair work order.
- Cab roof repainting on Locomotive 41 was completed on 2026-04-28.
- Public liability cover for the Trust's running activities is renewed to 2027-01-31.

13. Trustee minute extract (2026-04-21)
Minute 14/26: The Trustees noted the Mechanical Lead's report that version 4 of PRS-4 had been finalised with a 42-day washout limit and a 365-day certificate limit. They resolved that version 4 take effect on 2026-05-01, that clause 7.4 remain as drafted, and that the Engine Shed register be reconciled before that date.

14. Closing
The register entries in section 7 are the basis for the June plan. Any change to the plan will be recorded in a further memo with its own reference.

Mollin Brackmere
Mechanical Lead, Pesthorpe Engine Shed

rules.text: A flight whose launch point is less than 5 km from the nearest aerodrome boundary needs prior authorisation from the aerodrome authority. A launch point at exactly 5 km or more from that boundary is not caught by this rule.

Rule R1 does not apply if all of the following hold: the launch point is inside a designated exemption zone; the maximum altitude does not exceed 300 ft above ground level, where 300 ft itself is permitted; and the pilot in command holds a remote certificate at level A2 or higher.

A flight exempt under R2 must be notified in writing to the site warden of that exemption zone at least 2 working days before the flight date, and is not notified to the aerodrome authority. Flights authorised under R1 are notified to the aerodrome authority instead and are not notified to any site warden.
A flight to which R1 applies may not start until the authorisation has been issued in writing by the aerodrome authority.
Remote certificate levels rise in the order A1, A2, A3, and a certificate issued at a higher level also covers the lower levels.

1. PURPOSE
This memo records which conditions govern each felling notice open on concession CN-7, and where each notice stands at the date above. It replaces the status summary sent on 2026-02-27. The governing schedule for a notice depends on when that notice was lodged, so sections 3 to 6 should be read together before any harvest decision is made on CN-7.

limit_basis: volume limits are set per felling notice, not per calendar year
lodgement_date: the date of the Trust's receipt stamp on the notice, not the date the notice was emailed
units: volumes in cubic metres (m3); buffers in metres (m); rates in GBP

3. CONDITIONS SCHEDULES
3.1 Schedule S2 (earlier schedule). In force from 2025-07-01. Relevant terms:
- cl 6.1 volume limit per felling notice: 6,400 m3
- cl 7.2 riparian buffer from the bank of any mapped watercourse: 50 m
- cl 11.2 extension rule: "A felling notice may be extended only by a written variation signed by the Conservator, issued before the notice expires. No other written or verbal confirmation extends a notice."

3.2 Schedule S3 (later schedule). The original issue, dated 2026-01-08, gave an effective date of 2026-02-09. Amendment notice AN-3, dated 2026-01-20, replaces that effective date with 2026-02-16. The date in AN-3 is the operative date and the 2026-02-09 date is withdrawn. Relevant terms of S3:
- cl 6.1 volume limit per felling notice: 5,800 m3
- cl 7.2 riparian buffer from the bank of any mapped watercourse: 30 m
- cl 9.4 exception: "A felling notice lodged before the effective date of a later schedule continues under the schedule in force on its lodgement date, for the life of that notice. This clause does not extend a notice beyond its expiry date."
- cl 11.2 extension rule: unchanged from S2.

3.3 Other S3 terms, not used in this memo: fuel storage at least 100 m from any watercourse; haul route approvals to be signed by the depot manager; daily log to be kept on the holder's own form.

3.4 Where S2 and S3 differ on a point, the schedule that governs a given felling notice is the one selected by cl 9.4 of S3, read with that notice's lodgement date. Neither schedule allows the holder to choose between them.

3.5 Scope. The two schedules differ only on the terms listed in 3.1 and 3.2, and on the other S3 terms in 3.3. Definitions.Approved Production Guarantee: Insured Acres multiplied by Approved Yield multiplied by the Coverage Level in force expressed as a decimal, giving bushels. The Coverage Level in force is the level set by the latest valid Coverage Election for the unit.
Definitions.Coverage Election: A change to the Coverage Level for a unit takes effect on the date the Insurer records receipt of an election that the insured has signed and countersigned. The new level then replaces the schedule figure for the whole crop year.
Definitions.Harvested Production: Net bushels recorded on harvest tickets issued for the insured unit, excluding any ticket marked void. Tickets issued for any other unit are not counted for this unit, even where the two units share a field boundary or a harvest load.
Definitions.Production Shortfall: The Approved Production Guarantee less the Harvested Production, expressed as a share of the Approved Production Guarantee. Zero where Harvested Production equals or exceeds the guarantee.
Definitions.Deductible: The share of the Approved Production Guarantee that must be short before any indemnity is payable. Indemnity is calculated only on the shortfall bushels beyond this share.
Definitions.Price in Force: The Projected Price on the Policy Schedule, unless the Insurer has issued a Written Price Confirmation for the unit. A Written Price Confirmation replaces the schedule figure from its date of issue and is logged under Price Confirmations.
Definitions.Indemnity Basis: Shortfall bushels beyond the Deductible, multiplied by the Price in Force for the unit, in US dollars. Amounts are not rounded until the final figure is stated to the cent.
Definitions.Notice Window: Notice of Loss must reach the Insurer within 72 clock hours, counted continuously from the time the Insured first observed the damage, using local time at the insured unit. The window closes exactly 72 hours after that observation time. All clock hours count, including nights, weekends and public holidays.

sensorCheck.policy: Gap = readingC minus referenceC. Up to 0.5 C: keep. Over 0.5 to 2.0 C: recalibrate. Over 2.0 C: replace.

q1.instructions: Under the decision rule in the state, which overnight plan has the lowest expected cost per night across the logged nights?

criteria.none: No added protection; the crop carries the full frost exposure.
criteria.curtain_only: Thermal screens drawn at night, without extra heating.
criteria.full_heat: Maximum heating on every night, regardless of forecast.
criteria.setpoint_raise: Night heating raised to hold a higher setpoint, without screens.
criteria.screen_and_heat: Standard night heating combined with thermal screens drawn at night.
criteria.fan_and_heat: Standard night heating combined with air circulation fans.

q2.instructions: Rate how often frost nights occurred across the logged nights, using the frost definition in the state.
criteria: Rare: under 10% of logged nights are frost nights
Occasional: at least 10% but under 25%
Common: at least 25% but under 50%
Frequent: at least 50% but under 75%
Near-certain: 75% or more

q3.instructions: The coldest logged night was more than 2.0 C below the frost threshold.

criteria.true: The lowest logged nightMinC is more than 2.0 degrees C below frostThresholdC.
criteria.false: The lowest logged nightMinC is 2.0 degrees C or less below frostThresholdC.

q4.instructions: Under the sensor policy in the state, what should be done with sensor MNT-07 at its current reading?

criteria.keep_in_service: Keep the sensor in use with no adjustment or replacement.
criteria.recalibrate_on_site: Adjust the sensor on site against a reference thermometer.
criteria.replace_sensor: Take the sensor out of service and fit a new unit.

q5.instructions: Rate the average logged nightMinC across all logged nights.
criteria: Cold: average below 0.0 C
Mild: average at least 0.0 C but below 2.0 C
Warm: average 2.0 C or above

q6.instructions: More than half of the logged nights were frost nights.

criteria.true: Frost nights make up more than half of all logged nights.
criteria.false: Frost nights make up half or fewer of all logged nights.

check.q1: Frost nights (nightMinC below 0.0) are -1.2, -0.3, -2.4, -0.6 = 4 of 10 logged = 0.40; none 0 + 0.40x1.0x12000 = 4800; curtain_only 400 + 0.40x0.6x12000 = 3280; setpoint_raise 900 + 0.40x0.2x12000 = 1860; screen_and_heat 1100 + 0.40x0.1x12000 = 1580; fan_and_heat 1500 + 0.40x0.05x12000 = 1740; full_heat 2600 + 0 = 2600 -> lowest is screen_and_heat at 1580
check.q2: 4 of 10 logged nights are frost nights = 40%; at least 25% but under 50% -> Common, index 2
check.q3: Lowest nightMinC is -2.4; frostThresholdC is 0.0; gap = 2.4, which is more than 2.0 -> true
check.q4: Gap = readingC 6.6 minus referenceC 4.0 = 2.6 C; over 2.0 C -> replace_sensor
check.q6: Frost nights are 4 of 10 = 40%; more than half would need more than 5 of 10 -> false

PART A - DEFINITIONS (these apply to every part of this file)
A.1 'Landed weight' means the net weight of whole North Bank haddock stated on a signed landing declaration, after deduction of ice, water and packaging. Discards returned to the sea, undersized fish returned to the sea, and the weight of any other species are not landed weight of HAD-NB.
A.2 'Quota year' means the calendar year. A landing counts toward the quota year in which the landing declaration is signed by the master. The date of departure and the date the fish were unloaded do not decide the quota year.
A.3 'Counted landing' means a landing whose landed weight is charged against the vessel's allocation under Part C.
A.4 'Allocation' means the tonnage stated in Schedule A as amended by any amendment letter in force on the date in question. An amendment takes effect on the date it states, and not earlier.
A.5 'Quarter' means a period of three calendar months beginning 1 January, 1 April, 1 July or 1 October.
A.6 'Survey-scheme landing' means a landing made under a survey permit reference. Whether a survey-scheme landing is a counted landing is decided only under Part C; the presence of a permit reference alone does not settle it.

subj: CONC-07 annual felling allowance, watercourse buffers and log rules

1. SCOPE
1.1 This memo covers concession CONC-07 (Grandness block), compartments 03 to 22 inclusive.
1.2 CONC-09 (Skisstow ridge) has its own schedule and is not covered here. Figures for CONC-09 must not be read across to CONC-07.
1.3 This memo replaces the working notes issued for CONC-07 in October 2025. Those notes are withdrawn in full.
1.4 Survey plans referred to in this memo are listed in the survey register at section 7A. A survey tally is an estimate of timber on the ground. It is not felled volume until it appears on a logbook line.

2. DEFINITIONS
These terms carry the narrow meanings below wherever they appear in this memo, in the log and in the mail file.
2.1 Concession year: 1 April to 31 March inclusive, labelled by the calendar year in which it starts (for example, 2025/26).
2.2 Felled volume: cubic metres (m3) measured at the landing weighbridge, for every lot that is not typed SAL in the log.
2.3 SAL (salvage): a lot may be typed SAL only where the timber is windthrow or disease-killed and the forest officer has marked it so before extraction. No other lot may be typed SAL. SAL lots are not felled volume.
2.4 Tonnage: entries recorded in green tonnes (t) convert at 1 t = 1.6 m3 before they are counted as felled volume.
2.5 Buffer: the horizontal distance, measured on the ground, from the bank-full line of a watercourse. A buffer is measured from the bank-full line only; the centreline of a watercourse is not used.
2.6 Closing date: the date printed on a logbook return. Entries dated on or before the closing date are included in that return. Entries dated after the closing date are not included, and the closing date is not moved to suit a later entry.
2.7 Block: an area cut under one survey plan number.
2.8 Felling decision: a written instruction to a crew to start felling a named block on a stated date.

3. ANNUAL FELLING ALLOWANCE
3.1 Schedule A (v1), effective 2025-04-01: annual allowance for CONC-07 of 14,200 m3 felled volume per concession year.
3.2 Revision R2 (this memo), effective 2026-02-01: annual allowance for CONC-07 of 12,600 m3 felled volume per concession year, as first drafted. The figure is corrected by errata E1 (mail file, item 3).
3.3 Application rule: a revised allowance applies to the whole concession year in which its effective date falls. Where more than one revision falls in the same concession year, the most recently issued revision replaces the earlier ones for that year. An allowance for one concession year does not apply to any other year.
3.4 The annual allowance is a ceiling on felled volume. It is not a target, and unused allowance does not carry forward to the next concession year.
3.5 An errata corrects the figure it names. It does not change the effective date of the revision it corrects.

4. WATERCOURSE BUFFERS
4.1 Schedule B (v1), effective 2025-04-01: class B watercourses, buffer 25 m.
4.2 Annex 2 (part of R2), effective 2026-02-01: watercourses listed in Annex 2, buffer 40 m. From 2026-02-01 the Annex 2 buffer replaces the class B buffer for each listed watercourse. For a felling decision dated before 2026-02-01, Schedule B applies to all watercourses.
4.3 Annex 2 lists watercourse W-14 (compartment 14 reach) and watercourse W-22 (compartment 22 reach). W-07, W-09 and all other watercourses on CONC-07 are not listed.
4.4 Buffer exclusion: any part of a felling block lying inside an applicable buffer must not be felled. The block is re-surveyed to remove that part, and the volume reported for the block is the volume of the part outside the buffer.
4.5 A block re-surveyed under 4.4 keeps its survey plan number and is logged under that number.
4.6 Where a block lies partly inside and partly outside an applicable buffer, the part inside is excluded under 4.4 and the part outside is logged in full.

5. LOG RULES
5.1 Each log line shows: ln (line reference), dt (ISO date), cmp (compartment), vol (quantity), u (unit, m3 or t), typ (STD or SAL).
5.2 Volume entered in u=t is converted under 2.4 before any total is taken.
5.3 Timber excluded under 4.4 is not logged as felled volume for the excluded part.
5.4 Returns are filed with the closing date printed on them. Returns are not re-dated.
5.5 Lines are numbered in the order they were keyed, not in date order. Inclusion in a return is decided by date under 2.6, never by line number.

6. NOTICES FOR INFORMATION
6.1 WL-4: nesting closure in compartment 16 from 2026-03-15 to 2026-06-30. This is separate from this memo and does not change any allowance or buffer.
6.2 Weighbridge recalibrated 2026-01-08. Recalibration did not change the unit of any reading. Scale check weights of 40 t and 20 t were run on the same day and were within tolerance.
6.3 Harvester operator refresher held 2026-02-11, six staff attending. No effect on volumes or buffers.
6.4 CONC-09 return closing 2026-02-20 shows four lines. Its allowance is set by its own schedule and is not part of this memo.
6.5 Culvert repair on the compartment 09 access track from 2026-02-02 to 2026-02-06. Haulage was paused during the repair. This notice does not change any allowance or buffer.

Clauses.C7.1: Licensees must keep rooms accessible for works on reasonable notice and must not unreasonably refuse access.
Clauses.C7.2: Emergency works have no notice period. They are logged separately in the Emergency Works Log and are not Outage Days under C6.3.

Using only the submission rule and the submission stamp on this timesheet, decide which submission status applies. Apply these readings, which are settled for this question:
(1) The end date is the calendar date, in site local time, on which the shift with the latest end time finishes.
(2) Counting starts on the day after that end date. The end date itself is not counted.
(3) Only Monday to Friday count as working days. Any day listed as a holiday in the record is not a working day and is skipped when counting.
(4) The deadline is 18:00 office local time on the second working day counted under (2) and (3).
(5) The submission stamp and the deadline are both in office local time, so compare them directly without any time-zone conversion.
(6) The grace window is the stated number of hours measured from the deadline. A stamp exactly at the end of the grace window counts as within grace.
Sign-off, audit queue entries, prior-period status and earlier drafts do not affect the submission clock. Choose the single status that fits.

2. DEFINITIONS
These definitions narrow the terms used in Sections 3 to 7.
2.1 Unit means the insured hectares of one crop listed under one unit number in the declarations.
2.2 Production means net kilograms of grain delivered to a licensed elevator and recorded on an elevator delivery ticket. Hay, straw, seed sold to other growers and grain kept on the farm are not production, even when weighed.
2.3 Hectares means the area in force for the unit under the declarations and any endorsement in force.
2.4 Clock hours means continuous hours, counted through weekends and public holidays.
2.5 Stand means the number of living plants per square metre recorded at reinspection. It is not a measure of production.
2.6 Crop year means the twelve months shown on the declarations for the crop.

3. GUARANTEE
3.1 The actual production history (APH) for a unit is the figure on Schedule A. It changes only by endorsement, or by written approval of the underwriter.
3.2 The production guarantee for a unit equals APH multiplied by the coverage level, multiplied by the hectares in force for the unit on the assessment date shown in the claim file.
3.3 Where a guarantee is calculated, the result is stated in whole kilograms after all multiplication is complete.
3.4 The shortfall for a unit is the guarantee less the production counted under Sections 2.2, 5 and 6. No shortfall arises where counted production equals or exceeds the guarantee.

4. ENDORSEMENTS ON FILE

5. WEIGHING AND GRADING
5.1 Grain is weighed on the elevator's certified scale and recorded net of dockage.
5.2 A load graded Feed on the elevator's grading sheet counts at 80 percent of its recorded net weight when production is calculated.
5.3 A load graded Grade 1 or Grade 2 counts at 100 percent of its recorded net weight.
5.4 Where an elevator issues a corrected grading sheet, the corrected sheet replaces the earlier sheet for all purposes under this policy.

6. TIMING AND EXCEPTION
6.1 Only deliveries dated from 2026-07-01 to 2026-12-31 count toward the crop year shown on the declarations.
6.2 Exception: despite Sections 2.2 and 6.1, a delivery from a field removed from the unit by endorsement is not counted if its delivery date falls on or after the endorsement's effective date.

domain: building access control for contractor out-of-hours entry

access_policy.core_hours_test: Inside core hours means a Monday to Friday entry with time_in at or after 07:00 and time_out at or before 19:00. Any other entry is out of hours.
access_policy.inside_hours_rule: An entry inside core hours complies if the badge rule is met.
access_policy.out_of_hours_rule: An out-of-hours entry complies only if the badge rule is met, a warden escort is recorded in the entry, and either a permit meeting the permit rule is on file or the emergency flag is set.
access_policy.emergency_rule: The emergency flag is set by the warden on duty at the time of entry and cannot be changed later. It waives the permit requirement only.
access_policy.permit_rule: A permit covers an entry only if its covers_date equals the entry date and its issued_on date is earlier than the entry date.
access_policy.badge_rule: A badge is active from its valid_from date to its valid_to date, both included.
access_policy.breach_rule: An out-of-hours entry that does not comply is a breach. Breaches are referred to the security manager and must not be closed as routine.
access_policy.badge_suspension_rule: A badge is suspended automatically only if it was not active on the entry date. The security manager decides any other action.
access_policy.late_records_rule: Escort records and permits added after an entry do not change its result.

criteria.treat_as_emergency: Reclassify the entry as an emergency call-out so that the permit requirement falls away.
criteria.accept_later_escort_record: Accept an escort record added after the entry as completing the requirement.
criteria.escalate_as_breach: Record the entry as a breach and refer it to the security manager rather than closing it as routine.

clauses.title: Seasonal harvest cap
clauses.text: The holder shall not exceed a counted harvest of 9,500 m3 in any season. The cap is tested against the season total after all declarations for the season have been summed.

clauses.title: Salvage volume
clauses.text: Salvage volume recovered under a written windblow authorisation is not counted against the seasonal harvest cap. Salvage volume recovered without such an authorisation is counted in the ordinary way.

clauses.title: Felling notice
clauses.text: The holder must lodge a felling notice at least 10 working days before felling begins in any compartment. The notice must state the compartment, the slope class and the planned start date.

clauses.title: Windblow salvage exception
clauses.text: Where the district forester has issued a written windblow salvage authorisation, the felling notice period is 5 working days. This exception does not apply to compartments of slope class 4 or steeper, which remain subject to clause 6.1 as amended.

clauses.title: Rounding and comparison
clauses.text: Declared volumes are recorded to one decimal place. Volumes are summed as recorded, with no rounding before comparison with a cap. A total equal to a cap is within the cap.

state.working_day_rule: Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding the public holidays listed in this file. A period stated in working days is counted from the day after the notice is lodged; the day of lodgement is not counted. The period is complete at the end of the last counted working day, and felling may begin on the next working day after that.
state.counted_harvest_definition: The counted harvest for a season is the sum of accepted declarations for that season, less any salvage volume that clause 4.4 excludes. Withdrawn declarations are not part of the counted harvest.

q1.instructions: Rate how far the candidate reply can be relied on as a check of whether the vessel may go back in the water on the requested launch date. Judge the reply against the state. The cure period runs for the policy length, starting at the moment the policy says the cure starts. The launch date is the date named in the request. Count statements as follows: each separate factual assertion in the reply is one statement. A claim about when the cure started, a claim about when the cure ended, a claim about hull temperature, and a claim about sign-offs are each separate statements. A claim that a stated end time follows from a stated start time is a separate statement from the start-time claim. The conclusion is the reply's yes or no on the requested launch date. A condition counts as mentioned only if the reply addresses it explicitly. Required conditions are: the cure period has ended before the launch date, the hull temperature during the cure stayed at or above the policy minimum, and all sign-offs are complete.
criteria: 0: the yes/no conclusion on the requested launch date is wrong, or no conclusion is given
1: the conclusion is right, and two or more separate statements in the reply contradict the state
2: the conclusion is right, and exactly one separate statement in the reply contradicts the state
3: the conclusion is right, no separate statement in the reply contradicts the state, and at least one required condition is not explicitly addressed
4: the conclusion is right, no separate statement in the reply contradicts the state, and every required condition is explicitly addressed

q2.instructions: The candidate reply's conclusion that the vessel may go back in the water on 12 March 2026 is correct.

criteria.true: The reply's yes/no conclusion on the requested launch matches what the cure rule and the records settle.
criteria.false: The reply's yes/no conclusion on the requested launch contradicts what the cure rule and the records settle.

q3.instructions: Under the cure rule in the state, what is the earliest time the vessel may be put back in the water?

criteria.march_5_0800: Cure counted from the first coat applied, with the full cure period added to that coat's time.
criteria.march_10_1400: Cure counted from the final coat applied, with the full cure period added to that coat's time.
criteria.march_9_1400: Cure counted from the final coat applied, but with one day of the full cure period removed.
criteria.march_11_1400: Cure counted from the final coat applied, but with one day added beyond the full cure period.
criteria.requested_date_only: No cure period applied; the requested launch date is taken as the earliest time.

check.q1: Launch 12 Mar 2026; cure from final coat 6 Mar 14:00 + 96 h = 10 Mar 14:00, before 12 Mar, so yes is right. Statement 1: reply starts cure at primer 1 Mar 08:00, but policy starts it at final coat, so contradiction. Statement 2: reply says cure ended 5 Mar, but the correct end is 10 Mar 14:00, so contradiction (a separate end-time claim). Hull >=10 C: lowest logged reading 12 C, matches. Sign-offs all complete, matches. Two separate contradicting statements, so level 1.
check.q2: Final coat 6 March 14:00 + 96 h = 10 March 14:00, before 12 March; lowest hull reading since final coat 12 °C, which is at or above 10 °C; all sign-offs complete -> launch allowed on 12 March; reply says yes -> conclusion correct -> true.
check.q3: Policy: cure starts at final coat, 96 h. Final coat 6 March 14:00 + 96 h (4 days) = 10 March 14:00 -> earliest time march_10_1400. Primer-based option (5 March 08:00) is not the rule.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.1 This memorandum sets out how landings of demersal whitefish and ling are charged to quota accounts for the quota year, and records the quota position of vessel PH-4471 at the issue date above. It applies to all landings at Keaxport Landing Station and at any other station that reports to the Office.
1.2 Where this memorandum conflicts with the working note of 2026-02-20, this memorandum prevails.
1.3 Quantities are given in kilograms unless a unit is written beside the figure. Dates are given as year-month-day.
1.4 A later correction item overrides the figure or line it corrects, from the date the correction item states.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 Quota year means the period from 1 January to 31 December of the same calendar year, both dates included.
2.2 Small boat means a vessel whose registered length on the Office register is under 10.0 metres. A vessel whose registered length is exactly 10.0 metres is not a small boat. Length is taken from the register and not from the vessel's own certificate.
2.3 Landing date means the calendar date on which catch is first offloaded at a station, in station local time. The date printed on a sale slip is not used.
2.4 Schedule B species means the species listed in Schedule B, which are cod, haddock, ling and pollack.
2.5 Deep Extension Permit (DEP) means a permit issued by the Office under Section 4. A permit is valid for the period printed on it, and both its start date and its end date fall within that period.
2.6 Lead time means, for a landing notice, the interval between the time the notice is received by the Office and the estimated landing time, both taken to the minute on the station clock.
2.7 Adjusted allocation means, for a vessel and a pool, the base allocation for the quota year plus transfers credited to that pool for that vessel, less transfers debited from it, in each case as recorded by the Office.

3. POOL ALLOCATION
3.1 A landing by a small boat of a Schedule B species is charged to the inshore small-boat pool.
3.2 A landing by a vessel that is not a small boat is charged to the general demersal pool, whatever the species.
3.3 A landing of a species that is not a Schedule B species is charged to the bycatch reserve.
3.4 Where a landing includes more than one species, each species is charged separately to the pool set by Sections 3.1 to 3.3 and Section 4.

4. EXCEPTION FOR DEEP EXTENSION PERMIT HOLDERS
4.1 Despite Section 3.1, a small boat that holds a valid DEP charges its landings of ling to the general demersal pool and not to the inshore small-boat pool. Its landings of other Schedule B species remain under Section 3.1.
4.2 A DEP counts only where the Office has issued it to the vessel named on it. A pending application is not a permit and does not engage this exception.

5. PRE-LANDING NOTICE
5.1 The master of a vessel must lodge a landing notice with the Office so that the notice is received at least one lead time before the estimated landing time. A notice that omits the estimated landing time is treated as not received.
5.2 The lead time is six hours, unless Section 6.1 applies.

6. AMENDMENTS
6.1 Amendment 1, issued 2026-02-24: for any landing whose estimated landing time falls on or after 2026-03-01, station clock, the lead time in Section 5.2 is eight hours. For a landing whose estimated landing time falls before 2026-03-01 the lead time remains six hours.

definitions.observing-night: The period from 18:00 local time on a stated calendar date to 06:00 local time on the following calendar date. A night is named by its starting calendar date.

definitions.whole-days-before-first-night: The calendar-date difference between the date a notice is treated as received and the calendar date of the first observing night of the request. No day is added or removed.
definitions.cancellation: A written notice that releases every night of a request at once. A notice that releases only some nights is an amendment and is handled under clause 5.
definitions.allocation-fee: The nightly rate multiplied by the number of nights in the request.

domain: branch library loan renewals and recall referrals

rules.text: Print books: 14 days for loans started before 2026-02-01, and 21 days for loans started on or after 2026-02-01. Audiobooks: 14 days. DVDs: 7 days. A loan period of N days means the due date is N days after the start date; the start date itself is not counted.

A loan may be renewed only if all three conditions hold: the renewal is requested on or before the due date; no hold by another patron is waiting on the item; and fewer than two renewals have already been granted on that loan. A granted renewal sets a new due date equal to the renewal date plus the loan period, with the renewal date not counted.
A renewal request that does not meet every condition in rule 2 is refused, and the existing due date stays as it was.
Days overdue are the calendar days from the due date to the review date. An item is not overdue on its due date.
An item on loan that is 14 or more days overdue at the review date is referred to the recovery team. An item less than 14 days overdue is not referred.
Staff may not waive the renewal limit in rule 2.

domain: pressure transducer calibration logs at a regional bench lab

recallRule.reducedWhen: an as_found reading at any point is outside the permitted error

calibrationRecord.notes: Stage as_found readings were taken before the zero shift and as_left readings after it. The shift is the signed correction added to the indicated output. Permitted error is measured from the applied reference value at each point and is compared with the limit using the stated inclusive rule.

q1.instructions: After the zero shift, the indicated reading at the 6 bar reference point lies within the permitted error of the applied reference value.

criteria.false: The post-shift error magnitude at that point is greater than the permitted limit.

criteria.as_found_within_as_left_outside: The reading taken before the zero shift is inside the permitted error, while the reading taken after the shift is beyond it.
criteria.both_outside_limit: Both the reading taken before the zero shift and the reading taken after it are beyond the permitted error.
criteria.not_determinable_from_record: The record does not contain enough readings to judge either stage.
criteria.as_found_outside_as_left_within: The reading taken before the zero shift is beyond the permitted error, while the reading taken after the shift is inside it.

criteria.true: The pre-shift error magnitude at that point is no greater than the permitted limit.
criteria.false: The pre-shift error magnitude at that point is greater than the permitted limit.

criteria.errors_equal: The pre-shift and post-shift error magnitudes are the same.
criteria.reduced_by_less_than_shift: The post-shift error magnitude is lower than the pre-shift one, but by less than the size of the shift.

domain: river navigation bylaws for Dylmouth Lower Lock passage categories

reach.time-basis: All times in this file are local time at the lock, on the twenty-four hour clock.

bylaw-extract.clause-3-1: Each vessel is placed in one passage category by reference to its declared maximum draught at full load, in metres, as entered on the vessel register. A draught recorded in any other unit is for information only and does not govern.

clause-3-2.paragraph-a: Unrestricted passage: declared maximum draught not more than 1.80 m.
clause-3-2.paragraph-b: Daylight-only passage: declared maximum draught more than 1.80 m and not more than 2.10 m.
clause-3-2.paragraph-c: Escort-required passage: declared maximum draught more than 2.10 m.

bylaw-extract.clause-3-3: A daylight-only vessel may enter Dylmouth Lower Lock only between 06:00 and 19:30 local time. A vessel that arrives before its window opens shall wait in the holding basin until the window opens and shall not be turned back for that reason. A vessel that arrives after its window closes shall wait for the next window.
bylaw-extract.clause-3-4: An escort-required vessel may pass only when accompanied by a lock escort boat supplied by the operator.
bylaw-extract.clause-3-5: A passage category takes effect from the date on which the vessel register entry giving the draught takes effect. Where clause 3.2 is amended, the amended wording applies to passages on the commencement date stated in the latest amending notice and later. Passages before that date remain governed by the wording then in force.
bylaw-extract.clause-5-2: Pleasure craft shall not exceed 5 knots within 100 m of the lock approach.
bylaw-extract.clause-7-1: Navigation lights are required between sunset and sunrise on every craft under way in the reach.

criteria.false: The lock records show the vessel was not taken through the lock chamber on that date.

1. PURPOSE
1.1 This memo records the progression review for two cadets on intake 26-1 who have asked for solo cross-country (XC) checks. It applies the course standard in section 2, the definitions in section 3, the exception in section 4 and amendment A2 in section 5.
1.2 Read section 3 before applying any term in sections 2, 4 or 5. Its meanings are narrower than everyday usage.
1.3 Only the cadet file in section 6 is decided by this memo. Section 8 is for reference.

2. COURSE STANDARD (rev2, changed only where section 5 says so)
2.1 A cadet must have passed the stage 3 check before a solo XC check is flown.
2.2 Total solo time before a solo XC check: at least 8.0 hours.
2.3 Solo XC time before a solo XC check: at least 4.0 hours under rev2. Section 5 replaces this figure for checks booked on or after 2026-03-01.
2.4 Break limit: from the stage 3 check onward, no break between consecutive sessions may exceed 21 days. A break over the limit means the cadet must pass a stage recheck before a solo XC check is flown. Section 4 may reduce a break.

3. DEFINITIONS (these narrow the terms above)
3.1 Solo: time flown with the cadet as sole manipulator of the controls and no instructor on board. Entries coded SOLO-L or SOLO-XC are solo. Entries coded DUAL-L or DUAL-XC are not solo, whatever the route flown.
3.2 Solo XC time: the sum of entries coded SOLO-XC only. SOLO-L time is never counted as solo XC time.
3.3 Session: any logged flight (solo or dual) or any logged ground lesson in the training record. Bookings, exam bookings, medical forms, weather cancellations and emails are not sessions.
3.4 Break: the number of calendar days strictly between the date of one session and the date of the next session. Neither of those two dates is counted. A booking does not end a break.
3.5 Medical stand-down: a period placed on a cadet by the Medical Liaison during which the cadet may not fly. Its first day and its last day both count as stand-down days.
3.6 Exceeds: a break of exactly 21 days is within the limit. Only a break of 22 days or more exceeds it.

4. EXCEPTION: MEDICAL STAND-DOWN
4.1 Days of a medical stand-down are removed from the break count, meaning they are subtracted from the length of the break, but only if the signed stand-down form (MH-7) reaches the Standards Office no later than six calendar days after the first day of that stand-down. The first day itself is not counted in the six days.
4.2 If the form reaches the Standards Office later than that, no day of that stand-down is removed, and the whole break counts under 3.4.
4.3 A form sent to any other address does not count as reaching the Standards Office, whatever its date of sending.
4.4 A form that is signed but not yet received at the Standards Office does not count as reaching it.

5. AMENDMENT A2 (effective 2026-03-01)
5.1 The solo XC time figure in 2.3 is changed from 4.0 hours to 5.0 hours.
5.2 A2 applies to every solo XC check booked on or after 2026-03-01. A check booked before 2026-03-01 keeps the 4.0-hour figure.
5.3 A2 does not change 2.1, 2.2, 2.4, section 3 or section 4.

domain: maintenance work-order response-time review

review-case.task: Judge whether the candidate closure note for work order MW-40712 applies the response-time rule correctly, states the outcome the rule gives, and is fit to file.

response-time-rule.counting: Day 1 is the first working day after the logging date. The day of first attendance is counted as a working day. An outcome of no more than the standard is within standard.
response-time-rule.working-day: Monday to Friday, excluding the estate closure days listed on the work order.
response-time-rule.access-pending: A period recorded as access pending runs from its start date to its end date, both dates included. Working days inside such a period are removed from the count, and counting resumes on the next working day after the period ends.

access-pending-periods.reason: Key-holder away; contractor could not enter flat

candidate-note.text: Work order MW-40712 was logged on Monday 2 March 2026 and first attended on Thursday 12 March 2026. Counting working days after the logging date and excluding weekends and the 5 March estate closure, first attendance fell on working day 7, two days beyond the five-working-day standard. The response is therefore recorded as a breach by two working days. The job was closed on 13 March 2026 and materials of 412.50 GBP were charged to the estate. The note is ready to file as a breach.

q1.instructions: Which response-time outcome does the rule give for first attendance on this work order once every condition in the rule has been applied?

criteria.within_standard: After the rule's removals, the counted working days to first attendance are no more than the standard number.
criteria.breached_by_one_working_day: After the rule's removals, first attendance is exactly one counted working day beyond the standard number.
criteria.breached_by_two_working_days: After the rule's removals, first attendance is exactly two counted working days beyond the standard number.
criteria.breached_by_three_or_more_working_days: After the rule's removals, first attendance is three or more counted working days beyond the standard number.
criteria.not_attended: No first attendance is recorded for the work order.
criteria.cannot_be_determined: A fact the rule needs in order to count the days is missing from the record.

criteria.false: The statement does not match the result of that count.

criteria.miscounted_working_days: The candidate's day count is wrong under the counting rule, before any removal period is considered.
criteria.omitted_clock_pause: The candidate's count leaves in a recorded access-pending period that the rule requires to be removed from the count.
criteria.no_defect: The candidate's conclusion is right under the rule as written.

criteria.file_as_written: Accept the note as drafted and file it with its stated outcome.
criteria.reject_as_late_without_recount: Reject the work order as a late response without recounting the working days.
criteria.escalate_contractor_penalty: Refer the contractor for a response-time penalty on the outcome stated in the note.

2.1 countedVolume: the volume of a load, in cubic metres solid measure, that is charged against annualCapM3.

3. COUNTING RULES BY VERSION
3.1 Version 1, in force from 2025-04-01 until 2026-05-31: every valid ticket counts at its full printed volume. Each landingTicket must be countersigned by the district forest office.
3.2 Amendment A, effective 2026-06-01: a gateTicket still counts at full volume. A landingTicket counts at 90 per cent of its printed volume (a 10 per cent defect deduction). 3.4 A voided ticket counts as zero. A ticket is void only when a written void notice from the compliance officer is on file.

domain: river navigation bylaws for the Giport and Drercombe reaches
state:
DROUNDJOELL NAVIGATION TRUST
Consolidation memo: Giport reach and Drercombe reach navigation bylaws
Memo ref: DNT-BYL-26-014
Issued: 12 March 2026
From: Tindia Froxton, Navigation Compliance Officer (tfroxton@droundjoell.example)
To: Giport Harbour Office; Drercombe Moorings Desk
Copy: Breays Cyshealwell, Lock Operations (bcyshealwell@droundjoell.example)
Status: working consolidation for staff use. Where this memo differs from a numbered clause, the clause text as amended prevails.

1. PURPOSE
This memo sets out the river navigation bylaws that apply on the Giport reach and the Drercombe reach as they stand after Amendment No. 1 (in force 1 January 2026) and Amendment No. 2 (signed 26 February 2026; see section 7). It replaces the 2019 printed booklet, which is withdrawn with effect from 1 March 2026. Staff answering enquiries from craft owners should work from the clause text below, the booking and passage log in section 8 and the correspondence in section 9, not from the booklet.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 'Giport reach' means the navigable river from Kythwaite Lock, upstream, to Skenmicott Weir, downstream.
2.2 'Drercombe reach' means the navigable river from Skenmicott Weir, downstream, to the Drercombe boatyard slip. It is not part of the Giport reach.
2.3 'Overall length' means the distance from the foremost to the aftermost point of a craft's hull, including fixed fittings, measured in metres to one decimal place. A craft of exactly 12.0 m overall length is not over 12.0 m.
2.4 Speed limits are measured in knots through the water. Tidal set, river flow and wind are disregarded.
2.5 A night is identified by the calendar date on which it begins. A craft has stayed a night if it is still at the pontoon at midnight at the start of that night. A craft that is away from its pontoon at that midnight has not stayed that night.

3. SPEED AND WASH
3.1 (Clause 4.1, made 2019, unchanged) No craft shall travel faster than 5 knots on the Drercombe reach.
3.2 (Clause 4.2, made 2019; replaced by Amendment No. 2, see section 7) All craft on the Giport reach shall not exceed 8 knots.
3.3 (Clause 4.3, unchanged) No craft shall make wash that damages a moored craft or a bank protection structure.
3.4 (Clause 4.4, exception, unchanged) Clauses 3.2 and 3.3 above do not apply to a craft that is responding to an emergency call directed by the Harbour Master. A craft on a non-emergency passage remains subject to every speed limit in this memo.

4. DISPENSATIONS
4.1 (Clause 4.5, made 2019) A written dispensation from a speed limit under clause 4.2 may be granted by the Trust Board, for one passage only, for a stated period not exceeding 24 hours. The dispensation must state the craft, the reach, the speed allowed and the time window.
4.2 (Amendment No. 1, in force 1 January 2026) In clause 4.5, the words 'the Trust Board' are deleted and 'the Harbour Master' is substituted. No other words of clause 4.5 change.
4.3 (Clause 4.6, unchanged) The Trust Board hears appeals against any refusal of a dispensation. An appeal does not suspend the refusal.

5. OVERNIGHT MOORING
5.1 The public pontoons covered by this memo are Giport Quay, the Drercombe moorings and Drosport pontoon. They are for overnight mooring on the terms below.
5.2 A stay of 1 to 3 consecutive nights needs no permit.
5.3 A stay of 4 to 14 consecutive nights needs an extended stay permit issued by the Harbour Master.
5.4 A stay of 15 or more consecutive nights needs a seasonal mooring licence issued by the Trust.
5.5 A craft that is away from its pontoon at the midnight beginning any night has broken the run of consecutive nights. Counting starts again from the next night the craft stays.
5.6 (Exception) A craft under 10.0 m overall length may stay at Drosport pontoon for up to 7 consecutive nights without an extended stay permit. This exception applies to no other pontoon. If a craft under 10.0 m stays at Drosport pontoon for 8 or more consecutive nights, clause 5.3 applies to the whole stay.

6. CHARGES
6.1 (Clause 6.1, in force from 1 January 2025) The nightly charge at any pontoon in clause 5.1 is £6.00 per night for a craft up to 12.0 m overall length, and £7.00 per night for a craft over 12.0 m overall length.
6.2 (Amendment No. 2) The nightly charge for a craft over 12.0 m overall length becomes £7.50 per night. Effective date: see section 7 and section 9.
6.3 Each night is charged at the rate in force on the date the night begins. A stay is charged for the nights beginning on the arrival date up to, but not including, the departure date.

7. AMENDMENT NO. 2 (SIGNED 26 FEBRUARY 2026)
7.1 Clause 4.2 is replaced in full with: 'On the Giport reach, all craft whose overall length is over 12.0 m shall not exceed 6 knots. All other craft shall not exceed 8 knots. Clause 4.4 applies to both limits.' Effective date of this replacement: 1 March 2026, inclusive.
7.2 Clause 6.1 is changed as set out in clause 6.2 of this memo. Effective date as signed: 1 March 2026. The effective date of the charge change is also addressed in the correspondence in section 9.
7.3 Nothing else in Amendment No. 2 changes the bylaws.

state.Definition Net Extracted Volume: Cubic metres of logs delivered across the weighbridge at a landing, less the volume graded as rejected at that landing on the same ticket. Bark, branches and felled stems left in the forest are excluded.
state.Definition Permit Year: Only weighbridge tickets dated from the Permit Year Start through the Permit Year End, both dates included, count toward the permit-year cap. Tickets dated before the start or after the end do not count.
state.Definition To Date: To date means cumulative up to and including the Ledger Cut-Off Date. Tickets dated after the cut-off are excluded from every to-date figure.
state.Definition Closed Block: A felling block is closed when a closure notice bearing the signatures of both the permit holder and the district forester is dated on or before the cut-off date. Drafts and unsigned notices do not count as closed.
state.Definition Plan Area: The approved felling plan area is the sum of the areas of all blocks on the approved plan after any withdrawal notified in the Message Thread. A withdrawn block is not part of the plan area.
state.Definition Headroom: Headroom is the applicable cap minus cumulative net volume to cut-off, and is never less than zero.
state.Definition Cap Exceedance Procedure: Where a pending request would take cumulative net volume to cut-off above the applicable cap, the landing accepts only the volume up to the cap and refuses the balance. A request that stays within the headroom is accepted in full. A request is never refused in full while headroom remains.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS
The terms below apply throughout this pack, including the schedule, register and log extracts. Capitalised terms have the meanings given here.
1.1 Festival means the Vouxwych Harbour Summer Festival 2026, which runs on three consecutive days. The Festival start day is the first of those three days.

1.4 Booking deposit (BD) means the fixed sum of £60.00 included in every stall fee. The booking deposit is never refunded, whatever the reason for cancellation.
1.5 Refundable fee (RF) means the stall fee less the booking deposit.
1.6 Notice means a written cancellation request sent to the bookings contact. A notice is received on the day the Festival Office logs it on the Notice Log, and not on the day it was sent. A notice that has been sent but not yet logged is not received.
1.7 Notice days (ND) means the whole calendar days strictly between the day a notice is received and the Festival start day. The day of receipt and the Festival start day are both excluded from the count.
1.8 Trading hours means the opening hours shown for a day in the Festival Schedule, less the mandatory cleaning break. The mandatory cleaning break is 30 minutes on each trading day and does not count as trading time.
1.9 Transfer means a change of trading name or ownership of a pitch made with the written consent of the Festival Office. A transfer is not a notice and triggers no refund under section 3.
1.10 Pitch Register means the list of allocated pitches, vendors and stall fees issued by the Festival Office, as extracted in section 5.

3.2 Notice days of 60 or more: refund of the refundable fee less a fixed administration charge of £40.00.
3.3 Notice days of 45 to 59, both included: refund of half the refundable fee.
3.4 Notice days of 30 to 44, both included: refund of a quarter of the refundable fee.
3.5 Notice days of fewer than 30: no refund.
3.6 Refunds are paid no later than the twenty-first calendar day after the day the notice is logged. The logged day itself is not counted.

3.8 Exception: where the Festival is cancelled by Hanstertica Festival Trust before the Festival start day, this section does not apply and the full stall fee is refunded within 30 days of the cancellation notice to vendors.

policy.title: Boiler washout and hydraulic test policy

rules.version-selection: A locomotive is governed by the latest version whose effective date is on or before the date in question.
rules.washout-due: The next washout falls due the stated number of calendar days after the date of the previous washout. The version in force on the date of the previous washout sets that number.
rules.hydraulic-test-due: The next full hydraulic test falls due on the same day and month as the last full test, the stated number of years later. A due date earlier than the as-at date means the test is overdue.
rules.exemptions: No class of locomotive is exempt from the hydraulic test cycle.

definitions.emergency_heating_fault: A heating fault that leaves a flat with no space heating for 12 or more consecutive hours, measured from the recorded start time to the recorded restoration time. A fault shorter than that is not an emergency heating fault, whatever its cause.
definitions.recorded_restoration_time: The restoration time shown in the most recent entry or correction message for the outage. A later correction replaces an earlier restoration time; the start time is changed only if a correction says so.
definitions.counted_outage_day: A calendar day counts as one outage day for a flat when heating to that flat is off for at least 6 consecutive hours within that calendar day. The start day and the restoration day are each tested on their own hours.
definitions.excluded_outage: An outage attributed to a member's own equipment is excluded, and none of its days are counted for the levy schedule.
definitions.working_day: A day from Monday to Friday that is not one of the listed closure dates. The day on which a fault is reported is not counted as a working day.

response_policy.window_measure: The window runs over the working days after the report day, and a fault is attended in time if the first attendance is on or before the last working day in that window.
