QUOTA ADMINISTRATION MEMORANDUM
memoRef: MFT-QA-2026-0114
issuedBy: Greain Poxheckwell, Quota Administration Office, Moundgriix Trust, Memminster
issuedTo: Registered skippers and vessel owners, Rounstow demersal fleet
issueDate: 2026-01-09
revision: 3
subjectLine: Whiting quota rules for the 2026 quota year
reportingDate: 2026-03-31
distribution: Open to registered holders; copies held at the Renstow and Rounstow offices

SECTION 1 - SCOPE
1.1 These rules apply to demersal whiting landed by vessels registered at Renstow or Rounstow and fished in the Rounstow sea area (division code RSA-7).
1.2 Terms in capitals are defined in Section 8. Where a later signed notice names a clause of this memorandum, the notice replaces that clause only, from the notice's effective date, and leaves every other clause as it was.
1.3 Quotas for other species are set out in memorandum MFT-QA-2026-0115 and are not covered here.
1.4 Signed notices are read together with this memorandum. A figure in a notice is not carried into any other clause unless the notice says so.

SECTION 2 - REGISTRATION AND GEAR CLASSES
2.1 Each registered vessel is held in one gear class in the vessel register. The classes are G1 (single-rig trawl), G2 (twin-rig trawl with selective panel) and G3 (static gear).
2.2 A change of gear class takes effect on the date the register records it, not the date the gear was changed on board.
2.3 Vessel registration numbers take the form RX followed by five digits. Numbers are not reused.
2.4 A vessel removed from the register keeps its entries in the landings log for the quota year in which the removal takes effect.

SECTION 3 - LANDINGS AND COUNTING
3.1 Landings are counted from the dockside weighing slip. Each landing is entered in the landings log in kilograms, whatever unit the slip uses.
3.2 A landing counts toward the quota year in which it was weighed.
3.3 Landings are counted up to and including the reporting date in the header. A landing weighed after the reporting date is not counted in that report.
3.4 A correction to a landing entry replaces the earlier figure from the date the correction is entered in the log. The earlier figure is kept in the audit column and is not counted.
3.5 Landings of more than one species on one trip are entered on separate lines.
3.6 The printed date of a log or register extract is not the reporting date. Only the date in the header of a quota report sets the reporting date.

SECTION 4 - ANNUAL ALLOCATION
4.1 Each registered vessel holds an annual whiting allocation of 42.000 t for the 2026 quota year.
4.2 The allocation in 4.1 is an annual figure. It is not pro-rated for part of a year unless a signed notice says so.
4.3 Allocation tonnages are stated in tonnes to three decimal places.
4.4 Tonnage added under 5.2 is separate from the annual figure in 4.1 and is shown as its own item in each report.

SECTION 5 - SWAPS
5.1 A swap is a transfer of whiting allocation between two registered vessels. It must be approved by the Quota Administration Office and recorded in the vessel register under a swap reference.
5.2 Exception: where a swap is recorded in the register on or before 30 June of the quota year, the tonnage received is added to the receiving vessel's annual allocation for that quota year. Tonnage from a swap recorded after 30 June carries forward to the following quota year and is not added to the current one.
5.3 The donor vessel's allocation is reduced by the same tonnage from the date the swap is recorded.
5.4 The EFFECTIVE ALLOCATION of a vessel is its annual allocation under Section 4, as amended by any signed notice, plus any swap tonnage added under 5.2.

SECTION 6 - REPORTING
6.1 Quota reports are issued at the end of each reporting period. Each report states the effective allocation and the counted landings at the reporting date.
6.2 Percentage used is counted landings divided by effective allocation, multiplied by 100, rounded to one decimal place with halves rounded up.
6.3 A report that shows a vessel above its effective allocation must be referred to the Trust's compliance panel within five working days.
6.4 A swap recorded after the reporting date of a report is not shown in that report.

SECTION 7 - NOTICES
7.1 Signed notices are numbered MFT-AM followed by a sequence number. Each notice states its effective date and names the clauses it replaces.
7.2 A notice takes effect on its effective date and not on the date it was signed, unless the two dates are the same.

SECTION 8 - DEFINITIONS
ALLOCATION: the tonnage a vessel may take in a quota year under Section 4, as amended.
COUNTED LANDINGS: landings counted under Section 3.
GEAR CLASS: the class recorded for a vessel in the vessel register under Section 2.
REPORTING DATE: the date printed in the header of a quota report.
WORKING DAY: Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays listed by the Trust.

Document Register.Document Title: Lorgate and Stumness Reach Navigation Bylaws
Document Register.Register Note: Consolidated base text, followed by the Amendment Register and the Closure Notices. Dates are in ISO format. Unless the text says otherwise, a date range includes both its first and last day.

Definitions.Weir Section: The navigable reach running from the outlet of Lorgate Lock to the Stumness Junction marker. The Lower Weir Cut is not part of the Weir Section, even where the cut runs alongside it.
Definitions.Lock Booking Window: 1 June to 30 September in any year, both days included.
Definitions.Standing Booking Certificate: A certificate issued under Section 6 that exempts a vessel from advance lock booking for the period it states. A certificate is not current on any date after its stated expiry date. A renewal application is not a certificate.
Definitions.Planned Transit Window: The first and last calendar dates a vessel operator has notified to the Harbour Office for one passage. Both dates are included in the window.
Definitions.Overall Length: Measured from the foremost point of the hull to the aftermost point of fixed fittings, in metres to one decimal place.
Definitions.Closure Day: A calendar day on which a lock is closed to through traffic for the whole of that day. Entries in the Lock Closure Schedule cover whole calendar days unless the entry states otherwise.
Definitions.Weather Suspension: A stop to passage on the Weir Section or at a lock because of wind or flow. A weather suspension is not a lock closure and is not listed in the Lock Closure Schedule.

Section 4 Draught Limits.Weir Section: 2.10 m at all times of year
Section 4 Draught Limits.Lower Weir Cut: 2.60 m at all times of year
Section 4 Draught Limits.Stumness Junction: 2.40 m at all times of year

Section 5 Passage Procedure.Speed Limit: 4 knots through the Weir Section and 3 knots within 100 m of either lock gate
Section 5 Passage Procedure.Radio: Contact the lock keeper on the harbour channel 20 minutes before arrival
Section 5 Passage Procedure.Wash: Operators must reduce wash in the Lower Weir Cut where moored craft are present

Section 6 Lock Booking.Booking Requirement: Advance booking through the Harbour Office is required for any vessel of 12.0 m overall length or more that transits a lock during the Lock Booking Window, unless the vessel holds a current Standing Booking Certificate.
Section 6 Lock Booking.Lead Time: Bookings must be made at least 48 hours before the lock is to be used.
Section 6 Lock Booking.Certificate Validity: A Standing Booking Certificate is valid only for the dates stated on it. Renewal applications are processed separately and do not extend an expired certificate.

Base Rules.Section 7 Weather: Passage is suspended when mean wind on the Weir Section exceeds Beaufort force 7. Suspensions are posted on the Harbour Office board and in the bulletin series.
Base Rules.Section 9 Lock Closures: Closures are listed in the Lock Closure Schedule. Where a later closure notice changes an entry, the later notice governs for the dates it covers.

Amendment Register.Subject: Low-water draught reduction
Amendment Register.Change: For the Weir Section only, the draught limit during the low-water period is 1.85 m. The low-water period runs from 1 June 2025 to 30 June 2025, both days included. The Lower Weir Cut is not changed.

Amendment Register.Subject: Replacement of the low-water figure

Amendment Register.Subject: Certificate form change
Amendment Register.Change: Standing Booking Certificates are issued on form SBC-7 from 1 July 2025. Validity periods are unchanged.

Annual reissue. No change to draught limits or booking rules.
Low-water draught amendment issued (see Amendment Register).

The Stumness Lock sill inspection on 17 June 2025 will be carried out from the upper chamber. The lock stays closed to through traffic for the whole of 17 June 2025.

1. PURPOSE
This memo sets out the rules in force and one application before the panel. The panel is asked to record a decision on application PRM-2026-0931 at its sitting of 2026-08-04. This memo does not change any rule.

2. RULES IN FORCE
2.1 General Operating Order GO-9 (issued 2025-09-15). GO-9 applies to every uncrewed flight in the panel's area unless a site schedule sets a different term for that flight. Its terms relevant here are:
(a) Night flight means any flight whose planned take-off time is after 20:00 local time.
(b) The maximum planned height is 120 m above ground level (AGL).
(c) Every night flight must carry a lighting kit that is switched on for the whole flight.
(d) Notice. An application must be lodged at least ten working days before the flight date. Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding listed non-working days in section 4. The flight date is day 0 and is not counted. The first working day before it is day 1, the next is day 2, and so on. An application is in time if it is lodged on the day that is day 10 in this count or on an earlier calendar date.
(e) Sustained wind at take-off must not exceed 10 m/s. Gust speed does not by itself stop a flight.

2.2 Site Schedule FW-3, Fainwych turbine site (issued 2026-02-16). FW-3 applies to any flight whose nearest planned flight point lies within 2 km of the boundary of the Fainwych turbine site. Its terms are:
(a) The maximum planned height for such a flight is 80 m AGL.
(b) From 2026-05-01 onward, a second crew member must act as spotter for every night flight to which FW-3 applies. The spotter must be named on the application. Flights before that date are not subject to this term.
(c) Precedence. Where GO-9 and FW-3 set different terms for the same flight, FW-3 prevails. Where GO-9 sets a term that FW-3 does not address, GO-9 continues to apply.
(d) Amendment. A planned height above the ceiling that applies to a flight must be amended to a height within that ceiling before a permission is issued. A permission is not issued on a planned height above the applicable ceiling.

2.3 Withdrawn Order GO-6 (withdrawn 2025-10-01) set a height ceiling of 100 m for all night flights. It has no effect on any application lodged after that date.

clauses.heading: Response periods
clauses.text: Category A, hazard to life or safe occupation: make safe within 24 hours. clauses.heading: Counting days
clauses.text: The report date is not counted. The deadline is the report date plus the stated number of calendar days. A repair is late only if it is completed after the deadline day.

clauses.heading: Exception: agreed access delay for listed vulnerable members
clauses.text: Where a member on the vulnerability register asks for access to a repair to be delayed, the deadline in force for that repair may be extended by the number of calendar days stated in a written access-delay agreement signed by that member. clauses.heading: No other extensions

=== PART A: BYLAW EXTRACT (CONSOLIDATED TEXT) ===

A1. Definitions
A1.1 "Length for category" (LFC) means the length overall of a craft measured from the foremost to the aftermost point of the hull, excluding any bowsprit, bumkin, pulpit, davit or fender, stated in metres to one decimal place.
A1.2 "Continuous stay" means a period during which a craft occupies a berth on the Laigate Reach without interruption. An absence of 24 hours or more ends the continuous stay. A shorter absence does not end the continuous stay and does not pause the day count.
A1.3 "Day of stay": the day of arrival is day 1, and each later calendar day is the next day number, including weekends and listed holidays. The count runs up to and includes the day on which it is being checked.
A1.4 "Houseboat" means a craft with no means of propulsion fitted that is used principally as a residence.
A1.5 "Absence" means any period when the craft is not on its berth, measured from the time it leaves the reach to the time it returns, as shown on the gate log.

A2. Berth categories and maximum continuous stay
A2.1 Category A: LFC up to and including 12.0 m. Maximum continuous stay 7 days.
A2.2 Category B: LFC over 12.0 m and up to and including 18.0 m. Maximum continuous stay 10 days, subject to Amendment 2 (Part A4).
A2.3 Category C: LFC over 18.0 m. Maximum continuous stay 5 days.
A2.4 Houseboats are not assigned a category and are dealt with under Part B of the Trust's rules, which is not part of this extract.

A3. Repair extension (exception)
A3.1 The Harbourmaster may, by written notice to the owner, extend the maximum continuous stay of a craft that is awaiting a repair part by up to 5 days. The notice must be issued before the end of the last day of the maximum continuous stay under A2. A notice issued after that time has no effect. A notice takes effect on the date it is issued unless it states a later date.
A3.2 Section A3.1 does not apply to a Category C craft.

A4. Amendment 2 (in force from 1 May 2026)
A4.1 Section A2.2 is replaced by: "Category B: LFC over 12.0 m and up to and including 18.0 m. Maximum continuous stay 14 days."
A4.2 Amendment 2 applies to every continuous stay that is in progress on 1 May 2026 or that begins on or after that date.

A5. Records
A5.1 Berth Records keeps the movement log for each berth from the gate log. Where the gate log and the berth sheet differ, the gate log time governs.
A5.2 All times in the movement log are local time.

subject: Harvest standard for concession block K-14, Nourtport District, north compartment
concessionRef: NPD-K14-2019
blockAreaHa: 212.4

1. PURPOSE
This memo sets out which version of the K-14 harvest standard governs each felling notice and each felling, what annual cap applies, and where harvest returns are lodged. Keep it with the block file. Where this memo and the 2025 operating note disagree, this memo governs.

2. VERSIONS AND EFFECTIVE DATES
2.1 Version 2.1 of the K-14 harvest standard took effect on 2024-01-01. It governs every felling notice lodged before 2026-07-01.
2.2 Version 3.0 takes effect on 2026-07-01 (effectiveFrom). It governs every harvest year that begins on or after that date. Harvest years run from 1 July to 30 June.
2.3 A felling notice is judged under the version in force on the day the notice is lodged, whatever day the felling takes place.

3. PRE-FELLING NOTICE
3.1 Version 2.1: notice of intention to fell must be lodged with the district office at least 14 days before felling starts.
3.2 Version 3.0: notice of intention to fell must be lodged with the district office at least 21 days before felling starts.
3.3 For both versions, the notice period is the number of whole calendar days from the day after the lodging day up to and including the felling start day.

4. ANNUAL HARVEST CAP
4.1 Version 2.1: annual harvest cap for block K-14 is 4,200 cubic metres per harvest year.
4.2 Version 3.0: annual harvest cap for block K-14 is 3,600 cubic metres per harvest year (figure subject to the correspondence in section 9).
4.3 The cap is measured on counted harvest only. Entries marked VOID are not counted. Salvage volume under section 5 counts toward the cap.

5. WINDTHROW SALVAGE EXCEPTION
5.1 Timber felled after windthrow or wind damage may proceed without pre-felling notice under section 3 if all of the following are met: (a) the felling record gives the cause as windthrow; (b) the volume for that felling is 60 cubic metres or less; (c) a salvage notice is lodged with the district office within 48 hours of the felling start time recorded on the felling record.
5.2 Hours in 5.1(c) are counted from the recorded felling start time to the time the notice is lodged, using the 24-hour clock and calendar days.
5.3 A windthrow felling above 60 cubic metres is not covered by this exception and needs pre-felling notice under the version in force on the lodging day of that notice.
5.4 This exception was carried into version 3.0 without change.

6. HARVEST RETURNS
6.1 Version 2.1: harvest returns are lodged with the Nourtport District Office by 31 July after the end of each harvest year.
6.2 Version 3.0: from 1 July 2026, harvest returns are lodged with the Senport District Office, by the same date.
6.3 A harvest return is lodged with the office in force on the day it is actually lodged.

7. UNITS AND CONVERSION
7.1 Volumes are recorded in cubic metres (m3). Softwood pulpwood weighed in tonnes is converted at 1.90 m3 per tonne, green weight, as set out in Schedule B. Convert before adding to any total.
7.2 Log dates are felling start dates unless a line says otherwise.

Operating And Examination Rules: R1 Ticket validity: a boiler ticket is valid from its examination date up to but not including the same calendar day one year later. A repair does not shorten a ticket.
R2 Steam hours: only Daily Running Log entries dated after the washout date count toward the next washout. Entries with Status Void never count.
R3 Washout: a washout falls due once 200 steam hours have been counted since the last washout.

R4 Examination category: a stay or firebox crown replacement needs a full examination. Any other boiler repair needs an intermediate examination. Routine work needs only an annual inspection. Where more than one category applies, the highest applies, in the order full, intermediate, annual.

R5 Waiver exception: a stay repair counts as intermediate work only where a written Chief Engineer waiver covers that repair and is in force on the repair date. A revocation takes effect from the date it states, even if that date is earlier than the message.

R6 Next examination: the next boiler examination must be in the category required by all boiler work done since the previous examination, and must be completed by the expiry date of the current ticket.
R7 Defect classes: Class A stops all running. Class B bars passenger service only. Class C is recorded for attention at the next planned stop and bars no service.
R8 Passenger service: passenger trains may run on a day only when the boiler ticket is valid that day, no Class A or Class B defect is open, and the passenger certificate is in force.
R9 Later messages: where a later message in the Correction And Override Messages list conflicts with an earlier entry, the later message replaces that entry from the effective date it states.
R10 Counting days: count from the reference date to the first date on which the item is no longer valid. The reference date itself is not counted.

domain: tutoring services: fortnightly tuition hour-cap checks

request.requestText: Please confirm whether Drymin Gamere's delivered tuition from 2 March to 15 March 2026 stays inside the fortnight cap. Give the total delivered time, say whether it is within the cap, and list the session ids that were counted.

policy.windowRule: The window is 14 consecutive calendar days. Both the start date and the end date are inside the window.
policy.countingRule: Only sessions with status delivered count toward the cap. Sessions cancelled by the tutor and sessions the learner did not attend are not delivered and count as zero minutes.
policy.durationRule: Logged durations may be in minutes or hours; 1 hour equals 60 minutes. Sessions are counted at their logged length.

priorReview.comment: Earlier check on the January block was accepted. The reply then followed the same table format used in this case.

candidateReply.replyText: Between 2 and 15 March 2026, Drymin Gamere received 5 hours 45 minutes of delivered tuition across five sessions: S-101, S-102, S-104, S-106 and S-107. That is within the 12-hour fortnight cap. The cancelled session S-103 and the learner no-show S-105 are excluded because they were not delivered, and S-097, S-099, S-108 and S-110 fall outside the window.

state.notes: Coordinator asked for this check before the next block of sessions is confirmed. Room B2 was double-booked on 12 March, but the session still ran in A3 at the Monminster site. Tutor T-882 is on leave from 16 March, and the booked slots for the learner have not yet been changed. The parent has asked whether an extra session in late March would affect the cap; that question is outside this request and should be handled in the next planning review. The learner's school has also sent a revised exam timetable, which is held on the family file and is not part of this check.

definitions.reporting_window: Hours from the landed_at time on the landing ticket to the time the landing report is received by the Board. A report received exactly at the end of the window is in time.

1.1 Observing block means one continuous period of telescope time allocated to one programme under one booking reference. Any such break longer than 20 minutes ends the block, and the time either side of it is treated as separate observing blocks. A break of exactly 20 minutes does not end a block.
1.2 Night means the period from 18:00 to 06:00 local time, allocated to the calendar date on which it starts.
1.3 Allocated hours means the hours a programme holds for a semester under clause 3, including any hours restored under clause 3.3.
1.4 Semester means the period from the start date to the end date stated in the schedule for that semester.
1.5 Provider closure means a closure of the telescope by the Provider for maintenance, weather or safety. A closure caused by the User's own equipment is not a Provider closure.

state:
MOUXFRURIS NAVIGATION TRUST
Trallwych reach: bylaw consolidation memo

document-ref: MNT-NAV-2026-041
issued-by: Kuran Weaham, Harbourmaster, Trallwych reach
issued-to: Stockis Humwell (lock operations); Vylcott Goxthomton (quay wardens)
copy: Board secretariat, Questow office
issued-on: 2026-06-12
status: working consolidation for the season; supersedes MNT-NAV-2026-038

PURPOSE
This memo consolidates the speed and mooring clauses for the Trallwych reach so that lock and quay staff work from one text. Where an amendment replaces a clause, the replacement is the operative text. Where a later message in the thread below withdraws an earlier proposal, the withdrawal governs. Times in the logs are local times recorded by the quay warden at each berth.

SECTION 1. BASE TEXT (bylaw edition 2019, before amendments)

clause-7.1 speed: Vessels shall not exceed 6 knots on the Trallwych reach between Trallwych lock and Questow lock, or between Questow lock and Tuncombe weir.

clause-7.2 mooring: Mooring on the Questow public quay is limited to 72 consecutive hours. A span of consecutive hours runs from a vessel's first arrival at the quay to its final departure. An absence from the quay of 6 hours or more ends the span, and a new span starts on the next arrival. An absence shorter than 6 hours does not end the span; all time from first arrival to final departure counts toward it.

clause-7.3 wash: Vessels shall keep wash to a minimum within 50 metres of any bank carrying a wash notice. Notices shall be posted at each berth and at both locks. No wash notice is posted on the Trallwych reach at the date of this memo.

clause-7.4 pilotage: Vessels over 14 metres overall shall take a pilot through the Tuncombe weir cut.

clause-7.5 signs: Speed boards at each lock shall show the limit in force for the stretch below that lock. A board shall be replaced within 14 days of any change to a limit.

clause-9.3 changes: A change to any numeric speed limit in clause 7 takes effect only when the Trust board passes a resolution approving it, and the resolution is published with the amendment. A harbourmaster notice or a lock instruction cannot change a numeric speed limit.

SECTION 2. AMENDMENT A (effective 2026-03-01; replaces clause-7.1 in full)

Board resolution BR-2026-02, passed 2026-02-19, approved the following text.

Policy_Rules.Enrolment_Test: Applicant must be enrolled for at least 12 credit units in the award term.
Policy_Rules.Means_Test: The household income used is the figure for the most recently filed tax year. Figures for earlier tax years are not used. The income used must be at or below 38,000 GBP.
Policy_Rules.GPA_Test: At the end of each academic year, cumulative GPA on the 4.0 scale must be at least 2.80. Cumulative GPA is total grade points divided by total credit units across all completed terms, rounded to two decimal places. Terms with no recorded grade and non-credit courses are excluded.
Policy_Rules.Medical_Leave_Exception: Where a term was missed because of documented medical leave, the GPA_Test uses only the most recent completed term, and cumulative GPA is not applied for that academic year.
Policy_Rules.Renewal_Outcome: A renewal is granted in full only when all three tests are met. Where any one test is not met, the renewal is declined. No conditional renewal is available under this policy.
Policy_Rules.Precedence: Where a reviewer note and the policy rules differ, the policy rules prevail.

FORTMARTON RAILWAY HERITAGE TRUST
Locomotive Boiler Certification File - Skoxwold Valley Line
Compiled by the Operations Office on 2 March 2026

PART A - POLICY EXTRACT (Locomotive Boiler Certificate Policy, Issue 4)

Section 1 - Definitions
1.1 Passenger running means hauling one or more trips that carry members of the public. It does not include crew-only test runs, works trains, or any movement with no passengers on board, even where members of the public are present on the platform.
1.2 Certificate expiry date means the last calendar day on which a boiler certificate is valid. The certificate covers that day and no later day.
1.3 Inspector means the outside boiler inspector appointed under Section 6, and no other person.

Section 2 - Scope
2.1 This policy covers steam locomotives owned or leased by the Trust and running on the Skoxwold Valley Line or from Vammouth Halt. Diesel shunters are covered by a separate policy and are not addressed here.

Section 3 - Boiler Certificates and Passenger Running
3.1 A locomotive may not carry out passenger running on any day after the certificate expiry date of the boiler certificate in force for it.
3.2 The certificate expiry date is the date printed on the certificate, unless the Inspector has amended it under 3.3.
3.3 Only the Inspector may alter a certificate expiry date, and only by written amendment sent to the Trust Engineer. An amendment replaces every earlier expiry date given for that certificate, from the date of the amendment.
3.4 Passenger running after an expiry date requires a new or re-issued certificate, with a new expiry date, before the first such day.

Section 4 - Safety Valves and Water Gauges
4.1 Safety valve set-pressure checks are recorded on the Works Sheet for each locomotive.
4.2 Water gauge glasses are tested every 28 days while a locomotive is in steam. Results are kept on the Works Sheet and do not alter any certificate.

Section 5 - Records
5.1 Certificates and written amendments are entered in the fleet register within five working days of receipt.
5.2 Paper copies are kept in the Goxhaven shed office for ten years.

Section 6 - Appointment of Inspector
6.1 The Trust appoints one outside boiler inspector each year. For 2026 the appointment is held by Waion Dartby of Saisrairara Boiler Inspection Ltd, Vammouth.

Section 7 - Timetables
7.1 The Timetable Secretary publishes passenger timetables once the Trust Engineer has confirmed the boiler certificate position for each locomotive shown.

Section 8 - Withdrawal
8.1 A locomotive whose boiler certificate has passed its expiry date is withdrawn from passenger running until a new or re-issued certificate is in force.

1. PURPOSE
Decide what, if anything, to adopt for wind-hold crewing on the Foufell Peak Quad (lift 3) for the rest of the 2025-26 season. Board rule BRD-7 (section 5) governs the choice.

2. LOGGED HISTORY
Operating days logged to 2026-02-11: 120. An operating day is a day lift 3 opened to guests for at least one run. A further 11 days were closed for maintenance and are not counted.
Hold day: a day on which lift 3 was stopped by wind in one stop lasting 15 minutes or more. Several shorter stops on the same day do not count toward a hold day, however many there were.
Hold days logged: 21.
Anemometer stop level: 45 km/h sustained (a manufacturer setting; it is not a crewing trigger).

3. MEASURES ASSESSED
M1 Full extended cover: added crew works every remaining operating day at GBP 140 per day worked. M1 covers every hold day.
M2 Forecast trigger: added crew works only on days the wind forecast meets the trigger, at GBP 140 per triggered day.
Back-test over the same 120 logged days: the trigger would have fired on 30 days and would have covered 15 of the 21 hold days.
Under either measure, each covered hold day is expected to recover 2.5 guest-hours of lift access that would otherwise be lost.
M1 and M2 are alternatives, not add-ons: M1 already staffs every day M2 would staff.

4. REMAINING SEASON
Operating days remaining to season close: 80.
Modelling assumption: the remaining days have the same hold-day rate as the logged days. The trigger fires on the same share of days, and covers the same share of hold days, as in the back-test.
Value of one lost guest-hour, including refunds and lost lift sales: GBP 120.

5. DECISION RULE (BRD-7)
Only M1, M2 or no change may be adopted; any other course needs a separate paper. A measure is adopted only if its expected value of recovered guest-hours is strictly greater than its added crew cost over the remaining operating days. Equal values are not adopted. At most one measure may be adopted.

6. OTHER NOTES
- Vorness Chair (lift 2) ticket prices are unchanged this season and are not relevant to this paper.
- Ref VMC-LW3-25-02 (2024-25 crewing review) closed with no change.

1. PURPOSE
This memo records which licence category applies to the planned upstream passage of vessel SNT-V-0231 through Clomthorpe Lock into the Saillmouth restricted reach. It also summarises the reach-time entries on the lock log for 1 February to 11 March 2026, so that the booking desk can give the keeper a clear answer before the passage. The planned passage is on 16 March 2026. The vessel is due to leave the lock at 09:30 and to return the same day.
Bylaw extracts are in section 2, definitions in section 3, amendments in section 4, vessel and notice records in section 5, the reach log in section 6, procedure in section 7, correspondence in section 8, maintenance notices in section 9 and the 2025 season summary in section 10.

2. BYLAW EXTRACTS (Saillmouth Navigation Trust Bylaws 2019, as amended)
Clause 4.1 Vessel classes. Class A: length overall 12.0 m or more. Class B: length overall 6.0 m or more but less than 12.0 m. Class C: length overall less than 6.0 m.
Clause 4.2 Licences. A Class A vessel requires a full navigation licence. A Class B vessel requires a standard permit. A Class C vessel requires registration only.
Clause 4.3 Booking. A vessel entering a lock must hold a booking made at least 24 hours ahead through the Harbour Office booking line. A booking does not itself create a licence and does not affect the class of a vessel.
Clause 4.4 Night working. No vessel may enter a lock between 18:00 and 07:00 without the written consent of the duty lock keeper.
Clause 4.5 Laid-up exception. Clause 4.2 does not apply to a vessel for any period covered by a laid-up notice that has been lodged with the Harbour Office and is in force under this clause. A laid-up notice is in force from its start date to its end date, both dates included. A vessel covered by a laid-up notice must not enter the restricted reach.
Clause 4.6 Restricted reach speed. Vessels in the restricted reach must not exceed 5 knots over the ground.
Clause 4.7 Waste. Vessels must not discharge untreated waste within the Saillmouth reaches. Holding tanks are to be pumped out at the Clomthorpe pump-out point before a vessel leaves the lock.
Clause 4.8 Offences. A breach of clause 4.2 or clause 4.6 is an offence and may attract a notice of direction under section 9 of the Bylaws.

3. DEFINITIONS (Bylaws section 2)
2.3 'Length overall' means the hull length of a vessel, measured from the foremost point of the hull to the aftmost point with fittings excluded, plus any bowsprit projection added under clause 2.4.
2.4 'Bowsprit projection' means the distance a fixed bowsprit extends forward of the foremost point of the hull. Where the bowsprit projection is more than the threshold in this clause, the whole projection is added to hull length. A projection equal to the threshold is not added. The threshold is 1.0 m, subject to Amendment 2 in section 4.
2.7 'Reach time' means time a vessel spends between the upstream reach marker and the downstream reach marker. Time on the Miminster approach channel is not reach time, even where the lock log records it against the same trip.
2.9 'Entry' means one line of the lock-keeper log for one vessel. An entry that has been struck through by the Lock Operations Lead is void and is not counted.

4. AMENDMENTS
Amendment 2, made 10 February 2026, in force 1 March 2026. Sets the threshold in clause 2.4 at 2.0 m in place of 1.0 m. An amendment applies to every passage made on or after its in-force date. It does not reopen any passage made before that date.
Amendment 2A, draft proposing a threshold of 1.5 m in clause 2.4. Withdrawn on 20 February 2026. It has no effect and must not be applied to any passage.

subject: Simulator credit toward the instrument rating (policy IR-SC, versions 2 and 3)
status: version 3 in force from 2026-01-12; later amendments are recorded in the correspondence section

SECTION 1 - PURPOSE
1.1 This memo sets out how simulator time is credited toward the instrument rating course.
1.2 Which version applies depends on the student's instrument course start date. Version 3 applies to any student whose instrument course start date is 2026-01-12 or later. Version 2 applies to any student whose instrument course start date is earlier than 2026-01-12.
1.3 Credit is recorded per student and per course. Hours logged on any other course are not carried into the instrument credit.
1.4 Credit figures are recalculated only when the records officer opens a new entry. Entries already closed are not reopened by this memo.

SECTION 2 - VERSION 2 RULES (instrument course starts before 2026-01-12)
2.1 A simulator session counts only if its recorded duration is at least 60 minutes.
2.2 Credited time is the sum of counted session durations, capped at 15.0 hours.
2.3 Version 2 has no medical pause provision and no fixed-base trainer exception.

SECTION 3 - VERSION 3 RULES (instrument course starts on or after 2026-01-12)
3.1 A simulator session counts only if its recorded duration is at least 45 minutes. A session of exactly 45 minutes counts.
3.2 Each recorded duration is converted to minutes first (one hour is 60 minutes). Credited time is the sum of counted minutes divided by 60, giving hours. Individual sessions are not rounded.
3.3 The cap on credited time is 20.0 hours.
3.4 Fixed-base trainer exception. A session flown on a fixed-base trainer listed in Annex B counts regardless of the 45-minute minimum in 3.1. The exception applies only to trainers listed in Annex B.
3.5 Medical pause extension. Where a student has a documented flying restriction of 14 or more consecutive calendar days, counting both its first day and its last day, every session flown in the 7 calendar days that begin on the day after the restriction ends counts regardless of the 45-minute minimum in 3.1. Those sessions remain subject to the cap in 3.3.
3.6 Countersignature. An entry of a medical pause extension on a student record must be countersigned by the medical adviser, unless a later written instruction changes this for a given case.
3.7 Where clauses 3.4 and 3.5 both apply to a session, the session is counted once.

SECTION 4 - PROGRESS CHECK (versions 2 and 3)
4.1 The instrument progress check may be booked once the student's credited total is at least 16.0 hours.
4.2 If the credited total is below 16.0 hours, the student must fly additional simulator blocks of 2.0 hours each before the check is booked. The number of blocks is the shortfall in hours divided by 2.0, rounded up to the next whole block.
4.3 Multi-engine simulator sessions are recorded on a separate course and are not part of the instrument credit.
4.4 The progress check is booked by the student's instructor of record through the scheduling desk, after the records officer has confirmed the credited total in writing.

SECTION 5 - ANNEX B: FIXED-BASE TRAINERS APPROVED FOR THE 3.4 EXCEPTION
FB-1: fixed-base trainer, Trofell hangar, bay 2
FB-3: fixed-base trainer, Tralthorpe annex, bay 4
Trainers not listed in this annex do not qualify for the exception in 3.4.
The annex was last reviewed on 2025-11-14 by the simulator manager.

SECTION 6 - RECORD-KEEPING
6.1 Session logs are kept by the simulator operator and copied to the student record weekly.
6.2 Durations are entered as they appear on the simulator clock. Mixed formats are normalised by the records officer before the credited total is calculated.
6.3 Any medical restriction notice must be attached to the student record before a pause entry is made.
6.4 Records older than five years are archived to the Staickganis store at Queallcombe.

SECTION 7 - GLOSSARY
Calendar day: any day of the month, including weekends and public holidays.
Block: a booked 2.0-hour simulator session used to make up a shortfall under 4.2.
Shortfall: the progress check threshold minus the credited total, in hours.
Pause window: the 7 calendar days described in clause 3.5.
Credited total: the figure produced by the rules of the version that applies to the student.

domain: railway heritage trust steam boiler periodic examination registers

state.locomotive-description: 2-6-2 tank locomotive, rebuilt in 1961 and painted in lined green livery
state.standard-scope: This standard applies to every steam locomotive owned by the trust or operated by the operating company on the trust's lines, including locomotives on loan from other groups. Boilers taken out of service for more than 90 consecutive days are dealt with under the withdrawal annex, which is held separately by the chief engineer and is not reproduced in this register. Nothing in this standard alters the separate rules for pressure gauges, safety valves or boiler feed equipment, which are set out in the operating rules.
state.standard-version-history: Version 1 took effect on 2024-07-01 and applied until 2026-02-28. Version 2 took effect on 2026-03-01 and superseded version 1 from that date. The trustees approved version 2 at their meeting on 2026-02-12.
state.standard-definitions: 1. Examination date: the calendar date on which a full examination of a locomotive boiler was completed and passed. 2. In-service day under version 2: a calendar day on which the locomotive was steamed for public passenger running on a published timetable or a published special. Works-train, light-engine, static and test days are not in-service days under version 2. 3. In-service day under version 1: any calendar day on which the locomotive was steamed for passenger, works or test running. 4. Each calendar day counts at most once, however many trips were run on it. 5. When in-service days are counted from a full examination, the examination date itself is not counted; counting starts on the next calendar day and runs up to and including the review date. 6. Review date: the calendar date on which the register entry is made.
state.standard-interim-rule: An interim inspection is required once the number of in-service days counted from the last full examination reaches 45, using the definitions in this standard and the version in force on the review date. While that number is below 45, no interim inspection is required.
state.standard-full-exam-rule: A full examination is due on or before the boiler certificate end date in force on the review date. The chief engineer may extend a certificate end date by written letter for up to 30 days in total beyond the end date first issued. An extension letter takes effect on the date it is issued and replaces the end date for all purposes. Extensions are recorded in the register alongside the extension letter reference and the date of issue.
state.standard-test-procedure: Hydrostatic tests are carried out at each full examination and after any boiler repair that the chief engineer classes as major. Test pressure is one and a half times working pressure and is held for the period set in the annex. Test charts are filed with the register entry and kept for the life of the boiler. A repair classed as minor needs a witnessed leak test only and does not reset any examination interval.
state.standard-records-rule: The register entry must show the last full examination date, the certificate end date in force on the review date, the operating log count for the review period, the standard version applied and any interim inspection on file. Entries are dated on the day they are made. Corrections are entered as a new line that refers back to the entry it corrects; earlier lines are never altered.

Scope: repair requests logged 2026-02-23 to 2026-05-14, and the procedure and amendments that govern them.

SECTION 1. PROCEDURE IN FORCE
RP-4 Repairs Procedure, Issue 3, takes effect on 2026-03-01 and applies to every repair request logged on or after that date. Requests logged before 2026-03-01 remain under Issue 2 and are outside the review in Section 6. Requests already closed under Issue 2 are not reopened by Issue 3.

SECTION 2. DEFINITIONS (RP-4 clause 2)
2.1 Working day: a day from Monday to Friday that is not a closure day listed in Schedule B. Saturdays, Sundays and Schedule B closure days are not working days.
2.2 Day count: the day a request is logged is day 0 and is never counted. Day 1 is the first working day after the logging day. A period of N working days ends on day N.
2.3 Urgent fault: a fault that leaves a dwelling without heating, without hot water, without secure entry, or without a safe electrical supply. A fault is not urgent merely because a member describes it as urgent.
2.4 Routine fault: any fault that is neither an urgent fault nor an emergency.
2.5 Made safe or repaired: the fault is repaired, or the contractor has attended and restored the affected service, on the date written on the visit sheet.
2.6 Suspended day: a working day on which the member refuses or does not give access to a contractor visit that was booked and confirmed to the member in writing. A visit booked by telephone only, with no written confirmation on file, does not create a suspended day.

SECTION 3. RESPONSE PERIODS (RP-4 clause 4)
Emergency (gas smell or exposed live wiring): attend within 2 hours of logging.
Urgent fault: made safe or repaired within 1 working day of logging (Issue 3).
Routine fault: made safe or repaired within 10 working days of logging.

SECTION 4. EXCEPTIONS AND SUSPENDED DAYS (RP-4 clause 5)
5.1 A fault reported as urgent is treated as routine where the attending contractor's visit sheet records that no service listed in clause 2.3 is lost and that there is no water ingress.
5.2 Suspended days under clause 2.6 are not counted in the response period. The period is extended by one working day for each suspended day. The deadline is the working day on which the extended period ends, counting every working day from day 1, suspended days included.
5.3 Clause 5.1 is applied from the contractor's visit sheet only. The desk does not reclassify a request on the strength of a member's description.

PURPOSE
This file sets out the cadet's night currency on the position date, the night dual time logged to date, and whether the first night solo planned for 2026-04-09 may go ahead. Section 1 defines the terms used. Those definitions decide how each logged flight is treated, so read section 1 before the log in section 4. Section 3 gives the rules and records the amendment that changed the night-landing window. Where a later message disagrees with a rule, the rule governs, as set out in section 7.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 'Night landing' means a full-stop landing recorded in the log at a time after civil dusk and before civil dawn at Cindbury on the date of the flight, made with the cadet as pilot-flying. A touch-and-go is not a full-stop landing and is not a night landing. A landing made with the instructor as pilot-flying is not a night landing, whatever the time.
1.2 'Counted night landing' means a night landing as defined in 1.1. Each full-stop landing counts once.
1.3 'Dual time' means time flown with an instructor on board, whether or not the instructor is manipulating the controls. Time flown solo is not dual time.
1.4 'Night dual time' means the part of a dual flight that falls after civil dusk and before civil dawn. A flight that departs before civil dusk counts only from civil dusk onwards. Daylight time is never night dual time.
1.5 'Window' means a number of days ending on the position date, with both its first and last day counted. A window of N days begins on the day that is N minus 1 days before the position date. A landing on the first day of the window is inside it; a landing on the day before the first day is outside it.
1.6 'Civil dusk' and 'civil dawn' mean the times printed against each flight in section 4 for Cindbury on the date of that flight. No other source is used.
1.7 'Night currency' means that the cadet has at least three counted night landings inside the window in force on the position date.
1.8 'Position date' means the date shown as position-date in the header of this file.

2.8 Banksman: every possession needs a lineside banksman for the whole window. Banksmen are rostered separately from the volunteer roster and are not counted in it.

1.1 Circular TH-GO-04, Guest Occupancy Rule. Adopted by the Board on 2024-08-14, in force from 2024-09-01.
Standard allowance: a member may host a guest for up to 21 nights in a calendar year without written consent from the Allocations Panel. Consent is needed for any night beyond 21. This circular has no carer provision.

1.2 Circular TH-GO-06, Guest Occupancy Rule (Amended). Adopted by the Board on 2026-02-19. It applies to every stay whose arrival date is on or after 2026-03-01. A stay whose arrival date is before 2026-03-01 stays under TH-GO-04 in full, including any nights it runs past 2026-03-01.
Clause 2, standard allowance: up to 14 nights in a calendar year without consent. Consent is needed for any night beyond 14.
Clause 3, counting: a stay's nights are its departure date minus its arrival date. Each night is attributed to the calendar year in which it falls. Nights of stays governed by TH-GO-04 do not count toward the clause 2 allowance.
Clause 4, carer exception: a guest who is a registered carer for a member with a recorded medical need does not count against clause 2. Their nights count instead toward a separate carer allowance of 60 nights per calendar year, provided the Housing Office has received the carer letter before the arrival date of that stay. If the carer letter is received on or after the arrival date, the stay counts under clause 2.
Clause 5, confirmation: the Housing Office records each stay in the guest register and confirms the applicable allowance in writing within 5 working days of arrival.

1.3 Consent process (unchanged by either circular). A member who needs consent writes to the Allocations Panel through the Housing Office at least 10 working days before arrival. The Panel meets monthly, normally in the second week of the month. Requests received late are carried to the next meeting unless the Housing Office marks them urgent.

1.4 Definitions used in both circulars. A night is one overnight stay, counted once. A calendar year runs from 1 January to 31 December. SECTION C. STANDARD TERMS (form dated 2025-09-01)
The standard form applies to all three agreements in this register unless an addendum for a named licensee says otherwise.

Clause 2.1 Purpose. The Trust makes Instrument 1 available to licensees for observing programmes approved under the agreement. Nothing in this clause gives a licensee rights over the instrument's maintenance schedule.

Clause 3.1 Allocation. Each licensee receives an allocation of nights in each quarter, issued by the Access Desk. A night credit returned under this agreement is added back to the licensee's allocation.

Clause 4.1 Monthly caps. A Tier 1 licensee may use up to 40 observing hours in each calendar month. A Tier 2 licensee may use up to 24 observing hours in each calendar month, unless a signed addendum states a different cap for that licensee. Observing hours are the hours charged in the observing log for each session.

Clause 5.1 Clear days. A notice period is counted in clear days. The day on which notice is received and the day on which the session starts are both excluded. Notice is treated as received on the calendar day it arrives, whatever the time of day.

Clause 5.2 Licensee cancellations. Notice of cancellation by the licensee returns a credit to the licensee's allocation as follows: notice received 10 or more clear days before the session start returns the full night; notice received 3 to 9 clear days before returns half the night; notice received fewer than 3 clear days before returns no credit. Credits are night credits only. No cash refund is payable under any agreement in this file.

Clause 5.3 Trust-side losses. Clause 5.2 does not apply to a session lost to a Trust-side closure. Such sessions are dealt with under clauses 6.2 and 6.3.

Clause 6.1 Duty astronomer. The duty astronomer may close the dome for safety or weather at any time and must record the closure in the observing log with the time it was recorded.

Clause 6.2 Weather closures. Where the duty astronomer logs a weather closure of a session in the observing log by 18:00 local time on the session date, the full night is returned as a credit and the session counts as a Trust-side closure. 3.2 "Length overall" (LOA) means the distance from the foremost point of the bow to the aftermost point of the stern, measured along the centreline. It includes fixed fittings such as bow pulpits, bowsprits and fixed platforms. It excludes detachable items such as fenders, tenders carried on davits and boarding ladders.
3.3 "Commercial craft" means a craft carrying passengers or cargo for hire or reward, or used in a trade. A craft used only for private recreation is not commercial, whether or not its owner shares it with guests.
3.4 "Passage" means a continuous period during which a craft is within the upper reach. A hold of more than 15 minutes within the upper reach ends the passage, and movement after such a hold starts a new passage. A hold of 15 minutes or less does not end the passage.
3.5 "Effective date" means the first calendar day on which an amendment applies. A passage that starts on the effective date is covered by the amendment.
3.6 Every date in a certificate term is inclusive: the first and last days of the term both fall within it.

3. PERMIT REQUIREMENT (BYLAW 5)
5.1 A Class B passage permit is required before any commercial craft, or any craft with an LOA of 15.0 m or more, enters the upper reach.
5.2 Standing exemption. A craft that holds a standing exemption certificate issued under Bylaw 5.4 is exempt from Bylaw 5.1 for any passage that starts on a date within that certificate's term.
5.3 Rescue exception. A craft engaged on official rescue, pollution-response or search duty is exempt from Bylaw 5.1 for the duration of that duty.
5.4 The Authority may issue a standing exemption certificate to a craft owner for a fixed term stated on the certificate. A certificate cannot be renewed retrospectively. A replacement certificate must be issued before the previous term ends if the exemption is to continue without a gap.

AMENDMENT 2 (COUNCIL RESOLUTION, NOTIFIED 2026-04-09)
In Bylaw 5.1, the figure "15.0 m" is replaced by "14.0 m". The commercial-craft limb of Bylaw 5.1 is unchanged. The amendment takes effect on 2026-05-01.

4. WASH AND LIGHTS (BYLAWS 4 AND 7, NOT AMENDED)
4.1 Craft on the upper reach between sunset and sunrise must show navigation lights as set out in the Authority's lighting schedule.
4.2 Craft with an LOA under 12.0 m must keep wash below the bank-protection line at all times on the upper reach.
4.3 Craft must not pass a moored craft within 20 m on the upper reach without that craft's consent.

5. SPEED ON THE UPPER REACH (BYLAW 6)
6.1 General limit. Every craft on the upper reach must not exceed the general limit of 8 knots through the water.
6.2 Length-based limit. A craft with an LOA over 12.0 m must not exceed 6 knots through the water on the upper reach.
6.3 Where a craft is subject to both 6.1 and 6.2, the lower limit applies.

NOTICE 6/3 (SPEED), ISSUED 2026-04-14 BY QUAIYS TEAMBROOK
For craft with an LOA over 12.0 m, the limit in Bylaw 6.2 is reduced to 5 knots through the water on the upper reach. This notice takes effect on 2026-04-15. Other limits in Bylaw 6 are unchanged.

rules.clock: Round times are local clock times in the van's home zone, 24-hour, written YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM. Elapsed time is measured on that clock.
rules.paid_time: Paid trading time is the elapsed time from departure to return minus the unpaid break minutes logged for that round.
rules.per_hour_rounding: Takings per paid hour are rounded half up to the nearest whole pound before any band is applied.
rules.ice_share: ice_pct is the ice-cream share of gross takings, in percent of gross.
rules.melt: Melt write-off is a percentage of the ice-cream takings and is deducted from those takings before the share is reported.
rules.return_due: A cash-up return is due by the end of the second working day after the round day. The round day is not counted. Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding dates in the closures list.
rules.grace: A return filed after its due date is accepted without penalty if it is filed no later than the next working day after the due date. Filing stamps are in UTC.

std.YS-4: Antifouling cure: launch is permitted once at least 10 counted days have run after the application day of the last antifouling coat. The application day is not counted; the launch day is counted.
std.gate: Log items with gate 'pre-launch' must be closed and signed before water entry. Items with gate 'post-launch' do not hold the launch.
std.labour: Hull labour is the sum of log entries whose area is 'hull'. Entries may be logged in hours or minutes.

cand.reply: (a) Earliest permitted launch is 2026-06-11. Antifouling coat 2 was applied on 2026-06-01. Counting from 2026-06-02 with the launch day counted, 2026-06-11 is the tenth counted day, the first day the 10-day minimum in YS-4 is met, so launch on 2026-06-11 is approved subject to (c). (b) Hull labour logged to date is 26.0 h: hull entries L-01, L-03, L-04, L-05, L-06 and L-07 added together. Rigging entry L-02 and general entry L-08 are excluded. POLICY EXTRACT (VV-4, in force from 1 January 2025)

VV-4.1 Certificate currency: An enhanced check certificate (EC) is current for a placement up to and including the day that falls 36 months after its issue date. That day is the certificate's last current day.

VV-4.2 References: Two written references are required. At least one referee must not be a relative of the volunteer, and that referee must have known the volunteer for at least two years on the day the reference is signed.

VV-4.3 Lapsed-certificate exception: A volunteer whose EC is no longer current may still be placed only if all of the following apply:
(a) a renewal application was lodged on or before the certificate's last current day;
(b) the placement start date is no more than 60 days after the last current day; and
(c) the volunteer is never alone with a child under 11, meaning every session has at least one other adult present with the volunteer.
The exception does not waive VV-4.2.

VV-4.4 Day counts: Counts are in calendar days. A count from the last current day to a placement start date begins on the day after the last current day and ends on the placement start date, and both of those days are counted.

Choose the verdict by how the defects can be fixed: return_for_correction applies when the defects are confined to specific statements or omissions that can be corrected in place while the remaining statements stand. SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 This memo assesses one request under Quota Transfer Scheme Rules 6 and 7. Other holders, stocks and areas are outside its scope.
1.2 'Quota year' means 1 January to 31 December of the same calendar year.
1.3 'Annual allocation' means the holder's stock figure shown on the register on the lodging date. Tonnage held in the Banking Ledger is not part of the annual allocation for any purpose of Rule 6, even where the Ledger shows it against the same holder.

1.7 'Sales note' means the buyer's record of a landing at a designated port. A discard return or a research return is not a sales note and its tonnage is not a landing for any purpose in this memo.

===== ROUND 14 SCORING RULE =====
1. Eligible if constituted at least 12 months before the closing date.
2. Request total = sum of bud_1 to bud_4 only. Match funding is not part of the request.
3. avg = sum of the three reviewer scores / 3, rounded to one decimal place.
4. spread = highest reviewer score minus lowest reviewer score.
5. If spread is 4 or more, scores go back for moderation before any decision.
6. Otherwise the band is set by avg: 8.0 or above = fund in full; 6.0 to 7.9 = fund 60% of request; below 6.0 = decline.

===== PANEL PROCEDURE NOTES =====
Reviewers score independently and do not see each other's scores before the meeting. Scores are entered on the round 14 score sheet and copied into the application file by the grants officer. Scores are whole numbers from 0 to 10.
A reviewer who knows the applicant declares it and is replaced. No replacement was needed for GR-2026-0382. Declarations are logged on the conflicts register kept by the secretariat in Plendhaven.
The panel does not reopen scores at the meeting unless a moderation request has been logged under rule 5 of the scoring rule. That is the only route for changing a reviewer's score.
Decisions are minuted with the rule and band that applied, so that each outcome can be traced back to the scores recorded on the file.

definitions.scope-note: The definitions below govern how every clause, amendment and letter in this file is read. Where a later document uses a defined term, the definition here applies unless that document expressly varies it.
definitions.commencement-date: 1 April 2026, the date on which the lease term began.
definitions.review-date: A 1 April on which the rent is reviewed under clause 6. Review dates fall at the review interval set in clause 6.2 as most recently amended, counted from the commencement date.
definitions.reference-month: The January immediately before the review date, as published in the index series listed in the cpi-index section.
definitions.base-month: January 2026, published in the same index series. It is the base for every review under this lease.
definitions.cpi-change: The index value for the reference month minus the index value for the base month, divided by the base-month value, expressed as a percentage to two decimal places.
definitions.cap: The maximum percentage increase allowed at a review. A cap set by a later letter or amendment replaces the earlier cap for every review date after that document takes effect.
definitions.capped-increase: The lower of the cpi-change and the cap in force on the review date. Where the cpi-change is zero or negative, no increase applies and the rent is not reduced.
definitions.grace-period: The calendar days after an instalment's due date within which it may be paid without being late, as set in clause 5.4. The last day of the grace period is the due date plus that number of days.
definitions.days-beyond-grace: Calendar days counted from the day after the last day of the grace period up to and including the statement date.
definitions.frost-event: Any loss of vines caused by frost in the period 1 October to 31 May of the following year.
definitions.vine-loss: A vine confirmed dead by the vineyard surveyor at the September inspection for the season in which the loss occurred. A vine that is damaged but shows live growth, or that is pruned back, is not a loss, whatever an earlier count says.

clause-5-rent.5.2-payment: Payable in four equal instalments due on 1 April, 1 July, 1 October and 1 January.
clause-5-rent.5.3-reviewed-rent: Once a review takes effect, the reviewed rent applies from and including the review date, and every instalment due on or after that date is payable at the reviewed rate.
clause-5-rent.5.4-grace: Each instalment may be paid within 14 calendar days after its due date without being late.

clause-6-review.6.1: The rent is reviewed on each review date.
clause-6-review.6.2-interval: Three years from the commencement date, as originally drafted. Replaced by AMD-1.

deskPolicy.countingRule: The day a request is treated as received is not counted. Each later working day counts as one. Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding listed holidays.
deskPolicy.cutoffRule: A request logged after the daily cutoff is treated as received on the next working day.
deskPolicy.batchRule: A batch is due on the latest policy due date among its documents.

candidateReply.replyText: Document A (birth certificate) will reach you by Monday 11 May, document B (marriage contract) by Wednesday 13 May, and document C (technical manual) by Friday 15 May. The batch is complete on Friday 15 May.

q1.instructions: Work out each document's policy due date under the desk's policy as stated in the request record. For each document, take its turnaround in working days from its category. Count from the day the request is treated as received: if the request was logged after the daily cutoff, it is treated as received on the next working day; otherwise it is received on the day it was logged. The day of receipt is not counted. Each later day counts only if it is a working day (Monday to Friday) and is not a listed holiday, so a listed holiday is skipped and does not use up a day of turnaround. The policy due date is the day that falls on the last counted day. Then count how many of the three due dates stated in the candidate reply are the same as the policy due date for their document. Ignore any holiday handling or counting in the reply's own wording; only the desk policy counts.
criteria: None: none of the three stated dates matches its policy due date
Low: exactly one of the three stated dates matches its policy due date
Partial: exactly two of the three stated dates match their policy due dates
Full: all three stated dates match their policy due dates

q2.instructions: Under the desk policy, document A (birth certificate) is due on 11 May 2026.

criteria.true: The policy due date for document A, computed from the logged request under the counting and cutoff rules, is 11 May 2026.
criteria.false: The policy due date for document A, computed under the counting and cutoff rules, is any date other than 11 May 2026.

q3.instructions: Which clock-start basis does the desk policy require for this request?

criteria.logged_day_start: Counting starts from the calendar day the request was logged, whatever the time of logging.
criteria.calendar_day_count: Counting uses calendar days, so weekends and holidays are included in the count.
criteria.following_monday_start: Counting starts from the first Monday after the request is logged.
criteria.cutoff_next_working_day: Requests logged after the daily cutoff are treated as received on the next working day, and counting starts after that day.
criteria.client_named_start: Counting starts from whatever date the client names as the start.

q4.instructions: Rate how many working days the reply's stated due date for document C falls before the policy due date for document C. The policy due date is the one the desk policy yields for document C's category, counted from the day the request is treated as received. Start counting from the day after the stated date and stop at the policy due date, which is counted. Only Monday to Friday days that are not listed holidays count as working days. Weekend days are not counted, and a listed holiday is skipped, not counted. The stated date itself is not counted. Choose the level that matches this count.
criteria: None: the stated date is the same as the policy date
Minor: exactly one working day separates the stated date from the policy date
Moderate: exactly two working days separate the stated date from the policy date
Large: three or four working days separate the stated date from the policy date
Severe: five or more working days separate the stated date from the policy date

q5.instructions: The candidate reply's stated due date for document B is later than the policy due date for document B.

criteria.true: The stated due date for document B falls after the policy due date for document B.
criteria.false: The stated due date for document B is the same as or earlier than the policy due date for document B.

A medical declaration is valid up to and including 12 months after declaredOn.

criteria.general_period: The standard 12-month validity period that applies to members in general.

q4.instructions: Rate the member's attendance margin for the entry in the record. Step 1: Take the entry closing date. The counting window is the eight-week span (56 consecutive days) that ends on and includes that closing date. Both the first and last days of the span count as inside it. Step 2: Count the attendance-log entries whose date falls inside that window and whose status is exactly 'attended'. Entries with any other status (such as 'cancelled') do not count, and entries dated outside the window do not count. Step 3: Required = the minimum number of attended sessions that the club's attendance rule sets for entries closing on or after the start of April. Step 4: Margin = counted sessions minus required. Choose the single band that contains the margin.
criteria: none: margin is zero or below
slight: margin is exactly one

comfortable: margin is four or five

Policy_Clauses.Text: Cover applies to crops sown within the Term and damaged by an insured peril during the Term.

Policy_Clauses.Text: A hail-only loss on a field is payable where the assessed loss is at least 30 per cent of expected yield for that field. Assessed loss is measured against the expected yield recorded for the field.

Policy_Clauses.Text: A frost-only loss on a field is payable where the assessed loss is at least 15 per cent of expected yield for that field.

Policy_Clauses.Text: Payment is calculated on the scheduled area of the field, unless a boundary survey dated on or after the date of the loss event is on file for that field. Where such a survey is on file, the surveyed area replaces the scheduled area for payment purposes.

KOUXDRARTIX QUOTA DESK
MEMO QD-2026-014
issued: 2026-01-09
from: Quimia Vosmore, Quota Desk Lead <quimia.vosmore@kouxdrartix-desk.example>
to: skippers registered with the Rerplesis Fleet Association, Braickwold and Stustow ports
subject: cod quota allocation, swaps, landing records and carry-over for quota year 2026
classification: operational, not for onward circulation

1. PURPOSE
1.1 This memo sets out how the demersal cod quota held by coastal vessels is allocated, swapped, recorded and carried forward for the 2026 quota year. All tonnages are in metric tonnes. The vessel register in section 5 gives base allocations. The landing log in section 7 is the only landing record the Quota Desk uses for year-end calculations.
1.2 Where this memo and a later written notice from the Quota Desk differ on a point, the later notice governs. Notices are sent by e-mail to the distribution list and are filed in section 8.

2. DEFINITIONS
These definitions narrow the ordinary meaning of the terms used in sections 3 to 7. Where a term appears in those sections it has the meaning given here and no other.
2.1 allocation: the cod tonnage held by a vessel for a quota year, calculated as base-allocation plus approved swaps in, less approved swaps out. A swap counts only once its status in the swap register reads approved. A swap that is pending, withdrawn or refused counts for nothing.
2.2 landed-weight: the net weight entered in the net field of a landing declaration, after deduction of ice and box weight. Gross weight is never used in any quota calculation.
2.3 unused-allocation: allocation at 31 December less the total landed-weight of landings dated within the same quota year. A landing dated in one quota year belongs only to that quota year, even if it is entered on the log later. If the result is below zero, the unused-allocation is nil.
2.4 active-vessel: a vessel with at least one landing dated within the quota year. A vessel that is registered but has not landed in the quota year is not active.
2.5 cap-base: the allocation of a vessel at 31 December of the quota year, as defined in 2.1. It is not the base-allocation alone.
2.6 rounding: tonnages are recorded to two decimal places. Cap amounts are calculated exactly, without rounding, and are then compared with the unused-allocation as recorded to two decimal places.

3. CARRY-OVER
3.1 An active vessel may carry forward part of its unused-allocation into the next quota year. The amount carried is limited to a cap, which is a percentage of the vessel's cap-base.
3.2 For the 2026 year-end the cap percentage is 10.00 percent of cap-base.
3.3 Any unused-allocation above the cap is returned to the reserve at 31 December and cannot be carried forward.
3.4 Observer-penalty exception. A vessel whose observer-penalty entry in the vessel register reads recorded forfeits all carry-over for that year, and all of its unused-allocation returns to the reserve. A vessel whose entry reads none is not affected by this exception.
3.5 Carried tonnage is charged against the next year's allocation and is shown as a separate line in the vessel register.
3.6 Carry-over is calculated on the register and landing log as they stand at 31 December. Earlier snapshots are not used.

OFFICE MEMORANDUM

Memo Date: 2026-05-12
Subject: Length measurement, speed rule and lay-by stay for the motor cruiser Lark (Fleet Ref BX-4410)

1. Purpose and Versions
This memo answers a booking enquiry from Dixett Thoxby, received 2026-05-09, and sets out which version of the Cligate River Navigation Bylaws governs the matters raised. Version A is the Cligate Bylaws 2025, in force from 2025-04-01. Version B is Amendment Order 2026/2, made 2026-04-20 and effective 2026-06-01. Version B changes Sections 2 and 4 only; Section 6 is unchanged.

2. Definitions
2.1 Length (Version A): the length of the hull from stem to stern post, excluding any bowsprit, pulpit, bathing platform or outboard bracket.
2.2 Length (Version B): the overall length, including any bowsprit, pulpit, bathing platform or outboard bracket, but excluding a detachable tender carried on davits and excluding the rudder.
2.3 Restricted Length Craft: any craft whose Length, measured under the version that governs the relevant event, is more than 14.0 metres.
2.4 Governing Version: an act, passage or mooring is governed by the version in force on the date on which it begins. A mooring that begins before an effective date stays under the earlier version for its whole duration, even if it runs past that date.
2.5 Hull Measurement: hull length is taken in a straight line along the centreline on the water, to the nearest 0.1 metre.

3. Speed on the Stourthaven Reach
3.1 Version A: a Restricted Length Craft must not exceed 6 knots through water between Post A and Post D. All other craft: 8 knots.
3.2 Version B: a Restricted Length Craft must not exceed 5 knots through water between Post A and Post D. All other craft remain at 8 knots.
3.3 The Harbour Master may impose a temporary limit of 4 knots during a flood warning. Flood warning FW-07 for the Stourthaven Reach was cancelled on 2026-05-28. No other flood warning is recorded for the reach.

4. Cligate Lay-by (Section 6 of Version A, unchanged by Version B)
4.1 A craft may moor at the Cligate Lay-by for up to seven nights without written consent.
4.2 A night is counted as each midnight that falls between the time of arrival and the time of departure.
4.3 A stay longer than seven nights requires the written consent of the Harbour Master.

Requested departure from Cligate Lay-by: 4 June 2026, 09:00

6. Other Notices and Records
6.1 Cligate Lay-by closed for dredging 2026-06-15 to 2026-06-19. No bookings currently held are affected.
6.2 Wouxhaven lock closed 2026-07-01 for gate maintenance; the Stourthaven Reach is not affected.

6.4 Prior booking LB-2025-0902 (vessel Heron, Fleet Ref BX-2207) at the lay-by, 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-03, closed with no issues recorded.

subj: Solo time caps, log corrections and one held entry (students Drorham and Quiworth)

1. PURPOSE AND BACKGROUND
The Standards Panel asked for this review at its meeting on 2026-03-05, after the external auditor noted that some February logs had been checked against a cap that was no longer the right one for the month in question. This memo sets out how the solo time cap in Policy P-4 applies to the logs of two students for February and March 2026, records the log corrections received since the February close, and gives the position on one entry that cannot yet be posted. The Sondholm Annex logs are not covered; they follow procedure SA-11, which this memo does not change. Dates are written year-month-day throughout. Flight instructors are responsible for filing any correction to crew occupancy themselves; the records office does not amend occupancy from memory or from the flight desk diary.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 Solo sortie. A solo sortie is a flight on which the student is the sole occupant of the aircraft and no instructor is on board in any seat. A flight with an instructor on board is never a solo sortie, even where the instructor does not touch the controls. A flight with another student on board as an observer is also not a solo sortie.
2.2 Solo time. Solo time is the sum of the durations of a student's solo sorties, added in minutes. Solo time is never rounded before a cap or a band is applied. Where this memo states a figure in hours, multiply by 60 to get minutes.
2.3 Calendar month. A calendar month runs from 00:00 on the first day of the month to 23:59 on the last day, in local time at Dymthorpe Airfield. A sortie belongs to the month of its flight date, not the date on which it was logged.
2.4 Stage 4 or above. A student is at stage 4 or above when the stage record in the student file shows stage 4, 5 or 6. A student at stage 3 or below is not at stage 4 or above, whatever the training plan says.
2.5 Dual instruction. A dual instruction sortie is a flight with an instructor on board, logged in the dual column. Dual instruction does not count toward solo time or any solo cap. Simulator sessions are logged in a separate column and are not flights for this purpose.

3. POLICY P-4, MONTHLY SOLO TIME CAP
3.1 Version 2 of P-4 applied from 2025-09-01. It set the monthly cap at 12 hours of solo time per student per calendar month. Version 2 governs any calendar month that begins before 2026-03-01.
3.2 Version 3 of P-4 was approved by the Standards Panel on 2026-02-24 and takes effect on 2026-03-01. It sets the monthly cap at 15 hours of solo time per student per calendar month. Version 3 governs any calendar month that begins on or after 2026-03-01. It is not applied to February 2026 or to any earlier month.
3.3 A draft version 2.5, which proposed a cap of 14 hours, was withdrawn before the Panel vote and was never adopted. It has no effect on any log or any student.
3.4 Exception. A student at stage 4 or above may exceed the monthly cap only where the Chief Flight Instructor has recorded written approval in the student file before the sortie that takes the total above the cap. Approval recorded for one calendar month does not carry over to any other month. A student at stage 3 or below has no exception.
3.5 Held sorties. Where a solo sortie would take a student's solo time for the calendar month above the cap, and no written approval under 3.4 is on file at the time of that sortie, the whole sortie is held. A held sortie is not posted to any month, is not split between months, and is not moved to a later month. It stays on the held list until the Chief Flight Instructor records a decision. Reclassification is made only under section 4, never to avoid the cap.
3.6 The monthly summary sheet is prepared by the records officer from posted entries only. Held sorties do not appear on the monthly summary sheet.

4. LOG CORRECTIONS
4.1 The crew sheet is the primary record of who was on board. Where a log entry and the crew sheet disagree, the crew sheet governs, unless a written correction from the instructor on that sortie is filed and then confirmed in writing by the Chief Flight Instructor.
4.2 A correction is dated by the day it is filed. It applies to the original flight, not to the day of filing.
4.3 Where two corrections for the same sortie conflict, the later one that the Chief Flight Instructor has confirmed governs.
4.4 A correction changes who was on board or the category of a sortie. It does not change the recorded duration of a sortie.

5. STUDENT STATUS AT THIS REVIEW
5.1 Tunys Drorham: stage 3 (Advanced Basics). The exception in 3.4 is not available to this student.
5.2 Thartie Quiworth: stage 4 (Advanced Handling). A written approval under 3.4 was recorded in the file on 2026-02-20 and covers February 2026 only. As at the date of this memo, no approval for March 2026 has been recorded in the file.
5.3 Stage names for reference: 1 Familiarisation; 2 Basic handling; 3 Advanced Basics; 4 Advanced Handling; 5 Navigation; 6 Pre-licence check.
5.4 Stage changes take effect on the date the Chief Flight Instructor signs the stage record. No stage change is pending for either student at the date of this memo.
