domain: certified winter barley seed lot eligibility under germination retest and off-type field rules

Scheme Rules.Subject: Scope and day counting
Scheme Rules.Text: This scheme covers certified-class winter barley seed grown on holdings registered with the Skandterton Seed Board. Every period stated in this scheme is counted in calendar days unless it says otherwise.

Scheme Rules.Subject: Germination minimum
Scheme Rules.Text: For the Certified class, a lot must show a laboratory germination result of at least 85 per cent on a sample drawn from the lot. A result below 85 per cent does not qualify unless it is replaced by an accepted retest under clause SC-3.4. No amendment has changed this minimum since 2025-09-01.

Scheme Rules.Subject: Retest of a lot
Scheme Rules.Text: A lot whose first germination result is below the minimum may be re-tested once. The retest sample must be drawn no later than the 30th calendar day after the date of the first germination test. The day of the first test is not counted, so the 30th day after it is the last permitted day. The date the retest sample is drawn, not the date it is tested, decides whether it is within the period. A retest sample drawn after the last permitted day is not accepted, and the lot is rejected. An accepted retest result replaces the first result for every purpose in this scheme.

Scheme Rules.Subject: Off-type limit, Certified class
Scheme Rules.Text: A certified-class field passes the off-type standard when the number of off-type plants found, multiplied by 1,000 and divided by the number of plants inspected, is no more than 4. The result is compared exactly, without rounding, and a result exactly equal to 4 passes. This version governs field inspections carried out before 2026-02-01.

Scheme Rules.Subject: Off-type limit, Certified class
Scheme Rules.Replaces: SC-4.2 Version 1, for field inspections carried out on or after 2026-02-01
Scheme Rules.Text: Under this version a certified-class field passes the off-type standard when the number of off-type plants found, multiplied by 1,000 and divided by the number of plants inspected, is no more than 3. The result is compared exactly, without rounding, and a result exactly equal to 3 passes. Inspections carried out before 2026-02-01 are not re-assessed under this version.

Scheme Rules.Subject: Source field eligibility
Scheme Rules.Text: A lot is eligible for certification only when both of the following conditions are met. The first is that the field it was sampled from passed the off-type standard in force on that field's inspection date. The second is that the lot's germination result, or its accepted retest result, meets clause SC-3.1. Meeting one condition does not satisfy the other.

Scheme Rules.Subject: Isolation distance
Scheme Rules.Text: A certified-class field must be isolated by at least 200 metres from other cereal fields of a different variety. The isolation distance is recorded for the file and is not part of the off-type standard in clause SC-4.2.

Scheme Rules.Subject: Trial plots
Scheme Rules.Text: Trial plots sown for variety evaluation are outside the certification scheme. They carry no off-type limit, and no lot may be drawn from them.

From: Thisys Ruclonhurst, Site Operations, Ceallwold Events Trust
To: All food vendors, Thurtstow Lantern Festival 2026

Section 1: Dates and access
1.1 Vendors trade only from the pitch allocated on their VF-7 form, unless a later written notice from the organiser changes the allocation.
1.2 The festival runs from Friday 14 August to Sunday 16 August 2026, inclusive. These three days are the trading days. Thursday 13 August is a set-up day for access and marking out. It is not a trading day.

2.1 A food hygiene rating certificate must be lodged 21 days before the first trading day.
2.2 A public liability certificate with cover of at least £5 million must reach the organiser no later than 30 days before the first trading day.
2.3 Certificates may be lodged through the vendor portal. A lodgement is recorded on the date shown in the portal history.

3.1 Each standard pitch is 3 metres across the frontage and 4 metres deep, marked with white paint.
3.2 Zones are labelled A to F on the site plan. Zone letters are not reused between years.
3.3 Pitch changes are notified in writing and take effect from the date of the notice.

4.1 Every pitch includes a standard single-phase 16A supply at no extra charge.
4.2 Upgrades to single-phase 32A, three-phase 32A or three-phase 63A may be requested on form VF-7. An upgrade is granted only when the site power manager confirms it in writing for the specific pitch, subject to the capacity of the zone's distribution board.
4.3 Vendor-owned generators are not permitted in Zones A, B or C.

Section 5: Trading hours
5.1 Every stall must stop trading at its closing time, which is 23:00 on every festival day, unless a later amendment sets a different time for a zone.
5.2 Festival gates close at 23:30 each night. Gate closing is not a trading time, and stalls must still stop trading at their closing time.
5.3 Set-up and break-down may take place outside trading hours on the days shown in clause 1.2 only.

Section 6: Gas, waste and fire
6.1 LPG appliances must have a fire blanket and a dry powder extinguisher within reach of the cooking area.
6.2 Up to four 13 kg LPG cylinders per stall may be kept on site, stored in approved caged storage at the rear of the pitch.
6.3 Cooking oil and grease must be collected in vendor-supplied containers and removed from site by the vendor.

Section 7: Amendments
7.1 The organiser may amend these terms by numbered amendment notice. Each notice states which clause it replaces and for which zones, if any. Clauses that are not replaced stay in force.

Section 8: Conduct
8.1 Pitches must be kept free of litter at all times. Vendors clear their own pitch area at the end of each trading day.
8.2 No amplified sound may be used on any pitch without written consent from the organiser.
8.3 Vendors must display current certificates at the pitch when asked by a steward.

5.1 Notice. The insured must notify the Scheme of hail damage within 72 clock hours of the time the insured first becomes aware of it. 5.2 Late notice. A notification made after the period in 5.1 has ended is not accepted, unless clause 5.3 applies.
5.3 Outage exception. Clause 5.2 does not apply where the Scheme's outage log records a reporting-line outage that covers some part of the last 12 clock hours of the period in 5.1. An outage that ends before those last 12 hours begin, or that starts after the period has ended, does not qualify.
6.2 Threshold. A hail claim on a field is payable only where the assessed damage is at or above the threshold percentage in force on the loss date. The threshold is the figure in the schedule, as replaced by any endorsement that has taken effect.
6.3 Assessment. Assessed damage is the arithmetic mean of the sample row percentages, expressed as a percentage of expected yield to one decimal place. A written revision to a sample row replaces the earlier figure for that row only.
8.1 Payment. Where a claim is accepted, the Scheme first works out the expected crop value of the field: insured hectares x expected yield (t/ha) x unit price (GBP/t). 8.2 Excess. A fixed sum per field per claim, as set by the schedule or by the endorsement in force on the loss date.

policy.tolerance_definition: Overshoot is counted landings minus available quota, expressed as a share of available quota. definitions.reach: The stretch of river between Callbury Gauge Post and Skurtcomham Weir, as marked in Schedule A. Side channels, lock cuts and mooring basins are not part of the reach.
definitions.draught: The vertical distance from the waterline to the lowest fixed point of the hull, plus the projection of any retractable keel that is in the lowered position at the time of transit. A retractable keel in the retracted position is disregarded.
definitions.low-water-period: 1 June to 30 September, both days included.
definitions.date-of-transit: The calendar date on which the vessel enters the reach at its entry gauge post.

ROUTE SURVEY MEMO
To: Cynys Wasfalock, Route Cards Editor
From: Quairan Lyrtton, Surveys Officer, Mastuis Upland Trust
Contact: q.lyrtton@mastuistrust.example
Memo Date: 9 February 2026
Subject: Grading inputs for the Skusness Ridge Loop (Route Ref SR-7)

Cynys,

Please prepare the printed route card for the Skusness Ridge Loop (Route Ref SR-7) from the survey figures below. The survey was walked on 3 February 2026 by Drairon Kolldroley and Trylline Pistead. The team used two instruments, so some leg lengths are in kilometres and others in miles, and some leg ascents are in metres and others in feet. Section C gives the conversion factors and the grading rules. Please apply them exactly as written.

SECTION A: LEG RECORDS
The loop starts and ends at the Tirthorpe car park (CP1). Legs are listed in the direction of travel. Ascent is the climb recorded for that leg; descents are not recorded.

Leg 1 | CP1 (Tirthorpe car park) to CP2 | Length: 2.8 km | Ascent: 160 m | Hazard Flags: none
Leg 2 | CP2 to CP3 (the Col) | Length: 1.9 mi | Ascent: 1,410 ft | Hazard Flags: exposed ledge; loose scree
Leg 3 | CP3 to CP4 (summit cairn) | Length: 1.1 km | Ascent: 240 m | Hazard Flags: scramble section; exposed ledge
Leg 4 | CP4 to CP5 | Length: 3.4 km | Ascent: 40 m | Hazard Flags: none
Leg 5 | CP5 to CP6 | Length: 2.2 mi | Ascent: 530 ft | Hazard Flags: stream crossing
Leg 6 | CP6 to CP1 | Length: 1.6 km | Ascent: 85 m | Hazard Flags: none

SECTION B: EXCLUDED AND OTHER NOTES
- Route Shortcut S-2 links CP2 and CP5 directly. It is not part of SR-7 and must be left out of every figure. Its own survey gives 0.9 km, 300 m of ascent and an exposure flag.
- Leg 4 was re-walked on 5 February 2026 after a fence was moved. Its length and ascent were unchanged.
- The gate at CP6 was repaired on 20 January 2026 and is open.
- Car park charge at Tirthorpe: £4.50 per day, unchanged since 2024.
- Replacement waymarker quote from Stubanell Path Works: 14 posts at £38 each, delivery not included.
- Trail counter reading for the 2025 season: 2,140 counted crossings at CP1.

SECTION C: CONVERSION AND GRADING RULES
1. 1 mile = 1.61 km. 1 foot = 0.305 m. Convert every leg before adding.
2. Route length is the sum of the six legs in kilometres.
3. Route ascent is the sum of the six leg ascents in metres.
4. A leg is hazard-flagged if it has a scramble section, an exposed ledge or loose scree. A stream crossing is not a hazard flag.
5. Hazard share is the combined length of hazard-flagged legs divided by route length, shown as a percentage.
6. Estimated walking time in hours is route length in km divided by 4, plus route ascent in metres divided by 400.
7. Leg grade is set by that leg's ascent in metres: under 300 m is green; 300 m or more but under 500 m is blue; 500 m or more but under 800 m is red; 800 m or more is black.
8. A scramble section raises the leg grade by one step (green to blue, blue to red, red to black; black stays black). No other flag changes a leg grade.

Please send the finished card text to me by 13 February 2026 so the print run can be booked. The route notes are in the shared folder under Mastuis Upland Trust / Route Cards / SR-7.

Thanks,
Quairan

1.1 Isolation distance means the shortest distance in metres, measured on the ground, from the sown edge of the certified crop to the sown edge of any other barley crop of a different variety or seed class. state.policy-late-review-rule: Returns are reviewed over the window running from the window-start date to the check date, both days included. A return is late when it is checked in after its due date. A return checked in on its due date is on time.

domain: fishing quota rules: vessel monthly landing caps and carry-over

state.Units_Note: Landed weights are keyed by the port clerk in kilograms or tonnes. Caps and carry limits are in tonnes. Weights are converted at 1 t = 1000 kg and kept to three decimal places with no further rounding.

Vessel.Sister_Hull_Note: Vessel LQ-4471 is held by a different owner and is not covered by this extract.

Rule_Versions.Cap_Scope: Per vessel, per stock, per area, per calendar month

Carry_Over.Condition: An Active electronic monitoring certificate covers the last calendar day of the month in which the unused balance arises
Carry_Over.Treatment: The unused balance carries in full when it does not exceed the carry cap. When it exceeds the carry cap, only the carry cap amount carries and the excess lapses.

Rule_Versions.Counting: Landings count in the calendar month of their Landing_Date. Entries with Status voided_duplicate are not counted.

Policy_Text.Section_4_1: Version 2 applies to every landing whose Landing_Date is on or after its Effective_From date. Landings dated before that date remain under the previous version.
Policy_Text.Section_4_2: Unused balance for a month equals the applicable monthly cap minus the counted landings for the same vessel, stock and area in that month.
Policy_Text.Section_4_3: The applicable monthly cap is the Default_Monthly_Cap of the version in force, unless an Authority notice names the same vessel, stock, area and month and sets a cap. Where more than one notice covers the same vessel, stock, area and month, the notice with the latest Issued_On date applies and earlier notices for that month are withdrawn.
Policy_Text.Section_4_4: Notices affect only the month they name. They do not change the carry cap, the carry condition or the default caps.
Policy_Text.Section_4_5: Carried balances move from the month in which they arise into the ledger of the next calendar month for the same vessel, stock and area.
Policy_Text.Section_4_6: A period given as from one date to another includes both of those dates.

q2.instructions: The vessel's counted April 2026 haddock landings in Area C7 are greater than the applicable April 2026 haddock cap for Area C7.

criteria.true: The counted April landings in that area exceed the applicable cap for that month.
criteria.false: The counted April landings in that area are equal to or below the applicable cap for that month.

q3.instructions: Which treatment applies to the unused balance of the vessel's April 2026 haddock allowance in Area C7 when it moves into the May 2026 ledger?

criteria.no_carry_forward: Nothing from the unused balance moves into the next month's ledger.
criteria.carry_fixed_cap_amount: A fixed carry cap amount moves forward whatever the size of the unused balance.
criteria.carry_half_of_unused: Half of the unused balance moves into the next month's ledger.
criteria.carry_in_full: The whole unused balance moves into the next month's ledger under the carry-over rule.
criteria.carry_after_approval: The unused balance moves forward only after written approval from the issuing body.
criteria.carry_if_no_certificate: The unused balance moves forward only when no monitoring certificate covers the last day of the month.

q4.instructions: Rate the vessel's total counted haddock landings in Area C7 for the period from 1 March 2026 to 30 April 2026, with both dates included, in tonnes.
criteria: Under 10 tonnes
10 tonnes or more, but under 15 tonnes
15 tonnes or more, but under 20 tonnes
20 tonnes or more

check.q1: Counted April 2026 haddock in Area C7 for LQ-4417: LE-88170 4310 kg + LE-88181 2.800 t + LE-88190 1950 kg = 4.310 + 2.800 + 1.950 = 9.060 t; LE-88177 is voided and excluded; applicable cap is 9.5 t from N-26-023, which corrects and withdraws N-26-017 for this vessel, stock, area and month; 9.060 / 9.5 = 95.4% -> 90% or more -> High

check.q3: April unused balance = 9.5 t applicable cap - 9.060 t counted = 0.440 t; carry cap 0.5 t; 0.440 does not exceed 0.5, so the whole balance carries; EM-0118 is Active from 2026-04-01 to 2026-12-31 and covers 2026-04-30, so the carry condition is met -> carry_in_full

q1.instructions: Rate the candidate answer's accuracy on its stated cover start basis and the in-warranty conclusion, judged against the terms and the dates in the state.

1: The stated start basis contradicts the terms but the stated in-warranty conclusion is right
2: The stated start basis matches the terms but the start date given is not the one the terms yield
3: The stated start basis and start date match the terms but the stated end date does not
4: The stated start basis, start date and end date all match the terms

q2.instructions: The end date the candidate gives for cover is correct.

criteria.true: The candidate's stated end date equals the end date the terms produce from the dates in the state.
criteria.false: The candidate's stated end date differs from the end date the terms produce from the dates in the state.

q3.instructions: Where does the candidate's reasoning first depart from the terms?

criteria.claim_date_misread: The candidate gets the date the claim was lodged wrong.
criteria.decision_wrong: The candidate's in-warranty decision conflicts with the terms and dates.
criteria.end_arithmetic_only: The candidate's start basis is right and the only departure is the arithmetic that produces the end date.
criteria.start_rule_wrong: The candidate's stated basis for the cover start conflicts with the start rule in the terms.

q4.instructions: The candidate's decision that the compressor claim falls within warranty is correct.

criteria.true: The claim date lies inside the cover period that the terms give from the fitting date.
criteria.false: The claim date lies outside the cover period that the terms give from the fitting date.

criteria.sale_date: The date the unit was sold to the customer.
criteria.fitting_date: The date the unit was installed, as the terms define the start of cover.
criteria.registration_date: The date the customer registered the unit online.
criteria.manufacture_date: The date the unit was made.
criteria.claim_date: The date the warranty claim was lodged.

state.log_clock_basis: Check-in and check-out times are recorded in UTC. The market trades on local clock time, which is UTC+01:00 on the trading date.
state.contribution_rule: Contribution for one night equals the full session contribution multiplied by the staffed minutes divided by the full session minutes, rounded to the nearest penny. Staffed minutes run from check-in to check-out.

state.site_notes: Lurtdylock Lighting checked the row power at 19:10 local time. No stall moved pitch during the trading date.

q1.instructions: Rate the length of this stall's continuous staffed span on the trading date, from check-in to check-out, as a duration.
criteria: short: under 3 hours
medium: at least 3 hours but under 5 hours
long: 5 hours or more

q2.instructions: The stall's staffed span started on one calendar day in local market time and ended on the following calendar day in local market time.

criteria.true: The local start and the local end of the span fall on different calendar dates.
criteria.false: The local start and the local end of the span fall on the same calendar date.

q3.instructions: Into which band does the pro-rata site contribution for this night fall?

criteria.120_to_140: A contribution of at least 120.00 GBP but less than 140.00 GBP.
criteria.under_120: A contribution of less than 120.00 GBP.
criteria.over_140: A contribution of 140.00 GBP or more.

q4.instructions: Rate the stall's staffed span as a percentage of the full session length for one night.
criteria: minimal: under 25 percent of the full session
partial: 25 percent or more but under 50 percent of the full session
substantial: 50 percent or more but under 75 percent of the full session
near_full: 75 percent or more of the full session

q5.instructions: The stall's staffed span ended before 02:00 local market time on the calendar day after check-in.

criteria.true: The local check-out time is earlier than 02:00 on the day after check-in.
criteria.false: The local check-out time is 02:00 or later on the day after check-in.

check.q1: Check-in 2026-05-08T20:40Z = 21:40 local (UTC+01:00); check-out 2026-05-09T01:15Z = 02:15 local; 21:40 to 02:15 = 4 h 35 min; pauses logged: none; 4 h 35 min is at least 3 h and under 5 h -> medium (index 1)
check.q2: Local check-in 2026-05-08 21:40; local check-out 2026-05-09 02:15; the two calendar dates differ (8 May and 9 May) -> true
check.q3: Staffed minutes = 21:40 to 02:15 local = 275 min; 240.00 x 275 / 480 = 137.50 exactly (rounding not needed); 137.50 is at least 120.00 and less than 140.00 -> 120_to_140
check.q4: Staffed minutes 275 / full session 480 = 0.5729 = 57.29 percent; 57.29 is 50 or more and under 75 -> substantial (index 2)
check.q5: Local check-out 2026-05-09 02:15 (01:15 UTC + 1 h); 02:15 is not earlier than 02:00 -> false

domain: sweet cherry block yield grading for packhouse lots

state.Packhouse Channel Rule: Rejected share below 5%: export chain. 5% to below 10%: domestic fresh. 10% to below 15%: juice processing. 15% or more: destroy lot. Rejected share = rejected sample fruit divided by sample fruit counted.
state.Notes: Block picked in three passes; the third pass was delayed by rain. Sample fruit was drawn evenly across all passes. Spring audit date to be set by the grader.

q1.instructions: Rate the block's yield per hectare, counting only accepted crates (crates picked minus crates rejected at intake) at net crate weight.
criteria: Very low: under 6,000 kg per hectare
Low: 6,000 to under 9,000 kg per hectare
Moderate: 9,000 to under 12,000 kg per hectare
High: 12,000 to under 15,000 kg per hectare
Very high: 15,000 kg per hectare or more

q2.instructions: Rate the premium share of the counted sample, where the share is premium class fruit divided by total sample fruit counted.
criteria: Low: under 60%
Mid: 60% to under 75%
High: 75% to under 85%
Top: 85% or more

q3.instructions: The assessment date falls fewer than 10 calendar days after the harvest end date, counting the later date minus the earlier date.

criteria.true: The later date minus the harvest end date is less than 10 calendar days.
criteria.false: The later date minus the harvest end date is 10 or more calendar days.

q4.instructions: Rate the mean soluble solids of the block's sample, averaging all Brix readings, in degrees Brix.
criteria: Low: under 14.0 degrees Brix
Fair: 14.0 to under 16.0 degrees Brix
Good: 16.0 to under 18.0 degrees Brix
Very good: 18.0 to under 20.0 degrees Brix
Excellent: 20.0 degrees Brix or more

q5.instructions: Which dispatch channel does the lot's rejected-fruit share place it in under the packhouse channel rule?

criteria.export_chain: Sent to the export chain, which the channel rule assigns to the lowest rejected-share band.
criteria.destroy_lot: Destroyed without sale, which the channel rule assigns to the highest rejected-share band.
criteria.domestic_fresh: Sold as fresh fruit to the domestic market, which the channel rule assigns to a middle rejected-share band.
criteria.juice_processing: Diverted to juice processing, which the channel rule assigns to an upper-middle rejected-share band.
criteria.hold_for_recount: Held in the packhouse until the sample is counted again, used only when the sample count is in dispute.

q6.instructions: Rate the combined cracked and bird-pecked share of the defect sample, where the share is the total of those two defect counts divided by the defect sample size.
criteria: Low: under 4%
Moderate: 4% to under 7%
High: 7% to under 10%
Severe: 10% or more

check.q1: Crates picked 1650 - rejected at intake 50 = 1600 accepted crates; 1600 x 5.5 kg net = 8,800 kg; 8,800 / 0.8 ha = 11,000 kg per hectare; 9,000 to under 12,000 -> Moderate
check.q2: Premium class fruit 360 / sample fruit counted 500 = 0.72 = 72%; 60% to under 75% -> Mid
check.q3: Harvest end 2026-06-24 to assessment 2026-07-01: 30 - 24 = 6 days to 2026-06-30, plus 1 = 7 days; 7 is less than 10 -> true
check.q5: Rejected sample fruit 45 / sample fruit counted 500 = 0.09 = 9.0%; 5% to below 10% is the domestic fresh band -> domestic_fresh
check.q6: Cracked 12 + bird pecked 7 = 19 defective fruit; 19 / 250 = 0.076 = 7.6%; 7% to under 10% -> High

state:
SIMULATOR SESSION ALLOCATION MEMO
Norfexell Pilot Training Academy, Fralport campus
Document ref: SSA-FR-2026-07
Issued by: Pourtan Plurthurst, Simulator Scheduling Manager
Governing policy: Simulator Booking Policy SBP-4 (issued 12 January 2026), as amended by Amendment 2 (effective 6 April 2026)

1. PURPOSE
This memo sets out how simulator time is allocated to trainee pilots at the Fralport campus, how the weekly cap is measured, and how logged times are corrected. It covers the two full-motion simulators in Bay 3 and Bay 4 and the procedures trainer in Bay 1. The Maswold and Durwych campuses operate under their own booking policy and are not covered by this memo.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 'Week' means a calendar week running from Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59, local time. A session is placed in the week that contains its start date.
2.2 'Device time' means the minutes from the device-on time to the device-off time recorded in the simulator log for one session.
2.3 'Counted time' means device time less any briefing or debriefing minutes that the log records as falling inside that device time. Briefing or debriefing held outside device time is never counted and is never deducted.
2.4 'Cap' means the maximum counted time permitted for one trainee in one week. Counted time equal to the cap is permitted. Counted time is above the cap only when it is greater than the cap.

3. BOOKING RULES
3.1 Sessions are requested through the sim desk at least 24 hours in advance.
3.2 A trainee may not be booked onto two devices at the same time.
3.3 Instructor-led sessions take priority over self-study bookings for the same bay.
3.4 A booking is confirmed only when the trainee's instructor has signed the session plan.
3.5 A cancellation received less than six hours before the booked start is recorded as a late cancellation. A late cancellation creates no device time and no counted time, and the slot is offered to the waiting list in order of request.
3.6 Bay 1 procedures trainer bookings are made on the same terms as Bays 3 and 4, but the trainer is not a full-motion device and its entries are logged separately.

4. WEEKLY CAP
4.1 Each trainee has a weekly cap on counted time, set by Section 4.2.
4.2 The weekly cap is 12.0 hours of counted time per trainee per week.
4.3 The cap is reviewed once per term by the Training Standards Group. Any change takes effect only through a numbered amendment to this policy.
4.4 A trainee who reaches the cap in a week may still attend instructor-led briefings and debriefings held outside device time, but may not occupy a device.

5. LOGGING AND CORRECTIONS
5.1 Instructors enter device-on time, device-off time, and any briefing or debriefing minutes inside device time at the end of each session.
5.2 A written correction notice from the sim desk replaces the logged time it names for the session it identifies. No other person may alter a logged time.
5.3 Device-on and device-off times are recorded to the nearest minute. Briefing and debriefing minutes are recorded in whole minutes as they are given to the trainee.
5.4 Log extracts are issued to instructors each Thursday at 17:00 and are marked as at the time of issue.

6. AMENDMENT 2 (effective 6 April 2026)
6.1 Section 4.2 is replaced by the following: For any week beginning on or after 6 April 2026, the weekly cap is 10.5 hours of counted time per trainee. For any week beginning before 6 April 2026, the cap stated in the original Section 4.2 continues to apply.
6.2 Sections 2, 3 and 5 are not changed by this amendment.

PART A - SCHEME RULES EXTRACT (Issue 4, as amended)

1. Definitions
1.1 Lot: all seed of one variety and one class, sown under a single sowing declaration and presented for grading together.
1.2 Other cereal crop: a sown crop of a different variety or a different class of cereal in the same season. Volunteer plants, grass strips and weed patches are not other cereal crops for any distance check.
1.3 Off-type: a plant that differs from the declared variety in height, ear type or awn character.

2. Sowing deadlines
2.1 A deadline is the last day on which sowing may be completed. The deadline day itself is included.
2.2 Deadlines are those in Table A, as changed by any amendment in force for the sowing declaration concerned.
Table A (Issue 4): spring barley, certified class: 10 May.

3. Isolation
3.1 Isolation distance is measured along the ground, in whole metres, from the sown edge of the lot to the sown edge of the nearest other cereal crop.
3.2 Certified spring barley: minimum isolation distance 50 m.
3.3 Barrier exception: where a permanent barrier at least 2.0 m tall runs continuously along the whole boundary between the lot and the other cereal crop, and the barrier is recorded on the inspection form, the minimum may be reduced to 30 m. A barrier with any gap along that boundary does not qualify.

4. Inspection and off-types
4.1 At least one field inspection is made at flowering. The inspector records the isolation distance and any barrier on the inspection form.
4.2 Off-types are counted on four counts of 1,000 plants each, taken across the inspected area. The four counts are written on the form separately.
4.3 Certified class: an off-type rate up to and including 0.50% of plants counted passes. A rate above 0.50% fails.

5. Sampling
5.1 Sample size is set by net seed weight of the lot, with bag tare and pallets excluded:
    20 tonnes or less: 1.0 kg
    over 20 tonnes up to and including 40 tonnes: 1.5 kg
    over 40 tonnes: 2.0 kg

6. Release
6.1 The Certification Officer releases a lot once the checks in sections 3, 4 and 5 are recorded.
6.2 Where a lot relies on the barrier exception in 3.3, release needs countersignature by the Laboratory Manager as well as the Certification Officer.

domain: touring circus wind contingency planning
state:
RAILLSERIS TOURING CIRCUS - INTERNAL MEMO
Ref: OPS-WX-0342 | Date: 12 March 2026
To: Quuxie Lerhurst, Tour Manager
From: Jyson Gemham, Operations
cc: Faindus Trahurst, Site Engineer; route file RT-14
Subject: Stealmouth week - wind contingency

1. Background
The big top plays on the ring field at Stealmouth from Monday 6 April to Sunday 12 April 2026. The week holds 8 outdoor ring performances.

2. Season record (all venues)
Season 2025: 120 performances scheduled, 9 cancelled because of wind. Season 2024 figures are in file RT-09 and are not needed here.

3. Plockthorpe April record
Across the April weeks of the 2023, 2024 and 2025 seasons at Plockthorpe, 31 outdoor performances were scheduled and 7 were cancelled for wind. Indoor performances in those weeks are excluded from both counts. Rain and fog cancellations (4) are logged as 'weather other' and are not counted here.

4. Planning assumption
For the Stealmouth week, planning uses a 1-in-4 chance that any outdoor performance is lost to wind. Net loss per lost performance is GBP 1,500 (gate after refunds).

5. Options and fixed costs
a) Keep the outdoor schedule with no added measures. No fixed cost.
b) Move all 8 performances into a hired hall in Frourtmouth. Hall hire is GBP 3,600 fixed. The hall seats the same audience, so no wind losses are expected.
c) Buy a wind-loss policy for the week at a premium of GBP 2,700. The policy pays the full net loss on any wind-lost performance, so no wind loss remains.
d) Fit windbreak screens to the ring field at a fixed cost of GBP 900. The screens halve the wind-loss chance for each outdoor performance, so it becomes 1 in 8 under the planning assumption.
e) Drop two outdoor performances from the week, each lost in full at GBP 1,500 net. The other six stay outdoors at the planning assumption.
f) Cancel the whole week with refunds. All 8 performances are lost in full at GBP 1,500 net each; no wind losses arise separately.

6. Decision rule
Choose the option with the lowest total expected cost. Total = fixed cost + expected wind losses. Expected wind losses = outdoor performances still given outdoors x wind-loss chance x GBP 1,500. Performances lost in full under (e) or (f) are costed at GBP 1,500 each, as stated there, and are not counted again as wind losses.

subject: Fymhaven Reach bylaw FR-4, speed rules in the Plurthorpe Cut

1. Purpose
This memo sets out which speed rule applies in the Plurthorpe Cut, a wake-restricted stretch of the Fymhaven Reach, and which version of the bylaw governs each date. Read it together with the registers in sections 5 and 6 and the passage log in section 7.

2. Versions of the bylaw
2.1 Version 1 (bylaw FR-4, made 14 June 2019) set one limit of 8 knots through the Plurthorpe Cut for all vessels. It made no separate provision for towing.
2.2 Amendment 2 replaces section 4 of FR-4 in full. Its effective date is 1 May 2026, and it applies from and including that date.
2.3 A passage through the Plurthorpe Cut before 1 May 2026 is governed by version 1. A passage on or after 1 May 2026 is governed by Amendment 2.

3. Amendment 2, section 4 (signed text)
4.1 Limit by length. Subject to clause 4.3, the limit through the Plurthorpe Cut is:
    (a) 6 knots for a vessel of 12.00 m length overall (LOA) or less;
    (b) 5 knots for a vessel of more than 12.00 m LOA.
4.2 LOA is taken from the Authority's vessel register as at the date of the passage.
4.3 Tow exception. A vessel towing under a written tow permit issued by the Authority is exempt from clause 4.1 for the dates printed on that permit, but must not exceed 8 knots at any point in the cut. A permit covers only the vessel named on it.

3.1 Withdrawn draft. A draft of Amendment 2 circulated on 10 February 2026 gave the tow cap in clause 4.3 as 9 knots. That draft was withdrawn on 2 March 2026 and has no effect. The text in section 3 above is the only authoritative text.

4. Notice and posting
4.1 This memo is issued on the notice date shown in the header. Notice of Amendment 2 was given to operators on that date.
4.2 A copy of this memo was re-posted on the Brilbury Quay notice board on 20 April 2026 for operators who do not read e-mail. The re-posting does not alter any date in this memo.

q4.instructions: Using only the facts in the application record, which outcome should the decision note record? For the parking test, use the standard in force on the decision date: a local plan that was adopted on or before the decision date governs, and a draft plan does not. Assess the off-street provision shown on the current drawing set, for the dwelling as it would be after the works. Count the decision date itself as the date the standard is tested against. Treat any shortfall as one that conditions can cure only if the missing provision can be secured within land or works the applicant controls.

criteria.approve_unconditionally: Grant permission with no conditions attached. Applies only where the proposal meets the parking standard in force on the decision date without any further measures.
criteria.approve_with_conditions: Grant permission subject to planning conditions. Applies only where the proposal meets the parking standard in force on the decision date, or any shortfall can be secured by a condition within the applicant's control.
criteria.defer_for_further_consultation: Hold the decision open while a further round of public consultation runs. Applies only where new material matters require further consultation, which is not the case here.
criteria.refuse_parking_shortfall: Refuse permission because the current drawings show fewer off-street spaces than the parking standard in force on the decision date requires for the dwelling as proposed, and the applicant has confirmed in writing that no revised layout will be submitted and the missing provision depends on land or a boundary the applicant does not control, so neither a condition nor a revised scheme can cure the shortfall.
criteria.request_amended_layout: Ask the applicant for a revised layout and defer the decision until it is received. Applies only where the applicant has not refused to submit a revised layout and a revised layout could still meet the parking standard in force on the decision date.
criteria.close_as_withdrawn: Close the application without a decision because the applicant has formally withdrawn it. Applies only where a written withdrawal has been received; not applicable where the application remains live and has not been withdrawn.

domain: crop insurance production-guarantee loss settlement

scheme.preferred_channel: online portal; post is logged on receipt
scheme.store_approval_note: Only stores on this approved list produce weights that count as harvested production. The list is changed only by written endorsement from the scheme office.

definitions.section_note: The terms below are narrower than their everyday meaning and apply throughout this file.
definitions.harvested_production: Grain weighed across an approved store weighbridge and recorded on an accepted delivery ticket for the insured unit. Grain retained on farm for feed or seed is not harvested production, whatever its weight.
definitions.date_of_loss_event: The calendar date on which the insured peril started, as logged by the nearest weather station. Where an event runs past midnight, the date on which it started is used.
definitions.notice_period: Calendar days counted from the day after the date of loss event. The notice must be received on or before the last counted day. A notice logged on the portal is treated as received on the day it is logged.
definitions.insured_unit: One field listed in the schedule of guarantees, growing one crop type. Parts of one field divided by a public road are separate insured units.
definitions.guaranteed_production: The guaranteed yield per hectare in the schedule of guarantees multiplied by the insured area in hectares, expressed in kilograms. Area-damage estimates do not change it.

state.application_rule: The procedure version and the price schedule that apply to a claim are the ones whose effective dates include the date of loss event. Changes are not applied to earlier losses. Only a written endorsement issued by the scheme office varies the policy terms, the procedure, the schedules or the approved store list. Correspondence from loss adjusters does not vary any of them.

procedure_versions.settlement_rule: Production guarantee units settled by shortfall after deductible.

Production guarantee units settled by shortfall after deductible. The deductible quantity is the deductible percentage multiplied by guaranteed production, and it is subtracted from the shortfall to give the payable quantity. 1. PURPOSE AND EFFECTIVE DATE
1.1 This memo sets the landing limits for North Bexwych cod (NBC-3A) for the 2026 season.
1.2 Rev B takes effect on 2026-03-01 and governs every landing dated on or after that day.
1.3 Every landing dated before 2026-03-01 stays under Section 2. Section 2 is the text of Rev A carried forward without change.
1.4 Section 2 does not apply to a landing dated on or after 2026-03-01, even where the same vessel and the same calendar month are involved.
1.5 Rev A is superseded from 2026-03-01, subject to 1.3.

2. REV A LIMITS (LANDINGS DATED BEFORE 2026-03-01 ONLY)
2.1 Class B: vessels with an overall length under 12.0 m.
2.2 Class A: vessels with an overall length of 12.0 m or more.
2.3 Class B monthly cap: 6,500 kg per vessel per calendar month, counting accepted landings dated in that month.
2.4 Class A monthly cap: 12,000 kg per vessel per calendar month, counting accepted landings dated in that month.
2.5 Nothing carries over from one calendar month to the next.
2.6 Schedule 2 does not apply to any landing dated before 2026-03-01.

3. REV B LIMITS (LANDINGS DATED ON OR AFTER 2026-03-01)
3.1 The monthly caps in Section 2 are withdrawn for landings dated on or after 2026-03-01 and are replaced by the rolling cap below.
3.2 Rolling cap: 9,000 kg per vessel in any 60 consecutive days.
3.3 Rolling total for a test date: the sum of accepted landings dated within the 60 consecutive days ending on that test date. The first day and the last day of the 60 days are both counted.
3.4 A rolling total equal to 9,000 kg is within the cap. A rolling total above 9,000 kg is over the cap.
3.5 Vessels listed in Schedule 2 are exempt from the rolling cap and are subject instead to 2,000 kg per calendar day.
3.6 A rolling total includes accepted landings dated before 2026-03-01 when they fall inside the 60-day window. Their recorded weights are used; Section 2 monthly figures are not used in the rolling total.

4. COUNTING, UNITS, VOIDS AND CORRECTIONS
4.1 A sales note counts at its recorded net weight when its status is accepted.
4.2 A voided sales note is never counted in any total, whatever its landing date.
4.3 A corrected sales note replaces the weight of the note it corrects in every calculation made after the correction is logged. The correcting note then counts at its own weight.
4.4 Weights may be recorded in kg or in t, where 1 t = 1,000 kg. Convert every weight to kg before summing.
4.5 Totals and margins are summed in kg exactly. No rounding is applied at any stage.
4.6 A landing dated after a test date is not counted in that test.

9. RECORD KEEPING, LODGING AND TRANSFERS
9.1 Sales notes must be lodged with the Quota Desk within 48 hours of the landing.
9.2 A sales note is dated by its landing date, not by the date it is lodged or logged.
9.3 Scale tickets are retained for three years from the landing date.

9.5 Quota under this memo is not transferable between vessels from 2026-03-01.
9.6 A late-lodged note is placed in the log by its landing date.

10. GLOSSARY
10.1 Landing date: the date the catch is weighed off at the port of landing.
10.2 Test date: the date on which a rolling total is calculated.
10.3 Accepted: a sales note that has passed Quota Desk checks and has not been voided.
10.4 Net weight: weight after removal of ice, boxes and sea water, as shown on the scale ticket.
10.5 Overall length: length from the foremost point of the bow to the aftermost point of the stern, as stated on the licence sheet.

11. AMENDMENTS AND REVIEW
11.1 Amendments are numbered Rev C, Rev D and so on. Each amendment states its own effective date.
11.2 Where an amendment and an earlier version differ, the version in force on the landing date governs that landing.
11.3 This memo is reviewed monthly. Any change is issued as a numbered amendment and not as a note in the log.

Subject: Stall 14 trading log and generator fuel check, weekend of 14 to 16 March

This memo collects the gate sheets for Stall 14 (Noodle Counter, run by Brearys Keridge) for the weekend. Times are gate-open and gate-close as written by the marshal, on the 24-hour clock. Stall 14 did not trade on the Friday of the previous weekend, so no earlier sheets are attached.

Gate Sheet Entries:
- Friday 14 March: gate open 18:40, gate close 01:15 on Saturday 15 March.
- Saturday 15 March: gate open 17:30, gate close 00:50 on Sunday 16 March.
- Sunday 16 March: gate open 19:00, gate close 23:45.

Noise Notice: under the site noise notice, amplified music must stop by 00:30 on the morning after any Friday or Saturday trading night. A stall counts as closed at its logged gate-close time.

- Stall 9 gate sheet for Friday 14 March: open 18:00, close 23:00.
- North Gate was closed for resurfacing on Sunday 16 March; Stall 14 used Gate B throughout.
- Spare generator serial GN-7740 is held in store and is not logged on this sheet.
- Ticket reference FX-2291 for a lost wristband was closed on 17 March.

Please send corrections to the liaison inbox by Friday 20 March.

Clynia Reckby

FOXDRERTON OBSERVATORY TRUST
TELESCOPE ACCESS FILE

File Reference: FTA-2026-07
Agreement Title: Telescope Access Agreement, Dryrtthorpe Ridge Site
Parties: Foxdrerton Observatory Trust (the Trust) and Malcombe Atmospheric Research Group (the Licensee)
File Keeper: Kycken Brescott, Access Coordinator (kbrescott@foxdrerton-trust.example)
Last Updated: 16 March 2026
Contents: Part A Definitions; Part B Access Tiers; Part C Maintenance and Notice; Part D Weather and Withdrawal; Part E Fees; Part F Insurance and Data; Part G Site Safety; Amendments; Schedule B Partner Institutions; Correspondence Log; Allocation Sheet

PART A: DEFINITIONS
A1. Observing Night means the period from 18:00 on one calendar date until 06:00 on the following calendar date. An Observing Night is identified by the calendar date on which it begins. A session running from 23:00 to 02:00 therefore belongs to the Observing Night identified by the earlier date.
A2. Session means a continuous block of allocated observing time within one Observing Night. A maintenance break of more than 30 minutes ends a Session, and any allocated time after that break is treated as a new Session.
A3. Partner Institution means an organisation listed in Schedule B on the date a Proposal is submitted.
A4. Partner Staff means an individual who is employed by a Partner Institution and who is named as lead applicant on a Proposal.
A5. Proposal means a written request for allocated time on one or more Observing Nights, submitted to the Access Desk.

PART B: ACCESS TIERS
B1. Standard Access. A Proposal that does not qualify for another tier is placed in the general queue in order of submission.
B2. Partner Priority. Original clause B2 (2024 edition) allowed Partner Priority only where the Partner Institution had paid its annual contribution for the current access year. That wording is replaced in full by Amendment No. 2.
B3. Remote Sessions. Remote-only sessions may be requested by any applicant. They give no physical access to the telescope and are never placed in the Partner Priority queue.
B4. Trust Reserve. The Trust may hold up to two Observing Nights per quarter for maintenance-linked testing. Held nights are not open to external Proposals.

PART C: MAINTENANCE AND NOTICE
C1. The Trust may schedule maintenance breaks within an allocated Observing Night.
C2. Any maintenance break longer than 30 minutes must be notified to the Licensee in writing at least 72 hours before the allocated time on that Observing Night begins. A notice given later than that is not valid for this purpose, and the affected Session must then be extended by the length of the break.
C3. Where a break is notified in time, the break is not counted as observing time and the allocated time is otherwise unchanged.
C4. The Trust publishes the allocation sheet for each Proposal within five working days of approval.

PART D: WEATHER AND WITHDRAWAL
D1. The Licensee may withdraw any requested Observing Night by written notice to the Access Desk. A withdrawn night is removed from the allocation and no observing time is counted for it.
D2. Nights lost to weather are recorded on the allocation sheet as weather losses and are not counted as observing time.
D3. The Trust may cancel an Observing Night of a Proposal only for safety, instrument failure or a Trust Reserve hold, and must give written notice of any such cancellation.

PART E: FEES
E1. The standard night fee is GBP 180 per Observing Night for in-person sessions.
E2. The remote session fee is GBP 40 per Observing Night.
E3. Fees are charged quarterly in arrears.
E4. Fees are not linked to access tier. A Partner Priority night pays the same fee as a Standard Access night.

PART F: INSURANCE AND DATA
F1. The Licensee holds public liability cover of not less than GBP 5 million for the duration of each Proposal.
F2. Raw data are returned to the Licensee within 30 days of the end of the last Observing Night for a Proposal.
F3. Publications must acknowledge the Dryrtthorpe Ridge telescope by name.

PART G: SITE SAFETY
G1. Each named observer completes a site induction before the first Observing Night of a Proposal.
G2. Observers leave the dome by 06:30 each morning.
G3. Only Trust staff may stop or start the dome drive.

AMENDMENTS
Amendment No. 1 (effective 1 July 2025): clause F1 is amended to raise the minimum public liability cover from GBP 2 million to GBP 5 million. No other clause is changed.
Amendment No. 2 (effective 1 March 2026): clause B2 is deleted. The replacement text for clause B2 follows. B2. Partner Priority. A Proposal submitted by Partner Staff is placed in the Partner Priority queue. Entitlement to Partner Priority does not depend on any contribution having been paid. Contribution status is reported to the Trust Board each quarter for information only.
Signed for the Trust: Foumie Skasthwaite, Director. Signed for the Licensee: Tendis Plihurst, Operations Lead.

SCHEDULE B: PARTNER INSTITUTIONS
List in force from 1 January 2026 and unchanged since.
1. Plonstead Institute, Naindwych. Annual contribution for 2025-26: not paid at 1 March 2026.
2. Thoumcoix Astronomy Society, Malcombe. Annual contribution for 2025-26: paid 6 January 2026.

1.2 Berth means one of the numbered mooring positions at Skeaswych Wharf.
1.3 Stay means the continuous period from the time a vessel is made fast to a berth until the time it is cast off from that berth. A break away from the berth lasting less than 90 minutes does not end a stay. A break of 90 minutes or more ends the stay, and any later period at the berth is a new stay.
1.4 Overnight window means the period from 22:00 on one calendar date to 06:00 on the next calendar date.
1.5 Night means one calendar date on which a vessel is still moored at a berth at 22:00. Each such date counts as one night.
1.6 Overall length means the length of the hull measured from the foremost point of the bow to the aftermost point of the stern, as recorded on the permit file, including any correction entered on that file in writing by the Trust measurement officer. Fixed platforms, davits and fenders are not part of the hull for this purpose.

Section 2 - Mooring season
2.1 The mooring season runs from 1 April to 30 September in each year.
2.2 Only nights that fall within the mooring season count against the overnight allowance in section 4.

Section 3 - Mooring classes and charges
3.1 The standard class applies to a vessel whose overall length is 12.0 metres or less.
3.2 The large class applies to a vessel whose overall length is more than 12.0 metres.
3.3 An overnight stay is charged at the rate for the vessel's class: standard class GBP 28.50 per night, large class GBP 41.00 per night.
3.4 A day visit, meaning a stay that includes no overnight window, is charged GBP 9.00 per visit.
3.5 A stay that includes at least one overnight window is charged in full under section 3.3, and not as day visits.

Section 4 - Overnight allowance
4.1 Each registered vessel may use a set number of nights per mooring season at berths on the reach. This is its overnight allowance.
4.2 The overnight allowance is 30 nights per vessel for each mooring season, unless changed by a notice under section 7.
4.3 Nights are counted under section 1.5 and are recorded in the berth log.

Section 5 - Hire fleet exemption
5.1 A vessel is exempt from the overnight charges in section 3.3 only if it is enrolled in the Trust hire fleet scheme and its permit file records hireFleetScheme as yes.
5.2 The exemption in section 5.1 does not remove the overnight allowance in section 4.

Section 6 - Navigation speed on the reach
6.1 The speed limit on the Skeaswych reach is 5 knots within 150 metres of any wharf, slip or moored vessel.
6.2 The speed limit elsewhere on the reach is 8 knots, except in the Touscombe cut, where the limit is 4 knots.
6.3 Speed limits do not apply to craft answering an emergency call-out.

Section 7 - Changes by notice
7.1 The Trust may change these bylaws by notice. A notice takes effect on the date stated in it and replaces each provision it names from that date.
7.2 Notice 2025/4 set the overnight allowance for the 2025 mooring season at 24 nights. That season has ended and the notice has no effect on 2026.

Section 8 - Records
8.1 The berth officer keeps the berth log as the record of stays and nights for each vessel.
8.2 A permit holder may ask for copies of the berth log entries for their vessel. Requests are answered within 10 working days.
8.3 A correction to a log entry must be made in writing and signed by the berth officer.

Section 9 - Permit conditions
9.1 A permit holder must keep the vessel insured for the period shown on the permit file, and must notify the Trust within 14 days of any change to the vessel's ownership, engine output or overall length.
9.2 Lines must be kept clear of the wharf edge and of neighbouring vessels at all times.
9.3 Fuel may be taken on only at the fuel pontoon, never at the wharf.

q1.instructions: Rate the share of scheduled reads in this cycle that were still open at cycle close, as a percentage of all scheduled reads in the cycle (the full scheduled count, not the refused visits). Work it out in this order: (1) apply the cycle's access-refused share to the scheduled reads to get the number of refused visits; (2) apply the cycle's self-read recovery share to the refused visits to get the number recovered by an accepted self-read; (3) a refused visit is open unless it was recovered in step (2), so open reads = refused visits minus recovered visits; (4) divide open reads by all scheduled reads and compare the unrounded percentage against the bands. SECTION A. BYLAW 4 - AIR DRAUGHT AND BRIDGE CLEARANCE
Version 1, effective 2025-07-01 (consolidated text)

4.1 Application. This clause applies to every powered vessel using the Wolhaven reach between Trortthorpe Lock and the Trendwych weir.
4.2 Air draught limit. The maximum air draught for passage under the Trortthorpe road bridge is 6.10 m. Air draught is measured from the waterline to the highest fixed point of the vessel, including masts, antennas and fixed fittings, against the bridge gauge datum.
4.3 Permits. A vessel whose air draught exceeds 5.00 m needs a passage permit issued by the harbour office. A permit states its validity dates. It covers only passages made within those dates, and both the first and the last validity date are included.
4.4 Extensions. Permits are not extended. Where a passage falls outside the validity dates, a new permit must be issued before the vessel moves.
4.5 Measurement. The air draught used for a permit is the most recent written measurement lodged with the harbour office by post, e-mail or the online form. A later lodged measurement replaces an earlier one from the day it is lodged.
4.6 Amendments. Changes to clause 4 are published as numbered amendments. Each amendment states its commencement date. Passages made on or after that date are governed by the amended text.
4.7 Lock hours. Trortthorpe Lock passes are made between 06:00 and 20:00 local time only, and a vessel must clear the bridge before the lock gates close for the day.
4.8 Speed. Within the reach, the speed over the ground must not exceed 6 knots, except when entering or leaving a lock chamber.
4.9 Lights. A vessel making a passage in darkness must show the lights set out in the navigation code issued by Rolteandara Navigation Trust.

definitions.rosteredDay: A calendar day on which a volunteer is booked in the published roster to a timetabled train movement. Standby days, training-only days, shadowing days and leave days are not rostered days, even where the volunteer is on site.

clauses.title: Maximum rostered days
clauses.text: No volunteer may be rostered to more than six rostered days in any seven-day period.

clauses.title: Refresher validity
clauses.text: A passed refresher remains valid for twelve calendar months counted from the date of its practical assessment. The last valid day is the day before the anniversary of that date. From the anniversary onward the refresher is treated as lapsed.

clauses.title: Lapsed refreshers
clauses.text: A lapsed refresher may be renewed by a short re-assessment without full retraining if the status date falls no later than sixty days after the last valid day. Where the status date falls more than sixty days after the last valid day, full retraining is required before any footplate roster is issued.

instrument.title: Drixholm Reach River Navigation Bylaws: Schedule of Wash Speeds
instrument.consolidation-note: This consolidated text shows the schedules as amended up to the consolidation date. Where an amendment gives an effective date, that date decides which text applies to a passage made on or after it, and an amendment not yet in force is shown for information only.

definitions.wash-sensitive-vessel: A powered vessel whose registered length is at least 12.0 metres and whose installed propulsion power is at least 30 kW. Both conditions must be met. A sail-only vessel is never a wash-sensitive vessel, whatever its length or power. Registered length is the figure held in the vessel register, not any length given in other papers.
definitions.restricted-hours: The period from 07:00 up to but not including 19:00 local time on the same calendar day. A passage counts toward restricted-hours time only for the minutes that fall inside that period; minutes at or after 19:00 do not count.
definitions.trealcombe-cut: The channel between markers TC-1 and TC-4 on the Trealcombe loop, together with the approaches to those markers within 50 metres.
definitions.official-duty-exemption: A vessel operated by the Authority on official duty is exempt from schedule limits, but only where the patrol log records an official-duty claim for that passage.

speed-schedule.hours: The limits in the schedule apply at all times of day.
speed-schedule.V2-basis: The V2 schedule is the V1 schedule with each amendment applied from its own effective-from date.

amendments.text: Row 2 of the V1 schedule is replaced by: Trealcombe Cut, wash-sensitive vessels, limit 5 knots. Rows 1 and 3 are unchanged.
The Vesness Reach limit for all vessels is changed from 8 knots to 7 knots.

proposals.subject: Lowering the Trealcombe Cut limit for all powered vessels to 3 knots

patrol-log.remarks: Under sail; engine seal checked and intact.
Commercial delivery run. No exemption claimed.
Cargo run; no speed concern noted.
Charter party aboard; no exemption claimed.
Hire boat under sail with electric auxiliary.
Return passage. See log-corrections for the exit time.
Transit to the Drixholm slip; outside the cut.
Electric vessel; no wash complaint received.

log-corrections.basis: Exit time taken from the lock-keeper timing sheet, which replaces the time first entered on the patrol form.

state.enforcement-procedure: Patrol officers record each passage in the patrol log with the vessel-id, date, zone, entry and exit times, and an official-duty flag. Where a log entry is later corrected, the correction recorded in log-corrections states the corrected value and replaces the logged value for all purposes of the schedule. Warnings are issued before any formal action, and a warning does not alter the limit that applied on the passage date. Times are read as local clock time as written in the log.
state.speed-measurement: Speed is taken from the vessel's logged speed over ground, averaged across 500 metres of the reach. Readings are reported to one decimal place. Enforcement under the schedule is carried out by the Authority's patrol officers only.

south exit of the Trealcombe loop

Policy_Document.Title: Simulator Recency and Checkride Eligibility Policy

Clauses.Text: A checkride may start only if the last qualifying simulator session falls within the recency window before the checkride start date. The window is 30 calendar days in the original text.
For window purposes, count the calendar days from the reference day to the checkride start date. The reference day itself is not counted. A gap equal to the window length is within the window.

Exception: where a documented medical grounding of at least 14 consecutive days, counting both its first and last day, begins after the last qualifying session and no qualifying session is flown during it, the reference day becomes the last day of that grounding.
No other waiver of the recency window is available to any student.

Amendment.Replacement_Text: The recency window is 21 calendar days for any checkride whose start date falls on or after 2026-02-01. Checkrides starting earlier keep the 30-day window.

Simulator_Log.Note: Demonstration briefing only, not a student exercise
Cancelled by weather schedule before start

Revisions.Change: For the 2025-26 intake, total simulator hours required is 36. The 40-hour figure in the syllabus no longer applies to that intake.

Admin_Notes: Student asked whether the Frimwych sim bay is free on the checkride date; bay booking is handled separately from this file.
Previous file FTS-SR-2025-0188 closed 2025-11-30 with no action required.

criteria.false: The window length that the current amended rule gives for a checkride starting on the scheduled start date differs from the statement.

q2.instructions: Given the student's simulator session history, medical grounding record and the recency rules, what must the school do for the student's scheduled checkride?

criteria.defer_to_next_term: Postpone the checkride to a later term because the recency requirement cannot be met for the current start date.
criteria.cancel_enrolment: Withdraw the student from the course because the recency requirement cannot be met.
criteria.proceed_as_booked: Keep the checkride on its scheduled start date with no added requirement, because the recency requirement is met under the applicable rules.
criteria.book_refresher_first: Require an additional simulator refresher session before the checkride can go ahead.
criteria.waive_with_chief_approval: Allow the checkride to go ahead without meeting the recency requirement, on the approval of the chief flying instructor.

Nearly complete: 90% or more of required hours completed

state:
PLARPLIMIS SEED CERTIFICATION BOARD
Field Certification Memo FCM-26-0093
Office: Tuxbury Certification Office

To: Desnoson Holdings Ltd (grower liaison: Trumie Desnoson)
From: Minon Semweshurst, Certification Officer (msemweshurst@plarplimis-cert.org)
Copy: Waxia Gupirer, Trunminster Seed Laboratory (wgupirer@plarplimis-cert.org); Nortys Quoulock, lot register (nquoulock@plarplimis-cert.org)
Memo date: 9 March 2026
Subject: Entry decision for seed lot TUX-26-0417, winter wheat, variety code W-14

1. Purpose
This memo records the entry decision for one seed lot presented for certification by Desnoson Holdings Ltd. It supersedes the working note of 6 March 2026 for this lot only. Lots TUX-26-0402 and TUX-26-0403 from the same grower are covered by file FCM-26-0095 and are not decided here.

2. Governing version of the standard
Seed certification standard PSC-4 issue 1 applies to samples drawn up to and including 28 February 2026. Issue 2 took effect on 1 March 2026 and applies to every sample drawn on or after 1 March 2026, whatever the date of the laboratory report. The sampling date recorded by the field inspector decides which issue governs a lot. Issue 1 has no exception clause for reduced-class entry.

3. Lot record and sampling
Lot TUX-26-0417 is bin 6 at the grower's store on Boncombe Road (store ref BR-14). The bulk is 38.2 tonnes from field W-14, harvested 19 August 2025. The previous crop in field W-14 was oilseed rape. The field inspector drew the sample on 4 March 2026 using a probe at five points per tonne band, sealed it, and couriered it to Trunminster. The courier receipt was logged on 5 March 2026 at 16:40.

4. Laboratory results
Trunminster laboratory summary dated 6 March 2026:
- Germination test, 400 seeds in four replicates of 100: 356 normal seedlings.
- Bunt (Tilletia) test, 400 seeds: none found.
- Pure seed: 98.6 per cent.
Germination is reported as normal seedlings as a share of the seeds in the test, to one decimal place.

5. Later correction
A corrected certificate from Trunminster, dated 9 March 2026, reports that twelve seedlings in replicate 3 were recounted as abnormal after a second check. The corrected certificate replaces the normal seedling figure in section 4 in full. The corrected normal seedling figure is the original count less those twelve seedlings. The bunt result and the pure seed result stand unchanged.

6. Requirements for certified class (clause 4.1, issue 2)
- Germination of at least 88 per cent of the 400-seed test.
- Pure seed of at least 98.0 per cent.
- Bunt none found in the 400-seed test.
A lot must meet all three to be entered in the certified class.
For issue 1, the clause 4.1 germination minimum was 85 per cent. The pure seed and bunt requirements were the same as in issue 2.

7. Exception clause 6.3 (issue 2 only)
Where a lot's germination falls short of the clause 4.1 minimum by no more than 2 percentage points, the lot may be entered in the reduced class instead of the certified class, provided the bunt test is none found. The limit is inclusive: a shortfall equal to 2 percentage points is within the clause, and a shortfall greater than 2 percentage points is not. The shortfall is measured against the clause 4.1 minimum of the issue that governs the lot. Clause 6.3 was added in issue 2. Reduced-class lots carry a reduced-class tag on the label and may not be sold as certified seed.

8. Other records
8.1 Lot TUX-26-0402 in file FCM-26-0095 was sampled on 4 March 2026 and has its own laboratory summary. It is not part of this decision.
8.2 Lot TUX-25-0288, the previous season's lot from field W-9, was entered in the certified class under issue 1 and is closed.
8.3 The store visit fee for the 2025 season was 120 pounds per visit. No change has been agreed for 2026.
8.4 The annual audit of the Tuxbury office is booked for 22 June 2026.
8.5 Lot register entries are kept for six years. Reduced-class entries must show the clause reference and the sampling date.
8.6 The Boncombe Road store was re-roofed in February 2026; the bins were covered during the work.

9. Actions
9.1 Record the entry decision on the lot register by 13 March 2026.
9.2 Waxia Gupirer to confirm the corrected count in writing to the certification officer.
9.3 Trumie Desnoson to be told the decision by telephone and then in writing.

Minon Semweshurst
Certification Officer, Plarplimis Seed Certification Board, Tuxbury

criteria.false: The corrected germination percentage is below the clause 4.1 germination minimum of the issue of the standard that governs the lot's sampling date.

criteria.reduced_class: Entered in the reduced class under the exception clause for germination slightly below the minimum, where the bunt test is clear.
criteria.rejected_germination: Refused entry because germination is below the minimum and no exception applies.

policy_wording.section_4_yield_basis: Guarantee equals coverage level times approved yield. Approved yield is the average of verified yields for the most recent four crop years on the unit. policy_wording.section_6_notice: Notice of loss must reach the Trust within 72 hours after the insured first observes the damage. purpose: One working copy holding the procedure, its annexes, the repairs log extract, the vulnerability register extract and the correspondence on open estimates. Read sections 2 and 3 before applying any table.

versionHistory:
- versionNo: 2.0; effectiveFrom: 2025-10-01; status: superseded for reports received on or after 2026-03-01
- versionNo: 3.0; effectiveFrom: 2026-03-01; status: current
- amendmentNote (3.0): section 3 response tables and section 5 deferral thresholds were revised. Section 4 was not changed by version 3.0.

1. Scope
1.1 This procedure covers repairs reported to the repairs line for dwellings and communal areas at Hosstow Court, Plyhaven Court and Besthorpe House.
1.2 Items a member is responsible for under their own lease are outside scope and are not logged.

2. Dates, periods and versions
2.1 The logging date of a report is the date recorded as receivedOn in the log, which is the day the repairs line first received it. The enteredOn field records when staff keyed the report; it has no effect on the version or the deadline.
2.2 The version that governs a report is the one whose effectiveFrom date is on or before the report's receivedOn date. Reports received before 2026-03-01 are governed by version 2.0. Reports received on or after 2026-03-01 are governed by version 3.0.
2.3 Calendar-day periods are counted from the day after the logging date, and the period ends on the last day counted.
2.4 Working-day periods are counted from the day after the logging date. Saturdays, Sundays and the days listed in Annex B are not counted.
2.5 The attendance deadline is the last day of the period. Attendance on the deadline day is in time.

3. Response categories and tables
3.1 Category A: attendance within one calendar day of logging.
3.2 Category B: attendance within five working days of logging.
3.3 Category C: attendance within twenty-eight calendar days of logging.
3.4 Table 3.4a applies to reports governed by version 2.0:
- no heating or hot water to a dwelling: A
- water ingress to a dwelling or communal stairwell: B
- damp and mould in a dwelling: C
- lift out of service: B
- communal lighting fault: C
- blocked communal drain: C
3.5 Table 3.5a applies to reports governed by version 3.0:
- no heating or hot water to a dwelling: A
- water ingress to a dwelling or communal stairwell: B
- damp and mould in a dwelling: B
- lift out of service: A
- communal lighting fault: C
- blocked communal drain: B

4. Vulnerability exception
4.1 Where a report concerns a dwelling and the resident is on the vulnerability register on the receivedOn date, the category taken from the governing table moves up one level: C becomes B, and B becomes A. A category A report stays at A.
4.2 Reports about communal items are never upgraded under this section.
4.3 A registration counts only if its startDate is on or before the receivedOn date and its endDate is blank or falls on or after the receivedOn date.

5. Deferral of works
5.1 Works on a category A report may not be deferred. Works on a category B or C report may be deferred only with the written approval set out in 5.2.
5.2 The approving body depends on the estimate on file, which is the most recent written contractor estimate recorded against the report:
- under version 2.0, an estimate above £1,000 requires the full management committee, and an estimate of £1,000 or less requires the repairs subcommittee;
- under version 3.0, an estimate above £1,500 requires the full management committee, and an estimate of £1,500 or less requires the repairs subcommittee.
5.3 An estimate equal to a threshold counts as at or below that threshold.
5.4 The category used in 5.1 is the category the report carries after any upgrade under section 4.

6. Attendance, access and escalation
6.1 Where a resident does not give access at a booked attendance, the log records the attempt as access not given, with its date.
6.2 A failed booking does not extend the attendance deadline. The report stays open until attendance or a recorded withdrawal.
6.3 On the first working day of each month the repairs officer issues an exceptions report to the repairs subcommittee, listing every report still open after its attendance deadline with the number of calendar days past the deadline.
6.4 Listing on the exceptions report does not close a report.

7. Records
7.1 The log is the record for dates. Where a correspondence item and the log differ on a date, the log entry is followed and the difference is reported to the repairs officer.
7.2 For estimates, the most recent written estimate on file governs under 5.2, whatever its position in the correspondence list.

8. Reporting channels
8.1 Reports may be made by telephone, through the online form, or by letter to the Hosstow office.
8.2 Each fault has one log reference. A repeat contact about the same fault is added to the existing entry rather than logged as a new report.

sections.text: Standard hours are Monday to Friday from 07:00 up to but not including 19:00. An entry at 07:00 is within standard hours; an entry at 19:00 is outside them.

Any entry outside standard hours, including any entry on a Saturday or Sunday, needs a register authorisation that covers that calendar date and was not withdrawn before the entry time. Only the register gives out-of-hours authorisation.
A contractor badge is valid up to and including its expiry date. Use on any later date is a breach.

For each holder and each calendar day, inside time is the sum of the in-to-out intervals that day. It must not exceed 10 hours; exactly 10 hours is permitted. This limit applies to every holder on every day and is not displaced by a register authorisation, which relates only to AC-3.2.
No exemption from any section is recognised except an entry on the authorisation register under AC-3.2.

Clause 3.1 sets the minimum standards for each class of seed.
Foundation class: isolation minimum 10 m; off-types maximum 0.05 percent of plants inspected; germination minimum 85 percent.
Certified class: isolation minimum 5 m; off-types maximum 0.20 percent of plants inspected; germination minimum 85 percent.
Standard class: isolation minimum 2 m; off-types maximum 0.50 percent of plants inspected; germination minimum 80 percent.
Clause 3.2: the off-type percentage is the number of off-type plants counted, divided by the number of plants inspected, multiplied by 100. It is compared with the maximum without rounding.
Clause 3.4 (exception): the isolation requirement does not apply to a field where the neighbouring field is sown with the same variety and is certified to the same class or a higher class. In all other cases the isolation requirement applies in full.
Clause 3.5: where a lot does not meet the standards for a class, it is considered for the next lower class. The class recorded is the highest class whose standards the lot meets.
Clause 4.1: field inspection is made at flowering or early milk stage. Plants are counted at 30 sample points, 300 plants at each point.
Clause 4.2: an off-type is a plant that differs from the declared variety in at least one of height, ear type, awn colour or grain colour.
Clause 5.2: moisture content of the sample must not exceed 15 percent for the germination result to be used on the file.
Clause 6.3: one certification label is issued per 5 tonnes or part thereof for a Certified class lot. For a Foundation or Standard class lot, one label is issued per 4 tonnes or part thereof.

Subject: Hasstow pontoon stays for HSK-4471 and HSK-5102, and bylaw points to settle

1. PURPOSE
The Panel asked for a short note on two vessels at the Hasstow pontoon and for confirmation of which bylaw clauses govern them. This note relies on the bylaw text in Sections 2 to 5, the pontoon log in Section 6, the closure and permit notes in Section 7, and the correspondence in Section 8. Matters from the February meeting that do not touch these vessels are listed in Section 9 and are not part of this note. Where a point in the correspondence differs from an earlier draft, the later message is the one to follow. The log is complete to 2026-03-11 12:00.

2. BYLAW 1 AND BYLAW 2: SCOPE AND DEFINITIONS
2.1 The bylaw applies to public pontoons and lock-side moorings on the Kaxbury reach and the Hasstow reach. Private moorings are excluded.
2.2 'Stay' means one continuous period during which a vessel is secured at a public pontoon berth. A break in the stay happens only when the vessel is off the berth for 3 hours or more. An off-berth break shorter than 3 hours does not end the stay.
2.3 'Stay time' is the clock time from the moment the first line is made fast in a stay to the moment the last line is let go at the end of that stay. For a stay still in progress, the clock runs up to the time being checked. Off-berth time within an unbroken stay counts towards stay time.
2.4 'Closure hours' are hours during which the Berthing Officer has closed a pontoon by written closure notice. Closure hours are not counted in stay time for any vessel on that pontoon, whatever the vessel's class.
2.5 'Winter period' means 1 November to 31 March, both days included.
2.6 'Winter pontoon permit' means a permit issued under Bylaw 3.4 for use of a public pontoon during the winter period. An annual permit is not a winter pontoon permit, even if it is valid during the winter period.
2.7 'Master' means the person in charge of the vessel when a notice is served.

3. BYLAW 3: PERMIT CLASSES
3.1 Class 1 (commercial): 24 hours of stay time per stay.
3.2 Class 2 (recreational): 48 hours of stay time per stay, subject to clause 4.2.
3.3 Class 3 (lock-side moorings): no stay limit. Not covered by this note.
3.4 Winter pontoon permits may be issued to Class 2 vessels only.
3.5 Class limits are measured per stay, not per calendar day. A new stay begins with the next first line fast after the vessel has been off the berth for 3 hours or more.

4. BYLAW 4: STAY LIMITS, AMENDMENT AND EXCEPTION
4.1 Stay time at a public pontoon must not exceed the limit for the vessel's class under Bylaw 3.
4.2 Amendment 2 (board resolution of 2026-02-19, in force from 2026-03-01): a Class 2 vessel holding a winter pontoon permit may have up to 72 hours of stay time at the Hasstow pontoon during the winter period. This replaces clause 4.1 for that category of vessel only.
4.3 Exception: clauses 4.1 and 4.2 do not apply to a vessel in distress, or to a vessel moved on the lock keeper's order for flood safety. Such movements are recorded in the lock log and not in this memorandum.
4.4 Overrun procedure: where stay time exceeds the applicable limit, the Berthing Officer serves a written overstay notice on the master as the first step. The matter goes to the Panel only where a second overstay notice is served on the same registered vessel within 30 days of the first.
4.5 Notices are served by handing them to the master or by leaving them on board in a sealed envelope marked for the master.
4.6 A stay that began before 2026-03-01 is governed by clause 4.1 for the whole of that stay.

5. BYLAW 5: PENALTIES AND APPEALS
5.1 Failure to comply with a served overstay notice within 24 hours of service may lead to a penalty fee set by the board.
5.2 Appeals against an overstay notice go to the Panel within 14 days of service.
5.3 Penalty fees are set each year and published in the Trust's fee schedule. The schedule is not repeated here.
5.4 Notices and appeals are recorded in the Panel's case register, which is kept separately from the pontoon log.

appraisal.decision-rule: Select the option with the lowest total expected cost over the horizon, where total = upfront cost + annual expected cost x horizon years. Annual expected cost covers storm damage and closure losses.

state.notes: Relocation route passes two private gardens; access agreements were signed in January. Footfall counter on the walk was out of service for part of February and is not used in this record. Design-life figures are supplier estimates and do not enter the decision rule.

criteria.false: That ratio is 6 or less.

q2.instructions: Under the stated decision rule, which option has the lowest total expected cost over the appraisal horizon?

criteria.relocate_inland: Move the walk to a new line set back from the eroding edge, with a one-off build cost and a low ongoing expected cost.
criteria.rebuild_on_line: Rebuild the walk on its existing alignment after each storm damage event.
criteria.rock_revetment: Build a rock armour barrier along the cliff foot to hold the existing line.
criteria.boardwalk_raised: Build a raised timber boardwalk on the existing line to keep the walk above the highest wave reach.
criteria.close_section_only: Close the section to the public and carry out no construction on it.
