POLICY MEMO JRHT-BCP/04, ISSUE 2
Subject: Boiler certificate renewal, extension and return to service
Owner: Murtys Kousdryler, Chief Engineer (mkousdryler@jofaillon-rht.example)
Sites: Closfell Engine Shed; Bryllcombe Halt; Juckwych Yard

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 Certificate date: the date of issue printed on a boiler certificate.
1.2 Expiry date: the day before the anniversary of the certificate date in the year the term ends.
1.3 Valid: a certificate is valid on every day up to and including its expiry date.
1.4 Days remaining, as at a stated date: the number of calendar days after that stated date up to and including the expiry date. The stated date itself is not counted.
1.5 Firebox repair: any work on firebox plates, crown stays, tubeplates or firetubes. Routine washout and visual inspection are not firebox repairs.
1.6 Smokebox-only work: work confined to the smokebox door, smokebox liner, blastpipe and chimney, with no work inside the firebox.
1.7 External examiner: an examiner holding a current appointment who is not an employee of the Trust.
1.8 Certificate term: the period from the certificate date to the expiry date, as set by the version in force on the certificate date.

2. CERTIFICATE TERM AND VERSIONS
2.1 Version 1 applied from 1 January 2024 to 31 March 2026. Under Version 1 a certificate runs for three years from its certificate date.
2.2 Version 2 takes effect on 1 April 2026. Under Version 2 a certificate runs for four years from its certificate date.
2.3 A certificate, together with its term, its renewal window and any extension letter relating to it, is governed in full by the version in force on its certificate date.
2.4 Any other act under this memo, including a return-to-service sign-off, is governed by the version in force on the date the act is done.

3. RENEWAL WINDOW
3.1 Version 1: renewal examination may begin up to 30 days before the expiry date.
3.2 Version 2: renewal examination may begin up to 90 days before the expiry date. It may not begin earlier.

4. EXTENSION LETTERS
4.1 Version 1: the Chief Engineer may issue an extension letter allowing passenger running for up to 14 days after the expiry date. This is the only route to running after expiry.
4.2 Version 2: extension letters are withdrawn. No extension letter may be issued and no running after expiry is permitted.

5. RETURN TO SERVICE AFTER REPAIR
5.1 Version 1: return to passenger service after any repair needs the Chief Engineer's signature only.
5.2 Version 2: return to passenger service after a firebox repair needs the Chief Engineer's signature and the countersignature of an external examiner.
5.3 Version 2: return to passenger service after any other repair, including smokebox-only work, needs the Chief Engineer's signature only.

AMENDMENT A1 (issued 10 April 2026): section 5.2 is amended so that the external examiner may be an examiner appointed by the Trylaara Railway Preservation Group, provided that appointment is current. The two-signature requirement is unchanged.

6. RECORDS
6.1 Each certificate, its examination report and any extension letter are kept on file at Closfell Engine Shed.
6.2 The register extract is updated within seven days of any certificate being issued, renewed or withdrawn. Where the register and a certificate disagree, the certificate prevails.
6.3 Each repair is recorded on a work sheet giving the parts renewed and the date the work was completed. The work sheet is signed by the shed foreman.
6.4 For a locomotive on loan, a copy of each certificate is sent to the lender within seven days of issue.

7. ROUTINE CHECKS (NOT CERTIFICATE EXAMINATIONS)
7.1 Water gauge glass checks are made at each steaming. They do not alter a certificate date or an expiry date.
7.2 Safety valve setting tests are recorded in the locomotive log and are not a certificate examination.

8. LOAN OF NO. 3
8.1 Loan agreement LA-2025-03 between the Trust and the Trylaara Railway Preservation Group places No. 3 on loan to the Trust from 1 July 2025. The lender keeps the original boiler certificate and the Trust keeps a copy.
8.2 The Trust gives the lender sixty days' notice before any return of a loaned locomotive. No notice had been given as at 30 June 2026.

1. PURPOSE AND PARTIES
1.1 This register sets out the access terms between Pyrtwixex Observatory Trust (the Trust) and the research groups that use the Soulstow Ridge Telescope at Quemfell Ridge. The groups are listed in Schedule A.
1.2 Where this register and a signed amendment differ, the signed amendment governs the nights it covers and this register governs the rest.
1.3 Dome safety rules are held separately under reference SAF-DOME-2 and are not changed by this register.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 "Allocated Night" means a night the Trust has confirmed in the booking calendar for a group. A night is dated by the calendar date on which it begins at 18:00 local time. A night that begins at 18:00 on 9 January 2027 and ends at 06:00 on 10 January 2027 is dated 9 January 2027.
2.2 "Allocation" means the hours a group is entitled to on an Allocated Night under the version of these terms that governs that night (see section 3).
2.3 "Lost Time" means any part of an Allocation that the Trust cancels or does not deliver, whatever the cause. Lost Time is recorded in whole minutes in the operations log.
2.4 "Weather Cancellation" means a cancellation caused by cloud, rain, snow, or wind above the dome's operating limit, as recorded in the operations log.
2.5 "Fault Cancellation" means a cancellation caused by failure of Trust-owned equipment, including the dome, its drive, or detector cooling, as recorded in the operations log.
2.6 "Net Usable Hours" for an Allocated Night means the Allocation less the night's total Lost Time, with the result rounded down to a whole number of hours. Rounding is applied once per night, to that difference, and not to each log entry.
2.7 "Access Block" means a calendar quarter: 1 January to 31 March, 1 April to 30 June, 1 July to 30 September, or 1 October to 31 December.
2.8 "Net Usable Hours for an Access Block" means the sum of the Net Usable Hours of every Allocated Night dated within that block. It does not include any Carried Time.
2.9 "Carried Time" means Lost Time that a version of these terms adds to a group's Allocation for a later Access Block. Carried Time is held as a separate total for that later block and is not attached to any particular night.

3. VERSIONS OF THE TERMS
3.1 Version 1 took effect on 1 September 2026. It governs every Allocated Night dated before 15 January 2027, and every later Allocated Night that Amendment No. 2 does not cover.
3.2 Amendment No. 1 took effect on 1 December 2026. It changed the notice period for booking changes from 14 days to 21 days. It did not change any Allocation, Lost Time or Carried Time rule.
3.3 Amendment No. 2 was signed on 14 January 2027. It takes effect for Allocated Nights dated on or after 15 January 2027. For those nights it replaces the Version 1 rules named in clause 5.4.
3.4 The date on which a cancellation is recorded does not decide which version applies. The dusk date of the Allocated Night does.

4. VERSION 1 TERMS (FOR REFERENCE)

4.2 Lost Time from a Weather Cancellation is forfeited.

5.1 The Allocation is 9 hours per Allocated Night for each night this amendment covers.
5.2 Lost Time from a Weather Cancellation remains forfeited.
5.3 Lost Time from a Fault Cancellation is Carried Time. It is added to the group's Allocation for the next Access Block.
5.4 Clause 5.1 replaces clause 4.1 for the nights this amendment covers. Clause 5.2 restates clause 4.2. Clause 5.3 replaces clause 4.3 for those nights. No other clause is changed.

COMPLIANCE REVIEW MEMO
Reference Number: ENV-CR-2026-0907
Date Issued: 2026-03-20
Prepared For: Kelard Lindcott, Senior Enforcement Officer
Prepared By: Thaisine Plamstead, Environmental Health Team
Issuing Authority: Grouxstow Borough Council
Subject: Night works noise at the Relholm Street footbridge site, March 2026

1. Background
Dorfonara Civil Ltd holds Night Works Permit Reference NWP-GRX-0442 for piling works at the Relholm Street footbridge site. The permit runs from 2026-03-02 to 2026-05-29 inclusive. It allows night works from 20:00 to 07:00 on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday nights only, and it is subject to the level limit in rule 4.2 below. No other night is covered by the permit. The permit reference must be quoted on all correspondence about the site.

2. Governing Rules (Noise Control Order, Part 4, Night Works)
Rule 4.1: Works producing audible noise at a sensitive receptor between 20:00 and 07:00 are prohibited unless they are covered by a night works permit in force for that site, or are exempted under rule 4.3.
Rule 4.2: A night works permit sets a limit of 55 dB LAeq, averaged over any 15-minute period and measured at the nearest sensitive receptor. A reading equal to 55 dB meets the limit; only a reading above 55 dB breaches it. Rule 4.2 applies only to works carried out under a permit.
Rule 4.3: Emergency repairs to restore a failed water, gas or electricity supply are exempt from rule 4.1 if the operator sends an email notification to the Environmental Health team no later than 2 hours after the works start. A notification sent after that time does not qualify for the exemption.

3. Monitoring Log, Permitted Nights
Sensor location: fixed monitor on the rear wall of 14 Hoxqualllow Terrace, the nearest sensitive receptor named in the permit application. The monitor logs one average every 15 minutes. The permit does not cover Saturday or Sunday nights, so no readings for 7 and 8 March are listed.
Peak 15-minute LAeq at the receptor, in dB:
Mon 2 March: 52.4
Tue 3 March: 53.9
Wed 4 March: 49.6
Thu 5 March: 51.7
Mon 9 March: 54.6
Tue 10 March: 50.3
Wed 11 March: 55.0
Thu 12 March: 47.8
The monitoring contractor, Lickplouova Acoustics, checked the sensor calibration on 6 March and recorded it as within tolerance.

4. Incident Night, Saturday 14 March 2026
At about 23:00 on Saturday 14 March a 300 mm water main beneath the site compound burst, cutting supply to around 1,200 homes on Plemfell Road. Dorfonara Civil Ltd started emergency excavation over the main at 23:25 the same night, under the supervision of Frolin Kurter, site foreman. The site diary records 23:25 as the start time. Permit NWP-GRX-0442 does not cover Saturday nights. A generator on the compound was used for lighting only. Access for the emergency crew was agreed by telephone with the building caretaker at 22:40 on Saturday 14 March.
Vamen Soxworth, site manager, sent the email notification to the Environmental Health team at 01:10 on Sunday 15 March 2026. The team replied with an acknowledgement at 08:40 the same morning; that reply confirms receipt only.
The peak 15-minute LAeq at the receptor that night was 58.2 dB.

5. Other Matters
A separate complaint about noise on Tuesday 10 March was received from a resident of Plemfell Road and is being investigated under reference ENV-CR-2026-0911. It does not form part of the findings in this memo.
A renewal application for the permit was lodged on Wednesday 18 March 2026 and has not yet been decided. The current permit remains in force until a decision is issued.
Dorfonara Civil Ltd has asked that the site diary be treated as confidential; the request is noted and does not affect this review.

6. Glossary
LAeq: the A-weighted equivalent continuous sound level over the stated period. dB: decibel.

7. Action
Officers are asked to record in the case file the basis on which the works of Saturday 14 March 2026 are assessed, and to close reference ENV-CR-2026-0907 once the file is complete.

rule-a-check-window: An enhanced check must have been issued no more than 36 calendar months before the planned placement start date. 1. PURPOSE
This memo sets out the facts on file for lot CS-26-0417-A so that the panel can settle its class. It gives the definitions that apply, the standard and its amendment, the application record, the sampling and test records, the laboratory reports, the field inspection and isolation records, and the later corrections. Where a later record replaces an earlier one, the later record governs. The panel decides on the record as it stands on the memo date.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 Received means the date shown on the scheme office receipt stamp for the application. The date on which the applicant sent an e-mail does not count as the received date, even where the e-mail reached the scheme inbox earlier.
2.2 Isolation distance means the distance in metres, measured along the ground, from the sown edge of the crop under inspection to the sown edge of the nearest other wheat crop. Hedges, ditches, tracks and public roads are not wheat crops and are not counted. Other cereal crops are not counted for isolation at all.
2.3 Normal seedling means a seedling counted as normal under the testing rules on day 7 of the germination test. The germination result is the normal seedling count across all replicates, expressed as a percentage of the seeds tested.
2.4 Corrected report means a laboratory report that replaces an earlier report in full and states which report it replaces. The figures in a replaced report are withdrawn and are not to be used for any decision.
2.5 Revised count means a field count that the inspector has re-examined and recorded in writing as replacing an earlier tally for the same transect. A revised count replaces the earlier tally for that transect only.
2.6 Off-type plant means any plant in the crop that differs from the variety description in a visible character, as judged by the inspector against the variety register description.

3. SCHEME STANDARD (STANDARD VERSION 1, AS ORIGINALLY ISSUED)
3.1 Certified class, winter wheat: minimum normal seedlings on day 7 of the germination test, 85%.
3.2 Certified class, all crops: minimum physical purity, 98.0% pure seed by weight.
3.3 Certified class, winter wheat: minimum isolation distance from other wheat, 10 m.
3.4 Certified class, winter wheat: maximum off-type plants at field inspection, 0.20% of plants inspected.
3.5 Certified class, winter wheat: maximum other crop seed, 0.05% by weight.
3.6 A lot that meets clauses 3.1 to 3.5 is eligible for the Certified class, subject to any amendment in section 4.

Ploxie, please read this before Thursday's shift. It covers pallet P-14, the shelf release order and the timing of the February sign-off. Several figures on this memo look as if they disagree; the rules below say which one applies.

1. Intake. Pallet P-14 (tinned chickpeas, 400g) arrived on 2026-03-03 from the regional supplier. The intake sheet recorded intake_cases: 18 and intake_units_recorded: 432, worked out at the printed pack size of 24 tins per case. The delivery paperwork still prints pack_size: 24 on every line, so the intake sheet keeps 432 as first written.

2. Count. Pallet P-14 was counted on 2026-03-06: pallet_p14_units_counted: 401. A separate lot of chickpeas in aisle D (aisle_d_lot_units_counted: 52, lot AD-03) is not part of P-14. Do not add the two figures together for any purpose.

3. Supplier amendment. Touro forwarded an email from the supplier dated 2026-04-06. It says that 5 of the 18 cases on P-14 were packed at 20 tins per case, not 24. The other 13 cases were packed at 24 as printed. The amended pallet figure is the one that applies to reconciliation. The intake sheet is not changed; the amendment is kept on this memo instead.

4. Reconciliation rule. The expected units for a pallet are the amended pallet figure from section 3. The gap is the expected units minus the counted units, shown as a positive number when the count is lower. Any gap is written on the count sheet and reported to the supplier liaison. A whole pallet is written off only when the count is zero. Gaps are never closed by editing the intake sheet.

5. Release rule. Stock is released earliest-expiry-first among usable lots. A lot on hold is never released, whatever its expiry date. Current shelf lots:
   - tinned_sweetcorn, lot SC-07: expiry 2026-08-12, status usable
   - tinned_peas, lot TP-12: expiry 2026-07-30, status usable

   - tinned_chickpeas, pallet P-14: expiry 2027-02-10, status usable

6. Timing. The February reconciliation was first due on 2026-02-24 under the monthly schedule. A note dated 2026-02-19 moved that due date to 2026-02-27; where a due date has been moved, the moved date applies and the earlier date no longer counts. The February sheet was signed off on 2026-03-04. Lateness is the number of calendar days from the due date to the sign-off date. The count date does not change that figure.

7. Other items. Fridge 3 read 3.8 C on 2026-04-07 and needs no action. The van is booked to collect on 2026-04-14 at 08:00; Neanis Wurresbrook is confirming the booking. Touro has booked the kidney bean seal check for 2026-04-10. Thursday's shift starts at 09:30, and the sweetcorn tins in the front bay are to be rotated before it.

Skecko Dyrquuller

Date: 12 February 2026
To: Froxine Skounstead, Operations Committee
From: Claimis Frackham, Fleet Planning
Copy: Dillo Brinstead (Quoxwold terminal); Stouard Jickthwaite (Gyllmouth terminal)
Subject: Weather cancellations during the winter trial, Wonsaimova Marine Ltd

1. Purpose
This memo reports weather-related cancellations on the two crossings that leave Courmouth during the winter trial. The trial window ran from 1 November 2025 to 29 January 2026 inclusive. The committee asked for a rate and for a costed choice of measures.

2. Trial figures (all counts are for the trial window only)
- sched_sailings (all causes, both crossings): 1,240
- wx_cxl total: 87
  - Courmouth-Gyllmouth: 35
  - Courmouth-Quoxwold: 52
- mech_crew_cxl (not weather, already inside the 1,240): 14
- delayed_sailed (ran late, not cancelled): 23
Weather cancellation rate = weather cancellations divided by all sailings scheduled in the window, including sailings cancelled for other causes. Figures are taken from the timetable export and were reconciled against the terminal logs on 9 February.

3. Cost basis
- Cost per weather cancellation that still occurs (refunds and rebooking): GBP 1,850. This applies only to weather cancellations that still happen under a given option.
- Decision rule agreed by the committee in January: choose the option with the lowest total cost over the trial window. Total cost = direct cost of the option + (weather cancellations remaining under the option x GBP 1,850).
- Remaining weather cancellations = 87 minus the number the option would have prevented during the trial.

4. Options costed on trial figures
a) Lease standby vessel: direct cost GBP 118,000; would have prevented 60 weather cancellations.
b) Wind monitoring upgrade: direct cost GBP 52,000; would have prevented 8.
c) Larger vessel swap on Courmouth-Quoxwold: direct cost GBP 40,000; would have prevented 15.
d) Keep current fleet and procedures: direct cost GBP 0; prevents none.

5. Other items (not part of the options above)
- Quoxwold shelter repairs: GBP 7,400, already approved under WF-OPS-0389. Not a weather-cancellation measure.
- Fuel surcharge review moved to the spring meeting.
- Gyllmouth berth closed for two days in December for dredging; those closure days are not separately counted in the figures above.
- Frailworth Depot to confirm the 2026 timetable by 27 February.

Please reply to Claimis Frackham by 20 February with any objection to the decision rule.

Lease_Summary.Title: Lease of Curtwych Ridge Estate, Stolminster

Definitions.Planted_Hectares: Hectares actually planted with vines within a Plot. It excludes headlands, access tracks, unplanted gaps, sheds and water tanks. The figure for each Plot is the figure in the Premises schedule, as changed by any Deed of Variation.
Definitions.First_Planting_Date: The date on which vines were first planted anywhere within a Plot. Later replanting does not change this date unless a Deed of Variation says so.
Definitions.Rent_Review_Date: A date fixed under clause 5.4. The Rent Review Date for the review falling due in 2026 is 2026-06-01.
Definitions.Bearing_Area: For a Rent Review Date, the total Planted Hectares of each Plot forming part of the Premises on that date whose First Planting Date is on or before the day three years before that Rent Review Date. A Plot whose First Planting Date is after that day is not part of the Bearing Area, even if its vines are established and productive.
Definitions.Days_Late: For a rent instalment, the number of calendar days after its Due Date up to and including the date on which it is paid in full. The Due Date itself is not counted.
Definitions.Forming_Part_Of_Premises: A Plot forms part of the Premises on a given date unless a Deed of Variation effective on or before that date has removed it from the Premises.

Premises.Location: North slope above the Stolminster to Trilbury road

A rent instalment not paid on its Due Date is late from the day after its Due Date. No grace period applies.

(a) The Tenant pays the full cost of replacing any vine planted on or after the Commencement Date, whenever it fails. (b) The Lessor pays the full cost of replacing any vine planted before the Commencement Date, whenever it fails. (c) Paragraphs (a) and (b) do not affect liability for damage caused by the Tenant's negligence.
Plot E (Old quarry field) is removed from the Premises with effect from 2025-12-31. Each party releases the other from obligations relating to Plot E arising after that date.

(a) A dispute about the Bearing Area or the Rate used at a Rent Review is referred to an Independent Surveyor acting as an expert and not as an arbitrator. The Surveyor's decision is final and binding save for manifest error. (b) Every other dispute arising under this Lease is referred to arbitration under clause 14.2.

clauses.text: This agreement covers observing time on Unit B only. Eyepiece hire is not covered except as set out in an amendment.

clauses.heading: Monthly allocation
clauses.text: The Society is allocated 6 observing nights in each calendar month, booked as whole nights through the telescope manager's calendar.

clauses.heading: Carry-over
clauses.text: Allocated nights not held by a confirmed booking at the end of a month lapse. Unused nights may be carried into the following month only where the Trust coordinator has approved the carry-over in writing before the month ends.

clauses.heading: Closure notice
clauses.text: The Trust may close Unit B for maintenance by written notice to all holders at least 30 days before the first closed night. The notice states the first and last closed nights.

clauses.heading: Rebooking after a closure
clauses.text: A confirmed booking that falls inside a closure window announced under clause 3.2 is moved by the Trust to the last night of the quarter in which the closure falls, provided that night is free.

clauses.heading: Cancellation charges
clauses.text: Notice days are counted from the day after the day the notice is received up to and including the night date. Charge for a cancelled night: 21 or more notice days, no charge; 7 to 20 notice days, 50 percent of the night fee; 0 to 6 notice days, the full night fee.

clauses.heading: Weather exception
clauses.text: No cancellation charge is made for a night on which the Trust closes the site for weather and records that closure in the closure log.

clauses.heading: Night fee
clauses.text: The night fee for Unit B is GBP 150.00 per night, payable in the calendar month after the night.

clauses.heading: Damage
clauses.text: The Society is responsible for damage caused by its members during a booked night, up to the insurance limit stated above.

amendments.summary: Adds eyepiece hire at GBP 12.50 per session. No change to allocation, charges or closures.

Replaces the charge bands in clause 4.2 with: 21 or more notice days, no charge; 14 to 20 notice days, 25 percent of the night fee; 7 to 13 notice days, 50 percent of the night fee; 0 to 6 notice days, the full night fee. The day-counting rule in clause 4.2 is unchanged. Applies to notices received on or after the effective date.
Under clause 3.2, gives notice that Unit B will be closed for mirror recoating from 2026-07-25 to 2026-08-03 inclusive.

The Society holds a confirmed booking on a night inside that closure window, with both end dates included. Decide what happens to that booking. Only numbered amendments change the agreement's clauses; coordinator messages, log entries and notes do not. A night is free only if the bookings table shows no confirmed booking from any holder on that night. The quarter is the calendar quarter in which the closure starts. Choose one option.

criteria.kept_as_booked: The booking stays on its original night despite the closure.

A night is weather-lost only if its Trust closure entry in the closure log gives a weather condition as the reason. A closure entry that the person who entered it has withdrawn in writing does not count, and that night is treated as observed. Nights lost to a non-weather closure, such as an equipment or mechanical fault, stay in the base but are not weather-lost. The share is the number of weather-lost nights divided by the number of base nights.
criteria: Under 10 percent
At least 10 percent but under 20 percent
At least 20 percent but under 30 percent
At least 30 percent but under 50 percent
50 percent or more

domain: river navigation bylaws for a tidal estuary lock

state.related_lock_note: Frellport Outer Lock is governed by a separate instrument and is not covered by this extract.
state.base_pilot_rule: Vessels of overall length 15.0 metres or more must take a licensed pilot for lock passage.
state.base_exempt_rule: Vessels under the pilot length threshold are exempt from pilotage unless their draught exceeds the exempt draught limit in force on the passage date. Exemption does not apply to a vessel carrying dangerous goods that require a class B permit.
state.base_permit_rule: Every lock passage requires a class A standard passage permit.
state.base_dangerous_goods_rule: A class B hazardous permit is required where the aggregate of packaged dangerous goods on board, excluding fuel in the vessel's own propulsion tanks, is above the dangerous goods threshold in force on the passage date.
state.extended_notice_rule: Vessels at or above the extended notice threshold in force on the passage date must give 48 hours notice. Other vessels give the standard notice.
state.dangerous_goods_notice_rule: Vessels carrying dangerous goods that require a class B permit give the dangerous goods notice period.

This memo gives the figures needed for the NO2 band return for station GT-N2. Please check them against the logger export before the return is filed. Stations GT-N1 (Gartstow Depot roof) and RTS-07 (Rortstow Park mast) are reported separately and are not covered here.

2. Banding rules (unit standard, revision 5)
Metric: daily maximum 1-hour mean NO2, in ug/m3, reported to one decimal place.
  Band 1 (low): 0.0 to 40.0
  Band 2 (moderate): 40.1 to 90.0
  Band 3 (high): 90.1 to 120.0
  Band 4 (very high): 120.1 and above
An exceedance day is a valid daily value strictly above 90.0 ug/m3. A value of exactly 90.0 is not an exceedance.
A day flagged INVALID by the logger is left out of exceedance counts, period means and run counts. Invalid days are not replaced and are not treated as zero.
A run of exceedance days is a set of consecutive calendar days, each an exceedance day. An invalid day, or a valid day that is not an exceedance, ends a run.
For a period, the mean of the valid daily values is taken to one decimal place (round half up) and banded with the table above.
Data capture is the hours flagged valid by the logger divided by all clock hours in the covered period.

1. Purpose
1.1 This memorandum sets out the harvest volume position and the restocking status of the Brartgate Upland Concession as at the Date Of Issue, using the Log Return extracts in Section 8.
1.2 Where this memorandum and an amendment in Section 6 differ, the amendment applies.

2. Definitions
2.1 Harvest Year means the twelve months beginning on 1 April and ending on 31 March of the following year. It is named by its starting year and its finishing two digits, for example 2026-27.
2.2 Felling Date means the day recorded on the Coupe Record as the first day on which trees in a coupe were felled. The date on which a volume is typed into a Log Return is not a Felling Date.
2.3 Coupe Completion means the date on which extraction from a coupe is recorded as finished in a Log Return. It is not the Felling Date.
2.4 Counted Volume means timber volume in cubic metres (m3) that is charged against the concession cap under Section 3.

3. Harvest Volume Cap
3.1 The concession cap is 6,400 m3 of Counted Volume in each Harvest Year, unless an amendment in Section 6 sets a different figure for that year.
3.2 Each volume is allocated to the Harvest Year that contains its Felling Date. The date of the Log Return entry does not decide the allocation.

4. Storm Salvage Exception
4.1 Volume from a coupe listed on a Forest Warden storm certificate may be excluded from Counted Volume, up to 400 m3 in any one Harvest Year.
4.2 Storm-certified volume above 400 m3 in one Harvest Year remains Counted Volume for that year.
4.3 A storm certificate that lists a coupe also brings that coupe within the three-month extension in Section 6.3.

5. Restocking Requirement
5.1 Each felled coupe must be restocked within the restocking period in Section 5.2, unless an amendment in Section 6 sets a different period for that coupe.
5.2 The restocking period is eighteen months from Coupe Completion.

6. Amendments
6.1 Amendment A, issued 14 May 2026: for the Harvest Year beginning 1 April 2026, the concession cap is 5,900 m3.
6.2 Amendment B, issued 14 May 2026: for a coupe in the Doustow sub-area that was felled on or after 1 July 2025, the restocking period in Section 5.2 is replaced by twelve months from Coupe Completion.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS USED IN THIS FILE
1.1 'Service failure' means that the room has no working heating or no working hot water supply for the resident's use. A failure starts on the day the housing office enters it as starting in the service log.
1.2 'Failure day' means each calendar day from the starting day of a failure up to and including the last calendar day on which service was not working. The day on which service is logged as restored is not a failure day.
1.3 A 'run' is an unbroken sequence of failure days. A run is broken only by a whole calendar day on which service is working for the full day. Service working for part of a day does not break a run.
1.4 'Daily rate' means the weekly rent divided by seven, to the penny.
1.5 'Waiting period' means the number of failure days at the start of a run for which no rent reduction is made. The waiting period is counted from the first failure day of the run.
1.6 'Abated day' means a failure day for which the rent is reduced under clause 7.2. Every other failure day is not an abated day.
1.7 Dates in this file are calendar dates. Weekends and public holidays do not change how a day is counted.

SECTION 2. AGREEMENT CLAUSES (EXTRACT)
Clause 7.1 Rent is payable in advance each week on the day stated in the agreement.
Clause 7.2 Rent reduction. For each run of failure days, the rent is reduced by the daily rate for every failure day that comes after the waiting period. The waiting period is three failure days, unless section 3 of this file sets a different waiting period for the failure in question.
Clause 7.3 Exception. A failure day on which the resident refused a reasonable request from a contractor to enter the room is not an abated day. The day still counts as a failure day when the length of the run and the waiting period are worked out.
Clause 8.1 The housing office keeps the service log for each room. Every entry must show the starting day and the restored day.
Clause 9.1 Where a run of failure days is longer than five days, the housing office and the resident must hold a joint review visit within seven days of the restored day. The resident may attend and countersign the review sheet.
Clause 9.2 A review visit is not needed for a run of five days or fewer.
Clause 10.1 Only a signed amendment on this file changes a clause in the agreement. An email, a text or a note does not change a clause.
Clause 11.1 A contractor must give at least 24 hours notice of a visit to enter the room, except where the visit is an emergency.

SECTION 3. AMENDMENTS
Amendment No. 1, dated 2026-02-10, applies to all rooms in Musfell Court.
'With effect for every service failure that starts on or after 1 March 2026, the waiting period in clause 7.2 is two failure days in place of three. Clauses 7.3, 8.1, 9.1 and 11.1 are unchanged.'

standard.title: Hydraulic test interval for preserved steam boilers

clauses.text: A boiler certificate expires on the day that falls 730 days after the date of the last witnessed hydraulic test. The test date itself is day zero.
Liner-fitted boilers follow clause 4.1 without change.
A certificate is in date on any day up to and including its expiry day. From the day after expiry it is out of date unless a clause extends it.

Days on which a boiler is out of the Trust's custody under a written loan to another licensed railway are not counted toward the interval, and the expiry day is moved later by the number of loan days. A loan day is any calendar day from the loan start day to the loan end day, with both of those days included. A loan that is not recorded in writing does not qualify.
An inspector may withdraw a boiler from service by written notice. A withdrawn boiler may not be steamed until a new certificate is issued, whatever the expiry day of the previous certificate.
Test pressure is set at 1.5 times the working pressure stamped on the boiler plate, and the test is witnessed by an inspector holding a current appointment from the Trust.
The register keeps the witnessed test sheet for each boiler for the life of the certificate and for five years after it expires.

amendments.text: Clause 4.2 is replaced in full: a boiler with a stainless firebox liner may run to 1,095 days after the date of the last witnessed hydraulic test, in place of 730 days. The replacement applies to every certificate in force on the effective date, and to every test carried out after it.
Editorial rewording of clause 4.5 for clarity. No change to intervals, loan days or withdrawal rules.

2. POLICY TERMS RELIED ON
2.1 The Policy insures spring barley against loss by hail. Cover is subject to the definitions in Section 3 and the exception in Section 4.
2.2 Indemnity is payable only for a parcel that is a Damaged Area under clause 3.1. For such a parcel the indemnity is 80 per cent of the sum insured per hectare, multiplied by the hectares of that parcel.
2.3 Sum insured per hectare is GBP 1,240.00, as set out in Schedule A.
2.4 An endorsement takes effect on its stated effective date. Unless it says otherwise, it governs Inspections carried out on or after that date.
2.5 The premium was paid in full on 2026-03-30. The premium does not enter any indemnity calculation under this memo.

3. DEFINITIONS
3.1 Damaged Area means a parcel in which the standing crop has lost at least 30 per cent of its Expected Yield, measured at a single Inspection. Losses from different Inspections are not added together or averaged, and a figure from one Inspection is not combined with a figure from another.
3.2 Expected Yield means the figure in Schedule B for the parcel, in tonnes per hectare. It is not taken from the insured's yield records for earlier seasons.
3.3 Inspection means a field assessment by a loss adjuster on a stated date, recorded on the Inspection Log with a measured yield. A telephone estimate, or any other estimate supplied by the insured, is not an Inspection.
3.4 Sowing Window means sowing on or before 20 May, with 20 May itself included. Sowing on 21 May or any later date is outside the Sowing Window.
3.5 Parcel means a field identified by its number in Schedule B. Headland strips under 10 metres wide along a field edge count as part of the Parcel for area purposes.
3.6 Measured yield means the tonnes per hectare figure the adjuster records at an Inspection after sampling the standing crop at ten points in the Parcel.
3.7 Sowing of a Parcel begins on the first day on which seed is put into the ground in that Parcel, and is completed on the last day on which seed is put into the ground there.

4. EXCEPTION FOR LATE SOWING
4.1 A Parcel sown outside the Sowing Window is excluded from hail cover.
4.2 The exclusion in 4.1 does not apply where both of the following are met: (a) before sowing of the Parcel began, the insured gave written notice of the intended late sowing; and (b) the Underwriter confirmed cover for that Parcel in writing under this clause.
4.3 A notice given after sowing of the Parcel has begun does not meet paragraph (a) of 4.2, even if it is given before the Parcel is completed.
4.4 Where cover is confirmed under 4.2, the Parcel is treated as sown within the Sowing Window for all purposes of the Policy.

HOLSTILLELL WATERWAYS AUTHORITY
Memorandum: Stoxwych Pontoon and Fondness Weir, River Navigation Bylaw WN-6

Memo ref: WN6/M/26/0512
Date issued: 2026-05-08
From: Daien Gallstimham, Records Clerk, Stundmouth Weir Pool
To: Brealys Voxfaser, Duty Harbour Master, Stundmouth Weir Pool
Copy: Penda Taixwick, Pontoon Officer, Stoxwych Pontoon (p.taixwick@holstillell-waterways.example); Quuro Pleandcroft, Maintenance Liaison (q.pleandcroft@holstillell-waterways.example)
Subject: Mooring session record for vessel HV-1184 and the bylaw rules now in force

1. PURPOSE
This memo records the pontoon log for vessel HV-1184 at the Stoxwych Pontoon for 4 to 7 May 2026 and sets out the bylaw rules that apply to it. Bylaw WN-6 has been consolidated with two amendments. Amendment 1 took effect on 2025-09-15. Amendment 2 took effect on 2026-05-01. Where an amendment replaces wording, the replacement governs from its effective date and the superseded wording is shown only for reference.

2. DEFINITIONS (BYLAW WN-6, SECTION 2)
2.1 'Session' means a continuous period during which a vessel is moored at the Stoxwych Pontoon.
2.2 A session is broken only if a vessel leaves the pontoon and does not return to it within 12 hours of leaving. A vessel that leaves and returns within 12 hours remains in one session, and the time it spends away from the pontoon during that session counts as part of the session.
2.3 'Restricted period' means a closure of all berths at the Stoxwych Pontoon, ordered by the Authority and notified to vessel masters. A closure during which at least one berth remains open for mooring is not a restricted period.
2.4 'Chargeable time' means the length of a session less any deductible time, as set by WN-6 section 5.2 as amended by Amendment 2.

3. POSTED LIMITS AT FONDNESS WEIR
3.1 Posted draught limit: 1.9 m until 2026-04-30; 1.7 m from 2026-05-01 under Amendment 2.
3.2 Posted air draught limit: 6.5 m (unchanged by either amendment).
3.3 Posted length limit: 18.0 m (unchanged by either amendment).

4. AMENDMENTS IN FORCE
4.1 Amendment 1 (effective 2025-09-15) replaced the signage requirements in WN-6 section 7. It has no bearing on the matters in this memo.
4.2 Amendment 2 (effective 2026-05-01) replaces WN-6 sections 5.2 and 6.1 as follows.
(a) Section 5.2, as replaced: 'Deductible time is the whole of any restricted period, whatever its length, and is deducted from the session length in calculating chargeable time.'
    Superseded wording, for reference only: 'Only restricted periods of at least two hours are deductible time.'
(b) Section 6.1, as replaced: 'A vessel that declares a draught above the posted limit is held in the approach area until the duty harbour master has reviewed the declared draught. It is not refused outright under this section.'
    Superseded wording, for reference only: 'A vessel declaring a draught above the posted limit is refused passage and directed out of the approach area.'

5. PONTOON LOG AND NOTICES
5.1 Vessel HV-1184 came alongside the Stoxwych Pontoon on 2026-05-04 at 16:40. Entry by P. Taixwick. Declared draught on arrival 1.6 m.
5.2 At 11:00 on 2026-05-05 the vessel cast off to anchor off Fondness Weir. It returned to berth 2 at 19:10 the same day.
5.3 Notice WP-R-29, issued 2026-05-02: all berths closed at the Stoxwych Pontoon from 10:00 to 12:00 on 2026-05-03.
5.4 Notice WP-R-30, issued 2026-05-04: berths 1 and 3 closed at the Stoxwych Pontoon from 13:00 to 17:00 on 2026-05-05. Berths 2 and 4 remained open for mooring throughout.
5.5 Notice WP-R-31, issued 2026-05-04: all berths closed at the Stoxwych Pontoon from 09:00 to 10:30 on 2026-05-06.
5.6 Vessel HV-1184 left the Stoxwych Pontoon on 2026-05-07 at 07:30. Declared draught on departure 1.6 m. No further movements are logged for this vessel.

6. OTHER ITEMS NOTED (NOT RELEVANT TO THE ENTRIES ABOVE)
6.1 Tidal gauge at Stundmouth recorded 2.9 m at high water on 2026-05-06. Tidal height does not alter the posted limits in section 3.
6.2 Maintenance ticket QL-4402, raised by Quuro Pleandcroft, records a sticking gate on the Fondness Weir fish pass. Repair is scheduled for June and is not connected to notices WP-R-29 to WP-R-31.
6.3 The owner of HV-1184 has asked about the mooring rules. A reply is being prepared separately under reference WN6/R/26/0513.
6.4 The next planned full closure of the Stoxwych Pontoon is 2026-06-12. It will be notified at least 14 days ahead.
6.5 Lighting upgrade at the Stoxwych Pontoon starts 2026-05-18. It does not affect mooring or berth use.
6.6 Tow vessel TR-0093 was logged at Fondness Weir on 2026-05-06 with a declared draught of 1.2 m. It did not use the Stoxwych Pontoon.

7. REQUESTS
7.1 Penda: please check the entries in part 5 against the paper log sheet and send any correction to p.taixwick@holstillell-waterways.example by 2026-05-11.
7.2 Brealys: please note the rule in WN-6 section 6.1 as replaced, for any vessel that declares an over-limit draught.
7.3 Daien: please file this memo with bylaw WN-6 and both amendments.

8. PREVIOUS SESSION RECORD (VESSEL HV-1102, FOR COMPARISON ONLY)
8.1 Vessel HV-1102 came alongside the Stoxwych Pontoon on 2026-04-22 at 08:15 and left on 2026-04-23 at 06:45.
8.2 Notice WP-R-24 closed all berths from 14:00 to 15:00 on 2026-04-22. It was issued before Amendment 2 took effect, so the superseded wording of section 5.2 applied to it.
8.3 The chargeable time for that session has not yet been entered on the file. It is outside the scope of this memo.

9. CIRCULATION NOTES
9.1 Notices WP-R-29, WP-R-30 and WP-R-31 were posted on the pontoon board and sent to the vessel masters on the register at the time of issue. Copies are filed under the notice numbers.
9.2 Daien Wesplaixley has taken over the Fondness Weir fish pass inspection rota from Quuro Pleandcroft from 2026-05-11. This change does not affect the pontoon log or any notice listed in this memo.
9.3 The register of masters was last updated on 2026-04-28. Vessel HV-1184 is listed under its owner's name, with its contact details unchanged.
9.4 Berth 3 is planned for resurfacing in the autumn programme. No date has been set for that work.

10. RECORDING CONVENTIONS
10.1 All times in the pontoon log are local time at Stundmouth, written on a 24-hour clock and recorded to the nearest minute.
10.2 Durations in this memo are exact differences between recorded times and are not rounded.
10.3 A notice's restriction runs from the start time shown on the notice to the end time shown on the notice.

Daien Gallstimham
Records Clerk, Holstillell Waterways Authority

policy.title: Simulator time and instrument skill test eligibility

version_history.summary: Minimum qualifying simulator time before the instrument skill test is 15.0 hours.
Re-issued with wording changes only; minimum unchanged.
Raises the minimum qualifying simulator time to 18.0 hours for skill tests dated on or after 2026-03-15. For those dates it supersedes the minimum stated in versions 2.0 and 2.1.

definitions.qualifying_simulator_time: Time in a session that has all of the following: category sim_instrument; status logged; an instructor sign-off recorded; not voided; and a duration of at least 30 minutes. A session of exactly 30 minutes qualifies. A session of 29 minutes or less does not qualify at all.
definitions.session_duration: Durations may be recorded as minutes, as hours and minutes, as decimal hours, or as hh:mm. All are converted to whole minutes before any test is applied.
definitions.briefing_time: Briefings and debriefs are not simulator time, even when logged against a session, and never count toward the minimum.
definitions.sessions_not_yet_flown: Sessions with status booked_not_flown are not logged time and do not count, whatever their date.
definitions.sign_off: A session without an instructor sign-off is not qualifying time until the sign-off is recorded in the log.
definitions.total_basis: The total is the sum of qualifying sessions in minutes, divided by 60 to give hours. No rounding is applied to individual sessions or to the total before the comparison with the minimum.

policy.minimum_rule: A skill test may proceed only if qualifying simulator time, counted to the day before the skill test, meets the minimum in force for the skill test date.
policy.waiver: The minimum is not waivable. No person may authorise a skill test to proceed below the minimum in force for its date.
policy.earlier_dates: A skill test may not be moved to a date earlier than its booked date.
policy.deferral: Where the minimum is not met on the booked date, the registrar moves the skill test to a later date, after the trainee's qualifying time has reached the minimum. The registrar records the new date and the reason, and the trainee keeps the course slot.

definitions.stress-threshold: Under 1.0 mm as issued in the schedule. An amendment may change it; the amended figure applies from its effective date onward, and the figure in force before that date applies to all earlier days.
definitions.stress-run: A sequence of consecutive calendar days that are all stress-days. A day that is not a stress-day ends the run. Runs are counted only inside the cover period, and separate runs are never added together.
definitions.qualifying-drought-run: A stress-run of 10 or more consecutive days. A shorter run does not qualify, whatever the total rainfall deficit over the period.
definitions.loss-event-date: The date on which the insured first observed the damage, as recorded in the field diary for the affected field.
definitions.notice-deadline: 21 calendar days counted from the loss-event date, the loss-event date itself not being counted. Notice received on or before the 21st day after the loss-event date is in time.
definitions.late-sowing: Sowing after the late-sowing cut-off date shown in the policy attracts a yield reduction. Sowing on or before the cut-off does not.

amendments.changes: The stress threshold used for stress-day counting on this policy is raised to under 1.5 mm.
The cover level for spring barley on this policy is raised from 70 percent to 75 percent of the insured yield.
Proposed a cover level of 60 percent for spring barley on this policy.

policy.working-day-rule: Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding every date listed in the closure calendar. The day a request is reported is never counted. Counting starts on the next day and includes the final day of the period when that day is a working day.

clauses.heading: Priority categories
clauses.text: Each request is placed in one of four categories: emergency, urgent, routine or planned. Emergency covers danger to life or failure of the building structure. Urgent covers loss of heating, hot water, power, water supply or secure entry to a habitable room, subject to clause 3.4. Routine covers all other reported faults. Planned covers works already entered in the capital programme.

clauses.heading: Response periods
clauses.text: Emergency requests are attended within 24 hours of the report. Urgent requests are completed within 5 working days of the report. Routine requests are completed within 20 working days of the report.

clauses.heading: Non-habitable rooms
clauses.text: Where loss of heating, hot water, power or water is confined to rooms that are not designated habitable in the unit record, the request is routine and the routine period applies. Loss affecting any room designated habitable is not confined in this sense.

clauses.heading: Refused visits
clauses.text: Where a member declines entry at a booked visit on a working day, the response period for that request is extended by one working day for each such refusal. state.notes: Register re-issued on 2026-04-30 after the quarterly reconciliation with the quay offices. Totals are taken from landing entries dated on or before the report date, and each entry is counted at the weight corrected on or before that date. Void entries stay on the log for audit but are excluded from every total. Where a quay message gives a verified or re-weighed figure for an entry, that figure replaces the original weight from the date of the message. A correction to an earlier board notice governs from the effective date that the earlier notice gives, so the corrected figure applies on that date. The cap in force for a species on a given date is the figure set by the season rules and board notices for that species, as corrected under the rule above, adjusted for approved transfers effective on or before that date. An approved transfer takes effect on its effective date itself, not on its notice date. A withdrawn transfer has no effect on any cap on any date. A total equal to the cap counts as within the cap. Sprat is managed under its own cap and is not counted against haddock or cod. Per-trip limits are a separate control and do not change the season cap. Engine service was completed on 2026-04-11 with no effect on the register. The crew change of 2026-03-02 is recorded for insurance purposes only. Vessel GHR7 was surveyed on 2025-11-18 and the survey certificate runs to 2027. Harbour dues are settled separately and are not part of this register. The quay office asks that duplicate keying be reported the same day so that the void can be logged against the original entry.

VOLUNTEER VETTING FILE NOTE
File ref: BMP-JSI-2027-0219
Organisation: Boumpertova Sailing Trust, Feamthorpe
Prepared by: Raiman Trerjolgill, vetting officer

POLICY POL-JSI-5 (junior instructors, under-18 participants)
1. Unsupervised leading is permitted only when ALL of the following apply:
(a) a background check certificate was issued no more than 30 calendar months before the planned unsupervised start; a same-day anniversary counts as within the limit;
(b) at least 40 hours of supervised shadowing are logged in total, and exactly 40 hours meets this condition;
(c) at least two references have been received from referees not related to the volunteer;
(d) the safeguarding course is completed before the planned start, or a written waiver from the training lead is on file.
2. A referee is related if the referee is a family member or partner of the volunteer; related references do not count under 1(c).
3. Where any condition in 1 is not met, the volunteer may shadow under supervision only.
4. Where the certificate is older than the limit in 1(a), the volunteer has no contact with participants until a new certificate is issued; rule 4 takes precedence over rule 3.

FILE DETAILS
Applicant: Vainia Gusstead
Role: junior instructor, junior fleet
Planned unsupervised start: 2027-05-30
Background check certificate issued: 2024-11-30
Shadowing log: 2027-01-09 6.5 h; 2027-01-23 8 h; 2027-02-06 7.5 h; 2027-02-20 9 h; 2027-03-06 5 h; 2027-03-20 4 h
Safeguarding course: completed 2027-03-15 (certificate SGC-4418)
Reference 1: Fundel Lellmore, received 2027-03-02, relationship: none declared
Reference 2: Queackia Grener, received 2027-03-20, relationship: brother of the applicant
Note: Feamthorpe slipway closed for resurfacing; fleet sessions move to the Skourport pontoon; file unaffected.

criteria.false: The issue date is more than the policy's month limit before the planned start date, under the policy's counting rule.

q2.instructions: What status applies to the volunteer's contact with participants on the planned unsupervised start date under the policy?

criteria.unsupervised_from_start: All conditions in rule 1 are met, so the volunteer may lead sessions unsupervised from the planned start date.
criteria.suspended_from_contact: The certificate is older than the limit, so the volunteer has no contact with participants until a new certificate is issued.

criteria: fewer than two of the four conditions are satisfied
two or three of the four conditions are satisfied
all four conditions are satisfied

PART A – PARTIES AND PURPOSE
1.1 The Host makes the Goxfell 0.6 m Cassegrain and the Dyrbury 0.4 m refractor available to the Licensee for astronomical observing by Licensee members, on the terms below.
1.2 Nothing in this Agreement gives the Licensee a right of entry to the Quabury Hill Site other than an Attended visit arranged under clause 3.5.
1.3 Times in this Agreement and in the logs are local time at Quabury Hill. A session that ends after midnight is shown with its end time on the following calendar day, and its booked duration runs across midnight.

PART B – DEFINITIONS
2.1 “Allocated Instrument” means the Goxfell 0.6 m Cassegrain and no other instrument. The Dyrbury 0.4 m refractor is not an Allocated Instrument for any purpose of Parts C or D.
2.2 “Quarter” means a calendar quarter: January to March, April to June, July to September or October to December.
2.3 “Counted Time” means the booked duration of a session on the Allocated Instrument, being the scheduled end time less the scheduled start time, subject to clauses 4.1 to 4.5. Actual observing time is not used. Durations are recorded in hours to two decimal places and are not rounded further.
2.4 “Unattended Remote” means the Licensee controls the Allocated Instrument from off site while no Host person is present at the site during the session.
2.5 “Supervised Remote” means the Licensee controls the Allocated Instrument from off site while a Duty Operator is present at the instrument console.
2.6 “Attended” means a Licensee member is on the Quabury Hill Site with a Host operator, by arrangement.
2.7 “Notice time” means the time at which a Host cancellation notice is sent to the Licensee contact address, as shown in the outbound mail record for that notice.
2.8 “Booking recorded” means the calendar date on which a booking is entered in the booking log.

PART C – ACCESS AND ALLOCATION
3.1 Standard allocation. The Licensee may book up to the hours of Counted Time stated for each Quarter in Part F.
3.2 Unattended Remote is available only on the Allocated Instrument, and only for a session whose booking was recorded at least seven calendar days before the session’s start date. For this purpose a booking recorded on 1 June covers a session starting on 8 June or later.
3.3 Every other session on the Allocated Instrument is Supervised Remote.
3.4 Short-notice countersignature. A booking recorded less than seven calendar days before the session’s start date may run as Unattended Remote only if the Duty Operator has countersigned it in the booking log before the session starts. Without countersignature the session runs as Supervised Remote under clause 3.3.
3.5 Attended visits are arranged by written request to the Host contact. Attended visits are not Counted Time.
3.6 Sessions on the Dyrbury 0.4 m refractor are supervised visits by arrangement and carry no allocation.

PART D – CANCELLATIONS AND EXCEPTIONS
4.1 A session cancelled by the Host because of weather or a technical fault is not Counted Time.
4.2 Exception. Clause 4.1 does not apply where the Notice time is less than 24 hours before the scheduled start of the session. In that case the session remains Counted Time at its booked duration.
4.3 Moved sessions. A session moved to another slot by written agreement between the Host contact and the Licensee contact is Counted Time once only, at the date and booked duration of the new slot. The original slot is not Counted Time.
4.4 Corrections. Where a later written correction from the Host contact changes a recorded Notice time, the corrected Notice time governs.
4.5 A session cancelled at the Licensee’s own request is not Counted Time.

PART E – LICENCE CONDITIONS
5.1 Public liability cover is kept in force for the Term. The current certificate expires 2027-02-28, and a renewed copy is due at the Host office by 2027-02-01.
5.2 Each Licensee member who operates the Allocated Instrument on site completes the Host safety induction. An induction is valid for one year from the date it is signed.
5.3 Members use red light only inside the dome, close the shutter at the end of each session and do not touch the mirror cell. The Duty Operator switches off the dew heaters at the end of the night.
5.4 A guest may look through the instrument during an Attended visit only. A guest may not be given remote control access.
5.5 Images taken during a session are held by the Licensee. The Host may use them for outreach with written credit to the Licensee.

PART F – AMENDMENTS
F1 Amendment 1 was signed by both parties on 2026-03-30 and is effective from 2026-04-01. Clause 3.1 is replaced by: “The Licensee may book up to 44 hours of Counted Time for each Quarter beginning on or after 1 April 2026, and up to 40 hours of Counted Time for each earlier Quarter.”
F2 Amendment 2 was signed on 2026-06-02 and is effective from 2026-07-01. Clause 3.1 is replaced by: “The Licensee may book up to 36 hours of Counted Time for each Quarter beginning on or after 1 July 2026.” It does not change any Quarter that begins before 1 July 2026.
F3 Signed copies of both amendments are held at the Host office in Dyrbury under file reference TAA/26/0417.

1.3 reachDefinition: Doxhaven Reach means the controlled water between Doxhaven Pontoon and the Skixmouth gate, with both ends included.
1.4 transitDefinition (2025 text): A transit is a continuous movement of a vessel within the controlled reach, from entry to exit. Movements separated by a stop are one transit unless the vessel is secured alongside for longer than 20 minutes during that stop.
1.4 transitDefinition (Amendment No. 2 text): A transit is a continuous movement of a vessel within the controlled reach, from entry to exit. Movements separated by a stop are one transit unless the vessel is secured alongside for longer than 30 minutes during that stop. A stop of 30 minutes or less does not end a transit.
1.5 lengthOverall: Length overall (LOA) means hull length measured from the foremost point of the stem to the aftermost point of the transom. Bowsprits, davits, pulpits and other fittings are excluded.

SECTION 2 - SCOPE AND RECORDS
2.1 scope: These bylaws apply to all vessels entering the controlled water of the Tharnaickix River Board between Frondport and Skixmouth. Pleasure craft under 10 metres are excluded from sections 3 and 5 unless the Board directs otherwise.
2.2 logPractice: The gate office keeps a movement log for each vessel. Times are recorded to the nearest minute by the gate office clock. Where a log entry and a radio report differ, the log entry governs.
2.3 exemptionHolders: An exemption holder must carry its certificate on board and produce it on request.

SECTION 3 - PRE-NOTICE AT THE SKIXMOUTH GATE
3.2 preNoticeRule (2025 text): A vessel with an LOA of 24 metres or more must give the gate office at least two hours notice by radio before passing the Skixmouth gate, unless it holds a current exemption certificate under 3.5.
3.2 preNoticeRule (Amendment No. 2 text): A vessel with an LOA of 24 metres or more must give the gate office at least two hours notice by radio or e-mail before passing the Skixmouth gate, unless it holds a current exemption certificate under 3.5.
3.5 exemptionCertificates: A certificate exempts its holder from 3.2 up to and including its printed expiry date. It is not current after that date. A certificate whose renewal has been refused is not treated as extended.

SECTION 4 - GATE HOURS AND QUEUES
4.1 gateHours: The Skixmouth gate opens at 06:00 and closes at 21:00 local time every day, unless a notice says otherwise.
4.2 lockQueue: Vessels queue on the lower side of the gate in order of arrival at the gate office. A vessel may ask for priority only with a written reason.

SECTION 5 - SLOW-SPEED LIMITS, DOXHAVEN REACH
5.1 slowSpeedLimit (2025 text): 6 knots for all vessels in Doxhaven Reach.
5.1 slowSpeedLimit (Amendment No. 2 text): 5 knots for vessels with an LOA of 20 metres or more. 6 knots for vessels with an LOA under 20 metres.
5.4 floodAlertReduction (unchanged by Amendment No. 2): While a flood alert notice is in force for Doxhaven Reach, the limit set by 5.1 is reduced by one knot for every vessel. rules.text: Adult circulating items are lent for 21 calendar days from the loan date. The due date is the loan date plus 21 days.
A loan may be renewed at most 2 times. An item that is overdue on the request date may not be renewed.
Each renewal moves the due date forward by 14 calendar days from the due date in force immediately before that renewal.

From 2026-02-01 onward, a renewal is refused while one or more holds are waiting on the item. Before 2026-02-01 a waiting hold did not refuse a renewal. A hold with status filled or cancelled is not a waiting hold.

Overdue days for a returned item are the return date minus the due date, in whole calendar days, or zero if the item was returned on or before its due date. Only returns dated within the current calendar year count toward a patron's total.

A patron whose total overdue days for the current calendar year is 15 or more is barred from new loans and from renewals, whatever the status of the item. The bar is checked on the date the request is made.
All periods are counted in calendar days. Closure days and weekends are not excluded from any period.

1. Quarterly Sailing Record (Quarter 1 2026)
Route Code: DG-4 (Drickfell to Gestow crossing)
Scheduled Sailings: 260
Cancelled Sailings (all causes): 19
Counting rule: a cancelled sailing counts once, whatever the cause. Of the 19, 11 were weather-related and 8 were mechanical.
Average Delay on Non-Cancelled Sailings: 14 minutes (not used in this decision)
Terminal Berth Fee at Gestow, per month: £1,150 (fixed, not affected by sailings)
2. Passenger Loads, 16:10 Sailing (Surveyed Mondays)

February 2026: £47,120
Vessel 2 (hull ref PV-14) entered drydock on 4 April 2026.
4. Weather Decision for the 16:10 Sailing
Forecast disruption probability, sailing as scheduled: 30 per cent
Cost if a disruption occurs, any option: £18,400
Option A, run as scheduled: fixed cost £0
Option B, cancel sailing: fixed cost £6,250 (lost fares and refunds); no disruption risk once cancelled
Option C, delay departure by 90 minutes: fixed cost £2,900 (crew overtime and late-arrival refunds); residual disruption probability 20 per cent
Decision rule: the committee selects the option with the lowest expected cost. Expected cost equals fixed cost plus disruption probability (as a fraction of 1) multiplied by the cost of a disruption.
Forecast figures supplied by Rearto Valsaiswell, Met Liaison.
5. Next Steps
The committee is asked to confirm the decision by 16 May 2026. Fryan Tentondson will update the timetable notice at Pirport once the decision is recorded.
6. Background Notes
The committee last reviewed this crossing in February 2026 after a run of gusty weather. The Gestow linkspan was resurfaced in late March and the berth was closed for two working days, with sailings moved to the Pirport berth. Passenger feedback on the Pirport transfer has been mixed, and a survey is planned for June. Tickets for the 16:10 sailing sell out most summer weeks, so refunds are a real cost to the operator.

criteria.false: The recorded span is shorter than the minimum cure period.

criteria.launch_as_planned: Launch at the planned slot with no further drying or readings.
criteria.launch_with_owner_note: Launch at the planned slot and record the owner's acceptance as covering the moisture result.

criteria.strip_and_replace_panel: Strip out and replace the affected hull panel before any further step.
criteria.redry_reprobe_then_decide: Re-dry the affected panel, re-read all three probe points, and launch only if every reading is at or below the ceiling.

A. MEMO M-07
From: Skanus Wevaser, Chief Engineer
To: All running staff and locomotive custodians
Date: 4 May 2026
Subject: Boiler certification and passenger clearance, 2026 season

1. A boiler ticket is a certificate issued after periodic examination. A locomotive holds a current ticket only on a running date that falls within the ticket's validity period. Both the first and the last day of a validity period count as days of validity.
2. Ticket renewals this season. Locomotive 4711 received a renewed boiler ticket dated 1 May 2026, valid to 30 April 2027. Locomotive 4815 received a renewed boiler ticket dated 27 March 2026, valid to 26 March 2027. Locomotive 2290 ticket lapsed on 31 March 2026 and is awaiting examination.
3. Passenger clearance.
3.1 A locomotive without a current ticket is not to be steamed for any purpose.
3.2 A locomotive holding a current ticket is cleared for full passenger service on the Brairness Halt to Wumstow Junction section, subject to any later amendment to this item issued by the Chief Engineer.
3.3 Post-work steam test runs may be made without passengers, under the sign-off rules recorded in the locomotive log.
4. Crew for passenger days is set by the rota notice for each running day and is not restated in this memo.
5. The mid-season review of this memo is scheduled for the September meeting.
6. Fire lighting. A fire may be lit in a locomotive only by a person named as fireman or driver on the running day list for that locomotive. Lighting up for a steam test run follows the same rule.
7. Coal and water stock for each locomotive is recorded in the locomotive log at the start of each running week. The log entry is a stock record and does not affect clearance under items 3.1 to 3.3.
8. Questions about this memo should be sent to the Chief Engineer in writing. Verbal instructions given at the running shed do not change this memo.

B. AMENDMENT NOTICE
From: Wouna Quamore, Operations Manager (w.quamore@dundfraimis-rht.org.uk)
To: Running staff list
Date issued: 19 May 2026
Approved by: Skanus Wevaser, Chief Engineer, 18 May 2026
Effective: 1 June 2026
Subject: Amendment to item 3.2 of memo M-07, re-tubed boilers

Item 3.2 of M-07 is amended from 1 June 2026 as follows. Running before 1 June 2026 remains under item 3.2 as first written.
(a) A locomotive whose boiler tubes were replaced on or after 1 January 2026 is cleared for limited passenger service only, and not for full passenger service, until a post-work steam test for that locomotive has been signed off in its log.
(b) Limited passenger service means passenger running on the Brairness Halt to Wumstow Junction section only, with no more than six coaches attached.
(c) Sign-off means a sign-off entry made by the Chief Engineer in the locomotive log. A completed steam test run, on its own, is not sign-off.
(d) A locomotive whose boiler tube replacement was completed before 1 January 2026 is not affected by item (a) and remains under item 3.2 as written.
(e) Items 3.1 and 3.3 are not changed by this amendment.
This notice replaces the wording of item 3.2 for any locomotive within item (a). It does not restore full passenger clearance to a locomotive within item (a) while its sign-off is outstanding. Copies of this notice are to be kept in each locomotive cab file.

domain: crop insurance hail claim settlement for winter wheat units

state.Insured Address: Cearstead Holding, Haindwold Road Farm, Haindwold
state.Parcel A Location: Haindwold North, adjoining the field drain on the western boundary
state.Parcel B Location: Haindwold East, bounded by the hedge line and the Washolm road
state.Parcel C Status: Not part of unit HW-U07. Parcel C is an uninsured grazing paddock and carries no guarantee under this policy.
state.Policy Wording Extract: Clause 2.1: The guarantee per hectare is the coverage level elected multiplied by the approved production history yield for the crop and unit. Clause 3.2: Production is appraised by weighing harvestable grain from sample strips placed by the insurer's adjuster, each strip being at least 5 square metres and placed at random across the parcel, with weights converted to kilograms per hectare at 13 percent moisture. Clause 3.4: Where the insurer revises an appraisal in writing, the revised figure replaces the earlier figure for the same parcel from the date of the revision. Clause 4.1: Notice of loss must be given within 7 days of the damage being observed. Clause 4.3: Indemnity calculation has been amended; the current wording is in the amendment fields on this file. Clause 5.1: Where an indemnity is payable it is the shortfall in kilograms multiplied by the Price Election in force on the policy.
state.Amendment 1 Text: Dated 2026-03-24 and effective 2026-04-01. Following the boundary survey carried out by Taixo Teckfield, the insured area of Parcel B is reduced from 12.6 ha to 11.2 ha. The Parcel A and Parcel C areas, the approved yield, the coverage level and the Price Election are unchanged by this amendment.
state.Amendment 2 Text: Dated 2026-06-08 and effective 2026-06-10. Clause 4.3 (Indemnity Calculation) is replaced in full with the following wording: Indemnity is calculated on the whole insured unit. The total unit shortfall, being the total unit guarantee less the total governing appraised production, in kilograms, is multiplied by the Price Election. Indemnity is payable only where the total unit shortfall is at least 15.0 percent of the total unit guarantee; a total unit shortfall below 15.0 percent gives no indemnity. This amendment applies to every claim that was notified on or before its effective date and had not been settled on that date.
state.Original Clause 4.3 Summary: Superseded in full by Amendment 2. Under the original wording indemnity was calculated parcel by parcel, with each parcel tested separately against a 15.0 percent trigger, and any parcel below its own trigger paid nothing.
state.Loss Event Summary: Hail damage to the standing crop on Parcel A and Parcel B. The insured records the date of damage as the afternoon of 2026-06-03. The insured describes hailstones up to 30 mm across, which flattened the crop in patches. Parcel C was not affected because it carries no crop under this policy.
state.Claim Notified: Reported by telephone to the Washolm regional desk on 2026-06-05 and confirmed in writing the same day, with photographs of the damaged crop attached to the message.
state.Field Appraisals: Parcel B initial appraisal dated 2026-06-12 by Taixo Teckfield from 10 sample strips: 1,900 kg per ha. Parcel A appraisal dated 2026-06-16 by Taixo Teckfield from 12 sample strips: 2,600 kg per ha. Parcel C not appraised because it is not insured under this unit.
state.Latest Adjuster Message: Dated 2026-06-19, from Gruckel Jilmore, Washolm regional desk. The 12 June Parcel B figure of 1,900 kg per ha is withdrawn. A recount of the Parcel B sample strips gives 2,150 kg per ha. Under Clause 3.4 this revised figure replaces the 12 June figure and is the governing Parcel B appraisal. The Parcel A figure of 2,600 kg per ha stands unchanged. Please update the file before the settlement decision is issued.
state.Correspondence Log: 2026-06-05 Quyin Cearstead to Washolm desk: hail damage notified by telephone, photographs sent by message to washolm.desk@winplearica.example. 2026-06-08 Wonen Skearidge, underwriting: Amendment 2 issued and posted to the insured, receipt to be confirmed. 2026-06-09 Quyin Cearstead: receipt of Amendment 2 confirmed by return message. 2026-06-15 Taixo Teckfield: site visit carried out, sample strips placed on Parcel A and Parcel B; Parcel A strips show uniform loss across the parcel. 2026-06-19 Gruckel Jilmore: revised Parcel B appraisal entered on file, see Latest Adjuster Message. 2026-06-20 Wonen Skearidge: file reviewed against Amendment 2 and the policy wording; no further survey is required on the appraisals.
state.Field Survey Narrative: Survey carried out 2026-06-15 on a dry morning. Crop stage at survey was grain fill, with head emergence complete across both parcels. On Parcel B the strips were placed on the eastern half, where the hail track was heaviest. Weed pressure on Parcel A is light and does not bear on the loss. The adjuster observed that stripped heads and broken stems were common on the eastern side of Parcel B. Strip samples were bagged, labelled by parcel and strip number, and dried to the moisture basis set out in Clause 3.2 before threshing. A recount of the Parcel B threshed grain was carried out on 2026-06-18, and the result is the figure reported in the Latest Adjuster Message. The insured's expected harvest date is 2026-08-20.
state.Weather Log: Clelminster Met Station, about 14 km from the unit, daily readings. 2026-06-01: rainfall 6 mm, maximum 19 C. 2026-06-03: hail reported in the station's district at 15:40 local time, rainfall 11 mm, no hail size recorded by the station. 2026-06-04: dry, maximum 21 C. 2026-06-07: rainfall 31 mm over 24 hours, consistent with saturated soils and some lodging. The station does not record hail size, so hail size on this file is taken from the insured's description only. Wind on 2026-06-03 was recorded as gusty from the west.
state.Insured Statement: Quyin Cearstead wrote on 2026-06-09 that he expects the Parcel B yield to be better than either appraisal because the later tillers were not counted in the strips. The insured's expectations are not appraisal evidence and have not been used in the file. The insured has asked that the claim be settled promptly because of a loan repayment date.
state.Hail Track Description: The insured's description and the adjuster's sketch show a hail track running south-west to north-east across the eastern part of Haindwold East and the northern edge of Haindwold North. Parcel A is damaged on its eastern side only, while Parcel B is damaged across most of its area. The adjuster's sketch is held in the appraisal file and is not a measurement of area. Parcel areas on this file come from the surveyed schedules, not from the sketch.
state.Settlement Status: Open. No indemnity has been paid or authorised. The settlement decision is to be issued once the governing appraisals are entered on the file and the settlement wording in force on the claim has been applied.
state.Underwriter Comments: Wonen Skearidge, 2026-06-20: The claim is handled under the amendments on this file as they apply to the notification date. Parcel areas follow the most recent surveyed schedule. The Price Election has not been changed for this claim. Mileage and survey charges are reported separately and do not form part of the crop indemnity.
state.Barley Unit Note: Unit HW-U09 (spring barley, separate policy WPL-CR-2026-0449 held by the same insured) was inspected on 2026-06-11. No claim has been made on that unit. Its approved yield is 3,600 kg per ha and its coverage level is 75 percent. It is not linked to this claim and no figure from it has been used here.
state.Previous Claim: WPL-CR-2025-0311 on Unit HW-U07, frost damage, closed 2025-09-12 with no indemnity paid. Closed claims do not affect the current guarantee.
state.Adjuster Mileage Fee: GBP 84.50 for the site visit on 2026-06-15, charged by the adjuster to Winplearica and not part of the crop indemnity.
state.Grain Sample Note: Grain sample taken to Mylneaix Grain Store on 2026-06-22 for moisture and test weight. Results are for the harvest record only and are not used in the appraisal under Clause 3.2.
state.Desk Contact: Washolm regional desk, washolm.desk@winplearica.example, telephone line open 08:30 to 17:00 on working days.
state.Notes: The insured has asked for the file to be closed as soon as possible. Trounddale County Drainage Board confirmed in writing that the drain on the Parcel A boundary was cleared in May and is not relevant to the loss. The hail was not accompanied by flooding on either parcel.
