Status: Live. This file replaces the January working notes (circular WN-26-02), which should no longer be used.

1. PURPOSE AND PRECEDENCE
1.1 This file sets out the monthly demersal allowance schedule for vessels on the Woullbury district register, the definitions that must be used to apply it, and the record of landings and gear activity that feeds the monthly compliance check.
1.2 Where this file and an earlier circular differ, this file governs from the effective date of the change it records (section 3). Correspondence recorded in section 10 overrides an earlier entry only where it names that entry and states the new treatment.
1.3 Allowances are stated in tonnes (t). Sales note weights are stated in kilograms (kg).

2. DEFINITIONS
These definitions narrow the everyday meaning of the terms below. Use these meanings and no others.
2.1 Landed means the net weight, in kilograms, shown on a sales note that has been countersigned at the Nounbury landing point. A sales note awaiting countersignature is not landed until it is countersigned. Catch transferred to a carrier vessel at sea is not landed; it is reported on a transfer declaration and does not count against any allowance.
2.2 Length means overall length as stated on the most recent measurement certificate issued for the vessel. A length shown on the vessel register is superseded by any later certificate.
2.3 Class is set by Length: Class 1 is under 12.0 m; Class 2 is 12.0 m or more but under 18.0 m; Class 3 is 18.0 m or more.
2.4 Active fishing day means a calendar day (00:00 to 23:59 local time) on which at least one gear set starts. A set that starts on one day and is hauled on the next counts for the day on which it started. A day on which the vessel only transits, with no set starting that day, is not an active fishing day. A set entry voided by the skipper, as recorded in section 11, is treated as never made.
2.5 Allowance month means a calendar month. Unused allowance does not carry forward and lapses at the end of the allowance month.
2.6 Effective date means the first day on which a revised figure applies, and that day is charged at the revised figure.

3. ALLOWANCE SCHEDULE AND EFFECTIVE DATES
3.1 Schedule Rev A, issued 2026-01-12, effective from 2026-01-01. Monthly figures: Class 1, 4.5 t; Class 2, 9.0 t; Class 3, 14.0 t.
3.2 Schedule Rev B, issued 2026-03-02, effective from 2026-03-16. Rev B replaces the Class 2 monthly figure only, which becomes 7.5 t. The Class 1 figure (4.5 t) and the Class 3 figure (14.0 t) are unchanged by Rev B.
3.3 Where a revised figure takes effect on a day other than the first day of a calendar month, the allowance for that month is apportioned by calendar days. Days before the effective date are charged at the earlier figure. The effective date and every later day of that month are charged at the revised figure. Allowance for that month = (earlier figure * days at earlier figure / days in month) + (revised figure * days at revised figure / days in month). Count calendar days, not working days, and use the full number of days in the month.
3.4 A month that begins on or after the effective date of a revised figure is charged at the revised figure throughout, with no apportionment.
3.5 Rev B does not alter any rule in section 2.
3.6 Circular WN-26-02 (January) gave a Class 2 figure of 9.0 t for every month of 2026. It is withdrawn from the file date. Where it differs from section 3.1 or section 3.2, section 3 governs.

subject: Card draw checks at the Trimport, Beanwych and Quolfell depots

1. PURPOSE
This memo applies the fuel card standard to three card cases. Two were raised by depot supervisors at Trimport and Beanwych during March 2026. The third was raised by internal audit as a query on a February draw. All quantities are litres taken from the card provider export, to one decimal place, unless a line says otherwise. Vehicle registrations are held on the fleet register (revision 14, issued 2026-02-20) and are not repeated here.

2. STANDARDS IN FORCE
2.1 Fuel Card Use Standard FCS-4 applies to every card transaction dated on or after 2026-03-01. A transaction dated before 2026-03-01 is judged under the earlier Fuel Card Use Standard FCS-3.
2.2 Under FCS-4 the general weekly cap is 120 litres per card in any seven-day window. A seven-day window is any run of seven consecutive calendar days, counting both its first and last day. A total equal to 120 litres is within the cap. Only a total above 120 litres is a breach of the general cap.
2.3 Long-haul exception. A card fitted to a vehicle registered in the long-haul category may draw up to 180 litres in a seven-day window, provided that every draw in that window carries a trip reference and an odometer reading. Where the exception applies it replaces the general cap for that window. The odometer requirement is not relaxed by the exception. A total equal to 180 litres is within the exception limit.
2.4 Under FCS-3 the cap was 160 litres per card in any seven-day window. FCS-3 had no long-haul exception.
2.5 A window is assessed only once it has closed, which happens at the end of its last day.

memo.note: Contingency sheet to be finalised once the Drillholm field booking is confirmed. Figures below are the working set and may change.

stops.note: Indoor sports hall booked; no weather contingency needed.
Matinee tent sits on open field; seating not covered.

contingency.rule: Lowest expected cost wins. Expected cost = fix_gbp + rain_chance x lost_share x gate_gbp, using the stop's rain chance and gate. fix_gbp is paid whatever the weather. lost_share is the share of gate income lost if it rains under that option; 0 means no weather loss under that option.

cover.rule: Lowest expected total cost wins over next season. Expected total = premium_gbp + (1 - covered_share) x expected weather loss. Expected weather loss = expected weather cancels x loss_per_cancel_gbp. Expected weather cancels = (season weather cancels / season outdoor perfs) x next_outdoor_perfs, not rounded.

1.1 Isolation distance means the shortest straight-line distance measured on the ground between the outer edge of the sown seed crop and the nearest edge of any crop of a different variety, or of the same variety in a different class. Headlands, field roads and drainage strips are not counted as crop. A distance read from a field map, plan or aerial image is not an isolation distance and must not be used to decide compliance.
1.2 Declared class means the class named on the sowing declaration for the lot at the time of sowing.
1.3 Inspection date means the calendar date on which the field walk is carried out. It is not the date on which the report is typed up or signed.

SECTION 2 - MINIMUM STANDARDS (Standards Manual, edition 7, table 3)
Foundation: isolation 5.0 m; germination 85%; pure seed 99.0%
Certified: isolation 3.0 m; germination 85%; pure seed 98.0%
A figure meets a minimum when it is equal to or above that minimum.

SECTION 3 - AMENDMENT 2 (issued 2026-02-20)
Amendment 2 replaces the Certified isolation minimum in table 3 with 4.5 m. It takes effect for field walks whose inspection date falls on or after 2026-03-01. A field walk with an earlier inspection date is judged against the minimum printed in table 3. Amendment 2 does not change any germination or pure seed minimum. Amendment 2 does not change the Foundation isolation minimum.

SECTION 4 - PROCEDURES (Standards Manual, edition 7, clause 6)
6.1 A field that fails the isolation minimum for its declared class is rejected for that class.
6.2 Downgrading between certification classes is not permitted. A rejected field is not re-entered in a lower class.
6.3 Isolation measurements are final once the inspector signs the field walk record. No re-measurement is accepted after signature.
6.4 A lot is certified in its declared class only when the field walk meets the isolation minimum for that class and the current laboratory report meets the germination and pure seed minimums for that class. A corrected laboratory report replaces the report it corrects in full.
6.5 Roguing removes off-type plants inside the crop. It does not change the isolation distance, which is measured from the outer edge of the sown crop.

subject: Bylaw text as amended, with lock log and booking book extracts for 6 to 9 April 2026

1. PURPOSE
Operations asked for the bylaw text now applied at Wusminster Lock, with Amendment No. 2 worked in, and for the log and booking book extracts for 6 to 9 April 2026 to be read against it. Clauses 2 to 7 are the consolidated text. Where Amendment No. 2 replaces a clause, the replacement governs from its effective date. This memo does not change the bylaws.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 'Overall length' means length as recorded on the registration certificate, in metres to one decimal place. Lengths shown in the lock log are copied from those certificates and do not override them.
2.2 'Booked passage' means a passage for which a slot has been confirmed in the booking book.
2.3 'Schedule 3 cargo' means any cargo listed in Schedule 3 to these bylaws.
2.4 'Notice period' means the time from the moment a booking request is received to the requested passage time. It is the only measure used to test whether notice was adequate.

3. GENERAL OPERATION
3.1 No vessel shall enter the lock chamber without the lock keeper's signal.
3.2 Lock keepers record every arrival in the lock log, whether or not the vessel passes.

4. BOOKING AND PASSAGE WINDOWS
4.1 A vessel with an overall length greater than 15.0 m must hold a booked passage.
4.2 A booking must be requested with a notice period of at least 48 hours.
4.3 A vessel of 15.0 m or less, carrying no Schedule 3 cargo, may pass without a booking during the non-peak window, on a first-come basis.
4.4 The non-peak window runs from 06:00 to 18:00.
4.5 Any vessel not covered by clause 4.3 must hold a booked passage, including a vessel of 15.0 m or less that arrives outside the non-peak window.

5. EMERGENCY EXEMPTION
5.1 The harbourmaster may declare an emergency at the lock by notice posted at Neamcombe Quay Depot and sent to the lock keeper. A declaration stays in force until a withdrawal notice is filed in writing.
5.2 While a declared emergency is in force, a vessel responding to it may pass without a booking.
5.3 The exemption in clause 5.2 does not extend to Schedule 3 cargo. A vessel carrying Schedule 3 cargo must hold a booked passage whether or not an emergency has been declared.

6. FEES AND OTHER MATTERS
6.1 The passage fee is £14.50 per booked passage, payable in advance at the booking office.
6.2 Works on the Wourminster Reach training bank are not a lock closure and do not change clauses 4 or 5.
6.3 Gate two is inspected each quarter. Inspection days are posted at Neamcombe Quay Depot.

7. LOCK KEEPER DUTIES
7.1 The lock keeper checks the registration length against the certificate before signing any passage entry. Where the certificate is not on board, the length given by the master is recorded and flagged for follow-up.
7.2 Schedule 3 cargo must be declared on the passage form before the vessel is admitted, and the declaration is kept with the log entry.
7.3 Booking requests received by e-mail are logged at the time of receipt shown on the e-mail, not at the time they are keyed into the booking book.

SCHEDULE 3 (DANGEROUS GOODS)
Class 3 flammable liquids; class 8 corrosives. Cargo in these classes is Schedule 3 cargo whatever its quantity.

AMENDMENT No. 2
Signed by Pexon Poner on 26 March 2026.
A. Clause 4.2 is replaced by: 'A booking must be requested with a notice period of at least 24 hours.'
B. Clause 4.4 is replaced by: 'The non-peak window runs from 07:00 to 17:00.'
C. Clause 6.1 is replaced by: 'The passage fee is £15.20 per booked passage, payable in advance at the booking office.'
D. Amendment No. 2 takes effect on 1 April 2026 and applies to every booking request received, and every passage made, on or after that date.
E. Clauses 2, 3, 4.1, 4.3, 4.5, 5, 6.2 and 7 are unchanged.

EMERGENCY NOTICES
EM-01: declared 14 March 2026 for a bank collapse on the Wourminster Reach training bank; withdrawn in writing 20 March 2026 at 09:00.
EM-02: declared 7 April 2026 at 13:00 by the harbourmaster; notice posted at Neamcombe Quay Depot and sent to the lock keeper. Scope: vessels assisting with the Neamcombe reach bank works. No withdrawal notice had been filed as at 10 April 2026.

PART 4. DEMERSAL QUOTA RULES, VERSION 3
Effective 1 March 2026. Version 2 (in force 1 October 2025 to 28 February 2026) is kept on file for reference only.

Section 1. Definitions
1.1 Landing: a landing declaration in Part 2 for a vessel and stock, dated by the landing date.
1.2 Interim period: 1 January to 31 May of the same year, both days included.
1.3 Register: the Office quota register in which transfers are entered and dated.
1.4 Weather-hold notice: a notice issued by the Office that names one or more vessels and gives validity dates, both days included.

Section 2. Allocation
2.1 Adjusted annual allocation: for each vessel and stock, the base entitlement line for the year plus all transfers ENTERED in the register for the same year.
2.2 Transfers that are agreed but not entered do not count towards the adjusted annual allocation until they are entered.

Section 3. Interim comparison and declarations
3.1 For each stock, interim assessments are measured against the interim ceiling in Schedule 2. They are not measured against the adjusted annual allocation.
3.2 Declarations are lodged electronically within 24 hours of landing, or on paper within 72 hours. A late declaration carries a late flag in the register; late flags are reported at the quarterly review and do not change counted landings.

Section 4. Overlanding deduction
4.1 Counted landings: every landing of the stock dated inside the interim period is counted, except landings excluded under 4.3.
4.2 Where the counted landings for a stock exceed the interim ceiling, the excess is reduced and deducted as follows:
(a) Tolerance: an excess of 50 kg or less is not chargeable. Only the part of the excess above 50 kg is chargeable.
(b) Multiplier: the chargeable excess is multiplied by the overlanding multiplier of 1.25. The product is deducted from the vessel's next-period allocation for that stock.
4.3 Weather-hold exclusion: any landing made on a day within the validity dates of a weather-hold notice that names the vessel is excluded from counted landings for the calculation in 4.2. The exclusion does not apply to the adjusted annual allocation or to any other calculation.

Section 5. Versions and amendments
5.1 Each overlanding assessment is calculated under the version of these rules, including any amendment, in force on the date the assessment is issued.
5.2 An amendment changes only the clauses it names. Amendments are listed in Part 5.

Section 6. Procedure for an interim assessment
Step A: list the landings of the stock dated inside the interim period, using the Part 2 entries and no others.
Step B: remove any landing excluded under 4.3.
Step C: total the remaining landings and compare the total with the interim ceiling. If the total does not exceed the ceiling, there is no excess.
Step D: take the excess, deduct the tolerance in 4.2(a), and keep the remainder as the chargeable excess.
Step E: multiply the chargeable excess by the multiplier in force under 5.1 and record the product as the deduction carried forward.

Section 7. Records
7.1 Landing declarations are retained for six years from the end of the year they relate to.
7.2 Weather-hold notices are retained with the assessment file they support.
7.3 Correspondence is not a register entry. An agreement shown only in correspondence does not change an entitlement or transfer until it is entered.

1. DEFINITIONS (apply to every section, including amendments)
1.1 WD = working day: Monday to Friday, excluding the days listed in 1.4.
1.2 LT = lead time of a request: the number of WD that fall strictly after the lodgement date and strictly before the first night requested. The lodgement date and the first night are both left out of the count.
1.3 NIGHT: a night is named by the calendar date on which it starts. The night named 12 March starts on 12 March and ends in the early morning of 13 March.
1.4 HOL = holidays for the purposes of 1.1: 2026-01-01 New Year's Day and 2026-03-09 Founders' Day. No other day is a holiday for these terms.
1.5 CQ = calendar quarter: a period of three months beginning on 1 January, 1 April, 1 July or 1 October. The calendar quarter beginning 2026-01-01 runs to 2026-03-31 inclusive.
1.6 LOG = logged time. For a session that took place it is the shutter-open time on the shutter sheet. For a booking that was not used and not cancelled (a no-show) it is the booked length.
1.7 DAYS BEFORE = for a cancelled booking, the first night's calendar date minus the cancellation date, counted in calendar days. A cancellation with DAYS BEFORE of 2 or less is a late cancellation. A cancellation with DAYS BEFORE of 3 or more is an early cancellation.
1.8 EARLY CANCELLATION: a booking cancelled early is treated as if it had never been made. Its time is not counted in any total. A late cancellation is counted at its booked length.
1.9 BOOKING QUARTER: a booking belongs to the calendar quarter in which its first night falls. A request in the register is not a booking.
1.10 CAP = the maximum total LOG per holder per calendar quarter, stated in hours. Only bookings listed in section 5 or 5b count toward CAP. Compare LOG and CAP as decimal hours (90 minutes is 1.5 h).
1.11 DESK = the Scheduling Desk of Dreteis Observatory Ltd, which keeps the booking log and request register.
1.12 HOST = Kortgroson Trust, which owns unit R9 and the Cloxhaven Ridge site.

2. ORIGINAL TERMS (version 1, in force from 2025-09-01 until replaced under section 3)
2.1 LT minimum: 10 WD for every request.
2.2 CAP: 12 h per calendar quarter for each holder.
2.3 WAIVER: the host director may waive the LT minimum in writing for a single request.
2.4 Section 4 applies in full under version 1.

3. AMENDMENT 2 (signed 2026-02-10; replaces 2.1 to 2.3 only where the dates below apply)
3.1 CAP: for each calendar quarter beginning on or after 2026-01-01 the CAP is 15 h. For earlier quarters, 2.2 continues to apply.
3.2 LT: for any request lodged on or after 2026-03-01 the LT minimum is 7 WD. For a request lodged before 2026-03-01, 2.1 continues to apply. The lodgement date decides which minimum applies. The date on which this amendment was signed does not decide it.
3.3 WAIVER: 2.3 is withdrawn for every request lodged on or after 2026-03-01.
3.4 SHORT REQUESTS: where a request does not meet the LT minimum that applies to it, the Desk does not confirm the requested night. The Desk must offer the earliest night on which that minimum is met. The requester may accept that night or withdraw the request.
3.5 No other term of sections 2 or 4 is changed by this amendment.

4. STANDARD TERMS (all versions)
4.1 Access: holder staff only, with up to two named observers per session as listed on the booking.
4.2 Sessions run from 18:00 to 06:00 local time on the night named by the first night, unless the site engineer closes the dome for weather or fault.
4.3 Weather closure does not change the booking. LOG for a session that took place is the shutter-open time actually recorded.
4.4 Raw frames are delivered to the holder within 30 days of the session. The HOST keeps a copy for 5 years.
4.5 Staff must complete the site induction with the site engineer before first use.
4.6 No one enters the dome unaccompanied. Observers under 16 are accompanied by a staff member at all times.
4.7 Observers do not change filters, eyepieces or the guide camera without the site engineer's approval.
4.8 Any paper using data from unit R9 acknowledges the HOST and the unit number.
4.9 A dispute about a booking is raised with the DESK in writing. The host director decides it, and the decision is final under these terms.
4.10 The DESK keeps the booking log and request register for 6 years from the last entry.
4.11 PRIORITY: where two requests compete for the same night, the request with the earlier lodgement date has priority.
4.12 Observers record the start and end of each session on the shutter sheet at the dome door. The shutter sheet is the source for LOG.
4.13 Observers bring their own cold-weather clothing. The dome is not heated for observers.

measurement-rules
on-time-window: a departure is on time if it leaves no more than 1 minute before and no more than 3 minutes after its timetabled time. Both limits are inclusive, so a departure exactly 3 minutes late is on time.
cancelled-trips: a cancelled trip stays in the scheduled count and is never counted as on time.
on-time-share: on-time departures divided by scheduled departures (cancelled trips included), stated as a percentage to one decimal place.
cancelled-share: cancelled trips divided by scheduled departures, stated as a percentage to one decimal place.

spring-review-rule
share-at-or-above-85.0: keep the current timetable.
share-below-85.0-and-cancelled-share-at-or-below-2.0: retime departures within the current running time.
share-below-85.0-and-cancelled-share-above-2.0: add scheduled running time between timing points.

corridor-figure-basis: the corridor on-time share is the summed on-time count of both routes divided by the summed scheduled count of both routes. It is not an average of the two route percentages.

SECTION 1: DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
1.1 Visitor Vehicle. For Rule VP-4 a Visitor Vehicle is a vehicle that is not registered to the member's household and is not operated by a contractor booked through the Branch. Contractor vehicles booked through the Branch are outside Rule VP-4 and are not counted.
1.2 Visitor Bay. A Visitor Bay is a bay designated as a Visitor Bay in the bay schedule in Section 9.
1.3 Visitor Day. A Visitor Day is a calendar date on which a Visitor Vehicle is recorded in a Visitor Bay at any time during that date. A date counts once, however many arrivals and departures are recorded on it. A Visitor Day is counted in the calendar month in which its date falls.
1.4 Monthly Allowance. The Monthly Allowance is the number of Visitor Days a household may have counted in one calendar month. A total equal to the Monthly Allowance is permitted. Only a total above the Monthly Allowance is a breach.
1.5 Governing Version. The version of Rule VP-4 that sets the Monthly Allowance for a calendar month is the version in force on the first day of that month.
1.6 Waiver. A Waiver is a written decision by the Branch Office that named dates are not counted as Visitor Days for a household. A Visitor Day covered by a Waiver is not counted against the Monthly Allowance.
1.7 Corrections. Where a member or the Housing Officer has given a later written correction to a logged date, the corrected date replaces the logged date.
1.8 Date Ranges. In this file a date range written with the word to includes both the first date and the last date.

domain: demersal cod quota transfers and counted landings

definitions.landed_weight: Weight in kilograms from a designated port weighing. Only landed weight is counted against quota.
definitions.designated_port: Any landing entry that names a port is a designated port weighing. An entry marked at sea is not weighed at a port.
definitions.landing_date: The date of the designated port weighing, not the date the fish were caught.
definitions.stock_scope: An allocation or transfer for one stock code counts only toward that stock code. Notices and landings for another stock code are never added to it.
definitions.live_weight_conversion: A COD-7 weight recorded on a gutted basis is converted to live weight by multiplying the recorded weight by the gutting conversion factor of 1.25. Weights recorded on a live basis are counted unchanged. The factor applies to COD-7 only.
definitions.discards: Fish returned to sea are discards. Discards are never counted against quota, even when they appear in the log.
definitions.quota_year: The quota year runs from 1 January to 31 December. A landing dated after 31 December is charged to the following quota year.
definitions.transfer_notice: A later transfer notice that states it replaces an earlier one takes the earlier notice's place in full. A stated transfer total is the whole transfer for the year, not an addition.

criteria.exclusion_applies: The clause the reply cites would cover the fault, but a listed exclusion removes that cover on the logged facts.
criteria.conclusion_not_stated: The reply does not reach a conclusion on whether the failure is covered.

PART 1 - BYLAW EXTRACT (consolidated text as at 14/04/2026)

Clause 1 (Definitions). Overall length means the length shown on a vessel's current registration certificate. Passage means one continuous movement of a vessel within one zone, dated by its logged start time. Rolling 12-month period has the meaning given in clause 9.

Clause 2 (Lock hours). Welwold lock operates 07:00 to 19:00 from 1 April to 30 September. Outside those hours a vessel must give 24 hours notice to the lock keeper through the Trust booking line.

Clause 3 (Lights and signals). A vessel under way between sunset and sunrise must show navigation lights. A vessel of 7.0 m or less may show a single white lantern instead.

Clause 4 (Mooring). A vessel may moor at the Trixport visitor pontoons for up to 48 hours without a permit. A longer stay needs a permit issued by the Navigation office. Permits are charged at GBP 35 per month, payable in advance.

Clause 5 (Waste). No vessel may discharge bilge water inside Faxminster Basin. Discharge of sewage is prohibited on the whole reach.

Clause 6 (Zones). The reach is divided into three zones.
  Zone A: from the Welwold lock head to the upstream end of Trixport Weir.
  Zone B: from Trixport Weir to the inlet of Faxminster Basin.
  Zone C: from the inlet of Faxminster Basin to the sea lock.

Clause 7 (Speed limits), original text, in force from 01/01/2024 to 31/03/2026:
  Zone A: 5 knots, all vessels.
  Zone B: 6 knots, all vessels.
  Zone C: 8 knots, all vessels.

Clause 7 as replaced by Amendment No. 2, effective 01/04/2026:
  Zone A: 5 knots, all vessels.
  Zone B: 6 knots for a vessel of 12.0 m overall length or less; 4 knots for a vessel of more than 12.0 m overall length.
  Zone C: 8 knots, all vessels.
  Application: the amended clause 7 applies to any passage that begins on or after 01/04/2026. A passage that begins before that date remains under the original clause 7.

Clause 8 (Measurement and breaches). Overall length is stated in metres to one decimal place. A length of exactly 12.0 m falls in the 12.0 m or less band. A recorded speed equal to the applicable limit is not a breach. A breach is a recorded speed above the limit that applies to the vessel, the zone and the passage start date.

Clause 9 (Enforcement), original text, in force until 31/03/2026:
  First breach in a rolling 12-month period: written warning.
  Second breach in the period: fixed penalty of GBP 120.
  Third and any later breach in the period: referral to the Navigation Board.

Clause 9 as replaced by Amendment No. 2, effective 01/04/2026, for breaches recorded on or after 01/04/2026:
  (a) first breach in the period by a vessel of more than 12.0 m overall length: fixed penalty of GBP 75;
  (b) first breach in the period by a vessel of 12.0 m or less: written warning;
  (c) second breach in the period, any vessel: fixed penalty of GBP 120;
  (d) third and any later breach in the period, any vessel: referral to the Navigation Board.
  The rolling 12-month period runs back 12 months from the date of the breach being assessed and includes that date. Breaches recorded before 01/04/2026 count towards the period, but outcomes (a) to (d) apply only to breaches recorded on or after 01/04/2026.

Clause 10 (Wash). A vessel must not create a wash that causes damage to moored craft or banks. Compliance is judged by the patrol officer on the day.

Clause 11 (Reporting). A patrol officer must enter each logged passage in the patrol log within 24 hours of its start time. A correction to an entry must be dated and initialled by the Navigation Officer and does not change the start time shown. Readings are accepted as recorded at the sensor unit.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This procedure applies to cohorts A, B and C at Garness Training Campus, to the simulator bays at Drandthorpe Hangar, and to instructors rostered on those cohorts.
1.2 It sets the counted simulator hours needed before a student's first solo flight, the daily duty limit for instructors, and the medical condition for solo clearance.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 countedSession: a simulator session of at least 45 minutes, logged against the student record and signed by the instructor. A session of exactly 45 minutes counts. A session shorter than 45 minutes does not count.
2.2 dutyPeriod: the time from report to release for a rostered instructor. An unpaid break of 30 minutes or more is deducted from that time. A break shorter than 30 minutes is not deducted. Standby time is not duty and is not counted.
2.3 cohortStart: the date of the first scheduled lesson for the cohort, as confirmed in writing by the Head of Flight Training. A later written confirmation replaces an earlier one.

3. REQUIREMENTS (Revision 2)
3.1 Each student must complete 24 countedSession hours before first solo flight. (Clause 3.1 is replaced by Amendment A-3.)
3.2 Solo clearance: a student is cleared for solo only when the counted-hours requirement for their cohort is met AND a Class 2 medical certificate is valid on the planned solo date.
3.3 Instructor duty: a dutyPeriod must not exceed 9 hours in any one day. A dutyPeriod longer than 9 hours is a breach and must be reported to the Head of Flight Training.

4. ROSTER UPDATES
4.1 A report or release time changed by written message from the duty supervisor replaces the time in the published roster for that day.
4.2 Roster updates do not change the definitions in section 2.

5. AMENDMENT A-3 (effective 2026-05-01)
5.1 Clause 3.1 is replaced with the following text: 'For a cohort whose cohortStart falls on or after 2026-05-01, each student must complete 20 countedSession hours before first solo flight. For a cohort whose cohortStart falls before 2026-05-01, each student must complete 24 countedSession hours before first solo flight.'
5.2 Clauses 2, 3.2 and 3.3 are unchanged by this amendment.

1. SCHEME RULES (v2, adopted 2024-09-01)

1.1 Definitions
(a) Continuous occupancy: occupancy of one dwelling under membership agreements with no break longer than 14 days. A break is the number of days strictly between the last day of one agreement and the first day of the next agreement for that dwelling; neither of those two days is counted. A break of 14 days or fewer does not end continuity. A break of more than 14 days ends continuity, and the count restarts from the first day of the next agreement.
(b) Full months: counted from the start date to the same day of the month in each later calendar month. A full month is complete on the day that matches. Part months are disregarded.
(c) Decision date: the date recorded in the Allocations Panel minutes as the date the decision was signed off. The date of a meeting, or of a draft calculation, is not the decision date.
(d) Working day: any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a closure day in the annual calendar.
(e) Qualifying works: repair works to the structure, roof, drainage or external envelope of a dwelling block. Decorative or cosmetic finishes are not qualifying works.
(f) Qualifying cost: the schedule total less the items that are not qualifying works.
(g) Member share: the qualifying cost multiplied by the member share rate in clause 1.2 or 1.2A.
(h) Net contribution: the member share less any rebate.

1.2 Member share rate. The member pays 35 per cent of the qualifying cost of works approved under this scheme. The Co-op bears the remainder.

1.2A Glazing Programme. For window and external door works carried out under the Glazing Programme, the member share rate is 40 per cent of the qualifying cost. Clause 1.2 does not apply to those works.

1.3 Rebate tiers. A rebate is calculated on the member share by reference to continuous occupancy at the decision date.
 Tier one: 48 full months or more; rebate 40 per cent of member share.
 Tier two: 24 full months or more but fewer than 48 full months; rebate 25 per cent of member share.
 Tier three: fewer than 24 full months; no rebate.

1.4 Exclusions. Any item that is not qualifying works is removed from the surveyor's schedule before the qualifying cost is calculated.

1.5 Claim window. A claim must be lodged within 30 calendar days of the works notice date. Day one is the day after the notice date. If day 30 is not a working day, the window closes on the next working day.

1.6 Surveyor's classification. The surveyor's classification of each schedule line is final unless the Panel varies it in writing.

1.7 Rounding. Amounts are worked in pounds and pence. Each calculated amount is rounded to the nearest penny at the step where it is produced.

1.8 Appeals. A member may ask the Panel to review a rebate decision within 28 days of the minute being signed. The Panel's review is final.

1.9 Records. Occupancy is recorded on the membership ledger and works dates on the repairs log. Where the two disagree, the membership ledger governs occupancy and the repairs log governs works dates.

2. CIRCULARS

Clause 1.3 is replaced for decisions whose decision date is on or after 2026-02-01. The tier bands are unchanged. The tier two rebate becomes 30 per cent of member share (was 25 per cent). 1. PURPOSE
This memo sets out the COD-7 entitlement position for the inshore fleet at the date above. It covers transfer notice TN-0091, a weighbridge discrepancy on landing LD-4409, and the register and landing figures to be used for the weekly return. It supersedes the draft position summary circulated on 9 April 2026, which was prepared from the base register before TN-0091 was logged and before a keying error on the landing log was found. Use the figures in sections 6 to 8 only, and read sections 2 to 5 as the rules that apply to them. Nothing in this memo changes the Rules Annex except as stated in section 4.

2. DEFINITIONS
These definitions apply throughout this memo and the Rules Annex, and they narrow the ordinary meaning of the terms shown.
2.1 Working day: a Monday to Friday, excluding any day listed as a Trust closure day in section 9. Weekends and listed closure days are not working days and are not counted in any working-day period.
2.2 Received: for a transfer notice, the date the notice is logged in the Trust register. The time of day at which the notice arrives does not change its received date.
2.3 Class: set by registered length as shown on the vessel register. Class B is a registered length under 12.0 metres. Class A is a registered length of 12.0 metres or more.
2.4 Landing: a discharge of fish at a licensed landing point, recorded on a Landing Declaration (LD). A landing that is voided on the register is not counted in any total, whatever its weight.
2.5 Declared weight: the weight written on the LD by the skipper. Weighbridge weight: the weight printed on the weighbridge slip for the same landing.
2.6 Quota totals are kept in kilograms. Any weight given in pounds (lb) is converted at 1 lb = 0.4536 kg, and the converted figure is the one used in totals and comparisons.
2.7 Counting working days before a landing: count the working days after the day the notice is received, up to and including the day before the landing. Neither the notice day nor the landing day is counted.
2.8 Quota year: 1 January to 31 December. Landings dated in an earlier year are not counted against the current year's entitlement.
2.9 Audit referral: an open referral is one shown in the audit referral log as not yet cleared on the date concerned. A referral cleared before that date is not open on that date.
2.10 Reserve draw: a decision of the Trust to draw on the reserve pool under B.5. A reserve draw is never a transfer.

3. ENTITLEMENT AND TRANSFER CLAUSES (Rules Annex, base text)
B.1 Base COD-7 entitlement per quota year: Class B vessels 38.0 tonnes; Class A vessels 61.5 tonnes. Entitlements are recorded to one decimal place.
B.2 An entitlement may be transferred only between two vessels of the same class.
B.3 A transfer notice is accepted if it is received not fewer than ten working days before the first landing of the receiving vessel on or after the date the notice is received, and clauses B.2 and B.4 are also met. An accepted transfer adds its full tonnage to the receiving vessel's entitlement for the whole quota year, not from the next quarter.
B.4 A donor vessel with an open audit referral on the date of the notice may not transfer entitlement.
B.5 The reserve pool of 4.0 tonnes per quarter is drawn only on a decision of the Trust. A reserve draw is not a transfer and is not recorded as one.

4. AMENDMENT No. 2 (effective 1 March 2026)
A2.1 In clause B.3, the words 'ten working days' are replaced by 'five working days'.
A2.2 This amendment applies to transfer notices received on or after 1 March 2026. A notice received before that date remains under clause B.3 as it stood before this amendment.
A2.3 No other part of clauses B.1 to B.5 is changed by this amendment.

5. TOLERANCE RULE FOR WEIGHBRIDGE DISCREPANCIES (Rules Annex 3)
T.1 Compare the weighbridge weight with the declared weight on the same LD. Express the difference as a percentage of the declared weight.
T.2 Where the difference is 5% or less, the declared weight stands.
T.3 Where the difference is more than 5% and not more than 10%, the weighbridge weight replaces the declared weight in the quota record.
T.4 Where the difference is more than 10%, the landing goes to the audit desk and is not entered in the quota record until cleared.
T.5 Both weights are converted to kilograms under 2.6 before the comparison is made.

domain: inland river navigation bylaws for craft registration, mooring and lock passage

clause_2_4.title: Continuation of registration pending renewal
clause_2_4.text: Where a renewal application for a craft registration is lodged before the registration expires, the existing registration continues in force until the authority records a decision on the application.

clause_4_2.title: General speed limit
clause_4_2.text: Unless a reach is listed otherwise in the schedule, the speed limit for a craft is 6 km/h.

clause_4_2_c.title: Works exemption
clause_4_2_c.text: A craft whose works exemption is current and entered in the register, on a reach named in its entry, may proceed at up to 9 km/h on that reach.

clause_5_2.title: Passenger launch passage permit (original)
clause_5_2.text: A passenger launch of any length may pass a lock without a standard passage permit if it carries no more than 20 passengers on the trip.

clause_5_3.title: Extended-length craft
clause_5_3.text: A craft over 15 m in length requires an extended-length passage permit for any lock passage.

clause_5_5.title: Exception for emergency bookings
clause_5_5.text: Clause 5_2 as amended does not apply to a craft on a lock booking of type emergency_service.

clause_6_3.title: Mooring permit suspensions
clause_6_3.text: A mooring permit is not in force on any day covered by an active suspension notice. A withdrawn notice has no effect. A suspension does not extend the permit term. The first and last day of a term or notice are both counted.

standard.title: Drisdrelica Winter Cereal Seed Standard
standard.governing_rule: A field file is assessed under the version whose effective_from date is the latest date on or before the field's sowing_date.

versions.isolation_rule: Distance in whole metres from the field boundary to the nearest sown crop of the same species. A distance equal to the minimum is within the standard.
versions.offtype_rule: Total off-type plants across all walks, divided by total plants inspected, expressed as a percentage without rounding. A rate equal to the maximum is within the standard; a higher rate is not.
versions.clause_4_4: An allowance of 0.10 percentage points is added to offtype_max_pct only where rogueing is recorded as completed before the final walk.

versions.clause_5_2: Minimum isolation is reduced to 120 m where an approved barrier is recorded in the field file on or before the sowing_date.
versions.note: The clause 4.4 allowance is not carried into this version.

inspection_method.method: Plants are counted along fixed transects. Each walk records the number of plants inspected and the number of those that are off-type. Recount sheets are kept with the walk record.

Concession Register.Register Note: Compartments C1 to C7 are listed in the current harvest plan. Compartment C8 was removed from the concession boundary in 2024 and does not appear in any entry below.

Definitions.Season Year: The twelve months from 1 April to 31 March inclusive. A harvest entry belongs to the season year in which its Felling Date falls, and to no other.
Definitions.Felling Date: The date on the scale ticket on which the stems were felled. Entries are assigned to a season year by this date only, not by the date the entry was typed into the register.
Definitions.Counted Volume: The sum of harvest entries whose Status is Counted, expressed in cubic metres under bark (m3 UB). Voided and Pending entries are excluded, and so are entries whose Felling Date falls outside the season year or period being tested.
Definitions.Tonne Conversion: One green tonne equals 1.85 cubic metres under bark. Green tonne entries are converted at this rate before they are added to the counted volume.
Definitions.Within The Allowable Cut: Counted volume is within the allowable cut only when it is equal to or below the allowable cut in force on the test date. A total above the allowable cut is not within it.
Definitions.Allowable Cut In Force: The allowable cut stated in the latest amendment whose Effective From date is on or before the test date. An amendment with an effective date after the test date has no effect on that test date.
Definitions.Salvage Felling: Felling limited to stems that are already windthrown or standing dead. Living green stems are excluded from salvage felling, whatever their condition.
Definitions.Message Precedence: A later message from the Issuing Office that states the status of a compartment replaces any earlier message about the same compartment, from the date that the later message gives as taking effect. Dates given in a message are inclusive unless the message says otherwise.

- Rev 2, eff.date 2026-04-01: rewrote Sections 3 and 4; added the 9-hour extension; rest between footplate turns reduced from 12 hours to 10 hours.

1. PURPOSE
This pack sets limits on volunteer footplate time, duty day length and rest between footplate turns on the Myllminster Valley line. Each turn is judged under the revision in force on the date it is signed off. A turn signed off before the Rev 2 effective date stays under Rev 1, even if it is rostered or logged later.

2. DEFINITIONS (Section 2 is unchanged in Rev 2 and applies to both revisions)
2.1 "Footplate time" means time with a volunteer's hands on the controls of a locomotive under power, including shunting under power. It runs from taking charge of the controls to releasing them.
2.2 "Trainee time" means time on the controls under the direct supervision of a qualified driver. Trainee time is not footplate time. It must be logged separately and flagged T.
2.3 "Non-footplate duty" means any other rostered task, for example lineside patrol, signal box duty or fire cleaning. It is not footplate time, but it counts toward the duty-day limit.
2.4 "Duty day" means the period from sign-on to sign-off on one calendar date, covering all footplate and non-footplate duty.

3. REV 1 LIMITS (in force until 31 March 2026)
3.1 Maximum footplate time in one duty day: 9 hours. No extension is available.
3.2 Maximum duty day: 11 hours.
3.3 Minimum rest between sign-off of one footplate turn and start of the next: 12 hours.

4. REV 2 LIMITS (effective 1 April 2026)
4.1 Applies to any turn signed off on or after 1 April 2026.
4.2 Maximum footplate time in one duty day: 8 hours.
4.3 A duty day may run to 9 hours of footplate time only with written approval from the Operations Secretary, recorded on the duty sheet before the turn starts. A verbal agreement from a shift supervisor is not sufficient.
4.4 Minimum rest between sign-off of one footplate turn and start of the next: 10 hours, measured clock to clock. A rest of exactly 10 hours meets the minimum.

Triage Policy.Version Rule: A request is triaged under the version in force on the date it was logged.

Definitions.Heating Outage: Loss of space heating or of hot water across the whole dwelling. Loss confined to one room, one radiator, one tap or one appliance is not a heating outage and is triaged as routine.
Definitions.Working Day: Monday to Friday, excluding any day listed in the Closure Calendar.
Definitions.Working Days Elapsed: The number of working days after the logging day, up to and including the day of desk acknowledgement.
Definitions.Clock Hours: Hours counted continuously from the logging time, including nights, weekends and closure days.
Definitions.Desk Acknowledgement: A call or e-mail from repairs desk staff telling the member that the request is logged and booked. Attendance by an on-call operative is not a desk acknowledgement.

Version 4.2 Standards.Heating Outage Attendance: An operative attends the dwelling within 12 clock hours of logging.
Version 4.2 Standards.Heating Outage Temporary Heat: Temporary heat or hot water restored within 24 clock hours of logging.
Version 4.2 Standards.Heating Permanent Repair Target: 10 working days from logging, or 5 working days where the household is on the Priority Register for the request.

Priority Register.Entry Rule: Register status applies to requests logged on or after the entry's effective date.
Priority Register.Source Note: Occupational health letter dated 2026-03-02, received by the desk on 2026-03-03.

rules.rule: An athlete may enter an event only if their age on the event date falls within that event's band.

state.logger: Boiler fault flag is taken from the controller trip log. A fault night is any night with a flagged controller trip. Frost alarm nights are logged separately and are not counted as fault nights.
state.basis: Planning rate = n_bf / n_logged, applied to every season night. Expected season loss = rate x season_nights x loss_per_bf_gbp. Residual loss for an option = expected loss x (1 - cut), where cut is the share of loss the option removes.
state.rule_q1: Choose the option with the lowest option cost plus residual loss per season.
state.rule_q4: Discard any option whose residual loss per season is above risk_cap_gbp; among the rest, choose the lowest option cost plus residual loss per season.
state.sensor_note: Boiler fault flag was re-keyed after the January recalibration; the counts above are final.

q1.instructions: Use only the planning basis below, and do not apply any cap, threshold, or discard rule on residual loss. Fault rate = fault nights divided by logged nights. Apply this rate to every season night and value each fault night at the stated per-night loss to get expected season loss. For each option, residual loss = expected season loss × (1 − cut), where cut is the share of boiler-fault loss the option removes. Total = option cost (a one-off amount per season) + residual loss. Which option has the lowest total? Answer with the option name only.

criteria.do_nothing: Keep the current set-up with no added measure, so the full expected loss remains.
criteria.install_backup_heater: Fit a standby heater that takes over when the main boiler fails, removing a large share of boiler-fault loss at a fixed cost.
criteria.upgrade_alarm: Replace the existing alarm unit with a higher-sensitivity model, which removes only a small share of boiler-fault loss.
criteria.buy_crop_insurance: Take out a policy that pays for crop loss in full, for a stated premium, so no residual loss remains.
criteria.relocate_crop: Move the crop to a different house or site for the season, so no residual loss remains, at a higher cost than insurance.

policy.title: Running Day Crew Rest and Certification Procedure
policy.rest_exception: The Operations Manager may sign a one-off dispensation reducing the minimum rest to 10 hours for a single duty. Every dispensation must be entered in the amendments log.

definitions.in_certified_service: A locomotive is in certified service on a given day only when its boiler certificate is in date on that day, meaning the day falls on or before the certificate expiry date, and no open defect notice classed as restricts running is recorded against it on that day. The expiry date is the last day on which the certificate is valid.
definitions.consecutive_days: Consecutive days are calendar days run in unbroken sequence. A calendar day on which the person worked no duty breaks the sequence. The first day of a run counts as day one.
definitions.firing_duty: A firing duty is any duty on which a fireman is rostered.
definitions.rest_period: The rest period is the elapsed time from the finish of one worked duty to the start of the next rostered duty, counted in hours and minutes with no rounding.
definitions.worked_duty_list: The crew rota lists each duty with a status. Only a row with status worked counts as a duty worked; a person with no worked row for a calendar day did not work a duty on that day.
definitions.rest_shortfall: Where rest is short, the rostered person must not start the duty and the duty manager fills it from the reserve list. Rostered start times are not moved to create rest.

policy.reserve_rule: A firing duty may be cancelled only where no qualified reserve who meets the minimum rest is available.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Observing Night: the period from 18:00 on one calendar date until 08:00 on the following calendar date. An Observing Night is assigned to the calendar date on which it begins, and that date is its Start Date.
1.2 Session Start Date: the Start Date of the Observing Night in which a Session is booked to run. The clock time at which shutter-open activity begins within that night does not change the Session Start Date.
1.3 Logged Time: the total of all shutter-open minutes recorded by the spectrograph control system for a Session, added together. Minutes between recorded segments are not Logged Time. A Session that is booked but not yet run has no Logged Time.
1.4 Membership Letter: a signed letter of membership between the Trust and a licensee. It is in force on each calendar day from its Term Start Date up to and including its End Date. On any later day it is treated as ended.
1.5 Lapse Days: for a licensee whose Membership Letter has ended, the number of calendar days after the End Date up to and including a booking request date. The End Date itself is not counted, so a request made on the day after the End Date has Lapse Days of 1.
1.6 Allocation Quarter: January to March, April to June, July to September or October to December. A Session is debited against the Allocation Quarter that contains its Session Start Date.
1.7 Public Session: a Session approved in writing by the Trust for a public viewing evening. Public Sessions draw on no licensee allocation.
1.8 Working Day: Monday to Friday, excluding the closure dates listed in Schedule D.
1.9 Named Users: the individuals listed on a licensee's Named Users sheet as at the date of the relevant Session.

SECTION 2 - ACCESS CATEGORIES
2.1 Anchor Partner: a licensee holding a Membership Letter in force on the booking request date.
2.2 Reserve Partner: a licensee whose Membership Letter has ended and whose Lapse Days figure on the booking request date falls inside the reserve window in clause 7.1.
2.3 Open Applicant: any licensee not covered by clause 2.1 or 2.2. Open Applicants receive no quarterly allowance and book Sessions at the rate in Schedule E.
2.4 Suspension: a licensee in breach of Section 8 may be barred from new bookings under clause 8.4 until the Trust confirms in writing that the bar is lifted.
2.6 Reserve window (original text): a Lapse Days figure of 45 or fewer. This clause is replaced by clause 7.1.

SECTION 3 - QUARTERLY ALLOWANCES
3.1 Anchor allowance: 30 Logged Hours per Allocation Quarter. One Logged Hour is 60 minutes of Logged Time.
3.2 Reserve share: the percentage of the anchor allowance given to Reserve Partners, as set in Schedule C. Original figure: 50 percent.
3.3 Open Applicants receive no allowance.
3.4 The tier that sets an allowance is the tier in force on the first calendar day of the Allocation Quarter, and that tier applies to the whole quarter.
3.5 Unused allowance lapses at the end of each Allocation Quarter and does not carry forward.
3.6 Public Sessions are excluded from all allowance totals.

KAINESS REACH NAVIGATION BYLAWS - CONSOLIDATED WORKING FILE
Issued By: Dreckfeamex Navigation Trust, Kainess County
File Reference: KRN-BY-2026-07
File Status: Working copy. It reflects Amendment No. 2 and the notices logged in the correspondence section. Where a later item conflicts with an earlier one, the later item governs for the period it states.

PART 1 - APPLICATION AND DEFINITIONS
1.1 These bylaws apply to every vessel navigating the Kainess Reach, Numwych Landing and the Faxness Cut.
1.2 Light Craft means a vessel whose registered overall length is 12.0 metres or less.
1.3 Made Fast means the vessel is secured to the landing by lines or fixed mooring and is not under way.
1.4 Draught means the vertical distance from the waterline to the lowest point of the hull, as stated in the most recent survey on the vessel file. A survey dated after the registration replaces the draught figure on the registration for all purposes.
1.5 All times in this file are local time for Kainess County.

PART 2 - SPEED LIMITS
2.1 The standard speed limit in the Kainess Reach is 8 knots.
2.2 The standard speed limit in the Faxness Cut is 6 knots.
2.3 Within 50 metres of Numwych Landing no vessel may exceed 3 knots.
2.4 A speed limit varied by a notice under clause 7.2 applies in place of the standard limit in clause 2.1 or 2.2 for the period the notice states.

PART 3 - MOORING AT NUMWYCH LANDING
3.1 Vessels tie up at Numwych Landing on the face marked for their class.
3.2 A vessel may remain made fast overnight only if it is Light Craft or holds a current mooring slot.
3.3 Landing fees are 14.00 per 12 hours or part thereof, payable at the landing kiosk.
3.4 Continuous stay at Numwych Landing is 48 hours for all vessels. [Replaced by Amendment No. 2, clause 6.1.]

PART 4 - FAXNESS CUT TRANSIT
4.1 Every vessel transiting the Faxness Cut must hold a current vessel file showing its draught.
4.2 A vessel whose draught exceeds 1.50 metres must be escorted through the Faxness Cut by a harbour escort. [Replaced by Amendment No. 2, clause 6.2.]
4.3 A vessel whose draught exceeds 2.10 metres must not transit the Faxness Cut.
4.4 Escort fees are set by the Harbour Master and are not part of these bylaws.

PART 5 - VESSEL FILES AND STAY REVIEWS
5.1 Each vessel with a mooring record at Numwych Landing is reviewed by the lock keeper at the time stated in the file register.
5.2 Mooring times are taken from the entries in the mooring record, not from the vessel's own log.

PART 6 - AMENDMENT NO. 2 (EFFECTIVE 2026-04-01)
6.1 Clause 3.4 is replaced by the following text: Continuous stay at Numwych Landing: a Light Craft may remain made fast for up to 72 hours; all other vessels may remain made fast for up to 48 hours. Time runs from the moment the vessel is made fast. A departure of more than two hours from the landing breaks the stay, and a new stay starts when the vessel is next made fast. A departure of two hours or less does not break the stay, and the time away counts as part of it.
6.2 Clause 4.2 is replaced by the following text: A vessel whose draught exceeds 1.70 metres must be escorted through the Faxness Cut by a harbour escort.
6.3 All clauses not listed in this Part are unchanged.

PART 7 - NOTICES
7.1 The Harbour Master may issue a notice, numbered NOT-n, to vary a speed limit. A notice takes effect on the start date it states.
7.2 A notice varying a speed limit applies from its stated start date to its stated end date, inclusive, and overrides clause 2.1 or 2.2 for that period.
7.3 A notice that states no end date remains in force until withdrawn in writing.

PART 8 - WASH AND WAVE CONTROL
8.1 Vessels must not create wash that disturbs moored craft or the bank within 100 metres of any landing.
8.2 Commercial craft must keep a log of wash incidents and produce it on request.

PART 9 - LIGHTS, SIGNALS AND REPORTING
9.1 Every vessel under way after sunset must display the lights required by the Kainess County navigation code.
9.2 A vessel intending to transit the Faxness Cut must report to the lock keeper at least two hours before entry.
9.3 Reports may be made on the reach working channel or in person at the landing kiosk.

PART 10 - OFFENCES AND PENALTIES
10.1 Breach of any bylaw in this file is an offence and may attract a fixed penalty set by the Harbour Master.
10.2 Penalty schedules are published separately and are not reproduced in this file.

PART 11 - TRANSIT LOGBOOK
11.1 The master of every vessel transiting the Faxness Cut must enter the transit in the vessel logbook, giving the time of entry and the time of exit.
11.2 Logbook entries must be kept for three years from the date of entry.
11.3 A copy of the logbook page must be shown to the escort on request.

PART 12 - WASTE AND BILGE DISCHARGE
12.1 No vessel may discharge bilge water or sewage within the Kainess Reach.
12.2 Pump-out facilities are provided at the landing kiosk and are open during kiosk hours.
12.3 Oily waste must be landed at the approved reception point and a receipt obtained.

Revision Register.Summary: First issue. Stage 2 minimum dual instruction hours set at 18.0.
Added the check window, the session counting rule and the weather exception.

Definitions.Dual Instruction Minute: A minute in which an instructor is on station in the same qualifying device as the student. Briefing and debrief minutes are not dual instruction minutes, even when logged in the same session.
Definitions.Qualifying Device: A Full Flight Simulator with code FFS-B or a Flight Training Device with code FTD-2. Hangar trainers and classroom procedure trainers are not qualifying devices.
Definitions.Solo Minute: A minute run by the student with no instructor on station. Solo minutes are never dual instruction minutes.
Definitions.Check Window: The period that begins 89 calendar days before the stage check date and ends on the stage check date. Both end days are included.

Counting Rules.Session Counting Rule: A dual session counts only if it ran to its booked end time. A dual session that ended early counts zero minutes.
Counting Rules.Weather Exception: A dual session that the instructor ended early because of weather counts at its logged minutes, provided the early stop is recorded with the weather stop code WX.
Counting Rules.Stage Check Rule: A stage check whose dual instruction minutes in the check window fall below the requirement is held, not failed. A stage failure notice is issued only after a check has been sat and failed.

Amendments.Applies To: Stage checks dated on or after the effective date
Amendments.Change: Stage 2 dual instruction hours required raised from 18.0 to 20.0.

clauses.title: Annual extraction ceiling
clauses.text_as_issued: Annual extraction shall not exceed 48,000 cubic metres in any concession year.

clauses.title: Carry-forward of unused volume
clauses.text_as_issued: Up to 10 percent of the annual ceiling not extracted in a concession year may be carried forward into the following concession year.

clauses.title: Watercourse buffers
clauses.text_as_issued: No felling of any kind within 40 metres of a mapped watercourse, measured from the mapped bank edge.

clauses.title: Windthrow exception
clauses.text_as_issued: Stems felled by windthrow may be removed under clause 6.3 where the event is reported to the district officer within 10 days of the event date.

clauses.title: Extraction returns
clauses.text_as_issued: Monthly extraction returns are due at the district office by the 10th day of the following month. Returns may be given in cubic metres or in cubic feet; divide a cubic-foot figure by 35.3 to obtain cubic metres.

outputRules.text: Every output leaving the enclave needs a written Output Checking Panel sign-off dated on or before the release date.

While a hold listed in holdNotices is in force on a dataset, no output from that dataset may leave the enclave, of any type, whatever sign-off or exemption exists. A hold is in force from its issue date up to but not including its lift date, or indefinitely if no lift date is recorded.

A summary table may leave the enclave without panel sign-off if its smallest cell count is 10 or more. Below 10, no exception applies. The exception covers releases made on or after its applies-from date only.

criteria.false: The rules bar every output type from a dataset while its hold is in force, with no carve-out for summary tables.

q5.instructions: As at the snapshot date, which release route governs the summary table in request TRE-R-0421?

criteria.panel_signoff_required: Release only after a panel sign-off dated on or before the release date, with no exception available.
criteria.blocked_by_hold: Release is blocked because a hold applies to the dataset.
criteria.summary_exception: Release may proceed without panel sign-off because the table is a summary table whose smallest cell count meets the threshold and the exception is in force.
criteria.suppress_and_resubmit: Suppress the small cells and resubmit the table for panel sign-off before release.
